Then He said: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said: Allah and His Messenger had promised us only delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab 12].
* From this noble verse is derived: a statement that the hypocrites seize opportunities.
Its aspect: in this opportunity, and in their narrow and dark condition, they began their activity, seized the opportunity, and said: "Where is the promise?" In this there is evidence that the hypocrite lives up to his name: if he finds no opportunity he keeps silent, flatters and yields, and if he finds an opportunity he speaks out. This is their habit: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they are alone with their devils, they say: Indeed, we are with you﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].
* It is derived from this noble verse: caution regarding the hypocrites, for they spare no effort to corrupt the believers. Whenever they find a point of criticism or a place to attack, they pounce. We ask Allah to protect us from them.
* It is also derived from this noble verse: that hearts are divided into sound and diseased, based on His words: ﴿and those in whose hearts is disease﴾. Likewise bodies are divided into sick and healthy. Look at the state of people today: are they more keen on treating hearts than treating bodies, or on treating bodies than treating hearts? The latter, except for whom Allah wills. Most people today are keen to treat bodies, whose end is to become carrion eaten by worms, rather than hearts, on which depends the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. You find a person whose heart is sick, perhaps to the point of burning, yet he does not care about it. But if he gets a thorn in his body, he rushes to the doctors, even if that involves hardship and fatigue.
But the wise believer is the one who is always attentive to his heart, its illness and its health, its soundness and its ruin. This is the true believer. There is no doubt that when the heart is sound, the body is sound. I am not saying that the believer's body never falls ill; but if the believer falls ill, he sees that in this illness there is benefit and advantage for him, is it not so? Thus his bodily illness becomes health for his heart, because of the patience and contentment with Allah, mighty and majestic, that arise in him, the waiting for relief, and doing the means that Allah has made means, relying upon Allah with what He has made a cause.
In sum, the illness of the heart is far more dangerous than the illness of the body, and the wise person takes greater care of this.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that Allah and His Messenger have promised the believers victory, based on His words: ﴿what Allah and His Messenger had promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab 12]. The promise is mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah for the believers. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51], and He said: ﴿And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ [al-Rum 47]. Look at this great promise: ﴿incumbent upon Us﴾ is emphatic, ﴿help the believers﴾. And the one who guarantees this, my brothers, is the Lord, mighty and majestic, in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. But, regrettably, many believers do not take these things into account, although Allah has guaranteed it.
And in the Sunnah the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror across a distance of a month's journey" [agreed upon: al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both)]. His victory, peace and blessings be upon him, is not a victory for his person, but a victory for what he brought, so the victory belongs to him and to his community after him as well.
* It is derived from this noble verse: a clarification that the hypocrite's outlook is limited, and likewise whoever has disease in his heart has a limited outlook.
Its aspect: they looked only at the present moment, they did not consider the outcome. Such events that come upon them are passing circumstances, but the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. So no one builds upon passing circumstances except the weak of insight. Even in worldly matters, do not look at passing circumstances, for as it is said: "the permanence of a state is impossible." But as long as you are confident in Allah's promise, mighty and majestic, be certain that this promise will be fulfilled, though there may befall it passing circumstances, by a wisdom of Allah's wisdoms through which He tests, and then the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. I think the lessons are finished. (...).
Great, not one of them turned back from his religion, but there are words, for example, from one weak in faith, yet they do not settle.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, despite the intense propaganda of the hypocrites, for the hypocrites undoubtedly have great propaganda; they are not silent, they do not keep quiet. But, by the grace of Allah, Allah made them firm. (...)
﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 9–12 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿So We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ — the angels — ﴿and Allah is ever, of what you do, Seeing﴾ — with the ta' (you do), referring to those who dug the trench; and with the ya' (they do), referring to the confederation of the polytheists). That is, there are two readings: ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ and ﴿bima ta'malun basira﴾.

As for His saying ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾: what is this wind? I have told you that it is the east wind, and for this reason it came in the hadith: "I was given victory by theṣabā (the east wind), and 'Ād was destroyed by the dabūr (the west wind)"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1035) and Muslim (900/17), from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. The dabūr is the west wind.

He says: (﴿bima ta'malun﴾ with the ta', referring to those who dug the trench). But this restriction of the verse is not appropriate. Why is it not appropriate? Because if we restrict the generality of the verse, we limit the meaning of the wording, or we confine the wording to part of its meaning. The correct understanding is that ﴿bima ta'malun﴾ covers digging the trench and everything else you did in this battle.

(Basir) means: knowing. Or ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ means: the armies, ﴿when the armies came upon you﴾. So Allah the Exalted is Seeing of what they do, of the confederating against the Prophet ﷺ and of their coming to the city of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in order to eliminate him, as they supposed.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾ [al-Ahzab 10] — from the upper part of the valley and its lower part, from the east and the west). They came from the east and from the west: the Quraysh came from the north-eastern side, and the Ghaṭafān and the Jews of Banu Qurayẓa came from the south-western side, so they came from above the Muslims and from below them.

As I told you a little while ago: the trench extended from the eastern lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Sharqiyyah) to the western lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Gharbiyyah), and the whole north is now protected by the trench. They came from above them and from below them, so that they would be like the two jaws of a lion, closing in upon the city. This was their plan, but Allah the Exalted is ever encompassing of what they do.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the eyes swerved﴾. "Zāgha" means: it inclined, and from it comes "zāghat al-shams" (the sun declined), when it inclines at midday. And from it His saying: ﴿The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ [al-Najm 17], that is, it did not incline.

﴿Al-Abṣār﴾ (the eyes): the definite article here is for a known reference. Which reference? A mental one. That is: the eyes of you swerved. The author says in explaining it: (they inclined away from everything toward their enemy from every direction). That is, the eyes had no gaze except toward this enemy; they were heedless of everything else, looking only at this enemy.

Some exegetes explained it: ﴿zāgha﴾ means: it moved from its place of rest, i.e., they became fixed in a stare from the intensity of terror. A person looks only at what is before him, watching it and fearing it. This is something observed in human nature: when a person fears something, where does his gaze turn? To that thing, toward its direction. And you find the eye, as the common people say, stays wide open, fearing a surprise attack. So the eyes swerved. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾: "the hearts" means: of you; your hearts reached (﴿the throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe).

His saying: (from the intensity of fear) explains His saying ﴿swerved﴾ and ﴿reached﴾. ﴿The throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe, meaning from here. Is this literally ﴿the hearts reached the throats﴾? Some said: it is literal, and that when the fearful person's fear intensifies, his lungs swell; when they swell they press upon the heart so that it rises up. For this reason it is said of a coward or a frightened person: "his lungs have swollen" (inbaṭa saḥruh), meaning his lungs. The principle is to take a matter in its literal sense. It is also permissible that this is a depiction of the intensity of terror, meaning that from the intensity of terror the hearts left their places, so they neither breathe normally nor beat normally, because they had left their places.

Then He said: (﴿And you were thinking about Allah various thoughts﴾, diverse in regard to victory and despair). This is a difference between victory and despair. ﴿You were thinking﴾, that is, you, concerning Allah, ﴿the thoughts﴾, with the alif for the extension of the pronunciation. These "thoughts" are the plural of ẓann, and a verbal noun is not made plural except when it denotes kinds. If it is one single kind, it cannot be pluralized however many instances there are; but if it denotes kinds, its plural is valid. So here ẓann, which is a verbal noun, was made plural because of its variety. That is, the thoughts revolved in their minds or in their thinking, varying in length and breadth: Will these confederates be dispelled? Will they destroy us? Will we be victorious? You know what fear does to a person in terms of near and distant thoughts and imaginings. Among them were those who thought despair, or despaired, saying: there is nothing after this. Among them were those who thought victory, and how could that be, given the situation was extremely dark? Because he believes that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship is ease. They say: we are upon the truth, so if we are upon the truth and we are patient, then victory is, what? Guaranteed. Therefore they thought victory.

Among them were the people of material means and outward sensory appearances, who thought, what? Destruction, and despaired of victory, because they had no store of faith to rely upon. There is no doubt that among those who went out for this, there were hypocrites, as will become apparent in the story.

The point is that Allah said: ﴿You were thinking about Allah thoughts﴾ and left it unrestricted, and put it in the plural so that a person may take the imagining of this thought in every direction: many thoughts, diverse and conflicting.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. How? For this reason the "thoughts" came in the plural.

He said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾. Is ﴿there (hunalika)﴾ a demonstrative of place or of time? Of place, or of time, or of both together. ﴿Hunalika﴾ is suitable for time and for place, but the original usage is for place, and it also comes for time.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might; the custom of Allah that has passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost﴾ [Ghafir 85]: that is, at that time the disbelievers lost. So ﴿hunalika﴾ (there) is suitable for time and place; the lam indicates distance, and the kaf indicates address. ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: they were examined. And who tested them? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, examined them, through what befell them of this great constriction, which cannot be expressed in speech and cannot be felt except by one who experiences it. We here are unable to imagine that state and unable to depict it, but the one who was in it knows about it.

He says: (﴿There the believers were tested﴾, that is: they were examined, so that the sincere might be distinguished from others. ﴿And they were shaken﴾: they were stirred, ﴿with a severe shaking﴾ from the intensity of dread).

A great trial and a great shaking befell them. This shaking struck them, not an earthquake of the earth, but a shaking of souls. Souls were convulsed and something great happened to them, because in this battle there gathered the confederation of the Arab tribes, the treachery of Banu Qurayẓa, hunger, fatigue, exhaustion, and cold. How many? Five things, any one of which suffices to shake the soul. How much more so when they combine?

The affair was difficult. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was in that place, binding a stone to his stomach from hunger. How can you imagine the condition? A person cannot truly express it. For this reason He said: ﴿They were shaken with a severe shaking﴾, strong and great, shaking their souls because these trials gathered upon them, may Allah be pleased with them.

For this reason hypocrisy emerged and the hypocrites spoke, seeing in this an opportunity to talk, because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was promising them victory, even in that battle he was promising them victory. And the story of the rock that they could not get through, where the axes broke and they grew weary, until they came to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, you planned for us! Because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, had marked out the trench for them, drawing its line with his foot.

It was by the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the line fell upon this rock they could not get through. But out of their great obedience, may Allah be pleased with them, they did not say: let us bend it right or left; rather they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him. He descended from his shelter that had been built for him on a hill there to overlook the people, descended, took the pickaxe and struck it a blow. Ibn Ishaq says: when he struck it the blow, it gave off a great light, as if we were in daylight, and a part of it crumbled. Then he struck it again and said Allah is greatest, peace and blessings be upon him.

* Student: At night?

* The Shaykh: At night. He said Allah is greatest, then struck a second time, and it gave light, and he said the takbir of conquest, a great takbir. Then he struck a third time and said Allah is greatest. They said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this? He said: "In the first takbir I saw the palaces of Rome, and in the second the palaces of Kisra, and in the third the palaces of Ṣan'ā' in Yemen, and that they will be conquered"[[Narrated by Aḥmad (18694) from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to dig the trench. He said: a rock appeared to us in a place in the trench, which the pickaxes would not bite. So we complained of it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and 'Awf said: I think he said: he placed his garment, then descended to the rock, took the pickaxe and said: "In the name of Allah," and struck a blow that broke a third of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of al-Sham, and by Allah I see its red palaces from this place of mine." Then he said: "In the name of Allah," and struck another that broke a third of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of Persia, and by Allah I see the cities, and I see its white palace from this place of mine." Then he said: "In the name of Allah," and struck another blow that uprooted the rest of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of Yemen, and by Allah I see the gates of Ṣan'ā' from this place of mine."]].

What is this? Is it good news for the believers or not? It is good news and strengthening. But the hypocrites, may Allah protect us, who do not trust the promise of Allah and His Messenger, said: How can this be? One of us cannot even go to relieve himself, how will we possess the palaces of Kisra and Caesar and Tubba'? This is not true.

For this reason He says: (﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾: weakness of belief, ﴿said: Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab 12] of victory). I seek refuge in Allah. How can humans speak such words? But, may Allah protect us, as long as their hearts harbored disbelief or doubt, because those in whose hearts is a disease have doubt and weakness of belief, while the hypocrites have disbelief.

They said: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾. Glory be to the Mighty! Allah and His Messenger promise you delusion, and lie to you and deceive you?! This is impossible. Rather, what Allah and His Messenger promised is nothing but truth. But one cannot gather honey except after tasting the thorns of the bee; there must be hardship and patience, perseverance, for otherwise the truthful would not be distinguished from the liar, nor the believer from the disbeliever. So there must be trial.

For this reason, by the way, students of knowledge may face some difficulties in calling to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They may face that even within themselves, but they must be patient and bear it in calling to Allah, because they are not calling to the path of so-and-so or so-and-so among the ways of the tyrants, but to the path of Allah, which brings them and the servants of Allah to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So they must be patient. It is not that as soon as someone says to them: you are an extremist, you are a zealot, you have such-and-such in you, they retreat and abandon it. This is not right; they must be patient and persevere, act with wisdom and not with violence, and for everything there is a station, as we have often mentioned.

The summary is that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, promised his companions victory, so the believers believed it, and the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease spoke these words: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾.

They lied, by Allah. Allah and His Messenger promised them nothing but truth and sincerity. And it has come to pass, praise be to Allah. This Ummah, praise be to Allah, through the knowledge and guidance that His Messenger ﷺ left it, and through what the Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them, accomplished, conquered the palaces of Caesar and Kisra and Yemen. The treasures of Kisra and Caesar were spent in the way of Allah, and the crown of Kisra was brought from al-Madā'in to Madinah, brought in the caliphate of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Thus what Allah and His Messenger promised was fulfilled, although the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away before that happened. But in reality it was he who opened this, because the Companions did not open them except by the Shari'ah of Allah. So it became a victory for the Prophet ﷺ, because victory, as we often say, is not the triumph of a person by his own self, but his triumph through what he brought and called to, even if it is through his followers, and even if it is after his death, as long as what he brought prevails. And Allah knows best.

﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts (10) There﴾ [al-Ahzab 10, 11]: if you stop, you say: ﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts﴾, and the third reading: ﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts (10) there﴾, meaning in continuation and in pause. Similarly is His saying in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿We obeyed Allah and we obeyed the Messenger﴾ [al-Ahzab 66], ﴿and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab 67]; in them are these three readings.

What are the thoughts they thought about Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Shall we take the benefits then?

* From the noble verse is derived His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾: a statement of the favor of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon this Ummah, its first and last, through this defense by Allah, Glorified and Exalted, of the believers.
Its basis: Allah commanded us to mention this blessing.

* From the noble verse is derived: the blessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is either the bringing about of something beloved or the repelling of something disliked, and what is in the verse is of the category of repelling what is disliked.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a statement of the severity of the enmity of the disbelievers toward the believers, because they formed a confederation against them. These tribes may have no bond among themselves in themselves, but because they agreed in enmity toward Islam, they gathered.

* From the noble verse is derived: the Jews have no covenant, and they are people of treachery and betrayal.
Its basis: the breaking of the covenant by Banu Qurayẓa with the Messenger ﷺ. All three Jewish tribes had made a covenant with the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when he arrived in Madinah, yet they broke the covenant: Banu Qaynuqā', Banu al-Naḍīr and Banu Qurayẓa all broke the covenant, because the Jews are among the most treacherous and deceitful of people.

* From the noble verse is derived: a statement of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾ [al-Ahzab 9].

* And from it: what some scholars pointed out, that when the wind comes singular it is in punishment, and when it comes plural it is in mercy, except that it may come singular in mercy when it is described by something that indicates that, such as His saying: ﴿And they sailed with them by a good wind and rejoiced in it﴾ [Yunus 22].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the angels are soldiers of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿and armies you did not see﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. If you say: here it was not attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so how do you say they are the soldiers of Allah? Because He says: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, attributing their sending to Himself, and He said in another verse: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾ [al-Muddaththir 31].

If you say: Is the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in need of soldiers?
The answer: Of course not, and He cannot be in need. But why were they called soldiers even though He has no need of them?
Because they carry out His command and defend His allies, so they are in the position of soldiers. Otherwise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has no need of them or of anyone else, because He is free of need of every creature.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 9–12 (part 2 of 2):

* One of the lessons of this noble verse: people do not see the angels, based on His words: ﴿You did not see them﴾. This is so, but they may sometimes see them, just as the people saw Jibril (Gabriel) when he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him about Islam, faith, excellence (ihsan), the Hour and its signs.
* It is also derived from this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of everything we do: ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. Does this include the deeds of the heart? It does, by the evidence of the Most High's words: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16], and that is an action of the heart. As for the actions of the limbs, they are evident.
* It is derived from this noble verse: encouragement and warning (al-targhib wa al-tarhib). ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾. In this there is encouragement regarding righteous deeds, that such a deed will not be lost, because it is known to Allah, glorified and exalted, and He will surely reward for it. And a warning, for whom? 
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we do not say: the disbelievers. Whoever commits an evil deed, it is a warning to him. When your soul tempts you one day to do an evil deed because no one among the creation will see it, then remember that Allah sees you: ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what they do﴾. For this reason there came in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best of faith is that you know that Allah is with you wherever you are" [narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8796) from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him)]. Not with you in your place, but He is with you while He is upon His Throne, glorified and exalted, encompassing you.
And the Most High said: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab 10]. Five things by which Allah reminded them, so that the aspect of the blessing would become clear.
* It is derived from this noble verse: whoever is reminded should be told the aspect of what he was reminded of, or not? Generalities are not like details.
So from this we take a lesson: the one who reminds should elaborate on what he reminds of, so that this is more effective in the addressee's remembrance.
* It is derived from this noble verse: the condition that befell the Muslims was a great and terrifying condition, and that they could not repel it by themselves. Through this the aspect of Allah's blessing upon them becomes clear, because the enemies surrounded them, because their eyes shifted and their hearts reached their throats, and the illusions and thoughts they had may have stunned them from here and there, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾.
* It is derived from this noble verse: fears disturb a person even in his perceptions, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾. The settled person does not have conflicting, contradictory assumptions, because he is settled. But when alarm occurs and when fear occurs, assumptions come from every side, from every direction.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that a person's natural fear of a created being is not considered shirk. From where is this taken? From His words: ﴿the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, for this is from the intensity of fear, and it is fear of a created being. But the motive for it is a natural matter, and if it is a natural matter, a person is not held accountable for it. For this reason the messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, were described with it, and indeed the people of firm resolve among the messengers were described with it. Allah said about Musa: ﴿So he left it, fearful, watchful﴾ [al-Qasas 21], and when Allah charged him with the message he said: ﴿I fear that they will kill me﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 14]. This is natural fear for which a person is not blamed.
* And in this noble verse there is also evidence that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, despite their lofty rank, may be overtaken by assumptions because of distress, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾, and He is addressing the believers: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. So because of the intensity of distress such whisperings may come upon them, but in reality it is a summer cloud: when a person returns to Allah's promise, mighty and majestic, all of this departs from him and is replaced.
So in the sequence of the verses there will come to us His words: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said: This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. Subhan Allah! They see these great confederates, then they reassure themselves that this is what Allah and His Messenger promised, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth, because victory is with patience, and relief is with hardship. When they saw these great confederates and what follows from their presence of severity and distress, they knew that victory was near, for Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: When is the help of Allah? Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [al-Baqarah 214]. Look, the help of Allah is near in such a condition: ﴿they were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken﴾.
If you apply this to the condition of the believers at the time of the confederates, you will find that it applies. At the end of the verse: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾. Thus it was true of them that this is what Allah and His Messenger promised, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth regarding the nearness of victory.
In sum, such matters that come as passing states do not affect a person's rank or his condition, because they pass away.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that when a person is overcome by a condition such that these assumptions reach him, he does not lower his rank. But as I said a little while ago: when his condition settles and these assumptions calm down, he recognizes the truth.
* It is derived from this noble verse, from His words: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab 11]: a depiction of the state the believers were in at that moment, which was a great trial. This was a trial with respect to the events that occurred, and with respect to their souls: were they settled?
The answer: No, ﴿they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾. So there combined upon them the outward trial that is seen with the eye, and the inward trial, which is the shaking of souls and their lack of settledness. For this reason He said: ﴿they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾.
* And in this noble verse also: a statement of the general rule, that Allah, the Most High, mentions blessings attributed to Himself, and mentions calamities mostly in the passive voice. Here He said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾, ﴿and were shaken﴾. By whom did this occur? By Allah, glorified and exalted. But in matters of good He attributes the thing to Himself, praising Himself, and in matters of the opposite the verbs come in the passive voice.
And consider the words of the jinn: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 10]. In the case of evil they said: ﴿is intended﴾, and for guidance they attributed it to Allah, mighty and majestic, because evil is not attributed to Allah. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And evil is not to You" [narrated by Muslim (771/201) from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him)]. So it is not permissible for a person to attribute evil to Allah at all. Evil exists in created things, not in the act itself, because the created things of Allah, mighty and majestic, have two aspects: an aspect considered as an act of Allah, and an aspect considered in their own essence. As for their essence, in them there is good and evil by themselves: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak (1) from the evil of what He created﴾ [al-Falaq 1-2]. As for them considered as an act of Allah, there is no evil in them. Is this clear, brothers?
Considered as an act of Allah, there is no evil in them, and considered in their essence there is good and evil. Considered as an act, there is no evil in them, because Allah only decreed it for a wisdom. Moreover, if you reflect on the things that are evil, you will find that they contain good even though they are evil. Corruption on land and sea, from drought, poverty and other things, is evil, but its outcome is good: ﴿so that they may return﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said: Allah and His Messenger had promised us only delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab 12].
* From this noble verse is derived: a statement that the hypocrites seize opportunities.
Its aspect: in this opportunity, and in their narrow and dark condition, they began their activity, seized the opportunity, and said: "Where is the promise?" In this there is evidence that the hypocrite lives up to his name: if he finds no opportunity he keeps silent, flatters and yields, and if he finds an opportunity he speaks out. This is their habit: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they are alone with their devils, they say: Indeed, we are with you﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].
* It is derived from this noble verse: caution regarding the hypocrites, for they spare no effort to corrupt the believers. Whenever they find a point of criticism or a place to attack, they pounce. We ask Allah to protect us from them.
* It is also derived from this noble verse: that hearts are divided into sound and diseased, based on His words: ﴿and those in whose hearts is disease﴾. Likewise bodies are divided into sick and healthy. Look at the state of people today: are they more keen on treating hearts than treating bodies, or on treating bodies than treating hearts? The latter, except for whom Allah wills. Most people today are keen to treat bodies, whose end is to become carrion eaten by worms, rather than hearts, on which depends the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. You find a person whose heart is sick, perhaps to the point of burning, yet he does not care about it. But if he gets a thorn in his body, he rushes to the doctors, even if that involves hardship and fatigue.
But the wise believer is the one who is always attentive to his heart, its illness and its health, its soundness and its ruin. This is the true believer. There is no doubt that when the heart is sound, the body is sound. I am not saying that the believer's body never falls ill; but if the believer falls ill, he sees that in this illness there is benefit and advantage for him, is it not so? Thus his bodily illness becomes health for his heart, because of the patience and contentment with Allah, mighty and majestic, that arise in him, the waiting for relief, and doing the means that Allah has made means, relying upon Allah with what He has made a cause.
In sum, the illness of the heart is far more dangerous than the illness of the body, and the wise person takes greater care of this.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that Allah and His Messenger have promised the believers victory, based on His words: ﴿what Allah and His Messenger had promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab 12]. The promise is mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah for the believers. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51], and He said: ﴿And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ [al-Rum 47]. Look at this great promise: ﴿incumbent upon Us﴾ is emphatic, ﴿help the believers﴾. And the one who guarantees this, my brothers, is the Lord, mighty and majestic, in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. But, regrettably, many believers do not take these things into account, although Allah has guaranteed it.
And in the Sunnah the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror across a distance of a month's journey" [agreed upon: al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both)]. His victory, peace and blessings be upon him, is not a victory for his person, but a victory for what he brought, so the victory belongs to him and to his community after him as well.
* It is derived from this noble verse: a clarification that the hypocrite's outlook is limited, and likewise whoever has disease in his heart has a limited outlook.
Its aspect: they looked only at the present moment, they did not consider the outcome. Such events that come upon them are passing circumstances, but the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. So no one builds upon passing circumstances except the weak of insight. Even in worldly matters, do not look at passing circumstances, for as it is said: "the permanence of a state is impossible." But as long as you are confident in Allah's promise, mighty and majestic, be certain that this promise will be fulfilled, though there may befall it passing circumstances, by a wisdom of Allah's wisdoms through which He tests, and then the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. I think the lessons are finished. (...).
Great, not one of them turned back from his religion, but there are words, for example, from one weak in faith, yet they do not settle.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, despite the intense propaganda of the hypocrites, for the hypocrites undoubtedly have great propaganda; they are not silent, they do not keep quiet. But, by the grace of Allah, Allah made them firm. (...)
﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 9–12 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿So We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ — the angels — ﴿and Allah is ever, of what you do, Seeing﴾ — with the ta' (you do), referring to those who dug the trench; and with the ya' (they do), referring to the confederation of the polytheists). That is, there are two readings: ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ and ﴿bima ta'malun basira﴾.

As for His saying ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾: what is this wind? I have told you that it is the east wind, and for this reason it came in the hadith: "I was given victory by theṣabā (the east wind), and 'Ād was destroyed by the dabūr (the west wind)"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1035) and Muslim (900/17), from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. The dabūr is the west wind.

He says: (﴿bima ta'malun﴾ with the ta', referring to those who dug the trench). But this restriction of the verse is not appropriate. Why is it not appropriate? Because if we restrict the generality of the verse, we limit the meaning of the wording, or we confine the wording to part of its meaning. The correct understanding is that ﴿bima ta'malun﴾ covers digging the trench and everything else you did in this battle.

(Basir) means: knowing. Or ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ means: the armies, ﴿when the armies came upon you﴾. So Allah the Exalted is Seeing of what they do, of the confederating against the Prophet ﷺ and of their coming to the city of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in order to eliminate him, as they supposed.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾ [al-Ahzab 10] — from the upper part of the valley and its lower part, from the east and the west). They came from the east and from the west: the Quraysh came from the north-eastern side, and the Ghaṭafān and the Jews of Banu Qurayẓa came from the south-western side, so they came from above the Muslims and from below them.

As I told you a little while ago: the trench extended from the eastern lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Sharqiyyah) to the western lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Gharbiyyah), and the whole north is now protected by the trench. They came from above them and from below them, so that they would be like the two jaws of a lion, closing in upon the city. This was their plan, but Allah the Exalted is ever encompassing of what they do.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the eyes swerved﴾. "Zāgha" means: it inclined, and from it comes "zāghat al-shams" (the sun declined), when it inclines at midday. And from it His saying: ﴿The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ [al-Najm 17], that is, it did not incline.

﴿Al-Abṣār﴾ (the eyes): the definite article here is for a known reference. Which reference? A mental one. That is: the eyes of you swerved. The author says in explaining it: (they inclined away from everything toward their enemy from every direction). That is, the eyes had no gaze except toward this enemy; they were heedless of everything else, looking only at this enemy.

Some exegetes explained it: ﴿zāgha﴾ means: it moved from its place of rest, i.e., they became fixed in a stare from the intensity of terror. A person looks only at what is before him, watching it and fearing it. This is something observed in human nature: when a person fears something, where does his gaze turn? To that thing, toward its direction. And you find the eye, as the common people say, stays wide open, fearing a surprise attack. So the eyes swerved. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾: "the hearts" means: of you; your hearts reached (﴿the throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe).

His saying: (from the intensity of fear) explains His saying ﴿swerved﴾ and ﴿reached﴾. ﴿The throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe, meaning from here. Is this literally ﴿the hearts reached the throats﴾? Some said: it is literal, and that when the fearful person's fear intensifies, his lungs swell; when they swell they press upon the heart so that it rises up. For this reason it is said of a coward or a frightened person: "his lungs have swollen" (inbaṭa saḥruh), meaning his lungs. The principle is to take a matter in its literal sense. It is also permissible that this is a depiction of the intensity of terror, meaning that from the intensity of terror the hearts left their places, so they neither breathe normally nor beat normally, because they had left their places.

Then He said: (﴿And you were thinking about Allah various thoughts﴾, diverse in regard to victory and despair). This is a difference between victory and despair. ﴿You were thinking﴾, that is, you, concerning Allah, ﴿the thoughts﴾, with the alif for the extension of the pronunciation. These "thoughts" are the plural of ẓann, and a verbal noun is not made plural except when it denotes kinds. If it is one single kind, it cannot be pluralized however many instances there are; but if it denotes kinds, its plural is valid. So here ẓann, which is a verbal noun, was made plural because of its variety. That is, the thoughts revolved in their minds or in their thinking, varying in length and breadth: Will these confederates be dispelled? Will they destroy us? Will we be victorious? You know what fear does to a person in terms of near and distant thoughts and imaginings. Among them were those who thought despair, or despaired, saying: there is nothing after this. Among them were those who thought victory, and how could that be, given the situation was extremely dark? Because he believes that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship is ease. They say: we are upon the truth, so if we are upon the truth and we are patient, then victory is, what? Guaranteed. Therefore they thought victory.

Among them were the people of material means and outward sensory appearances, who thought, what? Destruction, and despaired of victory, because they had no store of faith to rely upon. There is no doubt that among those who went out for this, there were hypocrites, as will become apparent in the story.

The point is that Allah said: ﴿You were thinking about Allah thoughts﴾ and left it unrestricted, and put it in the plural so that a person may take the imagining of this thought in every direction: many thoughts, diverse and conflicting.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. How? For this reason the "thoughts" came in the plural.

He said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾. Is ﴿there (hunalika)﴾ a demonstrative of place or of time? Of place, or of time, or of both together. ﴿Hunalika﴾ is suitable for time and for place, but the original usage is for place, and it also comes for time.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might; the custom of Allah that has passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost﴾ [Ghafir 85]: that is, at that time the disbelievers lost. So ﴿hunalika﴾ (there) is suitable for time and place; the lam indicates distance, and the kaf indicates address. ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: they were examined. And who tested them? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, examined them, through what befell them of this great constriction, which cannot be expressed in speech and cannot be felt except by one who experiences it. We here are unable to imagine that state and unable to depict it, but the one who was in it knows about it.

He says: (﴿There the believers were tested﴾, that is: they were examined, so that the sincere might be distinguished from others. ﴿And they were shaken﴾: they were stirred, ﴿with a severe shaking﴾ from the intensity of dread).

A great trial and a great shaking befell them. This shaking struck them, not an earthquake of the earth, but a shaking of souls. Souls were convulsed and something great happened to them, because in this battle there gathered the confederation of the Arab tribes, the treachery of Banu Qurayẓa, hunger, fatigue, exhaustion, and cold. How many? Five things, any one of which suffices to shake the soul. How much more so when they combine?

The affair was difficult. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was in that place, binding a stone to his stomach from hunger. How can you imagine the condition? A person cannot truly express it. For this reason He said: ﴿They were shaken with a severe shaking﴾, strong and great, shaking their souls because these trials gathered upon them, may Allah be pleased with them.

For this reason hypocrisy emerged and the hypocrites spoke, seeing in this an opportunity to talk, because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was promising them victory, even in that battle he was promising them victory. And the story of the rock that they could not get through, where the axes broke and they grew weary, until they came to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, you planned for us! Because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, had marked out the trench for them, drawing its line with his foot.

It was by the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the line fell upon this rock they could not get through. But out of their great obedience, may Allah be pleased with them, they did not say: let us bend it right or left; rather they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him. He descended from his shelter that had been built for him on a hill there to overlook the people, descended, took the pickaxe and struck it a blow. Ibn Ishaq says: when he struck it the blow, it gave off a great light, as if we were in daylight, and a part of it crumbled. Then he struck it again and said Allah is greatest, peace and blessings be upon him.

* Student: At night?

* The Shaykh: At night. He said Allah is greatest, then struck a second time, and it gave light, and he said the takbir of conquest, a great takbir. Then he struck a third time and said Allah is greatest. They said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this? He said: "In the first takbir I saw the palaces of Rome, and in the second the palaces of Kisra, and in the third the palaces of Ṣan'ā' in Yemen, and that they will be conquered"[[Narrated by Aḥmad (18694) from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to dig the trench. He said: a rock appeared to us in a place in the trench, which the pickaxes would not bite. So we complained of it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and 'Awf said: I think he said: he placed his garment, then descended to the rock, took the pickaxe and said: "In the name of Allah," and struck a blow that broke a third of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of al-Sham, and by Allah I see its red palaces from this place of mine." Then he said: "In the name of Allah," and struck another that broke a third of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of Persia, and by Allah I see the cities, and I see its white palace from this place of mine." Then he said: "In the name of Allah," and struck another blow that uprooted the rest of the stone, and said: "Allah is greatest, I have been given the keys of Yemen, and by Allah I see the gates of Ṣan'ā' from this place of mine."]].

What is this? Is it good news for the believers or not? It is good news and strengthening. But the hypocrites, may Allah protect us, who do not trust the promise of Allah and His Messenger, said: How can this be? One of us cannot even go to relieve himself, how will we possess the palaces of Kisra and Caesar and Tubba'? This is not true.

For this reason He says: (﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾: weakness of belief, ﴿said: Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab 12] of victory). I seek refuge in Allah. How can humans speak such words? But, may Allah protect us, as long as their hearts harbored disbelief or doubt, because those in whose hearts is a disease have doubt and weakness of belief, while the hypocrites have disbelief.

They said: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾. Glory be to the Mighty! Allah and His Messenger promise you delusion, and lie to you and deceive you?! This is impossible. Rather, what Allah and His Messenger promised is nothing but truth. But one cannot gather honey except after tasting the thorns of the bee; there must be hardship and patience, perseverance, for otherwise the truthful would not be distinguished from the liar, nor the believer from the disbeliever. So there must be trial.

For this reason, by the way, students of knowledge may face some difficulties in calling to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They may face that even within themselves, but they must be patient and bear it in calling to Allah, because they are not calling to the path of so-and-so or so-and-so among the ways of the tyrants, but to the path of Allah, which brings them and the servants of Allah to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So they must be patient. It is not that as soon as someone says to them: you are an extremist, you are a zealot, you have such-and-such in you, they retreat and abandon it. This is not right; they must be patient and persevere, act with wisdom and not with violence, and for everything there is a station, as we have often mentioned.

The summary is that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, promised his companions victory, so the believers believed it, and the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease spoke these words: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾.

They lied, by Allah. Allah and His Messenger promised them nothing but truth and sincerity. And it has come to pass, praise be to Allah. This Ummah, praise be to Allah, through the knowledge and guidance that His Messenger ﷺ left it, and through what the Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them, accomplished, conquered the palaces of Caesar and Kisra and Yemen. The treasures of Kisra and Caesar were spent in the way of Allah, and the crown of Kisra was brought from al-Madā'in to Madinah, brought in the caliphate of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Thus what Allah and His Messenger promised was fulfilled, although the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away before that happened. But in reality it was he who opened this, because the Companions did not open them except by the Shari'ah of Allah. So it became a victory for the Prophet ﷺ, because victory, as we often say, is not the triumph of a person by his own self, but his triumph through what he brought and called to, even if it is through his followers, and even if it is after his death, as long as what he brought prevails. And Allah knows best.

﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts (10) There﴾ [al-Ahzab 10, 11]: if you stop, you say: ﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts﴾, and the third reading: ﴿And you were thinking about Allah thoughts (10) there﴾, meaning in continuation and in pause. Similarly is His saying in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿We obeyed Allah and we obeyed the Messenger﴾ [al-Ahzab 66], ﴿and they led us astray from the way﴾ [al-Ahzab 67]; in them are these three readings.

What are the thoughts they thought about Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Shall we take the benefits then?

* From the noble verse is derived His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾: a statement of the favor of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon this Ummah, its first and last, through this defense by Allah, Glorified and Exalted, of the believers.
Its basis: Allah commanded us to mention this blessing.

* From the noble verse is derived: the blessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is either the bringing about of something beloved or the repelling of something disliked, and what is in the verse is of the category of repelling what is disliked.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a statement of the severity of the enmity of the disbelievers toward the believers, because they formed a confederation against them. These tribes may have no bond among themselves in themselves, but because they agreed in enmity toward Islam, they gathered.

* From the noble verse is derived: the Jews have no covenant, and they are people of treachery and betrayal.
Its basis: the breaking of the covenant by Banu Qurayẓa with the Messenger ﷺ. All three Jewish tribes had made a covenant with the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when he arrived in Madinah, yet they broke the covenant: Banu Qaynuqā', Banu al-Naḍīr and Banu Qurayẓa all broke the covenant, because the Jews are among the most treacherous and deceitful of people.

* From the noble verse is derived: a statement of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾ [al-Ahzab 9].

* And from it: what some scholars pointed out, that when the wind comes singular it is in punishment, and when it comes plural it is in mercy, except that it may come singular in mercy when it is described by something that indicates that, such as His saying: ﴿And they sailed with them by a good wind and rejoiced in it﴾ [Yunus 22].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the angels are soldiers of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿and armies you did not see﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. If you say: here it was not attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so how do you say they are the soldiers of Allah? Because He says: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, attributing their sending to Himself, and He said in another verse: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾ [al-Muddaththir 31].

If you say: Is the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in need of soldiers?
The answer: Of course not, and He cannot be in need. But why were they called soldiers even though He has no need of them?
Because they carry out His command and defend His allies, so they are in the position of soldiers. Otherwise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has no need of them or of anyone else, because He is free of need of every creature.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 9–12 (part 2 of 2):

* One of the lessons of this noble verse: people do not see the angels, based on His words: ﴿You did not see them﴾. This is so, but they may sometimes see them, just as the people saw Jibril (Gabriel) when he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him about Islam, faith, excellence (ihsan), the Hour and its signs.
* It is also derived from this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of everything we do: ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. Does this include the deeds of the heart? It does, by the evidence of the Most High's words: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16], and that is an action of the heart. As for the actions of the limbs, they are evident.
* It is derived from this noble verse: encouragement and warning (al-targhib wa al-tarhib). ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾. In this there is encouragement regarding righteous deeds, that such a deed will not be lost, because it is known to Allah, glorified and exalted, and He will surely reward for it. And a warning, for whom? 
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we do not say: the disbelievers. Whoever commits an evil deed, it is a warning to him. When your soul tempts you one day to do an evil deed because no one among the creation will see it, then remember that Allah sees you: ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what they do﴾. For this reason there came in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best of faith is that you know that Allah is with you wherever you are" [narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8796) from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him)]. Not with you in your place, but He is with you while He is upon His Throne, glorified and exalted, encompassing you.
And the Most High said: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab 10]. Five things by which Allah reminded them, so that the aspect of the blessing would become clear.
* It is derived from this noble verse: whoever is reminded should be told the aspect of what he was reminded of, or not? Generalities are not like details.
So from this we take a lesson: the one who reminds should elaborate on what he reminds of, so that this is more effective in the addressee's remembrance.
* It is derived from this noble verse: the condition that befell the Muslims was a great and terrifying condition, and that they could not repel it by themselves. Through this the aspect of Allah's blessing upon them becomes clear, because the enemies surrounded them, because their eyes shifted and their hearts reached their throats, and the illusions and thoughts they had may have stunned them from here and there, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾.
* It is derived from this noble verse: fears disturb a person even in his perceptions, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾. The settled person does not have conflicting, contradictory assumptions, because he is settled. But when alarm occurs and when fear occurs, assumptions come from every side, from every direction.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that a person's natural fear of a created being is not considered shirk. From where is this taken? From His words: ﴿the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats﴾, for this is from the intensity of fear, and it is fear of a created being. But the motive for it is a natural matter, and if it is a natural matter, a person is not held accountable for it. For this reason the messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, were described with it, and indeed the people of firm resolve among the messengers were described with it. Allah said about Musa: ﴿So he left it, fearful, watchful﴾ [al-Qasas 21], and when Allah charged him with the message he said: ﴿I fear that they will kill me﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 14]. This is natural fear for which a person is not blamed.
* And in this noble verse there is also evidence that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, despite their lofty rank, may be overtaken by assumptions because of distress, based on His words: ﴿and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾, and He is addressing the believers: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ [al-Ahzab 9]. So because of the intensity of distress such whisperings may come upon them, but in reality it is a summer cloud: when a person returns to Allah's promise, mighty and majestic, all of this departs from him and is replaced.
So in the sequence of the verses there will come to us His words: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said: This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. Subhan Allah! They see these great confederates, then they reassure themselves that this is what Allah and His Messenger promised, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth, because victory is with patience, and relief is with hardship. When they saw these great confederates and what follows from their presence of severity and distress, they knew that victory was near, for Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: When is the help of Allah? Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [al-Baqarah 214]. Look, the help of Allah is near in such a condition: ﴿they were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken﴾.
If you apply this to the condition of the believers at the time of the confederates, you will find that it applies. At the end of the verse: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾. Thus it was true of them that this is what Allah and His Messenger promised, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth regarding the nearness of victory.
In sum, such matters that come as passing states do not affect a person's rank or his condition, because they pass away.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that when a person is overcome by a condition such that these assumptions reach him, he does not lower his rank. But as I said a little while ago: when his condition settles and these assumptions calm down, he recognizes the truth.
* It is derived from this noble verse, from His words: ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab 11]: a depiction of the state the believers were in at that moment, which was a great trial. This was a trial with respect to the events that occurred, and with respect to their souls: were they settled?
The answer: No, ﴿they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾. So there combined upon them the outward trial that is seen with the eye, and the inward trial, which is the shaking of souls and their lack of settledness. For this reason He said: ﴿they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾.
* And in this noble verse also: a statement of the general rule, that Allah, the Most High, mentions blessings attributed to Himself, and mentions calamities mostly in the passive voice. Here He said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾, ﴿and were shaken﴾. By whom did this occur? By Allah, glorified and exalted. But in matters of good He attributes the thing to Himself, praising Himself, and in matters of the opposite the verbs come in the passive voice.
And consider the words of the jinn: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 10]. In the case of evil they said: ﴿is intended﴾, and for guidance they attributed it to Allah, mighty and majestic, because evil is not attributed to Allah. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And evil is not to You" [narrated by Muslim (771/201) from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him)]. So it is not permissible for a person to attribute evil to Allah at all. Evil exists in created things, not in the act itself, because the created things of Allah, mighty and majestic, have two aspects: an aspect considered as an act of Allah, and an aspect considered in their own essence. As for their essence, in them there is good and evil by themselves: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak (1) from the evil of what He created﴾ [al-Falaq 1-2]. As for them considered as an act of Allah, there is no evil in them. Is this clear, brothers?
Considered as an act of Allah, there is no evil in them, and considered in their essence there is good and evil. Considered as an act, there is no evil in them, because Allah only decreed it for a wisdom. Moreover, if you reflect on the things that are evil, you will find that they contain good even though they are evil. Corruption on land and sea, from drought, poverty and other things, is evil, but its outcome is good: ﴿so that they may return﴾.
Then He said: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said: Allah and His Messenger had promised us only delusion﴾ [al-Ahzab 12].
* From this noble verse is derived: a statement that the hypocrites seize opportunities.
Its aspect: in this opportunity, and in their narrow and dark condition, they began their activity, seized the opportunity, and said: "Where is the promise?" In this there is evidence that the hypocrite lives up to his name: if he finds no opportunity he keeps silent, flatters and yields, and if he finds an opportunity he speaks out. This is their habit: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they are alone with their devils, they say: Indeed, we are with you﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].
* It is derived from this noble verse: caution regarding the hypocrites, for they spare no effort to corrupt the believers. Whenever they find a point of criticism or a place to attack, they pounce. We ask Allah to protect us from them.
* It is also derived from this noble verse: that hearts are divided into sound and diseased, based on His words: ﴿and those in whose hearts is disease﴾. Likewise bodies are divided into sick and healthy. Look at the state of people today: are they more keen on treating hearts than treating bodies, or on treating bodies than treating hearts? The latter, except for whom Allah wills. Most people today are keen to treat bodies, whose end is to become carrion eaten by worms, rather than hearts, on which depends the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. You find a person whose heart is sick, perhaps to the point of burning, yet he does not care about it. But if he gets a thorn in his body, he rushes to the doctors, even if that involves hardship and fatigue.
But the wise believer is the one who is always attentive to his heart, its illness and its health, its soundness and its ruin. This is the true believer. There is no doubt that when the heart is sound, the body is sound. I am not saying that the believer's body never falls ill; but if the believer falls ill, he sees that in this illness there is benefit and advantage for him, is it not so? Thus his bodily illness becomes health for his heart, because of the patience and contentment with Allah, mighty and majestic, that arise in him, the waiting for relief, and doing the means that Allah has made means, relying upon Allah with what He has made a cause.
In sum, the illness of the heart is far more dangerous than the illness of the body, and the wise person takes greater care of this.
* It is derived from this noble verse: that Allah and His Messenger have promised the believers victory, based on His words: ﴿what Allah and His Messenger had promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab 12]. The promise is mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah for the believers. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51], and He said: ﴿And it was ever incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ [al-Rum 47]. Look at this great promise: ﴿incumbent upon Us﴾ is emphatic, ﴿help the believers﴾. And the one who guarantees this, my brothers, is the Lord, mighty and majestic, in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. But, regrettably, many believers do not take these things into account, although Allah has guaranteed it.
And in the Sunnah the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror across a distance of a month's journey" [agreed upon: al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both)]. His victory, peace and blessings be upon him, is not a victory for his person, but a victory for what he brought, so the victory belongs to him and to his community after him as well.
* It is derived from this noble verse: a clarification that the hypocrite's outlook is limited, and likewise whoever has disease in his heart has a limited outlook.
Its aspect: they looked only at the present moment, they did not consider the outcome. Such events that come upon them are passing circumstances, but the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. So no one builds upon passing circumstances except the weak of insight. Even in worldly matters, do not look at passing circumstances, for as it is said: "the permanence of a state is impossible." But as long as you are confident in Allah's promise, mighty and majestic, be certain that this promise will be fulfilled, though there may befall it passing circumstances, by a wisdom of Allah's wisdoms through which He tests, and then the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. I think the lessons are finished. (...).
Great, not one of them turned back from his religion, but there are words, for example, from one weak in faith, yet they do not settle.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, despite the intense propaganda of the hypocrites, for the hypocrites undoubtedly have great propaganda; they are not silent, they do not keep quiet. But, by the grace of Allah, Allah made them firm. (...)
﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 9–12 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿So We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see﴾ — the angels — ﴿and Allah is ever, of what you do, Seeing﴾ — with the ta' (you do), referring to those who dug the trench; and with the ya' (they do), referring to the confederation of the polytheists). That is, there are two readings: ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ and ﴿bima ta'malun basira﴾.

As for His saying ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾: what is this wind? I have told you that it is the east wind, and for this reason it came in the hadith: "I was given victory by theṣabā (the east wind), and 'Ād was destroyed by the dabūr (the west wind)"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1035) and Muslim (900/17), from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. The dabūr is the west wind.

He says: (﴿bima ta'malun﴾ with the ta', referring to those who dug the trench). But this restriction of the verse is not appropriate. Why is it not appropriate? Because if we restrict the generality of the verse, we limit the meaning of the wording, or we confine the wording to part of its meaning. The correct understanding is that ﴿bima ta'malun﴾ covers digging the trench and everything else you did in this battle.

(Basir) means: knowing. Or ﴿bima ya'malun﴾ means: the armies, ﴿when the armies came upon you﴾. So Allah the Exalted is Seeing of what they do, of the confederating against the Prophet ﷺ and of their coming to the city of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in order to eliminate him, as they supposed.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾ [al-Ahzab 10] — from the upper part of the valley and its lower part, from the east and the west). They came from the east and from the west: the Quraysh came from the north-eastern side, and the Ghaṭafān and the Jews of Banu Qurayẓa came from the south-western side, so they came from above the Muslims and from below them.

As I told you a little while ago: the trench extended from the eastern lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Sharqiyyah) to the western lava field (al-Ḥarrah al-Gharbiyyah), and the whole north is now protected by the trench. They came from above them and from below them, so that they would be like the two jaws of a lion, closing in upon the city. This was their plan, but Allah the Exalted is ever encompassing of what they do.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the eyes swerved﴾. "Zāgha" means: it inclined, and from it comes "zāghat al-shams" (the sun declined), when it inclines at midday. And from it His saying: ﴿The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ [al-Najm 17], that is, it did not incline.

﴿Al-Abṣār﴾ (the eyes): the definite article here is for a known reference. Which reference? A mental one. That is: the eyes of you swerved. The author says in explaining it: (they inclined away from everything toward their enemy from every direction). That is, the eyes had no gaze except toward this enemy; they were heedless of everything else, looking only at this enemy.

Some exegetes explained it: ﴿zāgha﴾ means: it moved from its place of rest, i.e., they became fixed in a stare from the intensity of terror. A person looks only at what is before him, watching it and fearing it. This is something observed in human nature: when a person fears something, where does his gaze turn? To that thing, toward its direction. And you find the eye, as the common people say, stays wide open, fearing a surprise attack. So the eyes swerved. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾: "the hearts" means: of you; your hearts reached (﴿the throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe).

His saying: (from the intensity of fear) explains His saying ﴿swerved﴾ and ﴿reached﴾. ﴿The throats﴾, plural of ḥanjara, which is the end of the windpipe, meaning from here. Is this literally ﴿the hearts reached the throats﴾? Some said: it is literal, and that when the fearful person's fear intensifies, his lungs swell; when they swell they press upon the heart so that it rises up. For this reason it is said of a coward or a frightened person: "his lungs have swollen" (inbaṭa saḥruh), meaning his lungs. The principle is to take a matter in its literal sense. It is also permissible that this is a depiction of the intensity of terror, meaning that from the intensity of terror the hearts left their places, so they neither breathe normally nor beat normally, because they had left their places.

Then He said: (﴿And you were thinking about Allah various thoughts﴾, diverse in regard to victory and despair). This is a difference between victory and despair. ﴿You were thinking﴾, that is, you, concerning Allah, ﴿the thoughts﴾, with the alif for the extension of the pronunciation. These "thoughts" are the plural of ẓann, and a verbal noun is not made plural except when it denotes kinds. If it is one single kind, it cannot be pluralized however many instances there are; but if it denotes kinds, its plural is valid. So here ẓann, which is a verbal noun, was made plural because of its variety. That is, the thoughts revolved in their minds or in their thinking, varying in length and breadth: Will these confederates be dispelled? Will they destroy us? Will we be victorious? You know what fear does to a person in terms of near and distant thoughts and imaginings. Among them were those who thought despair, or despaired, saying: there is nothing after this. Among them were those who thought victory, and how could that be, given the situation was extremely dark? Because he believes that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship is ease. They say: we are upon the truth, so if we are upon the truth and we are patient, then victory is, what? Guaranteed. Therefore they thought victory.

Among them were the people of material means and outward sensory appearances, who thought, what? Destruction, and despaired of victory, because they had no store of faith to rely upon. There is no doubt that among those who went out for this, there were hypocrites, as will become apparent in the story.

The point is that Allah said: ﴿You were thinking about Allah thoughts﴾ and left it unrestricted, and put it in the plural so that a person may take the imagining of this thought in every direction: many thoughts, diverse and conflicting.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed. How? For this reason the "thoughts" came in the plural.

He said: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾. Is ﴿there (hunalika)﴾ a demonstrative of place or of time? Of place, or of time, or of both together. ﴿Hunalika﴾ is suitable for time and for place, but the original usage is for place, and it also comes for time.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might; the custom of Allah that has passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost﴾ [Ghafir 85]: that is, at that time the disbelievers lost. So ﴿hunalika﴾ (there) is suitable for time and place; the lam indicates distance, and the kaf indicates address. ﴿There the believers were tested﴾: they were examined. And who tested them? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, examined them, through what befell them of this great constriction, which cannot be expressed in speech and cannot be felt except by one who experiences it. We here are unable to imagine that state and unable to depict it, but the one who was in it knows about it.

He says: (﴿There the believers were tested﴾, that is: they were examined, so that the sincere might be distinguished from others. ﴿And they were shaken﴾: they were stirred, ﴿with a severe shaking﴾ from the intensity of dread).

A great trial and a great shaking befell them. This shaking struck them, not an earthquake of the earth, but a shaking of souls. Souls were convulsed and something great happened to them, because in this battle there gathered the confederation of the Arab tribes, the treachery of Banu Qurayẓa, hunger, fatigue, exhaustion, and cold. How many? Five things, any one of which suffices to shake the soul. How much more so when they combine?

The affair was difficult. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was in that place, binding a stone to his stomach from hunger. How can you imagine the condition? A person cannot truly express it. For this reason He said: ﴿They were shaken with a severe shaking﴾, strong and great, shaking their souls because these trials gathered upon them, may Allah be pleased with them.

For this reason hypocrisy emerged and the hypocrites spoke, seeing in this an opportunity to talk, because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was promising them victory, even in that battle he was promising them victory. And the story of the rock that they could not get through, where the axes broke and they grew weary, until they came to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, you planned for us! Because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, had marked out the trench for them, drawing its line with his foot.

It was by the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the line fell upon this rock they could not get through. But out of their great obedience, may Allah be pleased with them, they did not say: let us bend it right or left; rather they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him. He descended from his shelter that had been built for him on a hill there to overlook the people, descended, took the pickaxe and struck it a blow. Ibn Ishaq says: when he struck it the blow, it gave off a great light, as if we were in daylight, and a part of it crumbled. Then he struck it again and said Allah is greatest, peace and blessings be upon him.

* Student: At night?

* The Shaykh: At night. He said Allah is greatest, then struck a second time, and it gave light, and he said the takbir of conquest, a great takbir. Then he struck a third time and said Allah is greatest. They said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this? He said: "In the first takbir I saw the palaces of Rome, and in the second the palaces of Kisra, and in the third the palaces of Ṣan'ā' in Yemen, and that they will be conquered"[[Narrated by Aḥmad (18694) from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to dig the trench. He said: a rock appeared to us in a place in the trench, which the pickaxes would not bite.
