He said: "Is my judgment binding upon them?" pointing to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and pointing to them as well. They said: "Yes," and all of them agreed. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was content, and so were these Jews. He said: "The time has come for Saʿd that the blame of no blamer should deter him in the cause of Allah." This was a momentous trial, and he judged among them, may Allah be pleased with him, with a great judgment, a correct judgment in accordance with the truth. He said: "I judge that their fighting men be killed, their dependents be taken captive, and their property be taken as spoils." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You have judged among them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens."[[Ibid.; and see Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/240).]]

Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded that their fighting men be killed, namely the adult men, while the dependents, the women and the boys who had not reached puberty, were taken captive, and the property was taken as spoils. They killed in Madina between seven hundred and eight hundred men, killed on a single day, in accordance with a judgment that they themselves had accepted. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿a party you kill, and you take captive a party﴾. Here He placed the object first in ﴿a party you kill﴾, and delayed the object in ﴿and you take captive a party﴾. Is the purpose of that only the preservation of the verse endings (fawasil), so that the benefit is verbal, or is there a meaningful benefit as well?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, both.
* The Student: The two groups differ; they are not equal.
* The Shaykh: How so?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 22–27 (part 3 of 5):

* Student: The two groups differ. The last group means the women, and the first means only the men.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because the first are the men, and the second are those who do not fight. (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, this is the apparent meaning, because the first ruling is more severe and more emphatic. For this reason its object was placed first, ﴿a group you kill﴾. The second is less than that, because a captive may be freed by grace, so He said: ﴿and a group you take captive﴾. This is with regard to the wording, which is the consideration of the endings (al-fawasil, the rhyming endings of the verses). In Surat al-Baqarah He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿a group He denied and a group they kill﴾ [al-Ma'idah 70], or ﴿some you denied and some you kill﴾ [al-Baqarah 87]. Since denying the messengers was severe, the object was placed first in it, just as the object was placed first in their killing. This is the story of the Confederates, and it ended with His saying: ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and land you had not trodden﴾ [al-Ahzab 27]. Afterwards, that was Khaybar, and it was taken after Qurayzah. ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 27].
﴿He caused you to inherit their land﴾: this verb takes two objects. The first object is the "kaf" (the pronoun "you"), and the second is "their land." ﴿And their homes﴾. How do "land" and "homes" differ? The "diyar" (homes) is the plural of "dar," which refers to dwellings and quarters. As for "ard" (land), it is more general than that. The "amwal" (wealth) are goods, silver coins, gold dinars, and other things.
﴿And land you had not trodden﴾ means you had not stepped on it until now, but you will inherit it. It is the land of Khaybar, for the Prophet ﷺ conquered it afterwards in the sixth year. ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾, so nothing can overpower Him.
As for His saying ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾, He placed the object first to affirm that the action would certainly fall upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾. Do not say, as some people say, "He is competent over whatever He wills," because if you say "competent over whatever He wills," you restrict His power to what He wills, whereas power relates both to what He has willed and to what He has not willed. Even what He has not willed, He is able to do. And Allah knows best.
The Messenger ﷺ said: «Stand up for your chief» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6262) and Muslim (1768/64), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him], so they stood up for their chief Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and brought him down from his donkey. He sat in front of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «These people agreed to come down under your judgment». [Al-Bukhari (6262) and Muslim (1768/64) narrated with their chains from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the people of Qurayzah came down under the judgment of Sa'd. The Prophet ﷺ sent for him, and he came. He said: «Stand up for your chief», or he said: «the best of you». Then he sat beside the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: «These people came down under your judgment». He said: "I judge that their fighting men be killed and their children taken captive." He said: «You have judged by the judgment of the King».] So he said to them, then turned to them and said: "Are you content with this, and is my judgment binding?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to the other side, where the Muslims were, and said: "Are you content with this?" They said: "Yes." However, when he turned toward the Messenger ﷺ, he lowered his head out of reverence for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he issued this ruling, which the Prophet ﷺ affirmed, and said: «It is the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens». [Ibid.; see Sirah Ibn Hisham (2/240).] How many were these people?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: They said: when they saw the Confederates, they said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. The situation required that fear and terror overtake them, as it did the hypocrites.
* Among its benefits: the complete truthfulness of their belief in Allah and His Messenger, in their saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. They witnessed what Allah had promised, then they expressed certainty about it with their tongues, by their saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾.
Some ignorant people have used this verse to argue for the legitimacy of concluding the recitation of the Qur'an with the words "Allah has spoken the truth." They said: "How do you object to us when we finish the reading and say: 'Allah the Mighty has spoken the truth,' when Allah says: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾, and says: ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth﴾ [Al 'Imran 95]?" So what is the answer to this doubt?
* Student: The answer is that He did not say ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth﴾ at the end of the recitation (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. We say: We do not deny that someone may say "Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth." Rather, we consider it part of faith that a person says "Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth," and whoever does not hold this belief is a disbeliever. But we deny that this praise of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, be made at the end of the recitation, since it was not reported. Do we know the law of Allah better than the Messenger of Allah? Are we more eager than he to apply the law of Allah? Certainly not. If this is so, then it is obligatory for us to follow his example. If he used to say "Allah has spoken the truth" at the end of his recitation, we say it with honor and respect. If he did not say it, we do not say it.
We say to them: If you believe that this is legislated, then say it also in the prayer. When you finish the recitation in the prayer, before you say the takbir, say: "Allah has spoken the truth," because recitation in the prayer is more virtuous than outside the prayer. The point is that there is no evidence for these people in a verse like this.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the believer's faith increases upon seeing the signs, whether cosmic or legislative, because of His saying: ﴿And it only increased them in faith and submission﴾ [al-Ahzab 22].
* Among its benefits: the confirmation, or soundness, of the position of the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), who say that faith increases and decreases, is it not so?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: We have mentioned that the increase in faith is through several considerations: through the strength of certainty, through the soundness of the action, through sincerity in it, through following the Messenger ﷺ, and through the state of the doer himself. All these considerations increase faith. What was the first?
The first is the strength of certainty. Abraham, peace be upon him, said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: Have you not believed? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest﴾ [al-Baqarah 260]. Is not the report like seeing with one's own eyes? If someone you fully trust informs you of the existence of something, you believe it. But if you see it with your own eyes, that becomes a stronger faith (...). The second is the variation in the action (...). The third: the sincerity in worship. The more a person is sincere to Allah in worship, the more complete and stronger the increase of faith through it becomes. For this reason you find a great difference when you worship Allah, the Mighty, with sincerity, and when you worship Him with heedlessness: you find a great difference in how your heart is affected, even though the act of worship is the same. So how much more so when you worship Allah, the Exalted, with showing off and seeking reputation (we ask Allah to protect us and you from that), the heart will be even less affected by that worship. Also, through following: the more a person follows the Messenger ﷺ in his worship, the more his faith increases, because when he follows the Messenger ﷺ more closely, he feels as if the Messenger ﷺ is before him, following his footsteps. Without doubt, this increases faith. The fifth: through the state of the doer. The Prophet ﷺ said: «If one of you spent gold equal to Uhud, it would not reach the mudd of one of them nor half of it» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3673) and Muslim (2541/222), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him]. He means the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because their faith was stronger than those after them, and their steadfastness was greater.
In sum, the increase of faith has several considerations. Among them also, the sixth: abandoning sins out of fear of Allah, for faith increases through it. This will come to us, Allah willing, in the Book of Monotheism, where its explanation will be more complete.
The point is that the people of the Sunnah and the Community say faith increases and decreases. The Murji'ah said: faith neither increases nor decreases. Why? They said: because faith is in the heart, and righteous deeds have no bearing on faith, and what is in the heart does not vary. Now we all believe in the sun, and our belief in the sun is equal; it does not vary. So people, as Ibn al-Qayyim said of them:

People are one thing in faith,
like the comb when its teeth are equal.

This view is undoubtedly wrong, refuted by both reality and the law. The Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah said: faith neither increases nor decreases. It either exists completely or is entirely absent, because they say that the perpetrator of a major sin has left faith. He is either a disbeliever, or he is in an intermediate position between two positions. The Khawarij say the perpetrator of a major sin is a disbeliever, he has no faith at all. The Mu'tazilah say he has no faith, but we do not call him a disbeliever; rather he is in an intermediate position between two positions. As for those who do not commit major sins, people are equal in faith, all alike. Those who do not see faith as increasing or decreasing are two groups: either the Murji'ah, or the Wa'idiyyah, who are the Khawarij, and who? The Mu'tazilah.
Some people of the Sunnah, such as Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: faith increases, and we do not say it decreases, because the increase of faith is mentioned many times in the Qur'an and the Sunnah, but the decrease is not mentioned. But his view, may Allah have mercy on him, is weak, because in the Sunnah there is: «I have not seen anyone more deficient in reason and religion» [Al-Bukhari (304) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, and Muslim (79/132) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. Faith is without doubt part of religion, so it falls within this hadith.
Also, increase and decrease are opposites: when one exists, the other is absent, and one cannot conceive of one existing without the other. For example, increase cannot be conceived without decrease. So we say to him: you say that so-and-so has more faith than so-and-so. That means the one who is exceeded is deficient, and no other understanding is conceivable.
The correct view is that faith increases and decreases, and the causes of its increase and decrease are as we explained earlier.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: people differ in submission and surrender just as they differ in faith, in increase and decrease, because of His saying: ﴿except in faith and submission﴾. This is because most believers are all submissive to the law, but some of them submit with tranquility, openness, acceptance, and love, while others submit in a limited way. Among them is someone who comes to prayer, for example, seeing it as a blessing from Allah, the Mighty, and comes to it eagerly, not turning away, active, with an open heart, loving it, waiting for the next prayer with great impatience. Among them are people in the opposite condition, who come to prayer and never miss it, but slowly and reluctantly, without full submission. Is that not so? So people differ in submission, and for this reason He said: ﴿except in faith and submission﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: reflecting on the verses, and the clarity of the verses to the servant, increases his faith and submission, because of His saying: ﴿And it only increased them﴾, that is, what they saw of the Confederates, ﴿in faith﴾ in Allah, ﴿and submission﴾ to His law.
Who wants to ask?
* Student: (...) or that a person's faith is deficient?
* Shaykh: Yes, there is clear evidence that faith decreases.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but it is deficient in comparison with men.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, it increases and decreases. The Messenger affirmed its deficiency.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, not at all. It is not by degrees. This deficiency varies even for women, who are deficient. There is affirmation of the basic deficiency with respect to men, because they do not pray and do not fast. Then for them personally, since abandoning prayer is a deficiency, the more completely they perform the prayer, the more complete their faith is.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By evidence. That is, if a woman prays only four prayers, she would be more deficient than one who prays five, because once you know that the Prophet ﷺ made abandoning prayer a deficiency in itself, then abandoning part of the prayer is also a deficiency.
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they covenanted with Allah. Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits, and they did not change in the least﴾ [al-Ahzab 23].
From this noble verse is derived: praise of those believers who made a covenant with Allah and were true to Him. The reason for this is the context: ﴿men﴾, for ﴿men﴾ is indefinite for the sake of magnification: great men who were true to what they covenanted with Allah.
* Among its benefits: those who were true to what they covenanted with Allah include some who died and were martyred, and some who remained alive. We have mentioned an example of those who were martyred: who? Anas ibn al-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him. He was martyred at Uhud, and about eighty wounds were found on him.
* Among its benefits also: Allah praised those who fulfilled what they had covenanted with Allah in complete form, without deficiency or alteration, because of His saying: ﴿and they did not change in the least﴾.
* Among its benefits: whether someone died earlier or later, if both were equal in what they did of what was obligatory, there is no difference between the earlier and the later, as He said: ﴿Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits﴾. He made the praise for them one, but in other deeds, whoever dies later and increases in righteous deeds is more complete than the first. However, with regard to the righteous deed in which they were equal, there is no difference between the first and the last.
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab 24].
* From this noble verse is derived: the explanation of Allah's wisdom, may He be exalted, in recompensing deeds, because of His saying: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful﴾.
* Among its benefits: that the reward is of the same kind as the deed, because of His saying: ﴿for their truthfulness﴾. The "ba'" here indicates causation, and the caused thing is tied to its cause: it grows strong with its strength, weakens with its weakness, increases with its increase, and decreases with its decrease.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of the truthful, and that they deserve a good reward, because of His saying: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾: the truthful in belief, in speech, and what else? And in action. Allah has commanded truthfulness. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawbah 119]. The Prophet ﷺ, urging truthfulness, said: «Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and seek the truth until he is recorded with Allah as a truthful one. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and seek lies until he is recorded with Allah as a great liar» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6094) and Muslim (2607/103), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him].

Truthfulness, just as it earns praise from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and a generous reward, also earns praise from people. That is why you find that the traces of truthful people are spread, their sayings are transmitted, and they are praised in gatherings even after their death. The opposite is true of liars, may Allah protect us, and hypocrites. So hold to truthfulness, and do not think that the truthful person will ever be ruined. Sometimes Satan makes a person imagine that if he speaks the truth, it will harm him, so he should lie or be a liar. This is one of Satan's whisperings. Truthfulness is a means of deliverance. That is why one of them said: "I found deliverance in lying." The second said to him: "Truthfulness is more deliverant," and he spoke the truth.

Know that although the matter may be bitter for the truthful person at the beginning, the outcome is in his favor in the end. If you want an example of this, look at the state of the three who were left behind in the Battle of Tabuk. How was their beginning? They were in that great bitterness, until the earth, vast as it was, became constricted for them, their own souls became constricted for them, and the earth turned strange to them.

Ka'b ibn Malik said: "Until it was as though the people on the earth were not the people I knew."[[Ahmad (27175) narrated with his chain from Ka'b ibn Malik, who said: "... I went out to the market and no one spoke to me. The people turned strange to us, until they were no longer the people we knew, and the walls turned strange to us, until they were no longer the walls we knew." The hadith continues.]] The earth became constricted for him. The outcome was that verses were revealed about them that are recited until the Day of Resurrection. Had it not been for this truthfulness, these verses would not have remained. Then the people were told, when their story was mentioned: "O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful." This is a very great outcome for the truthful. So be truthful, even if harm befalls you at the beginning of your affair, for the outcome will be yours. Do not accustom yourself to lying. "That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness."

* From this noble verse is derived: the blameworthiness of hypocrisy, and that it is a cause of punishment, from His saying: "and that He may punish the hypocrites."

* It is also derived from it: that the hypocrite has a path to repentance, from His saying: "if He wills," for He wills to punish them if they die in hypocrisy. But if they repent, He has willed not to punish them. However, as you have heard in the explanation of this verse, the repentance of the hypocrite has conditions that must be observed: "except those who repent, amend, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah" (An-Nisa 146). These matters must become apparent in the hypocrite; otherwise his repentance is not accepted in this world. As for the Hereafter, his affair is with Allah. But in this world we do not accept it unless these qualities, which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has stipulated, appear in him.

* It is also derived from this: the encouragement of the hypocrite to repent, from His saying: "or He turns to them in forgiveness." He is a deceitful, betraying, scheming hypocrite, yet it is said to him: "or He turns to them in forgiveness." This is evidence that Allah's mercy precedes His wrath. That is why, concerning those who torment His allies and burn them in fire, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning" (Al-Buruj 10). Likewise, those who said: "Indeed, Allah is the third of three" were offered repentance by Allah. All of this is evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, loves pardon more than retribution.

* It is also derived from this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely Al-Ghafur (the All-Forgiving) and Ar-Rahim (the Most Merciful), and the two attributes they include, namely forgiveness and mercy, along with what relates to them of judgments and effects, which is that He forgives and shows mercy. These two noble names, Al-Ghafur and Ar-Rahim, are among the transitive names (muta'addi, names whose meaning extends to an object), and faith in them is not complete except with three things. What are they?

* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: No.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct. The names of Allah are of two kinds: transitive (muta'addi) and intransitive (lazim, names that do not extend to an object). For the transitive kind, your faith is not complete except with three things: that you believe in it as a name of Allah; that you believe in the attribute it includes; and the third: that you believe in the judgment and effect it includes. For Al-Ghafur, you believe that Al-Ghafur is one of Allah's names, that He, exalted is He, possesses forgiveness, and the third: that He forgives. The same applies to Ar-Rahim.

The second kind: if the name is intransitive, faith in it is not complete except with two things: believing in it as one of Allah's names, and believing in the attribute it includes. Examples are Al-Ali (the Most High), Al-Azim (the Great), Al-Karim (the Generous), and similar names. Perhaps we would say that Al-Karim belongs to the first kind.

There is a difficulty in the verse, and I do not know whether I have raised it and answered it before. It is His saying: "And ever has Allah been Forgiving and Merciful." In "ever has Allah been" (kana Allahu), what is meant by "kana"? Is it past tense, "and now"?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, but how do we answer regarding His saying: "kana Allahu"?
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, "kana" is not for continuity. Kana in itself does not indicate continuity.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. I said that it is established that Allah was Forgiving and Merciful, but kana... is clear.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. We say that kana is sometimes intended to indicate the attribution of its predicate to its subject, regardless of time. This is what is known as the kana of "time-negated" type (salbiyyat al-zaman), meaning that time is not intended by it at all; rather, what is intended is the realization of this attribute. Kana means "it is established." Do you understand? So "kana Allahu Ghafuran Rahiman" means that He, Mighty and Majestic, has not ceased and does not cease to be Forgiving and Merciful. I think we cannot complete (...).

* Student: Allah, glorified and exalted, says: "Among the believers are men..." Is this praise from Allah, glorified and exalted, upon the believers, that they are men (...)?
* The Shaykh: We might say, for example, that praise is achieved through the indefinite form (tankir), which indicates glorification. As for the mere word "rijal" (men), it is applied to both believers and non-believers.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but I do not recall it now. The number is four or five.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. They were hypocrites, then Allah bestowed His favor upon them and they repented of hypocrisy. If you return to the tafsir of "If We pardon a group of you, We will punish another group" (At-Tawbah 66), you will find this there.

* From this noble verse is derived: the demonstration of Allah's power, glorified and exalted, in that He repelled these great, numerous confederates along with their intense rage and fury against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. Allah repelled them in their rage. They did not gain satisfaction, nor did they attain their aim. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage" (Al-Ahzab 25). That is why the Prophet (ﷺ) praised his Lord for the defeat of the confederates. He said: "There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone."[[Al-Bukhari (3084) and Muslim (1218/147), the wording is Muslim's, from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these confederates had their hearts filled with rage against the Messenger (ﷺ), from His saying: "with their rage," for the letter ba' here indicates accompaniment and association (musahabah wa mulabasah).

* Among its benefits: that they, that is, the confederates, did not attain any good despite this great exhaustion, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. They did not attain any good in this world, such as spoils and other things, nor did they attain any good in the Hereafter, such as rewards and recompense.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, spared the believers from fighting after this battle. For this reason, none of the polytheists fought the Prophet (ﷺ) after that battle, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Now we will attack them, and they will not attack us."[[Al-Bukhari (4110), from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Surad, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is because Allah said: "And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting," in this battle and what followed it. The Arabs did not launch an attack against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after this.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, defends the believers, from His saying: "And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting."

What is the reason for restricting this to the believers? From where is it taken from the verse that it is specific to the believers?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, He specified it for the believers, and this indicates that He sufficed them in fighting because of their faith. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, suffices the believers for whatever concerns them and defends them because of their faith, as He, exalted is He, said: "And Allah will save those who feared Him by their attainment; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve" (Az-Zumar 61).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of strength and might for Allah, from His saying: "And ever is Allah Powerful and Mighty." In it is the affirmation of these two names among His names: Al-Qawi (the Strong) and Al-Aziz (the Mighty).

Then He, exalted is He, said: "And He brought down those among the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts."

* From this noble verse is derived another favor upon the believers, namely the bringing down of those Jews who betrayed, from the Banu Qurayzah, from their fortresses in which they had fortified themselves, from His saying?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, let him finish, because it seems he is about to become preoccupied in the house.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "And He brought down those among the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Jews and Christians are enemies of the Muslims and allies of the polytheists, because the Banu Qurayzah allied with the confederates and supported them against the Messenger (ﷺ), despite the covenant and pact between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that casting terror into hearts is among the greatest forms of defeat, from His saying: "and cast terror into their hearts."

* Among its benefits: an indication of the degradation and humiliation of these Jews, and their descent from high to low: "And He brought down those among the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses." Indeed, what befell them upon leaving their fortresses of humiliation, shame, and disgrace remains until the Day of Resurrection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, permitted the believers to kill and take captive these Jews, from His saying: "A group you kill and a group you take captive."

* Among its benefits, regarding His saying: "And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes" and so on: that when the believers conquer a town, they come to own the land, from His saying: "He caused you to inherit their land." When they own the land, is it to be divided among those who took spoils, or held for the public treasury (bayt al-mal), or distributed among the believers in exchange for a land tax (kharaj)?

There is a difference of opinion among the scholars on this. The correct view is that it is obligatory for the ruler to consider what is most beneficial. If he sees fit to distribute it among those who took spoils, he does so, as the Prophet (ﷺ) did at Khaybar. If he sees fit to keep it for the interests of the Muslims, he keeps it. If he sees fit to distribute it among the Muslims in exchange for a kharaj imposed upon it, he does so, as 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did. For example, he says: "We will divide it among you on the basis that for every hundred meters there is such and such a number of dirhams," like a heap (sabrah), and these dirhams will be for the Muslims to benefit from. The important point is that when the land of the disbelievers is conquered by force ('anwatan), to whom does it belong? It belongs to the Muslims, from His saying: "And He caused you to inherit their land."

* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, it became their possession without any compensation.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, no. The Muslims who came to own it did not impose anything on them. But the Jews of Khaybar were left in it as falahih (cultivators who work the land for a share), because they knew how to manage these farms. So a share of what it produced, of fruit or crops, was assigned to them. Or is the land not the Muslims' own?

* Also among them: the permissibility for Muslims of the wealth of the disbelievers, from His saying: "and their wealth," for spoils are lawful to the Muslims, and this is one of the distinguishing features of this Ummah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that none before me was given: I was supported with terror for a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification; spoils were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his own people, but I was sent to all of humanity."[[Agreed upon; Al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the glad tidings that the Muslims will take control of other lands of the disbelievers. From where is this glad tiding taken?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The student of knowledge must understand. The student of knowledge must have a book with him, whether it is the prescribed text in Qur'an, hadith, jurisprudence, or principles. The student of knowledge must not come as a mere listener, coming as a listener like the common people in the market. The student of knowledge must be a student in the true sense of the word, otherwise there is no benefit in being a student of knowledge. The student walks like a camel carrying a sieve that is split and full of holes, which carries no water. So my advice to you is to take books like the other students, to follow the teacher, and to attend the lessons.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying: "and a land you had not trodden." "And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden." This refers to Khaybar and other lands of the disbelievers. It contains only the glad tiding that Allah, glorified and exalted, will cause the Muslims to inherit the lands of the disbelievers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's power over everything, from His saying: "And ever is Allah, over all things, competent." Everything is something Allah is capable of, and nothing overpowers Him. "His command is only when He wills a thing that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is" (Ya-Sin 82). Whatever you imagine as remote concerning the occurrence of something, do not deem it beyond Allah's power, for the matter is easy for Him, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him" (Ar-Rum 27). Everything is easy for Him, but this is easier.

In sum, Allah, glorified and exalted, is competent over all things. The author of the tafsir Al-Jalalayn, in Surat al-Ma'idah, when he reached "And Allah is over all things competent" (Al-Ma'idah 17), said: "The intellect has specified His essence, so He is not capable of it." That is, Allah is not capable over His own essence. He claims that the intellect is what specifies this generality. It is said to him: What is this intellect that specifies this generality? How could Allah not be capable over His own essence? Rather, He, glorified and exalted, is capable over all things, even over His essence. He, glorified and exalted, is established above the Throne, descends to the lowest heaven, comes to judge between His servants, and does what He wills, and this is power over His essence. As for saying that He is not capable over His essence, so that He does not annihilate it, for example, it is said: this is an impossibility, and an impossibility is not something to which power applies at all. It is not an accepted possibility and is not included in the verse from the outset. To say that it is included in what the intellect specifies is to specify what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has generalized.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Which verse?
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent" (Al-Ma'idah 120), at the end of the surah.
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. For example, if someone asked: Is Allah able to make a thing both moving and still at the same moment? We say: This is impossible, because if it is moving it is not still, and if it is still it is not moving. So if Allah made it moving, it would not be still, and if He made it still, it would not have been moving at all.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.

Benefits derived: affirmation that the Jews are treacherous, and that they are a people of betrayal and deceit. This is something known about the Jews from their condition since the time their prophet, Musa (peace be upon him), was among them until today; they are the most cunning, treacherous and deceitful of people. This is from His saying: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who backed them from their fortresses﴾.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, this is something clear by reason; for when you describe a thing as moving, stillness is negated from it, and if you describe it as still, movement is definitively negated from it.

The Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, this is something well known; it does not need faith, just as if you said: every originated thing必 must have an originator. It is a rational matter, and rationally known matters that are known necessarily do not need reflection or contemplation.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Contradictories: movement and stillness are contradictories, while blackness and whiteness are contraries.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 22–27 (part 1 of 5):

Allah the Exalted said, at the start of today's lesson: (﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us"﴾, of trial and victory, ﴿and Allah and His Messenger had spoken truly﴾ in the promise, ﴿and it increased them not except in faith﴾, meaning affirmation of Allah's promise, ﴿and submission﴾ [Al-Ahzab 22] to His command.)

﴿لَمَّا رَأَى الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْأَحْزَابَ﴾ Here ﴿لَمَّا﴾ is conditional (shartiyyah) but does not apply jazm (jussive). The conditional verb in the verse is ﴿رَأَى﴾, and its response is ﴿قَالُوا هَذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ﴾. It has already passed us that (lamma) in the Arabic language has several uses: among them the conditional, as in this verse; among them the jussive (jazimah), as in His saying: ﴿Nay, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ [Sad 8], this is jussive; and among them that it means (illa, "except"), as in His saying: ﴿There is no soul but that over it is a guardian﴾ [At-Tariq 4], meaning: except that over it is a guardian.

﴿وَلَمَّا رَأَى الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْأَحْزَابَ﴾. The word "al-ahzab" here refers to the confederates who banded together against the Prophet ﷺ: from Quraysh, Ghatafan, Banu Asad and others. When they saw them, was it a visual seeing or a seeing of the heart? A visual seeing. When they saw them, ﴿they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us."﴾ How? Where did Allah and His Messenger promise that these confederates would come? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise without the example of those who passed on before you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [Al-Baqarah 214]. Allah the Exalted has made clear in this verse that they cannot enter Paradise except after these matters, so the promise of Allah the Exalted to them includes that they would see such things that shake them.

He says: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us﴾, and this is evidence of their steadfastness, their faith and the sincerity of their intentions. But the hypocrites, as has already been mentioned, used to mock the Messenger ﷺ when he struck the rock that obstructed them while digging the trench, and said that he had seen the cities of Kisra, the palaces of Caesar and Yemen. What did they say? ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾ [Al-Ahzab 12]. How can this one possess Yemen, Sham and Iraq when he is now confined? This is a lie and is not true. But the believers said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly﴾, the opposite of those hypocrites who said: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion﴾.

﴿وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾. Truthfulness (al-sidq) is the reporting of a matter in accordance with how it actually is. If you wish, say: it is a report that corresponds to reality. This is truthfulness, and its opposite is falsehood. It is said: ṣadaqanī al-ḥadītha and ṣaddaqanī al-ḥadīth, and there is a difference between them. ṣadaqanī al-ḥadītha means: he told me the truth. ṣaddaqanī al-ḥadīth means: he said that what I related to him is true. Do you understand?

﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]. What is the meaning of ﴿صَدَقَكُمُ﴾? It means: He informed you of the truth and made clear to you that what He promised you was true, when you were killing them by His permission.

He says: ﴿وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾. In this sentence, ﴿مَا وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾, was this speech stated as a dispraise or as a praise? As a praise. But it may be puzzling to you how the promise of the Messenger of Allah was joined with the promise of Allah by the conjunction "and" (wa), and how the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah was also joined with the truthfulness of Allah by "and". The Prophet ﷺ said to a man who said to him: "What Allah wills and you will," the Prophet ﷺ said to him: «Have you made me a rival (nid) to Allah?». So how do we reconcile this with what is in this verse?

The answer is that what belongs to the matters of the Sharia (law) may be attributed to Allah and His Messenger with "and", because what the Prophet ﷺ legislated is part of the legislation of Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa 80]. As for what belongs to the matters of qadar (divine decree), it is not permissible to attribute it to Allah and His Messenger with "and"; rather, it must be with (thumma, "then"), because the capability and will of a human being follow the will and power of Allah.

For example, if a man asks you: "What is the ruling on such and such?", meaning the ruling on congregational prayer, and you do not know its ruling, you say: "Allah and His Messenger know best", because this is a legislated ruling. But if the matter belongs to the matters of qadar, it is not possible to associate anyone other than Allah with Allah using "and", because the will and power of other than Allah follow the will of Allah, and it is not possible for them to be equal to it.

He says: ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلَّا إِيمَانًا وَتَسْلِيمًا﴾. The doer of ﴿زَادَهُمْ﴾ refers to what? That is, the sight of the confederates. That is, the sight of the confederates and their gathering against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not increase them except in ﴿إِيمَانًا﴾. The author says: (affirmation of Allah's promise ﴿وَتَسْلِيمًا﴾ to His command). Faith (iman) is in the heart and submission (taslim) and compliance (inqiyad) are in the limbs, because faith has its locus in the heart, and submission and compliance have their locus in the limbs. A person does not complete his religion except by these two matters: faith and submission. Whoever submits without believing is a hypocrite, and whoever believes without submitting is arrogant. When faith and submission are combined in a person, he becomes a true believer and a true worshipper.

So a believer who does not submit, we say: this is arrogant. And a submitter who is not a believer, we say: this is a hypocrite, because the hypocrites submit outwardly. Faith is not complete except by these two matters, faith and submission. The Sharia is not complete except by these two matters, faith and submission.

He says: ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلَّا إِيمَانًا وَتَسْلِيمًا﴾. ﴿إِيمَانًا﴾ here is a maf'ul li-ajlihi (object of purpose)? What is its i'rab (grammatical analysis)?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: An object of what?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The first object or the second?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The second object. And the first object?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The pronoun (ha'), yes. So ﴿زاد﴾ takes two objects: the first is the pronoun (ha'), and the second in this verse is ﴿إِيمَانًا وَتَسْلِيمًا﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah﴾, in steadfastness with the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ﴾. This sentence consists of a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar). The predicate is placed first and the subject is placed last. The subject is His saying ﴿رِجَالٌ﴾, and the predicate is ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.

.. Beginning with an indefinite noun (nakirah) is not permissible, and the answer is that Ibn Malik the grammarian, may Allah have mercy on him, said:
"And it is not permissible to begin with an indefinite noun, unless it conveys meaning, like (ʿinda Zaydin namirah)."
Does the verse we have resemble this example, or not? (ʿinda Zayd namirah). What justifies beginning with the indefinite noun here is the postponement of the subject. In ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا﴾ [Al-Ahzab 23], what justifies it is the postponement of the subject. Also, in the verse there is another justification: the description of this indefinite noun, because the description of an indefinite noun specifies it.

﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. The ﴿مِنَ﴾ in His saying ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is partitive (lil-tab'id), because it can be estimated as (some of). The grammarians differed concerning partitive (min). Some of them said it is a noun, and that it follows its governing factors, but the effect of the governing factor does not appear on it because it is a particle, so the effect transfers to what follows it. Others said it is a preposition (harf jarr) whose meaning is partition, and this is the view of most grammarians.

﴿صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿صَدَقُوا﴾? That is, they fulfilled it, as you say: "The promise was true to me," meaning: the promise was fulfilled for me. They fulfilled what they pledged to Allah, namely steadfastness with the Prophet ﷺ. Who are such people? Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr and others, Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, and many more of this kind.

The Mighty and Majestic Allah says: (﴿﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾﴾: died or was killed in the way of Allah, ﴿﴿and among them is he who awaits﴾﴾ that, ﴿﴿and they have not altered [their pledge] in the least﴾﴾ in the covenant, and they are unlike the hypocrites).

Allah divided these men who were true to what they pledged to Allah into two categories: one category has fulfilled its vow, meaning it has completed its life and was killed in the way of Allah, like Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, who was killed as a martyr in the way of Allah, and likewise the rest of the martyrs of Uhud. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ﴾ And what does he await? He awaits fighting in the way of Allah, because he has been true to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and they have been true to what they pledged to Allah, so they are waiting to be martyred.

But does this happen for them or not? It may happen, and it may not. For this reason it is said that Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, grieved during his illness that he had not been killed as a martyr in the way of Allah, and he said, meaning he regretted that he had not left a battle without fighting in it: «And here I am dying on my bed, as a donkey dies». [[Al-Dinawari recorded in "al-Mujalasah" (836), with his chain, that when the death of Khalid ibn al-Walid approached, he wept and said: "I have faced such and such assaults, and there is not a hand's breadth of my body without a sword strike, an arrow shot, or a spear thrust. And here I am dying on my bed, a natural death, as the donkey ('ayr) dies. May the eyes of cowards never sleep." The 'ayr, with the 'ayn vowelled, is the donkey, whether domestic or wild.]] Because they want to be martyred in the way of Allah.

He says: ﴿وَمَا بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا﴾. This is coordinated with ﴿صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, meaning: among them are men who did not alter in the least. Alter what? The author says: (in the covenant). Alteration in the covenant includes breaking it entirely, and includes violating some of its conditions. That is, it includes breaking it entirely and disregarding it, or violating some of its conditions.

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. The Mighty and Majestic Allah said: ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah﴾ [Al-Ahzab 23]. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is the predicate placed first, ﴿رِجَالٌ﴾ is the postponed subject, and ﴿صَدَقُوا﴾ with its clause is a description of ﴿رِجَالٌ﴾. ﴿صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ means that they made their words true by their deeds, so the covenant they made with Allah, they carried out and fulfilled.

Know that the meaning of His saying ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا﴾ is: among the believers are men who made a covenant with Allah and were true to what they covenanted with Allah. The meaning is not that among the believers there are men who were true and others among them who were not true, so that someone who reviles the Companions may cling to it, or says that they were not all truthful. Rather the meaning is: among the believers are men who made a covenant with Allah and were true to it. Furthermore, among the believers are those who did not make any covenant with Allah the Exalted, but who persist in obeying their Lord wherever they are commanded.

Among those who made a covenant with Allah was Anas ibn al-Nadr, may Allah be pleased with him. Anas ibn al-Nadr did not attend Badr. When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Badr, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the first battle in which you fought the polytheists, and by Allah, if Allah keeps me alive, Allah will see what I do." When the battle of Uhud came, he fought, may Allah be pleased with him, until he was killed, and he had some eighty wounds, between spear thrusts and sword strikes. [[Al-Bukhari (2805) recorded with his chain from Anas, who said: My uncle Anas ibn al-Nadr was absent from the battle of Badr, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was absent from the first battle you fought against the polytheists. If Allah lets me witness fighting the polytheists, Allah will see what I do." When the day of Uhud came and the Muslims gave way, he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these have done", meaning his companions, "and I disown before You what these have done", meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh met him and he said: "O Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, by the Lord of al-Nadr, Paradise! I smell its fragrance from beyond Uhud." Sa'd said: "I could not do what he did, O Messenger of Allah." Anas said: "We found on him some eighty wounds from sword strikes, spear thrusts or arrow shots. We found him killed, and the polytheists had mutilated him, and no one could recognize him except his sister by his fingertips." Anas said: "We used to think, or we believed, that this verse was revealed about him and those like him: ﴿Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah﴾" to the end of the verse.]], and so he was true to what he pledged to Allah. This is the meaning of the verse.

His saying "by Allah, Allah will see what I do" is a covenant, because it is an obligation he undertook upon himself.

He says: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضَى نَحْبَهُ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 23], meaning: among those who made a covenant with the Mighty and Majestic Allah is he who ﴿fulfilled his vow﴾, that is, his pledge and obligation. It has also been said that ﴿قَضَى نَحْبَهُ﴾ means his term, that is, he died and was killed. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 23], meaning: he awaits death and being killed as a martyr in the way of the Mighty and Majestic Allah.

He says: ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, in steadfastness with the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضَى نَحْبَهُ﴾ died or was killed in the way of Allah. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ﴾ that, ﴿وَمَا بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا﴾. That is, no alteration occurred from them, neither by complete abandonment nor by change. For this reason He said: ﴿وَمَا بَدَّلُوا﴾, and alteration may occur by complete abandonment, and it may occur by change, by decrease or by increase. For this reason He said: ﴿وَمَا بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا﴾. The author said: (and they are unlike the hypocrites), because the state of the hypocrites is the opposite: they make a covenant with Allah and do not fulfil it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and will surely be among the righteous." But when He gave them from His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while they were refusing. So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾ [At-Tawbah 75–77]. As for the believer, he fulfills what he pledged to Allah.

The Mighty and Majestic Allah said: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾ [Al-Ahzab 24]. ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ The lam here indicates purpose (ta'lil), meaning that the matter occurs in this way, with fulfillment and with breaking the covenant: fulfillment from whom? From the believers, and breaking it from the hypocrites. This has occurred: ﴿that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites﴾ [Al-Ahzab 24]. Had people not differed in their deeds, they would not have differed in the reward, and had they not differed in the reward, there would be no purpose in creating Paradise and Hell. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together"﴾ [Hud 118–119]. So Allah the Mighty and Wise «created Paradise and created for it its inhabitants, and created the Fire and created for it its inhabitants». [[Muslim (2662) recorded with his chain from 'Aishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said: A child died, and I said: "Blessed is he, a little bird of the birds of Paradise." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Do you not know that Allah created Paradise and created the Fire, and created for this one its people and for that one its people?»]], and the inhabitants of this and that must have deeds by which they perform, so that they deserve to be among its people.

As for His saying ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, the "bi" (with) here indicates causation and is not an exchange (iwad), because reward for deeds is not a matter of exchange, but it is a matter of linking the effect to its cause, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «No one will enter Paradise by his deeds». [[Muslim (2816/71) and Ahmad (7478), whose wording it is, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Therefore good deeds are means (asbab). Otherwise, if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to repay us for our deeds as a true exchange, then even one of His blessings upon us could not be matched by all our deeds. But deeds are a means.

His saying, ﴿with their truthfulness﴾: if the reward is according to truthfulness, then it will be in proportion to that truthfulness. Those who were true to what they pledged to Allah will be rewarded according to what they performed. If they were more obedient to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and more diligent in carrying out His commands and more active in His obedience, their reward will be greater. And the reverse is also true.

﴿And He will punish the hypocrites if He wills﴾ [al-Ahzab 24]. Who is the hypocrite (munafiq)? He is the one who shows faith and conceals disbelief. The word is derived from al-nafiqa'' (نافقاء), which is the hole of the jerboa (yarbu') that it makes in its burrow, so that when someone comes at it from the entrance, it escapes through that hole.

(﴿And He will punish the hypocrites if He wills﴾) by causing them to die in their hypocrisy. The author, in his saying "by causing them to die in their hypocrisy," indicates that the punishment of the hypocrites, which is made contingent upon His will here, does not mean that if He wills He punishes them and if He wills He does not punish them after they have died in hypocrisy. No. If they die in hypocrisy, Allah, exalted is He, has informed us that they are in the lowest level of the Fire, and they are not subject to His will. So His saying ﴿if He wills﴾ means: if they remain upon their hypocrisy until they die. When they remain upon their hypocrisy until death, we know that Allah has willed to punish them. However, if Allah guides them, then hypocrites may indeed be guided. Therefore He said ﴿or turn to them in forgiveness﴾ [al-Ahzab 24], meaning by granting them success in repentance.

The correct view, as we have often noted, is that the repentance of a hypocrite is valid. This is explicit in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper. Except for those who repent and amend and hold fast to Allah and purify their religion for Allah. Those will be with the believers﴾ [an-Nisa' 145–146].

So His saying ﴿or turn to them in forgiveness﴾ means by bestowing upon them repentance so that they repent, and at that point they will not be punished.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab 24]. ﴿Forgiving﴾ is an active participle in the form of intensification (sigha al-mubalagha), meaning: one who forgives much. It may also be an adjective of quality (sifa mushabbaha), meaning: possessor of forgiveness. The adjective of quality is more emphatic than the active participle, because the active participle indicates an act, whereas the adjective of quality indicates a description, that is, the constant attribution of that quality to the one it describes.

His saying, (﴿Forgiving﴾ for one who repents), contains something requiring consideration, because Allah, exalted is He, forgives even those who do not repent among those who are subject to His will, such as the perpetrator of sins. If the author, may Allah have mercy on him, had left it unrestricted, it would have been safer for him. So we say: ﴿Forgiving﴾ means one who forgives much, or one who possesses forgiveness, constantly characterized by it.

This is closer to what I have said, because it indicates the constant attribute, and His saying, the Exalted, confirms it: ﴿And indeed your Lord is possessor of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [ar-Ra'd 6].

His saying, (﴿Merciful﴾ toward them), he says "toward them," meaning toward those who repent.

The correct view is that He is merciful toward those who repent and toward others. The mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in its general sense encompasses the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and everyone is included in Allah's mercy. This is in the general sense. In the specific sense, however, mercy is restricted to the believers.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good﴾ [al-Ahzab 25]. "Repelled them" means He returned them, turned back on their heels, defeated and disappointed.

﴿Those who disbelieved﴾ means the confederates (al-ahzab) from Quraysh and others.

His saying, ﴿in their rage﴾: the preposition bi here is for accompaniment (lil-mulabasa), meaning: while clothed in rage. The prepositional phrase is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (hal), meaning that they returned in extreme fury. The reason for their fury was that they had come with this great host, the like of which had never been witnessed at that time, intending what? They intended to destroy the Prophet ﷺ. Yet what happened to them?

They suffered exhaustion, hardship, hunger, and affliction, and in the end they returned in flight. There is no doubt that such a thing affects a person; it fills his heart with rage, grief, and regret. How could he bring this army that he had gathered, and begin and repeat in it, and in the end be turned back without any battle? Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good﴾. Gained no good from what? 

No good, neither in the matter of this world nor in the matter of the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, they gained no good because they fought the Prophet ﷺ in every case. As for the matter of this world, what they regarded as good for themselves, did they attain it? No. They gained no good either in religion or in worldly life, and praise be to Allah. Even what they imagined to be good, namely the defeat of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his destruction along with his companions, did not happen to them. ﴿They gained no good.﴾

His saying ﴿good﴾ is an indefinite noun in the context of negation, and with ﴿lam﴾ it conveys generality, meaning they gained no good at all, neither little nor much. This is one of the blessings of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Allah attributed the repelling to Himself: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved﴾, because their turning back was not by the power or might of the Prophet ﷺ, nor by the power or might of his companions, but by the power and might of Allah, the Exalted. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾ [al-Ahzab 25].

The author says: (﴿They gained no good﴾ meaning their aim of victory over the believers).

﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾. Praise be to Allah. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾ means that Allah relieved the believers of fighting, so they did not fight. As for the skirmishes that took place between some of the Companions and some of the polytheists, these are not considered fighting, because the discussion concerns the entire army as a whole, and no battle took place among them. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾, and He is the best of protectors and the one who suffices, glory be to Him. He said: (by the wind and the angels). The wind: it has already been mentioned that Allah sent upon them a cold, fierce eastern wind, which overturned their cooking pots, toppled their tents, and pelted them with stones carried by the winds along with the severe cold, so that they were warming themselves by the fire and saying: "Rescue! Rescue!" This was the wind. As for the angels, Allah, glory be to Him, empowered the angels against them, casting terror, fright, and dread into their hearts, and driving them away until they departed from the place. This was part of the victory of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His Messenger ﷺ.

(﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle, and Allah is ever Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Ahzab 25], over bringing about whatever He wills; ﴿Exalted in Might﴾ overpowering in His command).

﴿And Allah is ever Powerful﴾. Strength (quwwa) is an attribute by which the strong one is able to do what he wills without weakness, and it is higher than power (qudra), because power is an attribute by which the capable one is able to do what he wills without incapacity. So strength is higher. Consider two men who carried a rock: one carried it with some difficulty, so we say: this one is capable but not strong; the other carried it as if it were something trivial, so we say: this one is strong.

The strength of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has no limit and no measure; rather He is beyond what a human being can imagine. When the people of ʿAd said: ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is greater than them in strength? And they were denying Our signs. So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of misfortune, that We might let them taste the punishment of disgrace in worldly life; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped﴾ [Fussilat 15–16].

As for His saying ﴿Exalted in Might﴾, the author says: (overpowering in His command). Al-ʿAziz is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted, and it has three meanings: ʿAziz of rank (ʿizzat al-qadr), ʿAziz of subjugation (ʿizzat al-qahr), and ʿAziz of inaccessibility (ʿizzat al-imtina').

As for ʿAziz of inaccessibility, it means that He is inaccessible to any evil or deficiency in all His attributes and all His acts.

As for ʿizzat al-qadr, it means that He possesses great and lofty rank, just as you say: so-and-so is ʿazīz al-nafs, meaning he has dignity and elevation above base things.

As for ʿizzat al-qahr, it means dominance, so it means that He dominates everything. Even in pre-Islamic times the poet said:

Where is the refuge, when the Deity is the seeker?
And al-Ashram is defeated; there is no victor.

So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Overpowering in His command, and He dominates everything; nothing can stand against His dominance. Thus al-ʿAziz has three meanings: ʿizzat al-qadr, ʿizzat al-qahr, and ʿizzat al-imtina', and all of them are established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

He said: (﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses﴾, that is, Qurayza, ﴿from their fortresses﴾, the fortresses, plural of ṣayṣa, which is that by which one fortifies oneself, ﴿and cast terror into their hearts﴾ [al-Ahzab 26]).

﴿He brought down those who supported them from the People of the Scripture from their fortresses﴾. The pronoun in ﴿brought down﴾ refers to whom? To Allah. His saying ﴿those who supported them﴾ means those who aided and assisted them. The word al-muzahara means assistance, and one says taẓāhara ʿalā kadhā, meaning to assist and back up against them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you two support each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector﴾ [at-Tahrim 4], and He said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants﴾ [al-Isra' 88], meaning helpers and supporters.

His saying ﴿supported them﴾ means they aided and assisted them from among the People of the Scripture.

His saying ﴿from the People of the Scripture﴾: the People of the Scripture are the Jews and the Christians, but what is meant here in the verse is a group of the Jews, namely the Banu Qurayza. It has already been mentioned that the Banu Qurayza, the Banu al-Nadir, and the Banu Qaynuqa' were three tribes of Jews among whom the Prophet ﷺ settled when he came to Madina. He made a covenant between them and himself, but they broke that covenant, and only the Banu Qurayza remained. Then the Banu Qurayza broke the covenant by supporting whom? The confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

When the Prophet ﷺ returned from the battle of the confederates, entered his house, and bathed, Jibril came to him and said: "Go out to these people," pointing to the Banu Qurayza, "for they have broken the covenant." So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded his companions to go out, and said: "Let none of you pray ʿAsr except in the land of Banu Qurayza."[[Al-Bukhari (2813) and Muslim (1769) reported with their chains from ʿA'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned on the day of the Trench, he put down his weapons and bathed; then Jibril came to him with dust clinging to his head, and said: "Have you put down the weapons? By Allah, I have not put them down." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Where?" He said: "Here," and pointed toward the Banu Qurayza... the hadith. And see al-Thiqat of Ibn Hibban (1/274).]]

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did not delay or hold back, despite their exhaustion and weakness. They went out and besieged the Banu Qurayza for about twenty days, until they came down under the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, may Allah be pleased with him.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says here: ﴿He brought down those who supported them from the People of the Scripture from their fortresses﴾. ﴿From their fortresses﴾ is a prepositional phrase governed by ﴿brought down﴾, meaning: He brought these people down from their fortresses, that is, from their places of refuge. The original meaning of ṣayāṣī is the enclosures of cattle, since cattle are secured in them. So ﴿from their fortresses﴾ means from their places of refuge and their strongholds in which they took shelter. But that did not avail them anything against Allah; He brought them down from their fortresses.

﴿And cast terror into their hearts﴾. Qadhafa means "threw," and it is more forceful in effect than waḍaʿa (placed). If He had said "placed terror in their hearts," it would indicate that terror existed in the hearts, but when He says qadhafa, it becomes stronger. Ruʿb means fear, and when fear falls upon the heart, you cannot ask about the one who is afraid: he thinks the trees are fleeing, he does not perceive matters as they truly are, and even if one of his companions calls him, he thinks his enemy is calling him to kill him. No weapon is more destructive to the enemy than terror. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I have been given victory through terror over a distance of a month's journey."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

As for when the heart is firm and at rest, the fighter will be steadfast, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah often that you may be successful﴾ [al-Anfal 45]. The remembrance of Allah the Exalted is that by which hearts find rest: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured﴾ [ar-Ra'd 28].

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed that He sent down rain upon the people of Badr to make their feet firm with it, and for it to bring tranquility.

The conclusion is that terror is one of the most destructive weapons against the enemy.

﴿And cast terror into their hearts; a party you kill, and you take captive a party﴾. The author said: (﴿a party﴾ you kill among them, namely the fighting men, ﴿and you take captive a party﴾ among them, that is, the dependents).

When the siege was prolonged for them and they came down under the judgment of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, he gave them a choice, saying: "Whose judgment do you want to come down under?"[[Al-Bukhari (6262) and Muslim (1768/64) with their chains from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the people of Qurayza came down under the judgment of Saʿd. The Prophet ﷺ sent for him and he came. He said: "Stand up for your master," or "for the best of you," and he sat beside the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "These have come down under your judgment." He said: "Then I judge that their fighting men be killed, and their dependents be taken captive." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You have judged by the judgment of the King."]] They said: "We want to come down under the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿadh." Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, may Allah be pleased with him, had been their ally. They thought he would do as ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy did for his Jewish allies, when he interceded for them with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and they were spared. But Saʿd, may Allah be pleased with him, when he came, having been in a tent in the mosque since he had been struck in the arm (akhal) during the battle of the Confederates, and since the Prophet ﷺ had pitched a tent for him in the mosque so he could visit him from nearby because he was the chief of his people, the chief of the Aws.

He came riding a donkey from the Messenger of Allah's mosque to the place of the siege. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed him that they had made him their arbiter. He said: "Is my judgment binding upon them?" pointing to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and pointing to them as well. They said: "Yes," and all of them agreed. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was content, and so were these Jews. He said: "The time has come for Saʿd that the blame of no blamer should deter him in the cause of Allah." This was a momentous trial, and he judged among them, may Allah be pleased with him, with a great judgment, a correct judgment in accordance with the truth. He said: "I judge that their fighting men be killed, their dependents be taken captive, and their property be taken as spoils." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You have judged among them by the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens."[[Ibid.; and see Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/240).]]

Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded that their fighting men be killed, namely the adult men, while the dependents, the women and the boys who had not reached puberty, were taken captive, and the property was taken as spoils. They killed in Madina between seven hundred and eight hundred men, killed on a single day, in accordance with a judgment that they themselves had accepted. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿a party you kill, and you take captive a party﴾. Here He placed the object first in ﴿a party you kill﴾, and delayed the object in ﴿and you take captive a party﴾. Is the purpose of that only the preservation of the verse endings (fawasil), so that the benefit is verbal, or is there a meaningful benefit as well?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, both.
* The Student: The two groups differ; they are not equal.
* The Shaykh: How so?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 22–27 (part 3 of 5):

* Student: The two groups differ. The last group means the women, and the first means only the men.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because the first are the men, and the second are those who do not fight. (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, this is the apparent meaning, because the first ruling is more severe and more emphatic. For this reason its object was placed first, ﴿a group you kill﴾. The second is less than that, because a captive may be freed by grace, so He said: ﴿and a group you take captive﴾. This is with regard to the wording, which is the consideration of the endings (al-fawasil, the rhyming endings of the verses). In Surat al-Baqarah He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿a group He denied and a group they kill﴾ [al-Ma'idah 70], or ﴿some you denied and some you kill﴾ [al-Baqarah 87]. Since denying the messengers was severe, the object was placed first in it, just as the object was placed first in their killing. This is the story of the Confederates, and it ended with His saying: ﴿and He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and land you had not trodden﴾ [al-Ahzab 27]. Afterwards, that was Khaybar, and it was taken after Qurayzah. ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 27].
﴿He caused you to inherit their land﴾: this verb takes two objects. The first object is the "kaf" (the pronoun "you"), and the second is "their land." ﴿And their homes﴾. How do "land" and "homes" differ? The "diyar" (homes) is the plural of "dar," which refers to dwellings and quarters. As for "ard" (land), it is more general than that. The "amwal" (wealth) are goods, silver coins, gold dinars, and other things.
﴿And land you had not trodden﴾ means you had not stepped on it until now, but you will inherit it. It is the land of Khaybar, for the Prophet ﷺ conquered it afterwards in the sixth year. ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾, so nothing can overpower Him.
As for His saying ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾, He placed the object first to affirm that the action would certainly fall upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾. Do not say, as some people say, "He is competent over whatever He wills," because if you say "competent over whatever He wills," you restrict His power to what He wills, whereas power relates both to what He has willed and to what He has not willed. Even what He has not willed, He is able to do. And Allah knows best.
The Messenger ﷺ said: «Stand up for your chief» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6262) and Muslim (1768/64), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him], so they stood up for their chief Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and brought him down from his donkey. He sat in front of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «These people agreed to come down under your judgment». [Al-Bukhari (6262) and Muslim (1768/64) narrated with their chains from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the people of Qurayzah came down under the judgment of Sa'd. The Prophet ﷺ sent for him, and he came. He said: «Stand up for your chief», or he said: «the best of you». Then he sat beside the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: «These people came down under your judgment». He said: "I judge that their fighting men be killed and their children taken captive." He said: «You have judged by the judgment of the King».] So he said to them, then turned to them and said: "Are you content with this, and is my judgment binding?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to the other side, where the Muslims were, and said: "Are you content with this?" They said: "Yes." However, when he turned toward the Messenger ﷺ, he lowered his head out of reverence for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he issued this ruling, which the Prophet ﷺ affirmed, and said: «It is the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens». [Ibid.; see Sirah Ibn Hisham (2/240).] How many were these people?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: They said: when they saw the Confederates, they said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. The situation required that fear and terror overtake them, as it did the hypocrites.
* Among its benefits: the complete truthfulness of their belief in Allah and His Messenger, in their saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 22]. They witnessed what Allah had promised, then they expressed certainty about it with their tongues, by their saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾.
Some ignorant people have used this verse to argue for the legitimacy of concluding the recitation of the Qur'an with the words "Allah has spoken the truth." They said: "How do you object to us when we finish the reading and say: 'Allah the Mighty has spoken the truth,' when Allah says: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾, and says: ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth﴾ [Al 'Imran 95]?" So what is the answer to this doubt?
* Student: The answer is that He did not say ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth﴾ at the end of the recitation (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. We say: We do not deny that someone may say "Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth." Rather, we consider it part of faith that a person says "Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth," and whoever does not hold this belief is a disbeliever.
