As for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the Qur'an Allah the Exalted did not address him by his name; that is, He did not say: "O Muhammad." Although that occurs in the hadiths, in the Qur'an it does not.

﴿O Prophet﴾: "al-Nabi" (the Prophet) is a softened form of "al-Nabi'" with a hamza. It is said that it is not a softened form. The root of this disagreement is whether "al-Nabi" derives from "al-naba'" (news) or from "al-nubuwwah" (elevation)? If we say it derives from "al-nubuwwah," there is no softening in it, because the ya' is original. If we say it derives from "al-naba'," then there is softening, and its original form is "al-Nabi'," so the hamza was softened into a ya'.

The correct view is that it derives from both meanings together: "al-Nabi'" is derived from "al-naba'," because he is informed and informs, and it is also derived from "al-nubuwwah," because of the high rank of the prophets.

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾: "Azwaj" is the plural of "zawj," and does it refer to the female or the male? In the Arabic language, "zawj" is applied to both the female and the male. There is also a dialect, but it is a poor and rare one, in which you say for the woman "zawjah." However, this poor and rare usage is the one employed by the jurists of inheritance (al-fara'iyyun), who say "zawj" for the male and "zawjah" for the female, for the sake of clarity and explanation, and this is a necessity in the field of inheritance.

﴿Say to your wives﴾: They were nine; five of them were from Quraysh, and four were not from Quraysh. They asked him for some of the adornment of this world that he did not have. They asked him for maintenance and clothing, and other things that women desire from men in terms of wealth. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as we all know, had little means, because he would spend what he had and would not keep anything for himself. So they asked him for maintenance and pressed him, and he took an oath to abstain from them for a full month; he withdrew from them. Then he came down at the end of the month, and Allah revealed to him this verse: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ to its end.

﴿If﴾ is a conditional particle; the conditional verb is ﴿you were﴾ (kuntunna), and the answer of the condition is ﴿then come, I will provide for you﴾ (fa-ta'alayna umatti'kunna). ﴿If you desire the worldly life and its adornment﴾: ﴿the worldly life﴾ means its enjoyments; ﴿and its adornment﴾ means what is in it of wealth, palaces, mounts, and the like. ﴿Then come﴾ (fa-ta'alayna) is an imperative verb, or is it an imperative noun? It is an imperative verb, because it takes the grammatical markers; since it takes those markers, it is an imperative verb. Hence one says "ta'alayn," and one says ﴿come to a word﴾ [Al 'Imran 64]. By contrast, "halumma" does not take those markers, so it is an imperative noun.

﴿Then come﴾ means: turn towards me. ﴿I will provide for you and release you with a fair release﴾: ﴿I will provide for you﴾ is the answer to the imperative in His words ﴿then come﴾; that is, I will give you provision with which you may enjoy yourselves. ﴿And release you with a fair release﴾ means: I will set you free, because "tasrih" is the opposite of restriction. This is from the lofty manners that Allah commanded His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with. Otherwise the situation would have required him to say: "If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will divorce you," and there is no good in one who desires nothing but the world.

But out of the completeness of care, ﴿I will provide for you and release you﴾: I will give you wealth with which you may enjoy yourselves, and ﴿release you﴾: I will divorce you, ﴿with a fair release﴾, meaning: without enmity, without hatred, and without any restriction upon you afterwards. For this reason, if this had happened, it would have been lawful for them to marry someone else, because this is a fair release; for there is no benefit in her being released from the Messenger ﷺ and then remaining restricted. But the matter did not occur.

﴿So come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release﴾: Is this for all women? ..

He says: (﴿And the Last Abode﴾: that is, Paradise; ﴿indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾: by desiring the Hereafter; ﴿a great reward﴾: that is, Paradise.)

He began with the worldly life, ﴿If you desire the worldly life﴾, because they were asking for maintenance, and that belongs to worldly matters.

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾: this is the second state for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾, and He did not say "for them," but said ﴿for the good-doers﴾, placing the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to make clear that this desire is goodness, and that if they desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, that is from goodness, and that Allah has prepared for the good-doers among them a great reward. And "min" (among) here is not partitive but explanatory, so it includes the case in which all of them desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode; for Allah prepares a great reward for all of them.

So at the very beginning he started with the one most beloved to him among his wives, 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said to her: "There is no harm upon you in not hastening, so that you consult your two parents." He feared that she, being a young girl, might hasten and say: "I want the world." So he asked her not to hasten until she consulted her parents, that is, sought their permission.

It is well known that her parents would not want her to choose the worldly life and its adornment over Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. But she, may Allah be pleased with her, despite her young age, had far-sighted insight, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, in this matter am I to consult my parents?" That is: do I consult my parents about this? No, rather I desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. But do not inform your wives of what I have said.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I was sent only as one who makes things easy, not one who burdens or causes distress, and whichever woman asks me, I will inform her."[[Recorded by Muslim (1478/29) with his chain from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Abu Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found people sitting at his door, none of whom had been given permission. He said: So Abu Bakr was given permission and entered. Then 'Umar came and sought permission, and he was given permission, and found the Prophet ﷺ sitting with his wives around him, silent and quiet. He said: So he said: "I will say something that will make the Prophet ﷺ laugh." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah asking me for maintenance, I rose to her and struck her neck." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance." So Abu Bakr rose to 'A'ishah to strike her neck, and 'Umar rose to Hafsah to strike her neck, both saying: "Do you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have?" So they said: "By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have, ever." Then he withdrew from them for a month, or twenty-nine days, and then this verse was revealed to him: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab 28], until ﴿for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab 29]. He said: So he began with 'A'ishah and said: "O 'A'ishah, I want to present to you a matter, and I would like that you not hasten in it until you consult your two parents." She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" So he recited the verse to her. She said: "In you, O Messenger of Allah, shall I consult my parents? Rather, I choose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, and I ask you not to inform any of your wives of what I have said." He said: "None of them will ask me except that I will inform her. Indeed, Allah did not send me as one who burdens or causes distress, but He sent me as a teacher who makes things easy."]]

However, not all of his wives asked; every one of them said that she desired Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. So they remained in the complete state, may Allah be pleased with them, upon what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was upon of hardship of living and lack of means. Despite this, Allah granted them success and bestowed His favour upon them. Undoubtedly this is from Allah's care for His Messenger, that He chose for him such women. Their reward was that Allah said to him: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. These women who chose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, after being given the choice, along with what is in the reward of the Hereafter, received this worldly reward: that the Messenger was prevented from marrying anyone of the women after that, or exchanging one for a new woman, ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever over all things an Watcher﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. And Allah knows best.

(﴿committing a clear immorality﴾: read with the vowelling of the ya' both fathah and kasrah: ﴿mubayyinah﴾ and ﴿mubayyanah﴾, meaning: made clear, or it is itself clear. ﴿Will be doubled﴾ (yudha'af): and in another reading yudha''af with shaddah, and in another nudha''if with the nun together with it—that is, with shaddah and the accusative of "the punishment"—﴿We will double for her the punishment﴾.)

So there are then three readings: yudha'af, yudha''af, and nudha''if. On the first two readings, "al-'adhab" is in the nominative, as the deputy subject (na'ib al-fa'il); on the third reading, nudha''if, "al-'adhab" is in the accusative as the direct object.

It is said: ﴿We will double for her the punishment twofold﴾ (twice the punishment of others, that is, double it, ﴿and that is for Allah easy﴾).

﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾: the address from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directed to the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, because of the importance of what will be directed to them, and to alert them to what is about to be conveyed to them.

﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality﴾: ﴿whoever﴾ here is conditional, the conditional verb is ﴿commits﴾, and ﴿will be doubled﴾ is the answer of the condition.

And His saying: ﴿Whoever of you commits an immorality﴾: what is meant by "fahishah"? Is the intended meaning adultery? Or the intended meaning is obscene speech, and vulgar insolence towards the Messenger ﷺ, and departure from decency, or is it both?

Some scholars said: the latter is intended, and not adultery, although "fahishah" in the Qur'an comes meaning adultery, and comes meaning foul tongue and insolence. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality, bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾ [al-Nisa' 15]. What is meant by "fahishah" here? Adultery.

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [al-Talaq 1], and the meaning of "fahishah" here is foulness of tongue and bad language. So if a woman is foul-tongued and ill-mannered, speaking words outside of decency, her husband has the right to expel her from the house during the waiting period.

This verse, if we say it includes both the immorality that is adultery and the immorality that is foulness of tongue, does not mean that it occurs from them; for the condition does not necessarily occur, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]. Is that possible? ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]. Is that possible? It is not possible. ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work will surely be lost﴾ [al-Zumar 65]. This also is not possible. So the mention of something attached to a condition does not necessarily entail that the condition is permissible to occur. On this basis, let the verse be: ﴿Whoever of you commits an immorality﴾, let it include adultery; but that is an impossible matter. As for if we say that what is meant by "fahishah" is the sharpness of the tongue and going beyond the norm and decency in speech, this may occur from women, even from the mothers of the believers, may Allah be pleased with them, and there is no blame upon them for that, because it is part of women's nature to be jealous, to fail to guard the tongue, and not to be patient in affairs. Whatever the case, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾, and that is because of her nobility and the elevation of her station. So the sin from her is greater than the sin from others. For this reason, if a free woman commits adultery she is lashed or stoned; and if a slave woman commits adultery, there is upon her only half the punishment of the chaste women; because of the nobility of the first and the lowliness of the second. So the wives of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, have such a lofty station and such an impregnable fortress that it requires the punishment to be doubled upon them if they commit a clear immorality. Hence He said: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for her twofold﴾.

If the recompense for an evil deed is an evil like it, then the recompense for the evil mentioned here—the clear immorality—with respect to the wives of the Messenger is two evils. For this reason He said: ﴿Her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾; that is, it will be repeated upon them twice. ﴿And that was﴾: that is, the doubling of the punishment upon them, ﴿was that﴾ upon Allah easy: the referent is the doubling of the punishment, and it is easy for Allah, not difficult for Him.

Why did He say: ﴿And that was upon Allah easy﴾? So that no one would suppose that this matter is difficult for Allah because it concerns the wives of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that this matter is easy for Him, because He, glorified and exalted, has no kinship between Him and His creation; the most noble of creatures in His sight is the most righteous of them to Him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat 13].

﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her reward twice﴾: this is the opposite of the first. When we said: if they commit a clear immorality, the punishment is doubled upon them, Allah recompenses them with justice from another direction, saying: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger﴾.

(﴿yaqnut﴾: yuti', obeys.) But devotion (qunut) to Allah the Exalted is other than devotion to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Devotion to Allah is devotion of worship, humility and exaltation; and devotion to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is devotion of obedience to the husband, and it is not like their devotion to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger﴾: ﴿to Allah﴾ by obedience and worship, and to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by fulfilling the rights that are due to the husband from his wife.

﴿And does righteous deeds﴾: does a righteous deed. A righteous deed is that which is sincere and correct. Sincere and correct means that it combines the two fundamental conditions in every act of worship: sincerity to Allah and following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Every act of worship must have these two conditions. Whoever follows the Messenger but is not sincere to Allah, his prayer is void, because it is showing off; and whoever is sincere to Allah but does not follow the Messenger ﷺ, his prayer is also void, his worship is void, because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."[[Recorded by Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

So what are the two fundamental conditions for the validity of worship?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, following together with sincerity?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, so if there is following without sincerity?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is not accepted. Sincerity without following is not accepted; both matters are necessary. And thus whenever Allah the Exalted mentions a righteous deed, the meaning of "righteous" is that which includes these two fundamental conditions.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We will give her reward twice﴾. ﴿We will give her﴾: He did not say "yu'tiha" with a ya', why?
* Student: (...).

**The Shaykh:** The response of the conditional (*jawab al-shart*), which is His saying ﴿whoever of you devotes herself﴾, and the response of the conditional must be in the jussive (*majzum*). The verb here is jussive by the dropping of the weak letter (*harf al-'illah*). Its original form is *nu'tihā*. When it became jussive, the weak letter was dropped, giving ﴿nu'tihā﴾. The meaning of ﴿nu'tihā﴾ is "We give her." For this reason it takes two objects: the first object is (*hā*, "her"), and the second is ﴿her reward﴾.

(﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾ means: double the reward of other women.) In one reading, there is a *ya* (*taḥtāniyyah*) in ﴿ta'mal﴾ (*ta'mal*, "does").

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** The *ya* in ﴿ta'mal﴾ gives ﴿ya'mal﴾ ("does"), and in ﴿nu'tihā﴾ it gives ﴿yu'tihā﴾ ("He gives her"). This reading is one of the seven canonical readings (*sab'iyyah*), according to the author's terminology. ﴿Yu'tihā﴾ means God, and ﴿nu'tihā﴾ means We. So to whom does the pronoun refer? To God: ﴿He will give her her reward twice﴾. Just as, if she commits a clear immorality, her punishment is doubled, so if she devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, God, exalted is He, will give her her reward twice. Giving a reward twice is not strange, for God has affirmed double reward in several matters. Such as what?

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** No. ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54]. And the Prophet ﷺ informed that a man from the People of the Book who believes in his Book and then believes in Muhammad ﷺ, God will give him his reward twice.

Many scholars said, regarding the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid 57:28]: this is the reward of this *ummah*, which is doubled over other nations. The important point is that God's bounty is vast; He may reward the doer twice for some reason.

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** That is in the hadith.

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** It is the one we recited: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them. (54) And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54–55].

He says: ﴿And We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾. ﴿We have prepared﴾ means We have readied for her. ﴿Provision﴾ means gift. ﴿Noble﴾ means good and abundant, because nobility (*karam*) differs in each context according to what suits it. So a "noble" (*karīmah*) ewe means one that is good, beautiful, and abundant in milk, as in the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Beware of the noble (*karā'im*) of their property." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1496) and Muslim (19/29), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.] Here, the "noble provision" means abundant, good, and beautiful gift. This happens, as the author says: (in Paradise, an increase).

Then God, exalted is He, said (...).

* From it is derived: the obligation for the Prophet ﷺ to give his wives a choice; from His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾.
* And among its benefits: God's protection of His Messenger and His defense of him, in that He commanded him to give his wives this choice when they constricted him and asked him for maintenance.
* And among its benefits: the virtues of the Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, since they chose God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode.
* And among its benefits: the perfection of the character of the Prophet ﷺ, in that God commanded him to say: ﴿If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release﴾. The situation would have called for them to be rebuked and reproached for this, but it was said: ﴿Come, I will provide for you and release you﴾.
* And among its benefits: the permissibility for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to be married to others if they chose the worldly life and its adornment; from His saying: ﴿and release you in a fair release﴾.
* And among the benefits of the following noble verse, ﴿And if you desire God and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾: that desiring God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode is a form of excellence (*ihsan*); from His saying: ﴿Indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that intention has a great effect in increasing reward, since He attached this reward to this desire and good intention.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over﴾.

* From this noble verse is derived: that the sin of those near (to God) is more severe than the sin of others. From where is this taken? From God's saying: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over﴾.
* And among its benefits: the protection of the Prophet's ﷺ marital bed in full, since when a woman among his wives commits a clear immorality, God doubles her punishment. All of this is for the sake of protecting the Prophet's ﷺ marital bed, whether we say that "immorality" means fornication or means foul speech of the tongue.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that God, mighty and majestic, has the right to do what He wills in doubling reward and punishment, and that this matter is easy for Him; from His saying: ﴿And that is ever easy for God﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾.

* From this noble verse is derived: a great distinction for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, since if a woman among them did a righteous deed and obeyed God and His Messenger, God gave her reward twice.
* And from it: the justice of God, exalted is He, His perfect justice. Since her punishment was doubled, her reward and recompense are doubled too. For this reason He said: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her﴾ and His saying: ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾.
* And among its benefits also: that God has prepared for these believing women among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ a noble reward, that is, abundant, beautiful, and good, ﴿We will give her her reward twice and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾.

As for the discussion of the noble verses, we begin with it too, and we continue with you in these lessons.

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, if you desire﴾: where is the object of the saying in His words: ﴿say to your wives﴾? (...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 28–31 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ [al-Ahzab 28].

﴿O Prophet﴾: Allah did not address His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ except by the description of prophethood and messengership: ﴿O Prophet﴾, ﴿O Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah 41]. Whereas with other prophets He often addressed them by their names: ﴿O Musa﴾ [al-A'raf 144], ﴿O Nuh﴾ [Hud 46], ﴿O Ibrahim﴾ [Hud 76], and the like. As for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the Qur'an Allah the Exalted did not address him by his name; that is, He did not say: "O Muhammad." Although that occurs in the hadiths, in the Qur'an it does not.

﴿O Prophet﴾: "al-Nabi" (the Prophet) is a softened form of "al-Nabi'" with a hamza. It is said that it is not a softened form. The root of this disagreement is whether "al-Nabi" derives from "al-naba'" (news) or from "al-nubuwwah" (elevation)? If we say it derives from "al-nubuwwah," there is no softening in it, because the ya' is original. If we say it derives from "al-naba'," then there is softening, and its original form is "al-Nabi'," so the hamza was softened into a ya'.

The correct view is that it derives from both meanings together: "al-Nabi'" is derived from "al-naba'," because he is informed and informs, and it is also derived from "al-nubuwwah," because of the high rank of the prophets.

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾: "Azwaj" is the plural of "zawj," and does it refer to the female or the male? In the Arabic language, "zawj" is applied to both the female and the male. There is also a dialect, but it is a poor and rare one, in which you say for the woman "zawjah." However, this poor and rare usage is the one employed by the jurists of inheritance (al-fara'iyyun), who say "zawj" for the male and "zawjah" for the female, for the sake of clarity and explanation, and this is a necessity in the field of inheritance.

﴿Say to your wives﴾: They were nine; five of them were from Quraysh, and four were not from Quraysh. They asked him for some of the adornment of this world that he did not have. They asked him for maintenance and clothing, and other things that women desire from men in terms of wealth. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as we all know, had little means, because he would spend what he had and would not keep anything for himself. So they asked him for maintenance and pressed him, and he took an oath to abstain from them for a full month; he withdrew from them. Then he came down at the end of the month, and Allah revealed to him this verse: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment…﴾ to its end.

﴿If﴾ is a conditional particle; the conditional verb is ﴿you were﴾ (kuntunna), and the answer of the condition is ﴿then come, I will provide for you﴾ (fa-ta'alayna umatti'kunna). ﴿If you desire the worldly life and its adornment﴾: ﴿the worldly life﴾ means its enjoyments; ﴿and its adornment﴾ means what is in it of wealth, palaces, mounts, and the like. ﴿Then come﴾ (fa-ta'alayna) is an imperative verb, or is it an imperative noun? It is an imperative verb, because it takes the grammatical markers; since it takes those markers, it is an imperative verb. Hence one says "ta'alayn," and one says ﴿come to a word﴾ [Al 'Imran 64]. By contrast, "halumma" does not take those markers, so it is an imperative noun.

﴿Then come﴾ means: turn towards me. ﴿I will provide for you and release you with a fair release﴾: ﴿I will provide for you﴾ is the answer to the imperative in His words ﴿then come﴾; that is, I will give you provision with which you may enjoy yourselves. ﴿And release you with a fair release﴾ means: I will set you free, because "tasrih" is the opposite of restriction. This is from the lofty manners that Allah commanded His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with. Otherwise the situation would have required him to say: "If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will divorce you," and there is no good in one who desires nothing but the world.

But out of the completeness of care, ﴿I will provide for you and release you﴾: I will give you wealth with which you may enjoy yourselves, and ﴿release you﴾: I will divorce you, ﴿with a fair release﴾, meaning: without enmity, without hatred, and without any restriction upon you afterwards. For this reason, if this had happened, it would have been lawful for them to marry someone else, because this is a fair release; for there is no benefit in her being released from the Messenger ﷺ and then remaining restricted. But the matter did not occur.

﴿So come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release﴾: Is this for all women? ..

He says: (﴿And the Last Abode﴾: that is, Paradise; ﴿indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾: by desiring the Hereafter; ﴿a great reward﴾: that is, Paradise.)

He began with the worldly life, ﴿If you desire the worldly life﴾, because they were asking for maintenance, and that belongs to worldly matters.

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾: this is the second state for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾, and He did not say "for them," but said ﴿for the good-doers﴾, placing the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to make clear that this desire is goodness, and that if they desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, that is from goodness, and that Allah has prepared for the good-doers among them a great reward. And "min" (among) here is not partitive but explanatory, so it includes the case in which all of them desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode; for Allah prepares a great reward for all of them.

So at the very beginning he started with the one most beloved to him among his wives, 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said to her: "There is no harm upon you in not hastening, so that you consult your two parents." He feared that she, being a young girl, might hasten and say: "I want the world." So he asked her not to hasten until she consulted her parents, that is, sought their permission.

It is well known that her parents would not want her to choose the worldly life and its adornment over Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. But she, may Allah be pleased with her, despite her young age, had far-sighted insight, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, in this matter am I to consult my parents?" That is: do I consult my parents about this? No, rather I desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. But do not inform your wives of what I have said.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I was sent only as one who makes things easy, not one who burdens or causes distress, and whichever woman asks me, I will inform her."[[Recorded by Muslim (1478/29) with his chain from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Abu Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found people sitting at his door, none of whom had been given permission. He said: So Abu Bakr was given permission and entered. Then 'Umar came and sought permission, and he was given permission, and found the Prophet ﷺ sitting with his wives around him, silent and quiet. He said: So he said: "I will say something that will make the Prophet ﷺ laugh." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah asking me for maintenance, I rose to her and struck her neck." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance." So Abu Bakr rose to 'A'ishah to strike her neck, and 'Umar rose to Hafsah to strike her neck, both saying: "Do you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have?" So they said: "By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have, ever." Then he withdrew from them for a month, or twenty-nine days, and then this verse was revealed to him: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab 28], until ﴿for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab 29]. He said: So he began with 'A'ishah and said: "O 'A'ishah, I want to present to you a matter, and I would like that you not hasten in it until you consult your two parents." She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" So he recited the verse to her. She said: "In you, O Messenger of Allah, shall I consult my parents? Rather, I choose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, and I ask you not to inform any of your wives of what I have said." He said: "None of them will ask me except that I will inform her. Indeed, Allah did not send me as one who burdens or causes distress, but He sent me as a teacher who makes things easy."]]

However, not all of his wives asked; every one of them said that she desired Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode. So they remained in the complete state, may Allah be pleased with them, upon what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was upon of hardship of living and lack of means. Despite this, Allah granted them success and bestowed His favour upon them. Undoubtedly this is from Allah's care for His Messenger, that He chose for him such women. Their reward was that Allah said to him: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. These women who chose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, after being given the choice, along with what is in the reward of the Hereafter, received this worldly reward: that the Messenger was prevented from marrying anyone of the women after that, or exchanging one for a new woman, ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever over all things an Watcher﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. And Allah knows best.

(﴿committing a clear immorality﴾: read with the vowelling of the ya' both fathah and kasrah: ﴿mubayyinah﴾ and ﴿mubayyanah﴾, meaning: made clear, or it is itself clear. ﴿Will be doubled﴾ (yudha'af): and in another reading yudha''af with shaddah, and in another nudha''if with the nun together with it—that is, with shaddah and the accusative of "the punishment"—﴿We will double for her the punishment﴾.)

So there are then three readings: yudha'af, yudha''af, and nudha''if. On the first two readings, "al-'adhab" is in the nominative, as the deputy subject (na'ib al-fa'il); on the third reading, nudha''if, "al-'adhab" is in the accusative as the direct object.

It is said: ﴿We will double for her the punishment twofold﴾ (twice the punishment of others, that is, double it, ﴿and that is for Allah easy﴾).

﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾: the address from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directed to the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, because of the importance of what will be directed to them, and to alert them to what is about to be conveyed to them.

﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality﴾: ﴿whoever﴾ here is conditional, the conditional verb is ﴿commits﴾, and ﴿will be doubled﴾ is the answer of the condition.

And His saying: ﴿Whoever of you commits an immorality﴾: what is meant by "fahishah"? Is the intended meaning adultery? Or the intended meaning is obscene speech, and vulgar insolence towards the Messenger ﷺ, and departure from decency, or is it both?

Some scholars said: the latter is intended, and not adultery, although "fahishah" in the Qur'an comes meaning adultery, and comes meaning foul tongue and insolence. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality, bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾ [al-Nisa' 15]. What is meant by "fahishah" here? Adultery.

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ [al-Talaq 1], and the meaning of "fahishah" here is foulness of tongue and bad language. So if a woman is foul-tongued and ill-mannered, speaking words outside of decency, her husband has the right to expel her from the house during the waiting period.

This verse, if we say it includes both the immorality that is adultery and the immorality that is foulness of tongue, does not mean that it occurs from them; for the condition does not necessarily occur, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]. Is that possible? ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]. Is that possible? It is not possible. ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your work will surely be lost﴾ [al-Zumar 65]. This also is not possible. So the mention of something attached to a condition does not necessarily entail that the condition is permissible to occur. On this basis, let the verse be: ﴿Whoever of you commits an immorality﴾, let it include adultery; but that is an impossible matter. As for if we say that what is meant by "fahishah" is the sharpness of the tongue and going beyond the norm and decency in speech, this may occur from women, even from the mothers of the believers, may Allah be pleased with them, and there is no blame upon them for that, because it is part of women's nature to be jealous, to fail to guard the tongue, and not to be patient in affairs. Whatever the case, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾, and that is because of her nobility and the elevation of her station. So the sin from her is greater than the sin from others. For this reason, if a free woman commits adultery she is lashed or stoned; and if a slave woman commits adultery, there is upon her only half the punishment of the chaste women; because of the nobility of the first and the lowliness of the second. So the wives of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, have such a lofty station and such an impregnable fortress that it requires the punishment to be doubled upon them if they commit a clear immorality. Hence He said: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for her twofold﴾.

If the recompense for an evil deed is an evil like it, then the recompense for the evil mentioned here—the clear immorality—with respect to the wives of the Messenger is two evils. For this reason He said: ﴿Her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾; that is, it will be repeated upon them twice. ﴿And that was﴾: that is, the doubling of the punishment upon them, ﴿was that﴾ upon Allah easy: the referent is the doubling of the punishment, and it is easy for Allah, not difficult for Him.

Why did He say: ﴿And that was upon Allah easy﴾? So that no one would suppose that this matter is difficult for Allah because it concerns the wives of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that this matter is easy for Him, because He, glorified and exalted, has no kinship between Him and His creation; the most noble of creatures in His sight is the most righteous of them to Him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat 13].

﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her reward twice﴾: this is the opposite of the first. When we said: if they commit a clear immorality, the punishment is doubled upon them, Allah recompenses them with justice from another direction, saying: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger﴾.

(﴿yaqnut﴾: yuti', obeys.) But devotion (qunut) to Allah the Exalted is other than devotion to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Devotion to Allah is devotion of worship, humility and exaltation; and devotion to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is devotion of obedience to the husband, and it is not like their devotion to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Whoever of you devotes herself to Allah and His Messenger﴾: ﴿to Allah﴾ by obedience and worship, and to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by fulfilling the rights that are due to the husband from his wife.

﴿And does righteous deeds﴾: does a righteous deed. A righteous deed is that which is sincere and correct. Sincere and correct means that it combines the two fundamental conditions in every act of worship: sincerity to Allah and following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Every act of worship must have these two conditions. Whoever follows the Messenger but is not sincere to Allah, his prayer is void, because it is showing off; and whoever is sincere to Allah but does not follow the Messenger ﷺ, his prayer is also void, his worship is void, because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."[[Recorded by Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

So what are the two fundamental conditions for the validity of worship?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, following together with sincerity?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, so if there is following without sincerity?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is not accepted. Sincerity without following is not accepted; both matters are necessary. And thus whenever Allah the Exalted mentions a righteous deed, the meaning of "righteous" is that which includes these two fundamental conditions.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We will give her reward twice﴾. ﴿We will give her﴾: He did not say "yu'tiha" with a ya', why?
* Student: (...).

**The Shaykh:** The response of the conditional (*jawab al-shart*), which is His saying ﴿whoever of you devotes herself﴾, and the response of the conditional must be in the jussive (*majzum*). The verb here is jussive by the dropping of the weak letter (*harf al-'illah*). Its original form is *nu'tihā*. When it became jussive, the weak letter was dropped, giving ﴿nu'tihā﴾. The meaning of ﴿nu'tihā﴾ is "We give her." For this reason it takes two objects: the first object is (*hā*, "her"), and the second is ﴿her reward﴾.

(﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾ means: double the reward of other women.) In one reading, there is a *ya* (*taḥtāniyyah*) in ﴿ta'mal﴾ (*ta'mal*, "does").

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** The *ya* in ﴿ta'mal﴾ gives ﴿ya'mal﴾ ("does"), and in ﴿nu'tihā﴾ it gives ﴿yu'tihā﴾ ("He gives her"). This reading is one of the seven canonical readings (*sab'iyyah*), according to the author's terminology. ﴿Yu'tihā﴾ means God, and ﴿nu'tihā﴾ means We. So to whom does the pronoun refer? To God: ﴿He will give her her reward twice﴾. Just as, if she commits a clear immorality, her punishment is doubled, so if she devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, God, exalted is He, will give her her reward twice. Giving a reward twice is not strange, for God has affirmed double reward in several matters. Such as what?

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** No. ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54]. And the Prophet ﷺ informed that a man from the People of the Book who believes in his Book and then believes in Muhammad ﷺ, God will give him his reward twice.

Many scholars said, regarding the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid 57:28]: this is the reward of this *ummah*, which is doubled over other nations. The important point is that God's bounty is vast; He may reward the doer twice for some reason.

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** That is in the hadith.

**Student:** (...).

**The Shaykh:** It is the one we recited: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them. (54) And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54–55].

He says: ﴿And We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾. ﴿We have prepared﴾ means We have readied for her. ﴿Provision﴾ means gift. ﴿Noble﴾ means good and abundant, because nobility (*karam*) differs in each context according to what suits it. So a "noble" (*karīmah*) ewe means one that is good, beautiful, and abundant in milk, as in the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Beware of the noble (*karā'im*) of their property." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1496) and Muslim (19/29), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.] Here, the "noble provision" means abundant, good, and beautiful gift. This happens, as the author says: (in Paradise, an increase).

Then God, exalted is He, said (...).

* From it is derived: the obligation for the Prophet ﷺ to give his wives a choice; from His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾.
* And among its benefits: God's protection of His Messenger and His defense of him, in that He commanded him to give his wives this choice when they constricted him and asked him for maintenance.
* And among its benefits: the virtues of the Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, since they chose God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode.
* And among its benefits: the perfection of the character of the Prophet ﷺ, in that God commanded him to say: ﴿If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release﴾. The situation would have called for them to be rebuked and reproached for this, but it was said: ﴿Come, I will provide for you and release you﴾.
* And among its benefits: the permissibility for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to be married to others if they chose the worldly life and its adornment; from His saying: ﴿and release you in a fair release﴾.
* And among the benefits of the following noble verse, ﴿And if you desire God and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾: that desiring God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode is a form of excellence (*ihsan*); from His saying: ﴿Indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that intention has a great effect in increasing reward, since He attached this reward to this desire and good intention.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over﴾.

* From this noble verse is derived: that the sin of those near (to God) is more severe than the sin of others. From where is this taken? From God's saying: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over﴾.
* And among its benefits: the protection of the Prophet's ﷺ marital bed in full, since when a woman among his wives commits a clear immorality, God doubles her punishment. All of this is for the sake of protecting the Prophet's ﷺ marital bed, whether we say that "immorality" means fornication or means foul speech of the tongue.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that God, mighty and majestic, has the right to do what He wills in doubling reward and punishment, and that this matter is easy for Him; from His saying: ﴿And that is ever easy for God﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾.

* From this noble verse is derived: a great distinction for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, since if a woman among them did a righteous deed and obeyed God and His Messenger, God gave her reward twice.
* And from it: the justice of God, exalted is He, His perfect justice. Since her punishment was doubled, her reward and recompense are doubled too. For this reason He said: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her﴾ and His saying: ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾.
* And among its benefits also: that God has prepared for these believing women among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ a noble reward, that is, abundant, beautiful, and good, ﴿We will give her her reward twice and We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾.

As for the discussion of the noble verses, we begin with it too, and we continue with you in these lessons.

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, if you desire﴾: where is the object of the saying in His words: ﴿say to your wives﴾? (...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 32:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women, if you are mindful of God.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾: the address here, which Allah directed to His Messenger, He then directed to his wives, saying ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾. This, after the choice (given to them), indicates that the marital bond with the wives of the Prophet ﷺ was firmly established. For this reason He addressed them with His words ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women﴾. Here ﴿lastunna﴾ originally was: laysa, but when the sin was made sukoon, the yā' was deleted, because it is a soft letter (ḥarf līn), and a soft letter is deleted when two sukūns meet, as Ibn Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Kāfiyah:

"If two sukūns meet, vowel the one before; and if it is soft, its deletion is deserved."

﴿You are not like anyone﴾ means that the wives of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, are not like anyone. The author says: (like a group of women).

And his saying: (like a group of women) is open to question, because (anyone) (aḥad) applies to an individual; that is, there is no one among women like you.

﴿You are not like anyone among women﴾ means: you do not resemble any one woman or more among women. And his saying ﴿among women﴾ means: other than you.

(﴿If you are mindful of God﴾) — that is, you are not like anyone among women if you are mindful. This is what is meant by the condition: an exhortation and encouragement to piety. That is, if you are truly mindful of God, then do not compare yourselves to others, for you are not like anyone among women. Why? Because of the distinction they have in their connection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Thus it was incumbent upon them to guard his bed more than others are obliged to guard the beds of their husbands, why? Because of the greatness of the right of the Prophet ﷺ and the loftiness of his rank.

So his saying ﴿if you are mindful﴾: the condition here is meant as an exhortation and encouragement to the piety of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that they do not compare themselves with others. The difference between the bed of the Prophet ﷺ and the bed of anyone else is great. For this reason, whoever accuses one of the wives of the Messenger ﷺ of adultery becomes a disbeliever, whereas whoever accuses the wife of someone else does not become a disbeliever, because accusing a wife of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, means disparaging the Messenger ﷺ and suggesting that he—may Allah protect us—is corrupt. Allah says: ﴿Corrupt women are for corrupt men, and corrupt men are for corrupt women﴾ [al-Nur 24:26].

Accordingly, guarding the bed of the Prophet ﷺ is more obligatory than guarding the bed of anyone else. For this reason He said: ﴿You are not like anyone among women, if you are mindful.﴾

(﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾) to men. ﴿Do not be soft in speech﴾: submissiveness (khuḍūʿ) means humbling oneself, abasement and servility. So the meaning is: do not humble yourselves, do not abase yourselves, and do not be servile to any man in speech; that is, your speech when addressing men should not be tender, submissive, or gentle. Why? Because woman is a temptation, and if she speaks submissively, Satan creeps in between her and the man she is addressing.

Whatever a person's nobility and integrity, if a woman addresses him in a submissive voice she may deceive him. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the intellect of a resolute man more than one of you." [Reported by al-Bukhari (304) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, whose wording is: "I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the intellect of a resolute man more than one of you."] The resolute, discerning, astute man—no one takes away his intellect, that is, his reason, as a woman does. For this reason He said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾. Rather, a woman must, when addressing men, be as far as possible from submissiveness in speech, from softness and playful tenderness, such that it does not lead to this grave matter, which is His saying: ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾. ﴿Feel desire﴾ for what? He desires you, either by committing an indecency, or by enjoying and taking pleasure in your speech. A person in whose heart is a disease, if a woman speaks to him submissively, will continue conversing with her until Satan entices him, and perhaps afterward there will be an appointment, a meeting, and an indecency, as many foolish people do now. You find—may Allah protect us—especially since the appearance of these phones, that he opens—for example—any number that comes up, and when a woman addresses him, he begins speaking with soft, submissive words until Satan entices him, entices him toward her and her toward him. For this reason He said: ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾. The author said: (hypocrisy).

The correct view is that the disease meant here is the disease of lust and enjoyment, not the disease of hypocrisy; for some hypocrites may not have this feeling in their souls, just as some believers may have it in their hearts. So the disease meant here is the disease of delight in and pleasure from a woman's voice: ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾.

﴿And speak a good word﴾: ﴿qulna﴾ is a past-tense verb built on sukūn because it is attached to the moving pronoun of the feminine plural. Is that right? Because it is attached to the feminine plural nūn, which is a moving subject pronoun, there is no contradiction. What do you say?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: An imperative verb? Yes, an imperative verb, not a past verb. Although if you said: "The women said such and such," it would be a past verb. But when you direct the command to them and say: "qulna qawlan ma'rūfan"—when He forbade them from submissiveness in speech, He commanded them to say a good word, so that no one would suppose that a woman may not address a man at all. That is not so; a woman's addressing men is permissible, but with a good word.

(﴿And speak a good word﴾) without submissiveness.

What is meant by "good" (ma'rūf)? Is it what is customary among people in addressing men and women, or is it what is not reprehensible?

The latter is meant; for if we said the first, namely what people customarily use in speech between men and women, that would be subject to differing customs. For example, among some people the custom is that a woman addresses a man, smiles at him and jokes with him, as is now found, unfortunately, in many lands of the Muslims: a woman stands with a foreign man she does not know, jokes with him and laughs, as if she were addressing her husband—may Allah protect us. This is without doubt forbidden, and an invitation to immorality.

So what is meant by "good" is what is not reprehensible, that is, what the Law recognizes and approves of speech that is far from submissiveness in speech and from enjoying and delighting in it.

His saying ﴿And speak a good word﴾: ﴿qawlan﴾ is a verbal noun, and ﴿ma'rūfan﴾ is its qualifier; it specifies the type of this speech, that it is good speech, not reprehensible speech.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No. If we say: what the Law approves, that suffices, because the Law approves everything people customarily do that does not contradict it. "Good" is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:110].

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: If we say: the good word is what the Law approves and recognizes, that suffices; this is clearer.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No. If he is connected with her, let him say: "as-salāmu ʿalaykum."

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, no, that is not good.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Nor should he say: "Peace upon those who follow guidance."

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, he says: "as-salāmu ʿalaykum," and there is nothing wrong with it. But he should not say "Alo," because "Alo" is the greeting of the Christians, although unfortunately it is now widespread; even people of knowledge and learning say "Alo" to you.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, it is the one who speaks.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, it is not required, unless (...).

﴿If you are mindful﴾: what is the benefit of the condition here? (...)

Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women, if you are mindful of God.﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the distinction and special status of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, from His saying ﴿you are not like anyone among women﴾. If you say: what is the wisdom in their not being like anyone among women?

The answer: because they are wed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the best of the best of creation, and Allah Almighty said: ﴿Good women are for good men﴾ [al-Nur 24:26].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may be ennobled by the nobility of the one he is connected to. From where is this taken? From the nobility of the Mothers of the Believers through their connection to the Messenger ﷺ. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ urged keeping company with the righteous companion and said: "The example of the righteous companion and the bad one is like the bearer of musk and the blower of the bellows. The bearer of musk either gives you some, or you buy from him, or you find a pleasant fragrance from him; the blower of the bellows either burns your clothes, or you find a foul smell from him." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534) and Muslim (2628/146) from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, whose wording is: "The likeness of the good and the bad companion is like the bearer of musk and the blower of the bellows..."] He warned against the bad companion, because a person without doubt is ennobled by the nobility of the one he is connected to, and is brought down by the lowliness of the one he is connected to.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of piety even upon the wives of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, from His saying ﴿if you are mindful﴾.

* Among its benefits: the prohibition of a woman's submissiveness in addressing men, from His saying ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾. If you say: could this not be specific to the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, because of their standing and nobility, so that they keep far from places of temptation? If you say this, what is the answer?

The answer: if the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who are the purest of women and the furthest from temptation, are forbidden from submissiveness in speech, with the prohibition explained by the fear of the desire of the one in whose heart is a disease, then the ruling revolves around its cause, existing or absent. If this applies to the pure and cleared women, then others are even more so. And if the cause is the fear of desire from one in whose heart is a disease, this cause is not specific to the wives of the Messenger ﷺ. Accordingly, it is forbidden for a woman to be submissive in speech to anyone at all, except her unmarriageable male relatives (maḥārim), provided there is also safety from temptation—that is, even the unmarriageable relatives—"Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3281) and Muslim (2175/24) from the hadith of Safiyyah bint Huyayy, may Allah be pleased with her].

Perhaps with her submissiveness in speech temptation may occur, especially with unmarriageable relatives through nursing and marriage, because the natural aversion toward unmarriageable relatives through nursing and marriage is less than the aversion toward unmarriageable relatives through blood kinship; this is an observed matter. For this reason one must guard against unmarriageable relatives through nursing and marriage more than guard against those related by blood.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: In any case, whenever there is kinship, a person becomes more averse to attaching himself to her with lustful attachment; he becomes more averse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no harm in a woman addressing men, but with what is good, from where is this taken? From His saying ﴿And speak a good word﴾.

* Among its benefits: that a woman's voice is not an awrah, contrary to those scholars who said it is an awrah. The correct view is that a woman's voice is not an awrah. For this reason women used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him questions while his companions were around him, and he did not forbid them. Had a woman's voice been an awrah, the Prophet ﷺ would have forbidden them from speaking in the presence of men.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory for a person to follow what the Law has brought in his words and actions; from His saying ﴿And speak a good word﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the temptation of women is a disease of the heart which a person needs to treat and remedy; from His saying ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾. This disease is a deadly one, which we ask Allah to save us from: a disease of the heart like cancer in the body. If Allah does not overtake the servant with His pardon, guidance and steadfastness, he will perish. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I have left after me no trial more harmful to men than women" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5096) and Muslim (2741/98) from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both]. So it is obligatory to beware of this matter and not to indulge oneself or give it respite in this domain.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever has a sound heart is furthest from places of temptation; from His saying ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾.

* Among its benefits: whoever Allah has made sound of heart, a woman will not entice him by the causes of temptation she employs, because He said: ﴿do not be soft in speech, lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾, and He did not say: "lest people desire you," but rather: ﴿lest the one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire﴾. Yet even if a person is sound-hearted and whole, if he senses in himself something of temptation, it is obligatory for him to keep away from it. He should not say: "I am sound, I am, praise be to Allah, not concerned with this matter." No, he should not say this, for a person may see himself fortified with the fortress of piety, yet Satan deceives him at places of temptation.

For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded whoever hears of the Dajjal to keep away from him, that is, to distance himself, for a person may come to him thinking himself a believer, and he keeps casting doubts at him until he follows him [Abu Dawud (4319) related with his chain from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever hears of the Dajjal, let him keep away from him, for by Allah, a man may come to him thinking himself a believer, and then follow him, because of the doubts he casts," or "because of the doubts he casts."]

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And stay﴾ with a kasra (on the qaf), and for this reason he said: (with a kasra or a fatha on the qaf). It derives from *al-qarar* (settling), which is remaining in a state of stillness and settledness. It is more emphatic than the phrase "remain in your houses," because *al-qarar* means remaining with an added stillness. For this reason he said: (﴿And stay in your houses﴾ is from *al-qarar*). Its origin is *iqrirna* (or *iqrarna*), with a kasra or fatha on the ra, from *qararta* (with a fatha or kasra on the ra: *qararta* or *qarirta*). The vowel of the ra was transferred to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl was dropped.

The origin of ﴿qarna﴾ is *iqraran* or *iqriran*. So what happened? The fatha of the ra was transferred to the quiescent qaf. Then, when its vowel was transferred to the quiescent qaf, the qaf became vowelled, and the qaf became either fatha or kasra. Then the hamzat al-wasl was dropped, and it became ﴿waqarna﴾.

﴿And stay in your houses﴾: the *idafa* (possessive construction) in ﴿your houses﴾ may be for ownership (*tamlik*), meaning the houses of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ belong to them. It may also be for specification (*ikhtisas*), meaning the houses belong to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Which is closer? The closer view is that it is for ownership, as evidenced by the fact that when the Prophet ﷺ died, these houses remained for whom? For his wives. Had the houses belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they would not have been inherited after him, because the Prophets are not inherited from, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity." Teach me if I err in the wording: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is *sadaqah*" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6727) and Muslim (1758/15), from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. "*sadaqatun*" (with a damma), yes, because otherwise the meaning is corrupted. The Rafidah say the wording of the hadith is: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is *sadaqatan*" (with a fatha), why? So that they may say: what they leave that is not charity is inherited, and that Abu Bakr, 'Umar and the rest of the Companions wronged the heirs of the Prophet ﷺ by not passing it on to them. But Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah say: You have lied, O Rafidah. Rather, the wording of the hadith is: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from," the sentence ends in the first clause, then he explained what becomes of the wealth after him, saying: "What we leave is *sadaqatun*," meaning: what we leave is charity.

The meaning the Rafidah adopt is false, because what is left as charity is not inherited even for non-Prophets, is it not so? That is, what a person leaves as charity after his death is not inherited by his heirs, even if he is not a Prophet. So they distort the hadith both in wording and in meaning.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: They say: "We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity," meaning: what we leave as charity is not inherited. For example, if we endow something and make it for the cause of Allah, we are not inherited from regarding that thing; rather, other properties are inherited. Is this specific to the messengers? No, it is not specific to them. So we say: his saying ﴿in your houses﴾, the closer view is that the *idafa* is for ownership.

﴿And do not display yourselves⁠ ﴾ (with one of the two *ta*'s omitted from the original): ﴿tabarrajna﴾. Is it a present (imperfect) verb or a past verb?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is the evidence?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The evidence is the prohibitive *la*. The prohibitive *la* only enters on the imperfect. Otherwise, the word *tabarraja* and "the women displayed themselves" is a past verb, but in the verse ﴿wa la tabarrajna﴾ it is an imperfect verb. The author says: (with one of the two *ta*'s omitted), and its original form is *tatabarrajna*. The omission of one of the two *ta*'s in the imperfect is common in the Qur'an, and among its examples is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So I have warned you of a fire that blazes﴾ [al-Layl 14], meaning *tatalaza*.

So ﴿la tabarrajna﴾ is an imperfect verb built on sukun because it is attached to the feminine plural nun, in a position of jazm (apocope) with the prohibitive *la*.

﴿la tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula﴾ (meaning: before Islam).

﴿la tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula﴾: *tabarruj* originally derives from elevation and exaltation, and from it comes *al-burj*, the strong and lofty fortress, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built high﴾ [al-Nisa 78], and as in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky great stars﴾ [al-Furqan 61], meaning He placed in it great masses of stars like lofty towers.

He says: ﴿wa la tabarrajna⁠﴾ meaning: do not exalt and elevate yourselves through clothing and other things. His saying ﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula⁠﴾ is a verbal noun (*masdar*) clarifying the type, by its attribution to *al-jahiliyyah*. He says ﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾, and it is known that the verbal noun may be for counting, for specifying the type, for emphasis, and other things mentioned by the scholars of grammar.

﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾ is attributed to *al-jahiliyyah* because it is built on ignorance and foolishness, since when a woman displays herself, that is regarded as ignorance and foolishness on her part. For this reason it is attributed to ﴿al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾, then attributed to ﴿al-ula⁠﴾. Does *al-ula* mean first in time, or first in rank, or both? That is, does the meaning of ﴿al-jahiliyyah al-ula⁠﴾ mean the greatest in ignorance of its kind, as one says: "This is the first in ignorance, this is the first in foolishness, this is the first in Islam, this is the first in reform," and similar? Or does *al-ula* mean first in time? Or both? Both in fact: it is a jahiliyyah of the first class of ignorance, and it is a first jahiliyyah because it preceded Islam. It does not mean that it is the jahiliyyah immediately preceding Islam, because the jahiliyyah immediately preceding Islam was an extension of a jahiliyyah that had preceded it long before. The first jahiliyyah continued until Islam erased it through knowledge and piety, and praise be to Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula⁠﴾.

The purpose of the attribution here, as I said a moment ago, is to specify the type, and how evil is a type that is ignorance. Accordingly, its purpose is denunciation: denouncing this *tabarruj*, and that it is a display built on ignorance and foolishness, and distance from faith, knowledge and right guidance.

(﴿And do not display yourselves as the displaying of the former times of ignorance⁠﴾: meaning, what preceded Islam, of women showing their adornments to men.)

In the jahiliyyah, a woman would display herself and go out in the finest clothing and jewellery she had. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]. So *tabarruj* occurs through the type of clothing, through perfume, through beautifying the body with henna and reddening, blackening the eyes with kohl, and what is called in our present time makeup, and what is called the most reprehensible of reprehensible things. Judge by this analogy: all of this is from the *tabarruj* of the first jahiliyyah.

For this reason he says: (from women showing their beauty to men; and showing after Islam is mentioned in the verse ﴿And do not expose their adornment except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]). May Allah have mercy on the author, for this is not correct of him. In Islam there is no display of adornment at all except in two types:

The first type: general display to everyone.

The second type: specific display to husbands and close relatives (*mahram*).

General display: ﴿except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾. What is meant by ﴿what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ is what custom has made unavoidable to appear, such as the outer garment (*jilbab*) and the cloak (*'abaya*) and similar, as Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, explained it. Accordingly, the exception in His saying ﴿except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*), not a connected one, because what appears is not in reality part of the adornment. What appears and what custom makes unavoidable to appear is something that is not truly adornment, even if it is called adornment and clothing, since it must appear. As for the other adornment that Allah specified for particular people, He said: ﴿And do not expose their adornment except to their husbands or their fathers⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]. This is the hidden adornment, such as the garments beneath the outer garment and cloak and similar. They may not expose it except to their husbands or fathers, and so on to the end. In sum, Allah has never permitted *tabarruj*; the prohibition of it is general.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, beautifying oneself for the husband is a desirable matter. That is, that a woman adorn herself for her husband, because in this is the affirmation of the wisdom for which marriage was legislated, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And of His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy⁠﴾ [al-Rum 21]. There is no doubt that when a woman adorns herself for her husband with all kinds of beauty, that is among what causes him to find tranquility in her and to feel affection for her, so this is from the affirmation of the wisdom for which marriage was legislated. For this reason a woman is commanded to adorn herself for her husband, just as the husband is also commanded, as some of the early generation (*salaf*) said: "Among her rights over me is that I adorn myself for her, just as among my rights over her is that she adorn herself for me" [[Ibn Abi Shaybah (19263) with his chain from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "I love to adorn myself for a woman just as I love a woman to adorn herself for me, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And due to them is similar to what is expected of them, according to what is reasonable⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 228], and I do not love to exhaust all my rights over her, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But the men have a degree over them⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 228]."]].

As for a husband who comes to his wife dressed in rough sackcloth and the like, and wants her to be pleasing to him, and says: "Why do you not adorn yourself for me?" while he wears the worst clothing, this is not just. A person must observe justice in all his dealings.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, roughness in certain situations: when he rides a horse, let him be rough and wear coarse cloth (...). But with a woman, no; every situation has its own speech.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We have not gone beyond a third (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning of the hadith.

﴿And establish prayer⁠﴾: perform it correctly, meaning by doing its conditions, pillars and obligations, and what else? And its recommended acts. The performance of the first three is obligatory, and of the fourth is for completeness and recommendation.

His saying ﴿establish prayer⁠﴾ includes the obligatory and the voluntary prayer. ﴿And give zakah⁠﴾: meaning give it. *Zakah* linguistically means growth and increase, and in the Sharia it is a specified, determined amount of a specified property, meaning a portion of specified wealth given to those entitled to it.

His saying ﴿give zakah⁠﴾: ﴿ataya⁠﴾ takes two objects, as it is of the pattern of *kasa* and *a'ta* (to clothe and to give). The first object is ﴿al-zakah⁠﴾, and the second object is omitted, meaning *mustahiqqaha* (its rightful recipients): give zakah to its rightful recipients, because giving zakah to other than its people is of no benefit, just as if a person prays outside its time.

His saying ﴿give zakah⁠﴾ after the command to establish prayer contains evidence for the emphasis on zakah. Does it necessarily follow that the Mothers of the Believers had property on which to pay zakah? It does not necessarily follow. If we say it does not follow, then directing the address to them to give zakah becomes a matter of wording, because they would say: "We have no property." Or it is said: they were commanded to give zakah either by undertaking it if they had nothing, or by actually giving if they had something. There is no doubt that they had something on which zakah is due, or some of them had jewellery, as in the hadith of Umm Salamah that she used to wear golden *awdah* (ornaments), and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it a treasure?" He said: "When you pay its zakah, it is not a treasure" [[Abu Dawud (1564) from Umm Salamah, who said: "I used to wear golden *awdah*, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, is it a treasure? He said: 'Whatever reaches the amount whose zakah is paid, and its zakah is paid, is not a treasure.'"]]. So they had something with which to pay zakah; it may not be dirhams and dinars, but it is jewellery.

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾: ﴿obey Allah⁠﴾. The scholars said that obedience (*ta'ah*) is conforming to the command. This is obedience, meaning not disobeying, complying with the command of the one obeyed if it is required in action, and if it is forbidden, by abstaining.

His saying ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾ conjoins obedience to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to obedience to Allah with the conjunction *wa*, because obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah⁠﴾ [al-Nisa 80]. We have previously mentioned many times that in legislative matters it is permissible to join Allah and the Messenger ﷺ together, because what the Prophet ﷺ brought of legislative matters is what Allah commanded.

His saying ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾: is obedience here the obedience of worship, or is it meant as non-opposition? As for obedience to Allah, it is the obedience of worship and humility, hoping for reward and fearing punishment. As for obedience to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, it is obedience in the sense of conforming to the command, whether it is in what he commands from the Sharia or in what he commands concerning his own particular needs. The Messenger ﷺ directs commands to his family either as acts of worship that Allah commanded him, or as particular matters connected to him, peace and blessings be upon him.

(﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: sin, O ﴿people of the household⁠﴾, meaning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿and purify you⁠﴾ from it ﴿with [complete] purification⁠﴾).

﴿Allah only intends to remove⁠﴾: ﴿innama⁠﴾ is a particle of restriction (*hasr*). The scholars say that restriction means affirming the ruling for what is mentioned and negating it for what is other than it. Is the restriction here relative (*idafi*) or real (*haqiqi*)? Relative. Real? Or relative and real, or neither relative nor real? The division is fourfold: either relative, or real, or both, or neither.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Relative. Why?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Because Allah wills this and other things. The relative restriction is one where the thing is not restricted to it in reality, and the real restriction is one where the thing is restricted to it in reality. So if you say: "No student pays attention except Khalid," what happens? Is it real or relative? Let us see: if there is no one else, it is real; if someone else pays attention, it is relative.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The benefit of the relative is that, for example, because this man pays so much attention, no one else pays attention. As if you say: "No one is brave except Khalid," meaning Khalid ibn al-Walid. "No one is brave except Khalid." What do you say? Real or relative?

* Student: (...).
