* Shaykh: No, it is not real, because there are many brave people other than Khalid ibn al-Walid. "There is no seal of the Prophets except Muhammad ﷺ": this is real, because there is no seal of the Prophets except Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. Is it clear?

Here, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intend for the people of the House only that?

The answer: No. Allah intends to remove impurity from them and purify them, and to bestow blessings upon them, and to lavish favour upon them, and so on.

His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: is the will here legislative (*shar'iyyah*) or cosmic (*kawniyyah*)? The will is cosmic, and this is the benefit of the specification of the People of the House with this. As for the will for the absence of impurity, it is for everyone from the legislative standpoint. And the will, as we have previously mentioned, is of two kinds: legislative will and cosmic will. Are they necessarily linked? No: one may exist without the other, and they may coincide. What is the difference between them, so that we know their coincidence and divergence?

First: cosmic will relates to what Allah loves and to what He does not love. Second: legislative will relates only to what Allah loves. So when you say ﴿wills⁠﴾, meaning legislatively, its meaning is "loves."

Second: in cosmic will, the willed thing necessarily occurs; in legislative will, the willed thing does not necessarily occur.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 33–34 (part 2 of 4):

So the distinction is from two angles. Now we consider: the two wills (al-iradatan) may be combined in one thing, may both be absent, or one may exist without the other.

If we ask the brother: What do you say about the faith of Abu Bakr? Is it willed by Allah legally (shar'an) or universally (kawnan)?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Universally and legally? Universally, because it occurred; legally, because Allah loves it. So the two wills have combined. What do you say about the faith of Abu Lahab?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed, neither universally nor legally?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed universally.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And willed legally? What do you say? Correct. Yes, willed legally: Allah wills that he become Muslim.
What do you say about the disbelief of Abu Bakr?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed either universally or legally. Correct. Not willed universally, because it did not occur; and not willed legally, because Allah does not love it.
And what does the brother say about the disbelief of Abu Lahab?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Willed universally but not legally, because Allah does not love it. Correct?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, what Allah willed is what happened, which is why he did not believe.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Known. Disbelief is willed by Allah universally; any person who disbelieves, Allah has willed his disbelief universally.

We want examples from the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. Brother, which of the two wills is this verse about?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Universal or legal? Has hardship not befallen people?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: You retracted from the universal? Universal-legal: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. You say this will is universal?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Legal-universal, is that so?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Legal. What is the evidence? Because Allah the Exalted may cause hardship for a person, is that not so? And if it were a universal will, it would in reality be a denial of the verse. So here ﴿yurid﴾ (intends) means yuhibb (loves): Allah loves ease for you and does not love hardship. As for universally, Allah the Exalted does will hardship for us. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship is ease﴾ [al-Sharh 5].

Allah, blessed and exalted, said concerning Hud: ﴿And my advice will not benefit you, if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you﴾ [Hud 34].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Correct? ﴿If Allah intends to mislead you﴾ — is this a universal will, or not? Because Allah does not will misguidance for His creation.
The evidence that He does not will misguidance is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa' 176], and ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ [al-Nisa' 26]. Who is Hud? Nuh? So this is the saying of Nuh, peace be upon him, to his people. May Allah bless you.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾. The lam here presents a difficulty: "yurid li-kadha" (intends for such-and-such). It is well known that (arada) transitively takes its object directly. Here it is transitive by what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: You don't know? But you are confused today. The lam here came in the object of ﴿yurid﴾, and it is well known that (yurid) is transitive directly or by the lam? You say: aradtu kadha (I intended such-and-such), or aradtu li-kadha? You say: aradtu kadha. Therefore the lam here is superfluous; grammatically it is superfluous, and the estimate is: "innama yurid Allah an yudhhiba 'ankumu al-rijs" (Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity). The grammarians say the lam is superfluous.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity﴾, the author says: (sin). The correct view is that rijs is impurity, because rijs originally means what is impure, whether it is an impurity of meaning or a physical impurity. From rijs in the sense of physical impurity is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, except that it be dead meat, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is rijs﴾ [al-An'am 145]. He said ﴿for indeed it is rijs﴾: is this physical or of meaning? This is physical.
And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are rijs from the work of Satan﴾ [al-Ma'idah 90]. This is rijs of meaning. Here, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the rijs﴾: which of the two kinds, physical or of meaning? Of meaning, of course, because physical rijs is not something Allah willed to remove from them; rather it is present in them. They urinate and defecate, and their urine is impure and their excrement is impure, is that not so? Therefore the rijs that Allah willed to remove from the People of the House is the rijs of meaning, which is base morals and deeds. This is the rijs. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So avoid the rijs of idols﴾ [al-Hajj 30]. Here the rijs is what: of meaning or physical? Of meaning. ﴿So avoid the rijs of idols﴾. So every base character or deed is of rijs.

As for His saying: ﴿ahl al-bayt (People of the House)﴾, the author has informed us, by his saying "O People of the House," that ﴿ahl﴾ is in the accusative by way of address, and the particle of address (ya) has been omitted from it. As for his saying "O People of the House," who is meant by the People of the House? There is no doubt that what is meant is the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, because all the verses are in the context of whom? In the context of the women, the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech (32). And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with thorough purification (33). And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 32–34].
So there is no doubt that what is meant by this is whom? It is the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him. Does this contradict what was established from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he "placed a cloak over 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and said: 'These are the People of the House. O Allah, remove from them the rijs and purify them with thorough purification.'"[[Al-Tirmidhi (3205) narrated with his chain from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, the stepson of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab 33], in the house of Umm Salamah, he called Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and covered them with a cloak, and 'Ali was behind his back, so he covered him with a cloak. Then he said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with thorough purification." Umm Salamah said: "And I am with them, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "You are in your place, and you are upon good."]], does it contradict it?
We say: it does not contradict it, because these are the People of the House by kinship, and those are the People of the House by marriage, so all of them are People of the House without doubt. Not only the family of 'Ali; rather the People of the House are more general than these four, because the People of the House include everyone for whom charity is forbidden from the Banu Hashim. So included among them are the family of 'Ali, the family of Ja'far, the family of al-'Abbas, the family of al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and every descendant of Hashim. The Messenger ﷺ is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. So everyone from the family of Hashim is of the People of the House, for whom charity is not lawful.
Accordingly we say: our interpretation of "People of the House" here, that they are the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, is determined by what? By the context. This is contrary to the Rafidah, who took the speech out of its context and made the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, into scattered fragments ('idin), saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity﴾ means only the four People of the House, while the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, are not included in Allah's will to remove impurity from them. For this reason they slander 'A'ishah with immorality—may Allah protect us—and do not care about that.
I say: His saying ﴿ahl al-bayt﴾ here, and regarding the four people of the cloak, and regarding the People of the House for whom charity is unlawful, all of this does not contradict one another. For this reason the preponderant view is that the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, are not permitted to receive charity, based on the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "Indeed charity is not lawful for the family of Muhammad"[[Abu Dawud (2985) narrated it from the hadith of al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Indeed this charity is only the filth of people, and it is not lawful for Muhammad, nor for the family of Muhammad," the hadith.]], and his wives are without doubt from his family, as in this hadith.
Accordingly we say: there is no contradiction between the evidences. A parallel to this is that the Messenger ﷺ was asked: "Which is the mosque founded upon piety from the first day?" He said: "This mosque of mine"[[Al-Tirmidhi (2099) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety from the first day. One man said: It is the mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is this mosque of mine."]], although the mosque founded upon piety from the first day is also the mosque of Quba. Each of them was founded upon piety from the first day: the Messenger, peace be upon him, founded his mosque from the first day he arrived, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, each of them was saying: "Stay with me, stay with me, stay with me," and he said: "Leave her, for she is commanded"[[Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan (2978) from the hadith of Siddiq ibn Musa, as a mursal report.]]—meaning his she-camel. When she reached the place of his mosque, she knelt down, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, urged her on, and she stood up, then turned right and left, then returned to her first place and knelt down. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The dwelling place is here, if Allah wills"[[Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat (134) narrated it from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Then he dismounted, and the nearest house to him was the house of Abu Ayyub, so he went to it.
From the first day he arrived, he was engaged in laying out the mosque. For this reason, those responsible in the municipalities and the endowments should make their greatest concern in new layouts the placement of mosques, to be attended to before anything else.
In any case, I say: describing one thing with a attribute and describing another with an attribute does not necessitate that this is a contradiction; rather each of them has a share of this description.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: I don't know.
And his saying—let us complete the verse—﴿the House﴾: here "al" in "al-bayt" is for prior reference (al-'ahd). Which references? Mental (dhihni), meaning the known, familiar People of the House, namely this pure house, the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: ﴿and purify you﴾ from it, i.e., from the rijs, ﴿with thorough purification﴾. Here ﴿tathir﴾ (purification) is a verbal noun of (tahhara), a verbal noun of the preceding verb, and it is meant for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 164]. Purification from rijs is more emphatic than the departure of rijs, because after the departure of rijs some trace may remain.
So when He says "He removes it and purifies you," that becomes what? More emphatic, because it removes that rijs and purifies its place such that no trace remains. There is no doubt that the house of the Messenger, peace be upon him, is the farthest of houses from rijs and the purest of houses from rijs. No believer ever doubts this. Whoever casts aspersions on the house of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his wives, is considered to be casting aspersions on whom? On the Messenger, peace be upon him, because Allah says in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women; and good women for good men, and good men for good women﴾ [al-Nur 26]. We know with certain knowledge that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would not choose for His Prophet except the best women of the worlds, without doubt. It has been established from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and it has been established in the Book of Allah that 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, is innocent of what the people of the slander, the hypocrites and others among the Muslims who were deceived, accused her of—may Allah pardon them. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said concerning this very slander: ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it was trivial while it was, with Allah, tremendous (15). And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this; exalted are You [O Allah]; this is a great slander"﴾ [al-Nur 15–16]. That is: why did you not say? "It is not for us"—"ma yakunu" means it is absolutely impossible, "an natakallama bihadha" (that we speak of this). "Subhanaka" (Exalted are You) is declaring You free of imperfection: "We declare You free, O our Lord, that such a thing should occur in one of the mothers of the believers, the wives of the seal of the Prophets." For this reason He said "Subhanaka," meaning: we declare You free that such a thing should occur among the wives of Your Prophet, peace be upon him.
This great emphasis we see now from those who ascribe themselves to Islam while they are free of it and Islam is free of them. They say that 'A'ishah—may Allah protect us—committed adultery, although Allah has already cleared her of that in the Noble Qur'an. Whoever slanders one of the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, 'A'ishah or others, is without doubt a disbeliever, and he must be killed even if he repents. If he repents sincerely, his matter is between him and Allah; but we must be jealous for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we must kill whoever slanders anyone or any one of the mothers of the believers. (...).
﴿...your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34].
The saying of the Exalted was mentioned earlier: ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, and we explained that ﴿give zakah﴾ — the verb takes the accusative? Brother.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Where are the first and second?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Is this the first or the second?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Implicit or elided?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. Fine, what is zakah?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Linguistically, growth. And technically?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No (...). Have you understood it now? A specified right in specified property for a specified group at a specified time. You have understood zakah now. Or we can say: worship of Allah the Exalted by giving out a known portion of wealth according to what the Shari'ah has brought. This is clearer.
Also in it is His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾: the lam in His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove﴾ (...).
﴿what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah﴾: the Qur'an. ﴿And wisdom﴾. ﴿Remember﴾: the imperative here is for guidance, and for explaining the favor and grace of Allah, glorified and exalted, upon them.
His saying ﴿remember﴾ may mean: reflect upon and ponder this matter, and recognize what grace of Allah is in it for you.
It may also mean: remember it by reciting it...
other than its covering, for the revelation did not descend upon the Messenger ﷺ in the wives' beds while he was under their covers except in the case of 'A'ishah[[Al-Bukhari (3775) narrated it from 'A'ishah.]].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 33–34 (part 3 of 4):

Allah's words: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾ [al-Ahzab 34]. ﴿Recited﴾ means ﴿read﴾. Tilawah (recitation) is of two kinds: verbal recitation (tilawah lafziyyah) and meaningful recitation (tilawah ma'nawiyyah). When you say, "He recited the Book of Allah until he finished it," the meaning is verbal recitation. When you say "sujud al-tilawah" (the prostration of recitation), what is meant? Verbal recitation. As for meaningful recitation, it is following the Qur'an. One says "talahu, yatluhu" when he follows something. So meaningful recitation means following the Qur'an in its creed, its morals, and its actions. Which of the two is the greater goal? The greater goal is meaningful recitation. Verbal recitation is undoubtedly intended, and whoever recites a letter from the Book has ten good deeds for it, but what matters most is meaningful recitation. Allah says: ﴿A blessed Book, which We have sent down to you, that they may reflect upon its verses and that people of understanding may take heed﴾ [Sad 29].

﴿...the verses of Allah﴾ undoubtedly refers to the Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, it is clear verses in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ [al-'Ankabut 49]. So "the verses of Allah" is the Qur'an. Here, "verses" refers to the legislated verses (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah), for the verses of Allah the Exalted are divided into two kinds:

Cosmic verses (ayat kawniyyah): these are what Allah has created and creates in this universe. All of it is a sign pointing to its Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, because of its wondrous craftsmanship and its wise, perfect order which contradicts nothing and clashes with nothing. For this reason Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor is there with Him any god. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overpowered others﴾ [al-Mu'minun 91]. If each god took away what he created, the universe would not be orderly, because each god would create as he wills. Furthermore, one of them must overpower the other, for if they opposed each other and neither could prevail over the other, they could not both be gods. And if one of them overcame the other, the defeated one could not be a god. In that case, the rational proof is that there must be one God alone, who is Allah the Exalted.

In short, cosmic verses are everything Allah creates in the universe. Legislated verses are what the messengers brought from revelation. They are called "verses" because they are signs pointing to the One who legislated them and sent them down, because they contain the ordering of benefits and the removal of harms. Indeed, the whole Shari'ah brings about benefit and reduces harm. For this reason, there is nothing that contains a predominant or pure benefit except that the Shari'ah has commanded it, and nothing that contains a pure or predominant harm except that the Shari'ah has forbidden it. However, some benefits we perceive with our minds, some harms we perceive with our minds, and some we do not perceive. Yet we know with certainty that the requirement of the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and one of His names is the All-Wise (al-Hakim), is that He cannot command except what contains benefit, whether pure or predominant, and cannot forbid except what contains harm, whether pure or predominant. For this reason, the books sent down from heaven were called "verses," because they are signs pointing to the One who legislated them, the Exalted, and to the One who sent them down. ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ [al-Nisa' 82]. They would not find discrepancy once or twice or thrice, but much discrepancy and much contradiction.

Here is a matter outside the topic that people have begun to do. They swear by the verses of Allah. One says: "By the verses of Allah, such and such did not happen," or "By the verses of Allah, I will certainly do such and such." What is your opinion about this oath?

There is detail. If he intends the cosmic verses, it is impermissible, because it is an oath by other than Allah, an oath by created things. If he intends the legislated verses, then it is an oath by the words of Allah, and swearing by the words of Allah is permissible, because the words of Allah are among His attributes. What is the usual intention of the common people when they swear this oath? In my opinion, it is mostly the legislated verses. They do not mean an oath by the verses of Allah as in an oath by the sun, the moon, the stars, the night, or the day. They do not swear by such things. When they swear by the verses of Allah, they mean the Qur'an. In that case, this oath is permissible based on the customary understanding of what is meant by it. But if we look at the wording itself, there must be detail.

* Student: Do the legislated verses include the Sunnah?
* Shaykh: Yes. But here He said ﴿and the wisdom﴾, so the author, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified it when he said: (﴿the wisdom﴾ is the Sunnah).
* Student: If he said: "By the verses of Allah (...)"?
* Shaykh: No, never. They only mean the Qur'an. They do not call the Sunnah "verses."
* Student: When we say ﴿yutla﴾ means ﴿yuqra'﴾ (is read)?
* Shaykh: Is read.
* Student: Yes, is read. How can recitation be meaningful?
* Shaykh: No. Here, meaningful recitation does not apply. Verbal recitation is meant here. But we divided recitation in general terms.
* Student: Is recitation not the same as reading?
* Shaykh: When it is said: ﴿Those who recite the Book of Allah﴾ [Fatir 29], and ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it should be recited﴾ [al-Baqarah 121], it includes both this and that, verbal and meaningful. But here, what is apparent is only the verbal.

He said: ﴿...of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: The mushaf?
* Student: Surat Bara'ah.
* Shaykh: Surat Bara'ah?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Why do they specify this surah?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But why do they specify this surah?
* Student: Because it is intimidating (murhibah).
* Shaykh: Intimidating, terrifying. ﴿Woe that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat 15]. Al-Mursalat.

In any case, swearing by the mushaf is an innovation (bid'ah), because it was not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ). What has been reported regarding the intensification of oaths is what Allah mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿The two shall swear by Allah, if you doubt them: "We will not sell this for any price, even if it were a relative"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 106]. His words ﴿you detain them﴾ come before it: ﴿you detain them after the prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer. It will come, Allah willing, in the chapter on claims that intensification can be by time, by place, by manner, and by wording.

﴿And the wisdom﴾: the author said: (it is the Sunnah), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Nisa' 113], and He said: ﴿And He purifies them and teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. The basic principle in conjunction is that the two are different. Otherwise, one could say that the noble Qur'an contains wisdom, so teaching the Qur'an is teaching the rulings and teaching the wisdom behind the rulings, because knowing the rulings of the Shari'ah is a very great matter. When a person knows the wisdom behind the legal rulings, his heart becomes more illuminated, he becomes more convinced of the legal rulings, and he knows more of the attributes and wisdoms of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. He can also convince the opponent. For if you tell an opponent, for example, "This is forbidden because the Qur'an forbade it," he may not believe in the Qur'an or feel reassured by it. But if you have knowledge of the wisdoms of the Shari'ah, you can convince that person. Therefore, knowing the wisdom of the Shari'ah is very important. Indeed, most qiyas (analogical reasoning) comes from knowing the wisdom, because it is attaching a branch to a root in a ruling because of a common cause ('illah jami'ah). Accordingly, someone might say that the intended meaning of wisdom is what is known of the secrets and wisdoms of the Shari'ah rulings. But the scholars of the early and later generations, the imams of the later generations, explained wisdom as the Sunnah.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34].
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Knowing the ambiguous (mutashabih)?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know. I am not aware of this.
* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 269].
* Shaykh: I say: I do not know this. It is not that whenever wisdom is mentioned it means the Sunnah. Rather, when He says "the Book and the wisdom," ﴿He teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Baqarah 129], ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Nisa' 113], and ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾, it does not mean that whenever wisdom is mentioned it is the Sunnah.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾: ﴿Subtle﴾, the author said: (with His allies), ﴿Acquainted﴾ (with all His creation). As for "Subtle," the people of falsehood explained it as the One who cannot be perceived because of His smallness. (I seek refuge in Allah.) "Subtle" in our language means small and not visible. They explained it this way and lied. The people of the Sunnah explained it, saying: the word "subtle" (latif) in the Book of Allah is used with the preposition "lam" and with the preposition "ba'." ﴿Allah is Subtle to His servants﴾ [al-Shura 19], and ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾ [Yusuf 100]. It is used with "ba'" and with "lam." Accordingly, "subtle" has two meanings. One is gentleness toward the servant, meaning that Allah the Mighty and Majestic arranges for him the places of goodness, that is, He is gentle with him and makes the matter easy and facilitated for him. As for being subtle to Him (with the preposition ba'), it means perceiving hidden matters, because "latif" means the One who perceives what is subtle. So the meaning of ﴿Subtle to His servants﴾ is: He perceives what is hidden of their affairs. It therefore means "Acquainted," indeed more precise than "Acquainted." For this reason Allah combined them when He said ﴿Acquainted﴾. The scholars said that "Acquainted" means the One who knows the inner realities of things. Ibn al-Qayyim says in his Nuniyyah, which is among the finest and most comprehensive poems composed on tawhid:

He is the Subtle toward His servant and to His servant,
and subtlety in His attributes is of two kinds:
Perceiving the secrets of affairs through wisdom,
and subtlety at the places of kindness.

This is the meaning of "Subtle." So "Subtle" has two meanings: Subtle to the servant and Subtle with regard to Him. Subtle with regard to Him means Acquainted with the inner realities of His affairs and what is subtle in His command. Subtle to the servant means that He arranges for him, from the secrets of His wisdom or the secrets of His kindness and bounty, what he cannot grasp with his intellect.

Now let us take the benefits of the verses. What was the last benefit we read?

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾ [al-Ahzab 33].

* In this noble verse: the obligation for a woman to remain in her house. Pay attention to this benefit, or should we say it is a legislated preference (mashru'iyyah)? It is legislated, because saying it is obligatory conflicts with what came in the Sunnah permitting women to go out without displaying themselves. So we say it is legislated, because the word "legislated" encompasses both the obligatory and the recommended.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the houses of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) belong to them, because of His words ﴿in your houses﴾.

If someone says: the idafah (possessive construction) here is for specification (ikhtisas), not for ownership (tamlik), as you say: "the saddle for the animal" or "the halter for the camel." Does the animal own it? If someone says that the idafah is for specification and that the houses of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are for the Prophet (ﷺ), what do we say?

We say: reality contradicts that, because if these houses belonged to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), they would not have remained with the Mothers of the Believers after his death, since the Prophet (ﷺ) is not inherited from.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the benefit derived from the idafah ﴿in your houses﴾, for in it is encouragement to stay in the house, because it is her house and her covering. The words ﴿in your houses﴾ are more eloquent than "stay in the houses." It is as if He says: this house was built only for you, as a covering and protection for you, so remain in this house which was built for your sake.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the prohibition of the display of the times of ignorance, because of His words ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾.

* Among its benefits: the permissibility of display (tabarruj) when it is based on knowledge and the Sunnah. The forbidden display is the display of the Jahiliyyah. For this reason, it is permissible for a woman to display herself in some places, and not every display is forbidden for her.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: censure of ignorance, because of His words ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Attributing this to ignorance is undoubtedly meant to create aversion.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of what is based on knowledge. From where is this derived? Because censure of the opposite indicates praise of its opposite, as it is said: "By their opposites things are made clear."

So if display based on ignorance is blameworthy, what is based on knowledge is not blameworthy.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when warning or caution is given, one should mention every attribute that necessitates the encouragement or the warning, because of His words ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. "Former," as we said before, may refer to time or to type.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to establish prayer for women, as it is obligatory for men, because of His words ﴿and establish prayer﴾, and the obligation to pay zakah, because of His words ﴿and give zakah﴾.

* Among its benefits: an indication that establishing prayer and paying zakah are barriers against prohibited things, because He said ﴿do not display﴾, then He said ﴿and establish﴾. This shows that among the causes of not displaying oneself is establishing prayer. There is no doubt about this, because Allah says: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 45], and He the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 45].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of establishing prayer and paying zakah. From where is this derived? From the command to do this. Then He said: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger includes establishing prayer and paying zakah. Specifying some individuals of a general category shows special concern for them, whether the specific is mentioned before or after the general. For example: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good﴾ [al-Hajj 77]. Here the specific came before the general, or not? ﴿Bow and prostrate﴾ is also a form of doing good, and then He said ﴿and do good﴾. And ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4] is an example of the general coming before the specific. Whether the general precedes or follows the specific, it indicates special concern for the specific, which is why it is singled out from among the individuals of the general.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to obey Allah and His Messenger, because of His words ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾.

* Among its benefits: obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ) is obedience to Allah, because of the conjunction with the letter "wa," which indicates sharing, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic said in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 80].

* Among its benefits: Allah, in His perfect wisdom, willed to remove impurity from the People of the House, because of His words ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾ [al-Ahzab 33].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: submissiveness in speech, that display like the display of the Jahiliyyah is impurity, that staying in houses, establishing prayer, paying zakah, and obeying Allah and His Messenger are causes of the removal of impurity. This is because what precedes consists of commands and prohibitions, and Allah the Exalted explained that He commanded them and prohibited them only so that He might remove impurity from this house: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a man's wives are among his household, correct? So if he says, "This is an endowment (waqf) for my household," it includes women. If he says in a sacrifice, "O Allah, this is on my behalf and on behalf of my household," it includes women, because Allah the Exalted made the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) part of his household.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 33–34 (part 4 of 4):

* One of the benefits of this noble verse is the exalting and honouring of this household, shown by His saying ﴿the People of the House﴾. The article in "ال" (al-) is for the mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), as if this household were known and familiar in people's minds and never absent from them, because of the high standing and the praiseworthy quality this household possesses.
* Another of its benefits is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to remove the filth (rijs) and also its trace. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. This is beyond the removal of filth. If we give this a physical example and say: this garment became soiled with impurity, and we scrubbed the impurity until its substance disappeared, what is this called? This is the removal of filth. But if we poured water until the place was completely clean and its trace was gone, that is called purification (tathhir). For this reason, a sound hadith has come in the opening supplication (du'a al-istiftah): "O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail."[[Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh); al-Bukhari (744) and Muslim (598/147), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He mentioned distancing first, before becoming entangled in the sin, then mentioned cleansing from the sin after becoming entangled in it, then mentioned something more emphatic than that, which is washing: washing this sin and its traces with water, snow and hail. The summary is that we say: His saying ﴿purify you with a thorough purification﴾ is beyond the removal of filth.
Another benefit of the noble verse is the affirmation of Allah's will (irada), by His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the filth, O People of the House﴾.
Another of its benefits is that a house purified from filth, whether it is the house of the Messenger (ﷺ) or of others, is considered among the best of houses, and its purification is considered among the greatest blessings upon its people. From where is this taken? From the fact that Allah bestowed this favour upon the family of the Messenger (ﷺ). This is something well known among people. People are like the ores of gold and silver: among people there is a wicked ore and among them a good ore. For this reason, if someone who comes from a good lineage and a good tribe becomes involved in some filth of the filths, what do people say? They find it strange and disapprove, and they consider it more grave. But if someone becomes involved in some filth of the filths while he comes from a tribe known for that, what do they say? It is not considered strange. They say: the branch comes from the tree, and it is no surprise that he does this deed, because his fathers, brothers, uncles and the like did the same. There is no doubt that when Allah bestows upon a household's family purity, nobility, cleanliness and freedom from blemish, that is one of Allah's blessings upon them.
Know that Allah, the Exalted, may place the purity of a whole tribe upon the hand of a single individual, as is observed. A single righteous, reforming man emerges, warning his closest kin and eager to call them to the truth, and Allah the Exalted reforms his entire tribe through him, provided that this is done sincerely and in compliance with His command, the Glorified and Exalted, in His saying ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 214]. But as for ourselves, I do not know what you say. Yes, by Allah, may Allah reform us. We have negligence and neglect. A person does not attend to the family in his own house, nor does he attend to his relatives who are outside his house. This is indeed the reality: people now, at most, only keep in touch in worldly matters, but the guidance of religion, how little of it there is, how little! Although, praise be to Allah, it does exist. I am not saying that I am making you despair of the mercy of Allah. Praise be to Allah, there are people who, when they see in the house of their relatives something disliked, advise and guide them and explain this to them. Sometimes some people even shun them and do not visit them, all of this out of eagerness to set them right.
* Student: In the past they needed one another; now (...).
* The Shaykh: True, they are not like the former people now. In truth, poverty is a good garment, as Hamidan al-Shuwai'ir said:
"Poverty is my generous guest, so go wherever you please, you who squeeze into every narrow place." [poem, colloquial Najdi]
So the summary is that poverty may contain good. "Among the servants of Allah are those whom, if Allah made wealthy, wealth would corrupt them."[[Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi (896) and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah (1249), both with their chains from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from Jibril, from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who said: "Among My believing servants is one whom only poverty will set right, and if I made him rich it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whom only health will set right, and if I afflicted him with illness it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whom only sickness will set right, and if I restored him to health it would corrupt him." The hadith.]] But despite this, do not despair, by Allah. How many a heart has softened to the truth while being among the most sinful of Allah's servants! What truly causes us to be dismayed is despair. Ya'qub, peace be upon him, said to his sons: ﴿Go and search for Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ [Yusuf 87]. Yet at that moment, what did he think? He thought they would not find him. But despite this, because of the strength of his hope in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and because you should not measure matters by what you see, there is something beyond the material, something beyond what is witnessed and heard, namely the will and power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq 2–3]. From a door he did not think the provision would come from. We ask Allah to grant us and you certainty.
* Student: Did Ya'qub know that Yusuf was alive?
* The Shaykh: No. Perhaps he thought so and hoped, because Allah had promised him that.
* Student: (...) ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ [Yusuf 86]?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. He thought and hoped, but such events may cause the heart to despair.
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34]. Among the benefits of this verse is a reminder to the Mothers of the Believers of this great blessing. And it is (no one asks me while I am deriving the benefits): a reminder to the wives of the Messenger (peace be upon him) of this great blessing, by His saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾.
* And among its benefits: whoever Allah has given knowledge, the demand for uprightness upon him is more emphatic and more binding. When Allah gives a person knowledge, more uprightness is required of him than of one who has not been given knowledge, because He said ﴿remember what is recited﴾, so there is no shortcoming in knowledge on your part; rather, knowledge is recited in your houses.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the house in which the Book of Allah is recited is better than the house in which the Book of Allah is not recited. This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not make your houses graves."[[Narrated by Muslim (780/212), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] That is, do not make them like graves in which you do not pray. And in a sound hadith from him: "The best prayer of a man is in his house, except the obligatory prayer."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7290) and Muslim (781/213), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording of al-Bukhari: "...the best prayer of a man is in his house, except the obligatory prayer."]] It was the custom of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, that the houses of the Companions would be heard to resound with the recitation of the Book of Allah, like the humming of bees, from the recitation of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, in their houses.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the Qur'an is among the signs of Allah, by His saying ﴿of the verses of Allah﴾. Its being among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has already been explained in the tafsir, because of what it contains of benefits, wisdoms and secrets.
* And among them (among the benefits of the noble verse): when wisdom (hikmah) is mentioned alongside the Book, what is meant by it is the Sunnah, because the Sunnah also contains wisdom. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not describe the Sunnah as wisdom because the Qur'an contains no wisdom; rather, since the Qur'an is from Allah and is the speech of Allah, the possibility that it does not contain wisdom is far-fetched, is it not? Very far-fetched. But since the Sunnah is the speech of the Messenger (peace be upon him), the speech of a human may admit the possibility that it does not include wisdom. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear that the Sunnah is wisdom. Whether it is his speech or his action (peace be upon him), it is wisdom, because it accords with what is correct.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah: al-Latif (the Subtle) and al-Khabir (the All-Aware).
* Another benefit of the noble verse: that Allah was Subtle and All-Aware, but now He is not.
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: No? Why? "Kana" here is stripped of indicating time. What is intended is only the attribution of the predicate to the subject, regardless of time. So what is its benefit? Why did He not say: "Allah is Subtle and All-Aware"? Its benefit is the realization of the attribute: "kana" means that this has been realized in His case, namely that He, the Glorified and Exalted, is Subtle and All-Aware.
* And among its benefits: what these two names include of the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: subtlety and awareness.
* Student: Could ﴿the People of the House﴾ be used to refute those who deny that the wives of the Prophet are of the People of the House?
* The Shaykh: Yes, how? It certainly does. I heard a recording of Brother Ihsan Zahir Ilahi.
* Student: Ilahi Zahir.
* The Shaykh: Ihsan Ilahi Zahir refutes a Shi'i man and speaks about this verse very strongly and forcefully. He says: whoever restricts this verse to the four members of his household does not know the Arabic language and does not know the styles of speech. How can he extract this verse from among all the verses surrounding it, which are addressed to the Mothers of the Believers, and single out this verse?
What is your question?
* Student: Is there no benefit in (...)?
* The Shaykh: On condition that the students of knowledge teach them.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict. If the husband is mute and says nothing, and she cannot read, and he has books and she does not read, and the husband does not teach her.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It may not be.
* Student: From His saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses﴾.
* The Shaykh: So its meaning is not (...). Perhaps the woman has, as the brother said, recordings to listen to. So it is said: every woman in whose house there is recited a letter of the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), or the words of the people of knowledge based upon the Book and the Sunnah, has a greater duty upon her than one who does not know.
* Student: The student of knowledge.
* The Shaykh: No, you obligate the wives of the students of knowledge who are mute.
* Student: (...) ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses﴾?
* The Shaykh: ﴿what is recited﴾.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is derived from it, because we mentioned it. We said: the remembrance here means that the woman should remember the grace and blessing of Allah upon her in this, and also remember what is recited by learning it and teaching it as well. Learning it, that is, because He commands teaching; otherwise, the wording itself does not indicate it, because He did not say "remind (dhakkir) what is recited," He said ﴿remember (udhkurna)﴾.
* Student: Shaykh, Allah the Glorified and Exalted said in His Book: ﴿of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾. In it there is also a refutation of Muslims who deny the Sunnah.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: They say: we take by the Qur'an and recite it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, how? There is a refutation of these people, and a refutation of others who oppose them, who take by the Sunnah and do not take by the Qur'an. For there are people now, unfortunately, who take great care with the Sunnah, to the point that they dig up things that may not be sound and bring them forward. But as for the Qur'an, ask them about the Qur'an and they know nothing of it, neither of its tafsir, nor its i'rab (grammatical analysis), nor anything of it at all. Meanwhile, they spend their nights and days on the Sunnah, and this is an error, because the first thing we must do is learn the Qur'an, and then the Sunnah, since the Qur'an is the foundation. The time for the talk has now ended, but we want to take (...).

﴿Say to your wives: If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release﴾ [al-Ahzab 28]. We must have mentioned the benefits, but I think we did not mention that the giving of choice is not a divorce, nor did we mention that in it there is a protection of the bed of the Messenger (peace be upon him) from anyone who desires the worldly life and its adornment, nor did we mention that in it there is also a defence of the Messenger (peace be upon him), so that they would not later demand any of their rights from him. I think we mentioned that there are virtues of the wives of the Messenger (peace be upon him). So the main point is that there are many benefits, which you may wish us to take up, and I fear that... some of them are already written down now.
* Student: (...) the mute.
* The Shaykh: No, that the giving of choice is not a divorce, and we did not take up that it contains a defence of the Messenger (peace be upon him). Did we take it? Good, God willing. Well, let us move on.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And stay﴾ with a kasra (on the qaf), and for this reason he said: (with a kasra or a fatha on the qaf). It derives from *al-qarar* (settling), which is remaining in a state of stillness and settledness. It is more emphatic than the phrase "remain in your houses," because *al-qarar* means remaining with an added stillness. For this reason he said: (﴿And stay in your houses﴾ is from *al-qarar*). Its origin is *iqrirna* (or *iqrarna*), with a kasra or fatha on the ra, from *qararta* (with a fatha or kasra on the ra: *qararta* or *qarirta*). The vowel of the ra was transferred to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl was dropped.

The origin of ﴿qarna﴾ is *iqraran* or *iqriran*. So what happened? The fatha of the ra was transferred to the quiescent qaf. Then, when its vowel was transferred to the quiescent qaf, the qaf became vowelled, and the qaf became either fatha or kasra. Then the hamzat al-wasl was dropped, and it became ﴿waqarna﴾.

﴿And stay in your houses﴾: the *idafa* (possessive construction) in ﴿your houses﴾ may be for ownership (*tamlik*), meaning the houses of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ belong to them. It may also be for specification (*ikhtisas*), meaning the houses belong to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Which is closer? The closer view is that it is for ownership, as evidenced by the fact that when the Prophet ﷺ died, these houses remained for whom? For his wives. Had the houses belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they would not have been inherited after him, because the Prophets are not inherited from, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity." Teach me if I err in the wording: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is *sadaqah*" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6727) and Muslim (1758/15), from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. "*sadaqatun*" (with a damma), yes, because otherwise the meaning is corrupted. The Rafidah say the wording of the hadith is: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is *sadaqatan*" (with a fatha), why? So that they may say: what they leave that is not charity is inherited, and that Abu Bakr, 'Umar and the rest of the Companions wronged the heirs of the Prophet ﷺ by not passing it on to them. But Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah say: You have lied, O Rafidah. Rather, the wording of the hadith is: "We, the company of the Prophets, are not inherited from," the sentence ends in the first clause, then he explained what becomes of the wealth after him, saying: "What we leave is *sadaqatun*," meaning: what we leave is charity.

The meaning the Rafidah adopt is false, because what is left as charity is not inherited even for non-Prophets, is it not so? That is, what a person leaves as charity after his death is not inherited by his heirs, even if he is not a Prophet. So they distort the hadith both in wording and in meaning.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: They say: "We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity," meaning: what we leave as charity is not inherited. For example, if we endow something and make it for the cause of Allah, we are not inherited from regarding that thing; rather, other properties are inherited. Is this specific to the messengers? No, it is not specific to them. So we say: his saying ﴿in your houses﴾, the closer view is that the *idafa* is for ownership.

﴿And do not display yourselves⁠ ﴾ (with one of the two *ta*'s omitted from the original): ﴿tabarrajna﴾. Is it a present (imperfect) verb or a past verb?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is the evidence?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The evidence is the prohibitive *la*. The prohibitive *la* only enters on the imperfect. Otherwise, the word *tabarraja* and "the women displayed themselves" is a past verb, but in the verse ﴿wa la tabarrajna﴾ it is an imperfect verb. The author says: (with one of the two *ta*'s omitted), and its original form is *tatabarrajna*. The omission of one of the two *ta*'s in the imperfect is common in the Qur'an, and among its examples is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So I have warned you of a fire that blazes﴾ [al-Layl 14], meaning *tatalaza*.

So ﴿la tabarrajna﴾ is an imperfect verb built on sukun because it is attached to the feminine plural nun, in a position of jazm (apocope) with the prohibitive *la*.

﴿la tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula﴾ (meaning: before Islam).

﴿la tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula﴾: *tabarruj* originally derives from elevation and exaltation, and from it comes *al-burj*, the strong and lofty fortress, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built high﴾ [al-Nisa 78], and as in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky great stars﴾ [al-Furqan 61], meaning He placed in it great masses of stars like lofty towers.

He says: ﴿wa la tabarrajna⁠﴾ meaning: do not exalt and elevate yourselves through clothing and other things. His saying ﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula⁠﴾ is a verbal noun (*masdar*) clarifying the type, by its attribution to *al-jahiliyyah*. He says ﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾, and it is known that the verbal noun may be for counting, for specifying the type, for emphasis, and other things mentioned by the scholars of grammar.

﴿tabarruja al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾ is attributed to *al-jahiliyyah* because it is built on ignorance and foolishness, since when a woman displays herself, that is regarded as ignorance and foolishness on her part. For this reason it is attributed to ﴿al-jahiliyyah⁠﴾, then attributed to ﴿al-ula⁠﴾. Does *al-ula* mean first in time, or first in rank, or both? That is, does the meaning of ﴿al-jahiliyyah al-ula⁠﴾ mean the greatest in ignorance of its kind, as one says: "This is the first in ignorance, this is the first in foolishness, this is the first in Islam, this is the first in reform," and similar? Or does *al-ula* mean first in time? Or both? Both in fact: it is a jahiliyyah of the first class of ignorance, and it is a first jahiliyyah because it preceded Islam. It does not mean that it is the jahiliyyah immediately preceding Islam, because the jahiliyyah immediately preceding Islam was an extension of a jahiliyyah that had preceded it long before. The first jahiliyyah continued until Islam erased it through knowledge and piety, and praise be to Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿tabarrajna tabarruja al-jahiliyyati al-ula⁠﴾.

The purpose of the attribution here, as I said a moment ago, is to specify the type, and how evil is a type that is ignorance. Accordingly, its purpose is denunciation: denouncing this *tabarruj*, and that it is a display built on ignorance and foolishness, and distance from faith, knowledge and right guidance.

(﴿And do not display yourselves as the displaying of the former times of ignorance⁠﴾: meaning, what preceded Islam, of women showing their adornments to men.)

In the jahiliyyah, a woman would display herself and go out in the finest clothing and jewellery she had. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]. So *tabarruj* occurs through the type of clothing, through perfume, through beautifying the body with henna and reddening, blackening the eyes with kohl, and what is called in our present time makeup, and what is called the most reprehensible of reprehensible things. Judge by this analogy: all of this is from the *tabarruj* of the first jahiliyyah.

For this reason he says: (from women showing their beauty to men; and showing after Islam is mentioned in the verse ﴿And do not expose their adornment except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]). May Allah have mercy on the author, for this is not correct of him. In Islam there is no display of adornment at all except in two types:

The first type: general display to everyone.

The second type: specific display to husbands and close relatives (*mahram*).

General display: ﴿except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾. What is meant by ﴿what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ is what custom has made unavoidable to appear, such as the outer garment (*jilbab*) and the cloak (*'abaya*) and similar, as Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, explained it. Accordingly, the exception in His saying ﴿except what [necessarily] appears thereof⁠﴾ is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*), not a connected one, because what appears is not in reality part of the adornment. What appears and what custom makes unavoidable to appear is something that is not truly adornment, even if it is called adornment and clothing, since it must appear. As for the other adornment that Allah specified for particular people, He said: ﴿And do not expose their adornment except to their husbands or their fathers⁠﴾ [al-Nur 31]. This is the hidden adornment, such as the garments beneath the outer garment and cloak and similar. They may not expose it except to their husbands or fathers, and so on to the end. In sum, Allah has never permitted *tabarruj*; the prohibition of it is general.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, beautifying oneself for the husband is a desirable matter. That is, that a woman adorn herself for her husband, because in this is the affirmation of the wisdom for which marriage was legislated, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And of His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy⁠﴾ [al-Rum 21]. There is no doubt that when a woman adorns herself for her husband with all kinds of beauty, that is among what causes him to find tranquility in her and to feel affection for her, so this is from the affirmation of the wisdom for which marriage was legislated. For this reason a woman is commanded to adorn herself for her husband, just as the husband is also commanded, as some of the early generation (*salaf*) said: "Among her rights over me is that I adorn myself for her, just as among my rights over her is that she adorn herself for me" [[Ibn Abi Shaybah (19263) with his chain from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "I love to adorn myself for a woman just as I love a woman to adorn herself for me, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And due to them is similar to what is expected of them, according to what is reasonable⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 228], and I do not love to exhaust all my rights over her, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But the men have a degree over them⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah 228]."]].

As for a husband who comes to his wife dressed in rough sackcloth and the like, and wants her to be pleasing to him, and says: "Why do you not adorn yourself for me?" while he wears the worst clothing, this is not just. A person must observe justice in all his dealings.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, roughness in certain situations: when he rides a horse, let him be rough and wear coarse cloth (...). But with a woman, no; every situation has its own speech.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We have not gone beyond a third (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning of the hadith.

﴿And establish prayer⁠﴾: perform it correctly, meaning by doing its conditions, pillars and obligations, and what else? And its recommended acts. The performance of the first three is obligatory, and of the fourth is for completeness and recommendation.

His saying ﴿establish prayer⁠﴾ includes the obligatory and the voluntary prayer. ﴿And give zakah⁠﴾: meaning give it. *Zakah* linguistically means growth and increase, and in the Sharia it is a specified, determined amount of a specified property, meaning a portion of specified wealth given to those entitled to it.

His saying ﴿give zakah⁠﴾: ﴿ataya⁠﴾ takes two objects, as it is of the pattern of *kasa* and *a'ta* (to clothe and to give). The first object is ﴿al-zakah⁠﴾, and the second object is omitted, meaning *mustahiqqaha* (its rightful recipients): give zakah to its rightful recipients, because giving zakah to other than its people is of no benefit, just as if a person prays outside its time.

His saying ﴿give zakah⁠﴾ after the command to establish prayer contains evidence for the emphasis on zakah. Does it necessarily follow that the Mothers of the Believers had property on which to pay zakah? It does not necessarily follow. If we say it does not follow, then directing the address to them to give zakah becomes a matter of wording, because they would say: "We have no property." Or it is said: they were commanded to give zakah either by undertaking it if they had nothing, or by actually giving if they had something. There is no doubt that they had something on which zakah is due, or some of them had jewellery, as in the hadith of Umm Salamah that she used to wear golden *awdah* (ornaments), and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it a treasure?" He said: "When you pay its zakah, it is not a treasure" [[Abu Dawud (1564) from Umm Salamah, who said: "I used to wear golden *awdah*, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, is it a treasure? He said: 'Whatever reaches the amount whose zakah is paid, and its zakah is paid, is not a treasure.'"]]. So they had something with which to pay zakah; it may not be dirhams and dinars, but it is jewellery.

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾: ﴿obey Allah⁠﴾. The scholars said that obedience (*ta'ah*) is conforming to the command. This is obedience, meaning not disobeying, complying with the command of the one obeyed if it is required in action, and if it is forbidden, by abstaining.

His saying ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾ conjoins obedience to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to obedience to Allah with the conjunction *wa*, because obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah⁠﴾ [al-Nisa 80]. We have previously mentioned many times that in legislative matters it is permissible to join Allah and the Messenger ﷺ together, because what the Prophet ﷺ brought of legislative matters is what Allah commanded.

His saying ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾: is obedience here the obedience of worship, or is it meant as non-opposition? As for obedience to Allah, it is the obedience of worship and humility, hoping for reward and fearing punishment. As for obedience to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, it is obedience in the sense of conforming to the command, whether it is in what he commands from the Sharia or in what he commands concerning his own particular needs. The Messenger ﷺ directs commands to his family either as acts of worship that Allah commanded him, or as particular matters connected to him, peace and blessings be upon him.

(﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: sin, O ﴿people of the household⁠﴾, meaning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿and purify you⁠﴾ from it ﴿with [complete] purification⁠﴾).

﴿Allah only intends to remove⁠﴾: ﴿innama⁠﴾ is a particle of restriction (*hasr*). The scholars say that restriction means affirming the ruling for what is mentioned and negating it for what is other than it. Is the restriction here relative (*idafi*) or real (*haqiqi*)? Relative. Real? Or relative and real, or neither relative nor real? The division is fourfold: either relative, or real, or both, or neither.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Relative. Why?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Because Allah wills this and other things. The relative restriction is one where the thing is not restricted to it in reality, and the real restriction is one where the thing is restricted to it in reality. So if you say: "No student pays attention except Khalid," what happens? Is it real or relative? Let us see: if there is no one else, it is real; if someone else pays attention, it is relative.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The benefit of the relative is that, for example, because this man pays so much attention, no one else pays attention. As if you say: "No one is brave except Khalid," meaning Khalid ibn al-Walid. "No one is brave except Khalid." What do you say? Real or relative?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not real, because there are many brave people other than Khalid ibn al-Walid. "There is no seal of the Prophets except Muhammad ﷺ": this is real, because there is no seal of the Prophets except Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. Is it clear?

Here, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intend for the people of the House only that?

The answer: No. Allah intends to remove impurity from them and purify them, and to bestow blessings upon them, and to lavish favour upon them, and so on.

His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity⁠﴾: is the will here legislative (*shar'iyyah*) or cosmic (*kawniyyah*)? The will is cosmic, and this is the benefit of the specification of the People of the House with this. As for the will for the absence of impurity, it is for everyone from the legislative standpoint. And the will, as we have previously mentioned, is of two kinds: legislative will and cosmic will. Are they necessarily linked? No: one may exist without the other, and they may coincide. What is the difference between them, so that we know their coincidence and divergence?

First: cosmic will relates to what Allah loves and to what He does not love. Second: legislative will relates only to what Allah loves. So when you say ﴿wills⁠﴾, meaning legislatively, its meaning is "loves."

Second: in cosmic will, the willed thing necessarily occurs; in legislative will, the willed thing does not necessarily occur.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 33–34 (part 2 of 4):

So the distinction is from two angles. Now we consider: the two wills (al-iradatan) may be combined in one thing, may both be absent, or one may exist without the other.

If we ask the brother: What do you say about the faith of Abu Bakr? Is it willed by Allah legally (shar'an) or universally (kawnan)?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Universally and legally? Universally, because it occurred; legally, because Allah loves it. So the two wills have combined. What do you say about the faith of Abu Lahab?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed, neither universally nor legally?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed universally.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And willed legally? What do you say? Correct. Yes, willed legally: Allah wills that he become Muslim.
What do you say about the disbelief of Abu Bakr?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Not willed either universally or legally. Correct. Not willed universally, because it did not occur; and not willed legally, because Allah does not love it.
And what does the brother say about the disbelief of Abu Lahab?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Willed universally but not legally, because Allah does not love it. Correct?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, what Allah willed is what happened, which is why he did not believe.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Known. Disbelief is willed by Allah universally; any person who disbelieves, Allah has willed his disbelief universally.

We want examples from the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. Brother, which of the two wills is this verse about?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Universal or legal? Has hardship not befallen people?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: You retracted from the universal? Universal-legal: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. You say this will is universal?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Legal-universal, is that so?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Legal. What is the evidence? Because Allah the Exalted may cause hardship for a person, is that not so? And if it were a universal will, it would in reality be a denial of the verse. So here ﴿yurid﴾ (intends) means yuhibb (loves): Allah loves ease for you and does not love hardship. As for universally, Allah the Exalted does will hardship for us. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship is ease﴾ [al-Sharh 5].

Allah, blessed and exalted, said concerning Hud: ﴿And my advice will not benefit you, if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you﴾ [Hud 34].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Correct? ﴿If Allah intends to mislead you﴾ — is this a universal will, or not? Because Allah does not will misguidance for His creation.
The evidence that He does not will misguidance is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa' 176], and ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ [al-Nisa' 26]. Who is Hud? Nuh? So this is the saying of Nuh, peace be upon him, to his people. May Allah bless you.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾. The lam here presents a difficulty: "yurid li-kadha" (intends for such-and-such). It is well known that (arada) transitively takes its object directly. Here it is transitive by what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: You don't know? But you are confused today. The lam here came in the object of ﴿yurid﴾, and it is well known that (yurid) is transitive directly or by the lam? You say: aradtu kadha (I intended such-and-such), or aradtu li-kadha? You say: aradtu kadha. Therefore the lam here is superfluous; grammatically it is superfluous, and the estimate is: "innama yurid Allah an yudhhiba 'ankumu al-rijs" (Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity). The grammarians say the lam is superfluous.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity﴾, the author says: (sin). The correct view is that rijs is impurity, because rijs originally means what is impure, whether it is an impurity of meaning or a physical impurity. From rijs in the sense of physical impurity is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, except that it be dead meat, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is rijs﴾ [al-An'am 145]. He said ﴿for indeed it is rijs﴾: is this physical or of meaning? This is physical.
And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are rijs from the work of Satan﴾ [al-Ma'idah 90]. This is rijs of meaning. Here, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the rijs﴾: which of the two kinds, physical or of meaning? Of meaning, of course, because physical rijs is not something Allah willed to remove from them; rather it is present in them. They urinate and defecate, and their urine is impure and their excrement is impure, is that not so? Therefore the rijs that Allah willed to remove from the People of the House is the rijs of meaning, which is base morals and deeds. This is the rijs. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So avoid the rijs of idols﴾ [al-Hajj 30]. Here the rijs is what: of meaning or physical? Of meaning. ﴿So avoid the rijs of idols﴾. So every base character or deed is of rijs.

As for His saying: ﴿ahl al-bayt (People of the House)﴾, the author has informed us, by his saying "O People of the House," that ﴿ahl﴾ is in the accusative by way of address, and the particle of address (ya) has been omitted from it. As for his saying "O People of the House," who is meant by the People of the House? There is no doubt that what is meant is the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, because all the verses are in the context of whom? In the context of the women, the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech (32). And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with thorough purification (33). And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 32–34].
So there is no doubt that what is meant by this is whom? It is the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him. Does this contradict what was established from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he "placed a cloak over 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and said: 'These are the People of the House. O Allah, remove from them the rijs and purify them with thorough purification.'"[[Al-Tirmidhi (3205) narrated with his chain from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, the stepson of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab 33], in the house of Umm Salamah, he called Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and covered them with a cloak, and 'Ali was behind his back, so he covered him with a cloak. Then he said: "O Allah, these are the People of my House, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with thorough purification." Umm Salamah said: "And I am with them, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "You are in your place, and you are upon good."]], does it contradict it?
We say: it does not contradict it, because these are the People of the House by kinship, and those are the People of the House by marriage, so all of them are People of the House without doubt. Not only the family of 'Ali; rather the People of the House are more general than these four, because the People of the House include everyone for whom charity is forbidden from the Banu Hashim. So included among them are the family of 'Ali, the family of Ja'far, the family of al-'Abbas, the family of al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and every descendant of Hashim. The Messenger ﷺ is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. So everyone from the family of Hashim is of the People of the House, for whom charity is not lawful.
Accordingly we say: our interpretation of "People of the House" here, that they are the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, is determined by what? By the context. This is contrary to the Rafidah, who took the speech out of its context and made the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, into scattered fragments ('idin), saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity﴾ means only the four People of the House, while the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, are not included in Allah's will to remove impurity from them. For this reason they slander 'A'ishah with immorality—may Allah protect us—and do not care about that.
I say: His saying ﴿ahl al-bayt﴾ here, and regarding the four people of the cloak, and regarding the People of the House for whom charity is unlawful, all of this does not contradict one another. For this reason the preponderant view is that the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, are not permitted to receive charity, based on the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "Indeed charity is not lawful for the family of Muhammad"[[Abu Dawud (2985) narrated it from the hadith of al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Indeed this charity is only the filth of people, and it is not lawful for Muhammad, nor for the family of Muhammad," the hadith.]], and his wives are without doubt from his family, as in this hadith.
Accordingly we say: there is no contradiction between the evidences. A parallel to this is that the Messenger ﷺ was asked: "Which is the mosque founded upon piety from the first day?" He said: "This mosque of mine"[[Al-Tirmidhi (2099) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety from the first day. One man said: It is the mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is this mosque of mine."]], although the mosque founded upon piety from the first day is also the mosque of Quba. Each of them was founded upon piety from the first day: the Messenger, peace be upon him, founded his mosque from the first day he arrived, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, each of them was saying: "Stay with me, stay with me, stay with me," and he said: "Leave her, for she is commanded"[[Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan (2978) from the hadith of Siddiq ibn Musa, as a mursal report.]]—meaning his she-camel.
