When she reached the place of his mosque, she knelt down, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, urged her on, and she stood up, then turned right and left, then returned to her first place and knelt down. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The dwelling place is here, if Allah wills"[[Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat (134) narrated it from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Then he dismounted, and the nearest house to him was the house of Abu Ayyub, so he went to it.
From the first day he arrived, he was engaged in laying out the mosque. For this reason, those responsible in the municipalities and the endowments should make their greatest concern in new layouts the placement of mosques, to be attended to before anything else.
In any case, I say: describing one thing with a attribute and describing another with an attribute does not necessitate that this is a contradiction; rather each of them has a share of this description.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: I don't know.
And his saying—let us complete the verse—﴿the House﴾: here "al" in "al-bayt" is for prior reference (al-'ahd). Which references? Mental (dhihni), meaning the known, familiar People of the House, namely this pure house, the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: ﴿and purify you﴾ from it, i.e., from the rijs, ﴿with thorough purification﴾. Here ﴿tathir﴾ (purification) is a verbal noun of (tahhara), a verbal noun of the preceding verb, and it is meant for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 164]. Purification from rijs is more emphatic than the departure of rijs, because after the departure of rijs some trace may remain.
So when He says "He removes it and purifies you," that becomes what? More emphatic, because it removes that rijs and purifies its place such that no trace remains. There is no doubt that the house of the Messenger, peace be upon him, is the farthest of houses from rijs and the purest of houses from rijs. No believer ever doubts this. Whoever casts aspersions on the house of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his wives, is considered to be casting aspersions on whom? On the Messenger, peace be upon him, because Allah says in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women; and good women for good men, and good men for good women﴾ [al-Nur 26]. We know with certain knowledge that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would not choose for His Prophet except the best women of the worlds, without doubt. It has been established from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and it has been established in the Book of Allah that 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, is innocent of what the people of the slander, the hypocrites and others among the Muslims who were deceived, accused her of—may Allah pardon them. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said concerning this very slander: ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it was trivial while it was, with Allah, tremendous (15). And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this; exalted are You [O Allah]; this is a great slander"﴾ [al-Nur 15–16]. That is: why did you not say? "It is not for us"—"ma yakunu" means it is absolutely impossible, "an natakallama bihadha" (that we speak of this). "Subhanaka" (Exalted are You) is declaring You free of imperfection: "We declare You free, O our Lord, that such a thing should occur in one of the mothers of the believers, the wives of the seal of the Prophets." For this reason He said "Subhanaka," meaning: we declare You free that such a thing should occur among the wives of Your Prophet, peace be upon him.
This great emphasis we see now from those who ascribe themselves to Islam while they are free of it and Islam is free of them. They say that 'A'ishah—may Allah protect us—committed adultery, although Allah has already cleared her of that in the Noble Qur'an. Whoever slanders one of the wives of the Messenger, peace be upon him, 'A'ishah or others, is without doubt a disbeliever, and he must be killed even if he repents. If he repents sincerely, his matter is between him and Allah; but we must be jealous for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we must kill whoever slanders anyone or any one of the mothers of the believers. (...).
﴿...your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34].
The saying of the Exalted was mentioned earlier: ﴿And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, and we explained that ﴿give zakah﴾ — the verb takes the accusative? Brother.

* The Shaykh: No (...). Have you understood it now? A specified right in specified property for a specified group at a specified time. You have understood zakah now. Or we can say: worship of Allah the Exalted by giving out a known portion of wealth according to what the Shari'ah has brought. This is clearer.
Also in it is His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾: the lam in His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove﴾ (...).
﴿what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah﴾: the Qur'an. ﴿And wisdom﴾. ﴿Remember﴾: the imperative here is for guidance, and for explaining the favor and grace of Allah, glorified and exalted, upon them.
His saying ﴿remember﴾ may mean: reflect upon and ponder this matter, and recognize what grace of Allah is in it for you.
It may also mean: remember it by reciting it...
other than its covering, for the revelation did not descend upon the Messenger ﷺ in the wives' beds while he was under their covers except in the case of 'A'ishah[[Al-Bukhari (3775) narrated it from 'A'ishah.]].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 33–34 (part 3 of 4):

Allah's words: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾ [al-Ahzab 34]. ﴿Recited﴾ means ﴿read﴾. Tilawah (recitation) is of two kinds: verbal recitation (tilawah lafziyyah) and meaningful recitation (tilawah ma'nawiyyah). When you say, "He recited the Book of Allah until he finished it," the meaning is verbal recitation. When you say "sujud al-tilawah" (the prostration of recitation), what is meant? Verbal recitation. As for meaningful recitation, it is following the Qur'an. One says "talahu, yatluhu" when he follows something. So meaningful recitation means following the Qur'an in its creed, its morals, and its actions. Which of the two is the greater goal? The greater goal is meaningful recitation. Verbal recitation is undoubtedly intended, and whoever recites a letter from the Book has ten good deeds for it, but what matters most is meaningful recitation. Allah says: ﴿A blessed Book, which We have sent down to you, that they may reflect upon its verses and that people of understanding may take heed﴾ [Sad 29].

﴿...the verses of Allah﴾ undoubtedly refers to the Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, it is clear verses in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ [al-'Ankabut 49]. So "the verses of Allah" is the Qur'an. Here, "verses" refers to the legislated verses (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah), for the verses of Allah the Exalted are divided into two kinds:

Cosmic verses (ayat kawniyyah): these are what Allah has created and creates in this universe. All of it is a sign pointing to its Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, because of its wondrous craftsmanship and its wise, perfect order which contradicts nothing and clashes with nothing. For this reason Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor is there with Him any god. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overpowered others﴾ [al-Mu'minun 91]. If each god took away what he created, the universe would not be orderly, because each god would create as he wills. Furthermore, one of them must overpower the other, for if they opposed each other and neither could prevail over the other, they could not both be gods. And if one of them overcame the other, the defeated one could not be a god. In that case, the rational proof is that there must be one God alone, who is Allah the Exalted.

In short, cosmic verses are everything Allah creates in the universe. Legislated verses are what the messengers brought from revelation. They are called "verses" because they are signs pointing to the One who legislated them and sent them down, because they contain the ordering of benefits and the removal of harms. Indeed, the whole Shari'ah brings about benefit and reduces harm. For this reason, there is nothing that contains a predominant or pure benefit except that the Shari'ah has commanded it, and nothing that contains a pure or predominant harm except that the Shari'ah has forbidden it. However, some benefits we perceive with our minds, some harms we perceive with our minds, and some we do not perceive. Yet we know with certainty that the requirement of the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and one of His names is the All-Wise (al-Hakim), is that He cannot command except what contains benefit, whether pure or predominant, and cannot forbid except what contains harm, whether pure or predominant. For this reason, the books sent down from heaven were called "verses," because they are signs pointing to the One who legislated them, the Exalted, and to the One who sent them down. ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ [al-Nisa' 82]. They would not find discrepancy once or twice or thrice, but much discrepancy and much contradiction.

Here is a matter outside the topic that people have begun to do. They swear by the verses of Allah. One says: "By the verses of Allah, such and such did not happen," or "By the verses of Allah, I will certainly do such and such." What is your opinion about this oath?

There is detail. If he intends the cosmic verses, it is impermissible, because it is an oath by other than Allah, an oath by created things. If he intends the legislated verses, then it is an oath by the words of Allah, and swearing by the words of Allah is permissible, because the words of Allah are among His attributes. What is the usual intention of the common people when they swear this oath? In my opinion, it is mostly the legislated verses. They do not mean an oath by the verses of Allah as in an oath by the sun, the moon, the stars, the night, or the day. They do not swear by such things. When they swear by the verses of Allah, they mean the Qur'an. In that case, this oath is permissible based on the customary understanding of what is meant by it. But if we look at the wording itself, there must be detail.

* Student: Do the legislated verses include the Sunnah?
* Shaykh: Yes. But here He said ﴿and the wisdom﴾, so the author, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified it when he said: (﴿the wisdom﴾ is the Sunnah).
* Student: If he said: "By the verses of Allah (...)"?
* Shaykh: No, never. They only mean the Qur'an. They do not call the Sunnah "verses."
* Student: When we say ﴿yutla﴾ means ﴿yuqra'﴾ (is read)?
* Shaykh: Is read.
* Student: Yes, is read. How can recitation be meaningful?
* Shaykh: No. Here, meaningful recitation does not apply. Verbal recitation is meant here. But we divided recitation in general terms.
* Student: Is recitation not the same as reading?
* Shaykh: When it is said: ﴿Those who recite the Book of Allah﴾ [Fatir 29], and ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it should be recited﴾ [al-Baqarah 121], it includes both this and that, verbal and meaningful. But here, what is apparent is only the verbal.

He said: ﴿...of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: The mushaf?
* Student: Surat Bara'ah.
* Shaykh: Surat Bara'ah?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Why do they specify this surah?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But why do they specify this surah?
* Student: Because it is intimidating (murhibah).
* Shaykh: Intimidating, terrifying. ﴿Woe that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat 15]. Al-Mursalat.

In any case, swearing by the mushaf is an innovation (bid'ah), because it was not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ). What has been reported regarding the intensification of oaths is what Allah mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿The two shall swear by Allah, if you doubt them: "We will not sell this for any price, even if it were a relative"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 106]. His words ﴿you detain them﴾ come before it: ﴿you detain them after the prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer. It will come, Allah willing, in the chapter on claims that intensification can be by time, by place, by manner, and by wording.

﴿And the wisdom﴾: the author said: (it is the Sunnah), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Nisa' 113], and He said: ﴿And He purifies them and teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [Al 'Imran 164]. The basic principle in conjunction is that the two are different. Otherwise, one could say that the noble Qur'an contains wisdom, so teaching the Qur'an is teaching the rulings and teaching the wisdom behind the rulings, because knowing the rulings of the Shari'ah is a very great matter. When a person knows the wisdom behind the legal rulings, his heart becomes more illuminated, he becomes more convinced of the legal rulings, and he knows more of the attributes and wisdoms of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. He can also convince the opponent. For if you tell an opponent, for example, "This is forbidden because the Qur'an forbade it," he may not believe in the Qur'an or feel reassured by it. But if you have knowledge of the wisdoms of the Shari'ah, you can convince that person. Therefore, knowing the wisdom of the Shari'ah is very important. Indeed, most qiyas (analogical reasoning) comes from knowing the wisdom, because it is attaching a branch to a root in a ruling because of a common cause ('illah jami'ah). Accordingly, someone might say that the intended meaning of wisdom is what is known of the secrets and wisdoms of the Shari'ah rulings. But the scholars of the early and later generations, the imams of the later generations, explained wisdom as the Sunnah.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34].
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Knowing the ambiguous (mutashabih)?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know. I am not aware of this.
* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 269].
* Shaykh: I say: I do not know this. It is not that whenever wisdom is mentioned it means the Sunnah. Rather, when He says "the Book and the wisdom," ﴿He teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Baqarah 129], ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom﴾ [al-Nisa' 113], and ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾, it does not mean that whenever wisdom is mentioned it is the Sunnah.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾: ﴿Subtle﴾, the author said: (with His allies), ﴿Acquainted﴾ (with all His creation). As for "Subtle," the people of falsehood explained it as the One who cannot be perceived because of His smallness. (I seek refuge in Allah.) "Subtle" in our language means small and not visible. They explained it this way and lied. The people of the Sunnah explained it, saying: the word "subtle" (latif) in the Book of Allah is used with the preposition "lam" and with the preposition "ba'." ﴿Allah is Subtle to His servants﴾ [al-Shura 19], and ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾ [Yusuf 100]. It is used with "ba'" and with "lam." Accordingly, "subtle" has two meanings. One is gentleness toward the servant, meaning that Allah the Mighty and Majestic arranges for him the places of goodness, that is, He is gentle with him and makes the matter easy and facilitated for him. As for being subtle to Him (with the preposition ba'), it means perceiving hidden matters, because "latif" means the One who perceives what is subtle. So the meaning of ﴿Subtle to His servants﴾ is: He perceives what is hidden of their affairs. It therefore means "Acquainted," indeed more precise than "Acquainted." For this reason Allah combined them when He said ﴿Acquainted﴾. The scholars said that "Acquainted" means the One who knows the inner realities of things. Ibn al-Qayyim says in his Nuniyyah, which is among the finest and most comprehensive poems composed on tawhid:

He is the Subtle toward His servant and to His servant,
and subtlety in His attributes is of two kinds:
Perceiving the secrets of affairs through wisdom,
and subtlety at the places of kindness.

This is the meaning of "Subtle." So "Subtle" has two meanings: Subtle to the servant and Subtle with regard to Him. Subtle with regard to Him means Acquainted with the inner realities of His affairs and what is subtle in His command. Subtle to the servant means that He arranges for him, from the secrets of His wisdom or the secrets of His kindness and bounty, what he cannot grasp with his intellect.

Now let us take the benefits of the verses. What was the last benefit we read?

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾ [al-Ahzab 33].

* In this noble verse: the obligation for a woman to remain in her house. Pay attention to this benefit, or should we say it is a legislated preference (mashru'iyyah)? It is legislated, because saying it is obligatory conflicts with what came in the Sunnah permitting women to go out without displaying themselves. So we say it is legislated, because the word "legislated" encompasses both the obligatory and the recommended.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the houses of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) belong to them, because of His words ﴿in your houses﴾.

If someone says: the idafah (possessive construction) here is for specification (ikhtisas), not for ownership (tamlik), as you say: "the saddle for the animal" or "the halter for the camel." Does the animal own it? If someone says that the idafah is for specification and that the houses of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are for the Prophet (ﷺ), what do we say?

We say: reality contradicts that, because if these houses belonged to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), they would not have remained with the Mothers of the Believers after his death, since the Prophet (ﷺ) is not inherited from.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the benefit derived from the idafah ﴿in your houses﴾, for in it is encouragement to stay in the house, because it is her house and her covering. The words ﴿in your houses﴾ are more eloquent than "stay in the houses." It is as if He says: this house was built only for you, as a covering and protection for you, so remain in this house which was built for your sake.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the prohibition of the display of the times of ignorance, because of His words ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance﴾.

* Among its benefits: the permissibility of display (tabarruj) when it is based on knowledge and the Sunnah. The forbidden display is the display of the Jahiliyyah. For this reason, it is permissible for a woman to display herself in some places, and not every display is forbidden for her.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: censure of ignorance, because of His words ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. Attributing this to ignorance is undoubtedly meant to create aversion.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: praise of what is based on knowledge. From where is this derived? Because censure of the opposite indicates praise of its opposite, as it is said: "By their opposites things are made clear."

So if display based on ignorance is blameworthy, what is based on knowledge is not blameworthy.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when warning or caution is given, one should mention every attribute that necessitates the encouragement or the warning, because of His words ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance﴾. "Former," as we said before, may refer to time or to type.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to establish prayer for women, as it is obligatory for men, because of His words ﴿and establish prayer﴾, and the obligation to pay zakah, because of His words ﴿and give zakah﴾.

* Among its benefits: an indication that establishing prayer and paying zakah are barriers against prohibited things, because He said ﴿do not display﴾, then He said ﴿and establish﴾. This shows that among the causes of not displaying oneself is establishing prayer. There is no doubt about this, because Allah says: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 45], and He the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 45].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of establishing prayer and paying zakah. From where is this derived? From the command to do this. Then He said: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger includes establishing prayer and paying zakah. Specifying some individuals of a general category shows special concern for them, whether the specific is mentioned before or after the general. For example: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good﴾ [al-Hajj 77]. Here the specific came before the general, or not? ﴿Bow and prostrate﴾ is also a form of doing good, and then He said ﴿and do good﴾. And ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4] is an example of the general coming before the specific. Whether the general precedes or follows the specific, it indicates special concern for the specific, which is why it is singled out from among the individuals of the general.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to obey Allah and His Messenger, because of His words ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾.

* Among its benefits: obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ) is obedience to Allah, because of the conjunction with the letter "wa," which indicates sharing, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic said in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 80].

* Among its benefits: Allah, in His perfect wisdom, willed to remove impurity from the People of the House, because of His words ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾ [al-Ahzab 33].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: submissiveness in speech, that display like the display of the Jahiliyyah is impurity, that staying in houses, establishing prayer, paying zakah, and obeying Allah and His Messenger are causes of the removal of impurity. This is because what precedes consists of commands and prohibitions, and Allah the Exalted explained that He commanded them and prohibited them only so that He might remove impurity from this house: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a man's wives are among his household, correct? So if he says, "This is an endowment (waqf) for my household," it includes women. If he says in a sacrifice, "O Allah, this is on my behalf and on behalf of my household," it includes women, because Allah the Exalted made the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) part of his household.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 33–34 (part 4 of 4):

* One of the benefits of this noble verse is the exalting and honouring of this household, shown by His saying ﴿the People of the House﴾. The article in "ال" (al-) is for the mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), as if this household were known and familiar in people's minds and never absent from them, because of the high standing and the praiseworthy quality this household possesses.
* Another of its benefits is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to remove the filth (rijs) and also its trace. From where is this taken? From His saying ﴿and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. This is beyond the removal of filth. If we give this a physical example and say: this garment became soiled with impurity, and we scrubbed the impurity until its substance disappeared, what is this called? This is the removal of filth. But if we poured water until the place was completely clean and its trace was gone, that is called purification (tathhir). For this reason, a sound hadith has come in the opening supplication (du'a al-istiftah): "O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail."[[Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh); al-Bukhari (744) and Muslim (598/147), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He mentioned distancing first, before becoming entangled in the sin, then mentioned cleansing from the sin after becoming entangled in it, then mentioned something more emphatic than that, which is washing: washing this sin and its traces with water, snow and hail. The summary is that we say: His saying ﴿purify you with a thorough purification﴾ is beyond the removal of filth.
Another benefit of the noble verse is the affirmation of Allah's will (irada), by His saying ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the filth, O People of the House﴾.
Another of its benefits is that a house purified from filth, whether it is the house of the Messenger (ﷺ) or of others, is considered among the best of houses, and its purification is considered among the greatest blessings upon its people. From where is this taken? From the fact that Allah bestowed this favour upon the family of the Messenger (ﷺ). This is something well known among people. People are like the ores of gold and silver: among people there is a wicked ore and among them a good ore. For this reason, if someone who comes from a good lineage and a good tribe becomes involved in some filth of the filths, what do people say? They find it strange and disapprove, and they consider it more grave. But if someone becomes involved in some filth of the filths while he comes from a tribe known for that, what do they say? It is not considered strange. They say: the branch comes from the tree, and it is no surprise that he does this deed, because his fathers, brothers, uncles and the like did the same. There is no doubt that when Allah bestows upon a household's family purity, nobility, cleanliness and freedom from blemish, that is one of Allah's blessings upon them.
Know that Allah, the Exalted, may place the purity of a whole tribe upon the hand of a single individual, as is observed. A single righteous, reforming man emerges, warning his closest kin and eager to call them to the truth, and Allah the Exalted reforms his entire tribe through him, provided that this is done sincerely and in compliance with His command, the Glorified and Exalted, in His saying ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 214]. But as for ourselves, I do not know what you say. Yes, by Allah, may Allah reform us. We have negligence and neglect. A person does not attend to the family in his own house, nor does he attend to his relatives who are outside his house. This is indeed the reality: people now, at most, only keep in touch in worldly matters, but the guidance of religion, how little of it there is, how little! Although, praise be to Allah, it does exist. I am not saying that I am making you despair of the mercy of Allah. Praise be to Allah, there are people who, when they see in the house of their relatives something disliked, advise and guide them and explain this to them. Sometimes some people even shun them and do not visit them, all of this out of eagerness to set them right.
* Student: In the past they needed one another; now (...).
* The Shaykh: True, they are not like the former people now. In truth, poverty is a good garment, as Hamidan al-Shuwai'ir said:
"Poverty is my generous guest, so go wherever you please, you who squeeze into every narrow place." [poem, colloquial Najdi]
So the summary is that poverty may contain good. "Among the servants of Allah are those whom, if Allah made wealthy, wealth would corrupt them."[[Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi (896) and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah (1249), both with their chains from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from Jibril, from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who said: "Among My believing servants is one whom only poverty will set right, and if I made him rich it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whom only health will set right, and if I afflicted him with illness it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whom only sickness will set right, and if I restored him to health it would corrupt him." The hadith.]] But despite this, do not despair, by Allah. How many a heart has softened to the truth while being among the most sinful of Allah's servants! What truly causes us to be dismayed is despair. Ya'qub, peace be upon him, said to his sons: ﴿Go and search for Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ [Yusuf 87]. Yet at that moment, what did he think? He thought they would not find him. But despite this, because of the strength of his hope in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and because you should not measure matters by what you see, there is something beyond the material, something beyond what is witnessed and heard, namely the will and power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq 2–3]. From a door he did not think the provision would come from. We ask Allah to grant us and you certainty.
* Student: Did Ya'qub know that Yusuf was alive?
* The Shaykh: No. Perhaps he thought so and hoped, because Allah had promised him that.
* Student: (...) ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ [Yusuf 86]?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. He thought and hoped, but such events may cause the heart to despair.
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab 34]. Among the benefits of this verse is a reminder to the Mothers of the Believers of this great blessing. And it is (no one asks me while I am deriving the benefits): a reminder to the wives of the Messenger (peace be upon him) of this great blessing, by His saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾.
* And among its benefits: whoever Allah has given knowledge, the demand for uprightness upon him is more emphatic and more binding. When Allah gives a person knowledge, more uprightness is required of him than of one who has not been given knowledge, because He said ﴿remember what is recited﴾, so there is no shortcoming in knowledge on your part; rather, knowledge is recited in your houses.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the house in which the Book of Allah is recited is better than the house in which the Book of Allah is not recited. This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not make your houses graves."[[Narrated by Muslim (780/212), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] That is, do not make them like graves in which you do not pray. And in a sound hadith from him: "The best prayer of a man is in his house, except the obligatory prayer."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7290) and Muslim (781/213), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording of al-Bukhari: "...the best prayer of a man is in his house, except the obligatory prayer."]] It was the custom of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, that the houses of the Companions would be heard to resound with the recitation of the Book of Allah, like the humming of bees, from the recitation of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, in their houses.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the Qur'an is among the signs of Allah, by His saying ﴿of the verses of Allah﴾. Its being among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has already been explained in the tafsir, because of what it contains of benefits, wisdoms and secrets.
* And among them (among the benefits of the noble verse): when wisdom (hikmah) is mentioned alongside the Book, what is meant by it is the Sunnah, because the Sunnah also contains wisdom. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not describe the Sunnah as wisdom because the Qur'an contains no wisdom; rather, since the Qur'an is from Allah and is the speech of Allah, the possibility that it does not contain wisdom is far-fetched, is it not? Very far-fetched. But since the Sunnah is the speech of the Messenger (peace be upon him), the speech of a human may admit the possibility that it does not include wisdom. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear that the Sunnah is wisdom. Whether it is his speech or his action (peace be upon him), it is wisdom, because it accords with what is correct.
* Another benefit of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two names of Allah: al-Latif (the Subtle) and al-Khabir (the All-Aware).
* Another benefit of the noble verse: that Allah was Subtle and All-Aware, but now He is not.
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: No? Why? "Kana" here is stripped of indicating time. What is intended is only the attribution of the predicate to the subject, regardless of time. So what is its benefit? Why did He not say: "Allah is Subtle and All-Aware"? Its benefit is the realization of the attribute: "kana" means that this has been realized in His case, namely that He, the Glorified and Exalted, is Subtle and All-Aware.
* And among its benefits: what these two names include of the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: subtlety and awareness.
* Student: Could ﴿the People of the House﴾ be used to refute those who deny that the wives of the Prophet are of the People of the House?
* The Shaykh: Yes, how? It certainly does. I heard a recording of Brother Ihsan Zahir Ilahi.
* Student: Ilahi Zahir.
* The Shaykh: Ihsan Ilahi Zahir refutes a Shi'i man and speaks about this verse very strongly and forcefully. He says: whoever restricts this verse to the four members of his household does not know the Arabic language and does not know the styles of speech. How can he extract this verse from among all the verses surrounding it, which are addressed to the Mothers of the Believers, and single out this verse?
What is your question?
* Student: Is there no benefit in (...)?
* The Shaykh: On condition that the students of knowledge teach them.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict. If the husband is mute and says nothing, and she cannot read, and he has books and she does not read, and the husband does not teach her.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It may not be.
* Student: From His saying ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses﴾.
* The Shaykh: So its meaning is not (...). Perhaps the woman has, as the brother said, recordings to listen to. So it is said: every woman in whose house there is recited a letter of the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), or the words of the people of knowledge based upon the Book and the Sunnah, has a greater duty upon her than one who does not know.
* Student: The student of knowledge.
* The Shaykh: No, you obligate the wives of the students of knowledge who are mute.
* Student: (...) ﴿and remember what is recited in your houses﴾?
* The Shaykh: ﴿what is recited﴾.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is derived from it, because we mentioned it. We said: the remembrance here means that the woman should remember the grace and blessing of Allah upon her in this, and also remember what is recited by learning it and teaching it as well. Learning it, that is, because He commands teaching; otherwise, the wording itself does not indicate it, because He did not say "remind (dhakkir) what is recited," He said ﴿remember (udhkurna)﴾.
* Student: Shaykh, Allah the Glorified and Exalted said in His Book: ﴿of the verses of Allah and the wisdom﴾. In it there is also a refutation of Muslims who deny the Sunnah.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: They say: we take by the Qur'an and recite it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, how? There is a refutation of these people, and a refutation of others who oppose them, who take by the Sunnah and do not take by the Qur'an. For there are people now, unfortunately, who take great care with the Sunnah, to the point that they dig up things that may not be sound and bring them forward. But as for the Qur'an, ask them about the Qur'an and they know nothing of it, neither of its tafsir, nor its i'rab (grammatical analysis), nor anything of it at all. Meanwhile, they spend their nights and days on the Sunnah, and this is an error, because the first thing we must do is learn the Qur'an, and then the Sunnah, since the Qur'an is the foundation. The time for the talk has now ended, but we want to take (...).

﴿Say to your wives: If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair release﴾ [al-Ahzab 28]. We must have mentioned the benefits, but I think we did not mention that the giving of choice is not a divorce, nor did we mention that in it there is a protection of the bed of the Messenger (peace be upon him) from anyone who desires the worldly life and its adornment, nor did we mention that in it there is also a defence of the Messenger (peace be upon him), so that they would not later demand any of their rights from him. I think we mentioned that there are virtues of the wives of the Messenger (peace be upon him). So the main point is that there are many benefits, which you may wish us to take up, and I fear that... some of them are already written down now.
* Student: (...) the mute.
* The Shaykh: No, that the giving of choice is not a divorce, and we did not take up that it contains a defence of the Messenger (peace be upon him). Did we take it? Good, God willing. Well, let us move on.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 35 (part 1 of 5):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women...﴾ and so on to the end of the verse.

First: The Noble Qur'an, in most of what it says concerning penal and practical rulings, addresses men most of the time, because men are more noble than women, because men are the qawwamun (protectors and maintainers) over women, so that when men are righteous, women are righteous, and because when two sexes are combined, what is given precedence (taghlib) is which of them? The more noble and the higher of the two. For this reason, most of the address in the Qur'an is directed to men, for these three reasons and others. Nevertheless, in some verses the rulings are mentioned for both men and women, either in detail (tafsil) or in summary (ijmal).

An example of the first is: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾ and so on to the end. An example of the second is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them: "I will not let the work of any worker among you be lost, whether male or female; you are of one another"﴾ [Al Imran 195]. In this there is summary, ﴿I will not let the work of any worker among you be lost, whether male or female﴾.

Concerning these verses, the exegetes mentioned that among the reasons for their revelation is that Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "O Messenger of Allah, when Allah the Exalted speaks, He speaks of... and does not mention women." So Allah the Exalted revealed these verses: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾ and so on to the end. In the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, this (inna) is the emphatic particle which puts the subject in the accusative and makes the predicate nominative.

(...) males and females.

﴿He has prepared for them﴾ — what? Males or females? Males. He did not say "prepared for them and for them (feminine)"; He said ﴿He has prepared for them﴾. This indicates the precedence of the masculine aspect, just as in His saying ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, the placing of the males first indicates the nobility of the males, and this is a matter about which no intelligent person has doubt. But when the wicked West came, corrupt in its natural disposition and religion, and began to put women first for the sake of stirring up temptation through them and elevating them over men, when this wicked West came, those who follow every caller followed it, and they began to put women before men, until they would not call women anything except "sayyidat" (ladies/masters), meaning that they are masters over men. Thus they reversed the realities and circumstances, because Allah the Exalted has altered their natural dispositions, so they worshipped matter instead of its Creator. Likewise they acted in these conducts of theirs. It is obligatory upon the Muslims to be cautious and alert to the deceptions of those disbelievers, not only in this but in anything else, so that they may be upon clarity regarding their affair. And their religion, praise be to Allah, has been clarified by Allah in every matter.

﴿The Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women﴾: Islam refers to outward acts of the limbs, because it encompasses, or is intended to mean, that a person submits to Allah outwardly with his limbs: with his tongue, his hands, his feet, his eyes, his ears. This outward submission is called... what do you say? It is called Islam. And it may occur from one who is not a believer, it may occur from a hypocrite, and it may occur from one weak in faith. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts"﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14]. This Islam's rank is below faith. Why? Because it occurs from the true believer, from the hypocrite, and from one weak in faith, since it is submission to Allah with the outward limbs.

﴿And the believing men and believing women﴾: this is submission to Allah inwardly, and that is by faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, both its good and its evil. We have no need for anyone's explanation of faith after the Prophet ﷺ explained it, when Jibril asked him: "What is faith?" He said: «That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in the decree, its good and its evil»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50), and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). It is also in Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and the wording is his.]]. The details of this sentence we have discussed many times, and this is not the place to expand upon it.

So faith is what? Submission to Allah inwardly, such that a person believes in what must be believed in, and it is... complete it: faith in Allah and His angels, and so on.

Faith is higher than Islam, because faith necessitates Islam, and not the reverse. Every believer must be a Muslim, because when the heart is sound, what? The limbs are sound, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]. But some people commit sins and argue with the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: «Piety is here»[[Narrated by Ahmad (7727) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. When you say: "O brother, fear Allah, pray with the congregation, fear Allah, leave shaving the beard, fear Allah, abandon backbiting," and similar things, he says to you: "Piety is here." How do you respond?

* Student: Yes, it is true that piety is in the heart, but if the heart is sound, the limbs are sound; faith inwardly (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes. We say: If piety were here, it would have been manifested here; that is, if the inner were pious, the outer would be pious, because the Messenger ﷺ says: «If it is sound, the whole body is sound», so he made the matter a conditional sentence, and what is known in language, custom and the Shari'ah is that in a conditional sentence the conditioned matter is realized when when is the condition realized? When the condition is realized.

* Student: Some of them argue against us during discussion with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa 48]. So how do we respond to it?

* The Shaykh: We say: True, we agree with you that this sin you commit, apart from shirk, is liable to be forgiven by Allah. But Allah did not say: "and He forgives what is less than that for everyone"; rather He said: ﴿for whom He wills﴾. So do you testify that you are one whom Allah wills to forgive? What do we say? Then you are in danger. The principle is that the threat regarding sins is established; this is the principle, because its removal is subject to His will, and its occurrence is in accordance with the promise, so the principle is its establishment. Is it clear? So he has no proof in this.

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women﴾: the author says, and did not explain it. ﴿And the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾. May Allah guide him: he says "(the obedient females)." It should have been that he says — may Allah guide him and forgive him, or has the time of guidance ended? — but he says: ﴿And the devoutly obedient men﴾; he should have said: "the obedient men," or not? And it would become: ﴿and the devoutly obedient women﴾, which is known to be "the obedient women." Is it clear? Yes.

﴿And the devoutly obedient men﴾: qunut is not mere obedience, as is understood from the author's words, but rather obedience with constancy, humility and stillness. This is supported by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [Al-Baqarah 238]. When this verse was revealed, they were commanded to do what? To be silent, and they were forbidden from speaking. This indicates that qunut is not merely performing obedience, but it is obedience with humility, submission and constancy.

And His saying: ﴿The devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾: qunut is higher than what preceded it, because the one who is devoutly obedient has with him faith and Islam, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ [Az-Zumar 9].

﴿And the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, and the truthful men and truthful women﴾: in faith. Truthfulness is the reporting of what corresponds to reality; this is the basic meaning of truthfulness: reporting what agrees with the actual state. For example, if I say to you, "This fan is working," that is truthful, because it is a report that corresponds to reality. And if I said, "This fan is not working," it would not be truthful, because it is a report that contradicts reality. But is truthfulness only in speech, or does truthfulness exist in speech, action and belief?

The answer: the latter. Truthfulness exists in belief, by a person being truthful in sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his deeds, truthful in belief such that it corresponds to what the Shari'ah has brought. And truthfulness likewise exists in speech, by not saying except the truth, even if it is against himself: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives﴾ [An-Nisa 135]. And look at the outcome of truthfulness in the story of the three who were left behind from what?

* Student: From the battle.

* The Shaykh: Which battle?

* Student: Yarmouk.

* The Shaykh: Yarmouk?! Where are you... Yarmouk, O Shaykh? Yes, those who were left behind?

* Student: From the expedition of Tabuk.

* The Shaykh: From the expedition of Tabuk? No, that is wrong. He did not say "they stayed behind," so we say: from the expedition. But "khullifu" means their matter was deferred; because they came and reported with truthfulness. The hypocrites used to come and say: "O Messenger of Allah, we have an excuse, we have an excuse," and he would ask forgiveness for them and leave their inner states to Allah. But these were truthful, so they were left behind (khullifu), left behind from what? From the judgment against them with what was judged against the hypocrites. It is not meant that they were left behind from the expedition; had that been the case, it would have said "those who stayed behind" (alladhina takhallafu). These three, namely Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabi', were truthful with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The most eloquent and clearest of those three in speech and the most articulate was Ka'b ibn Malik, for he was the most mature of them (may Allah be pleased with him). He spoke a remarkable speech, and it would be good for you to review his story, for in truth it increases faith.

These were truthful. What was the outcome of their truthfulness? Allah revealed about them a Book recited until the Day of Resurrection, praising them and commending them, until Allah said to all people: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [At-Tawbah 119]. As for the others, He said: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone; indeed, they are defilement, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn﴾ [At-Tawbah 95]. Notice the difference between the two matters: those lied and were cast down, may Allah protect us, and these were truthful and were raised. So upon you is truthfulness, for truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise. A man continues to be truthful and seek truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a siddiq (a person of great truthfulness)[[Al-Bukhari (6094) and Muslim (2607/103), both with their chains from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise, and a man continues to be truthful until he becomes a siddiq. And lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire, and a man continues to lie until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.»]].

So the point is that the truthful men and truthful women: we say, in faith, in speech, and in action. How is truthfulness in action? What is its form? Truthfulness in action is that it corresponds to the inner state, so you do not act for show, nor for reputation, nor for flattery, nor for courtesy, nor for any worldly purpose.

An example of that: a man takes a thousand dirhams out of his pocket and gives them in charity because people are watching, saying: "I want people to say: how generous is so-and-so!" Has he been truthful in his deed? Its outward appearance is that it is for Allah, and he is truthful; but the reality of his matter is the opposite, rather he was a liar.

Among truthfulness in deeds is following the Messenger ﷺ, for it is evidence of the truthfulness of a person's love for Allah and His Messenger: ﴿Say: "If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins"﴾ [Al Imran 31]. So truthfulness becomes in belief, in speech, and in action.

And what is the basic principle of truthfulness? What is the original meaning of truthfulness?

Someone tells you that the dawn has broken, and you look and the dawn has come up; and another tells you that the dawn has not broken, and you look and it has come up. So what are truthfulness and falsehood? What is the meaning of truthfulness? It is reporting what corresponds to reality; this is truthfulness.

We have mentioned that truthfulness exists in belief, in speech, and in action: truthfulness in belief is sincerity to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and that what one believes corresponds to what the Shari'ah has brought; truthfulness in speech is reporting what corresponds to reality, even if it is against yourself. One says: "Lying is a means of salvation; if you commit a crime and someone asks you, say: 'I did not do it,' and you are saved." The second says: "But truthfulness is more saving." Which of them is more correct? The latter. If you lie, and it is assumed that you escape, the outcome is grievous; but if you are truthful, and it is assumed that you are punished, the outcome is praiseworthy. Truthfulness in action is that it corresponds to what is in the inner self, in the heart, such that the outward and inward coincide.

* Student: Truthfulness and lying: "najwa" (salvation). Truthfulness is "anja" (more saving), "anjawayn" (twice more saving).

* The Shaykh: If it is in lying.

* Student: "Najwa," meaning salvation, so truthfulness is "anja," "anjawayn," meaning...

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, "anja" twice, correct. We will stop here, because the time has ended. (...)

* * *

﴿And the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾ and so on to the end.

How Allah, glory be to Him, addresses the believers (...).

Whoever believes what agrees with the Shari'ah concerning the signs of Allah and His names and attributes, this is part of truthfulness. Truthfulness in speech, I think (...).

﴿And the patient men and patient women﴾: since truthfulness may entail some struggle against the self, as it does, because a person's reporting of truthfulness, especially with regard to himself, is a difficult matter, He followed it with mention of what? Patience. As if He is saying: be truthful and be patient in your truthfulness. So He said: ﴿And the patient men and patient women﴾. Patience (sabr) linguistically means restraint, and from it comes the saying: "He was killed sabran," meaning restrained (confined). In the Shari'ah, it is restraining the self from aversion and resentment toward the decree of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and from complaining about it.

I say: patience is what? Restraining the self from discontent and aversion to the decree of Allah. Pay attention to this. Our saying "the decree of Allah" includes the universal decree (al-hukm al-kawni) and the legislative decree (al-hukm al-shar'i). This definition includes the three types of patience which the scholars have discussed, for they said: patience is of three kinds or three types: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. So when we say: restraining the self from discontent and aversion to the decree of Allah, does it include the three types or not? Because he says: the decree of Allah, universal and legislative. The universal relates to patience with the decrees of Allah, and the legislative relates to patience in obedience to Allah and in refraining from His disobedience.

The patience in obedience to Allah is the highest type of patience, because it is the self's patience in an act, a movement, and an exertion. Patience in refraining from Allah's disobedience is lower in rank, because it involves restraining the self from what it desires, for the sake of it being disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. But does it involve action, as patience in obedience to Allah does? It involves no action; there is only restraint, the self's restraint from this forbidden thing. By this, patience in obedience to Allah is distinguished from patience in refraining from His disobedience, because in each of them there is striving (jihad) of the self. However, patience in obedience involves obligating the self to act, whereas this (refraining) does not involve obligating the self to act, but rather what? Restraint from Allah's disobedience. Therefore it is lower in rank than the first. Yet we say: it is lower in rank considering the type itself, not considering the individuals who are patient, because some of the patient people suffer more hardship in patience against Allah's disobedience than in patience in obedience to Allah. Is that not so? If we suppose a man whose self pressures him and calls him to commit indecency with strong insistence, but when he prays he finds himself at ease, without difficulty or hardship, there is no doubt that his first suffering is more severe. But we are speaking of the types of patience as types, setting aside the patient person and what relates to his condition.

As for the third category, it is patience in the painful decrees of Allah, and this is the lowest type of patience, because it is patience concerning what is not the person's own action, patience concerning a matter that is neither his doing nor within his capacity. Is that not so? But patience in obedience and in refraining from disobedience is within one's capacity, whereas Allah's decrees are not within one's capacity. So this is patience concerning a matter that is not within your capacity, and therefore it is lower than that.

For this reason some of the Salaf said concerning the afflicted person: "Either he is patient with the patience of the noble, or he forgets with the forgetting of animals." This is true. Who among us has not been afflicted in his body, his family, or his wealth, and then the affliction was very great, yet after a period of time he forgets it, as though it were nothing? For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Patience is only at the first shock." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1302) and Muslim (926/14) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is the reality of patience. After that, the self cools down and is diverted by matters that occur to it in its affairs of life, until it becomes consoled, as though nothing had happened.

So, how many types of patience are there?
* Student: Three.
* Shaykh: Three: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from His disobedience, and patience in His painful decrees.
What do you say about the patience of Ayyub (peace be upon him)? Which type of patience is it?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is it?
* Student: Patience in obedience to Allah.
* Shaykh: With what?
* Student: And in truth it is patience in Allah's decrees.
* Shaykh: We want nothing but the truth. His patience with the harm that touched him, is it from the category of patience? In Allah's decrees. What do you say about the patience of Yusuf concerning committing indecency with the wife of the ruler?
* Student: In refraining from Allah's disobedience.
* Shaykh: Patience in refraining from Allah's disobedience. What do you say about the patience of Yusuf regarding the pain of the prison and the harm he suffered?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: (...) he finished with it. But his being imprisoned, he suffered, was harmed, and was patient.
* Student: Allah's decrees.
* Shaykh: In Allah's painful decrees. Did Yusuf have patience in obedience to Allah?
* Student: His entering the prison was by choice. "My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me" [Yusuf 33]. This indicates that he chose obedience (...).
* Shaykh: Also, his calling the people of the prison to worship Allah and to His Oneness, this is from patience in obedience to Allah. Thus all three types of patience were combined in his case. And likewise, the three types of patience are found in many of Allah's servants. The Messenger ﷺ was patient in obedience to Allah, and in refraining from His disobedience, and what else? And in His decrees, and this is a great deal.

So, is patience obligatory or recommended? Patience is obligatory. We said: restraining the self from what?
* Student: Disobedience.
* Shaykh: No. The general meaning of patience is restraining the self from resentment and aversion toward the rulings of Allah. We did not say "toward the Shari'ah of Allah," but "toward the rulings of Allah," so that it includes patience in Allah's painful decrees. Therefore patience is obligatory, and in it there is great reward. Allah, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account" [Az-Zumar 10]. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said regarding fasting, in the hadith: "Every deed of the son of Adam is for him, the good deed is multiplied tenfold, except fasting, for it is for Me and I will reward it" [[Al-Tirmidhi (764) reported with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your Lord says: every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and fasting is for Me and I will reward it, and fasting is a shield from the Fire," the hadith.]]; because fasting in reality combines the three types of patience: it is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from His disobedience, and patience in His painful decrees. So let us ask the brother to analyze for us these three types in fasting.
* Student: Patience in obedience to Allah, because Allah commanded it.
* Shaykh: Because? Do not say "because Allah commanded it," say "because it is He."
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Be patient, we have not finished with you yet. Patience in obedience to Allah, why?
* Student: Because Allah commanded it.
* Shaykh: Because it is patience in fasting, and he restrains his self, consenting to it, so he fasts. And patience in refraining from Allah's disobedience?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. The fasting person is commanded to avoid many things, and he avoids them. Therefore he was patient in refraining from Allah's disobedience. Patience in Allah's decrees?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Did you fast this year in Ramadan?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Praise be to Allah. You were hungry and thirsty, and you suffered from this hunger and thirst. Therefore it is patience in Allah's painful decrees. In fasting are the three types of patience: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from Allah's disobedience, and patience in Allah's painful decrees. "The patient men and the patient women" [Al-Ahzab 35].
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, it is not related to the universal will (al-iradah al-kawniyyah); it is related to the legislative will (al-iradah al-shar'iyyah). It is willed by Allah, the Exalted, legislatively. As for universally, it is willed by Him only in the one who fasts. Is the time finished now?
* Student: Yes.
* Another student: The author says: "(upon the acts of obedience)."
* Shaykh: No, there is a deficiency in it: "(patient upon acts of obedience)." I say: there is a deficiency in this. The correct version is: "the patient in obedience, and in refraining from disobedience, and in Allah's painful decrees."
* Student: (...) Patience is restraining the self from distress, the tongue from complaining, and the limbs from slapping the cheeks and tearing the collars.
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. We said: from resentment toward the decree of Allah, general, more comprehensive than what he (may Allah have mercy on him) said. (...)
Or its reward and its rank are not attained except by the presence of its causes. As for a person saying "I am patient," and then he is not patient, he does not attain that rank. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ experienced more of Allah's painful decrees than others, as was established from him that he said: "Indeed he is feverish as two men are feverish" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5660) and Muslim (2571/45). Also reported by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (368) with this wording, all from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]], meaning that he is afflicted with fever as two men are afflicted. And in the context of death, the Prophet ﷺ was made to suffer hardship so that this rank, the rank of the patient, would be completed for him, until he attained its highest level.

He said: "And the patient men and the patient women, and the humble men and the humble women" [Al-Ahzab 35]. The author says: "(the humble)" -- this is the beginning of today's lesson -- the khashi' (humble) is the one who is lowly and submissive, and its opposite is the one who is proud and arrogant. Khushu' is therefore lowliness, submission, and humility, and it is among the highest ranks of faith and among the most perfect states of the heart. Khushu' has places (applications), among them: khushu' in prayer. The jurists defined it as a stillness in the heart that becomes apparent on the limbs. Some of them said: it is a meaning in the self from which the stillness of the limbs appears. So it is in the heart, and its effect appears on the limbs. For this reason it is narrated from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he saw a man fidgeting with his beard while praying, and he said: "If this man's heart were still, his limbs would be still" [[Reported by Abd al-Razzaq (3308) from Ibn al-Musayyib as a statement of his own, and its wording: that he saw a man fidgeting with his beard in prayer and said: "I see that if this man's heart were humble, his limbs would be humble."]]. It has also been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, but it is not authentic; it is from Umar, with weakness in it.

So khushu' in prayer is the stillness of the heart whose effect appears on the limbs, or a meaning that stands in the self from which the stillness of the limbs appears. There is also khushu' in the rest of the acts of obedience, by a person performing them while he is humble and lowly before Allah, the Exalted. Among this is what occurred to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he conquered Makkah and prevailed over its people. He ﷺ did not enter like one who is high and arrogant, but entered with his head bowed, ﷺ, submitting to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

Also among it is khushu' in Hajj and 'Umrah, where a person performs them with lowliness and humility, believing that he is worshipping Allah. So when you enter into 'Umrah or Hajj, believe that you are in worship from the moment you say "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk" until you finish. But unfortunately we do not feel this; you find a person engaging in the prohibitions of ihram and other forbidden things, except whom Allah wills.

So khushu' encompasses all acts of obedience, by a person performing them with humility, lowliness, and submission, with no arrogance or haughtiness in his heart. There is no difference in this between khushu' during the act of worship and khushu' after performing the act of worship. For some people are humble during worship, but when they finish it, they see themselves at a high level, and that they are elevated, and that they have attained a rank that others did not attain. This is self-admiration and admiration of one's deed. So a person, when he has performed the act of worship, should be as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Their hearts are fearful" [Al-Mu'minun 60], that when they look at their shortcomings they fear, and when they look at Allah's bounty they hope.

"And the charitable men and the charitable women" [Al-Ahzab 35]. "Al-mutasaddiqin" means those who give out charity. Sadaqah is the giving of wealth seeking nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It includes zakat, for it is the highest of charities, and it includes voluntary giving, such as voluntary charity, spending on a guest, on family, and on oneself. All of this is from sadaqah. So what a person puts into his wife's mouth is from sadaqah, and what he eats is from sadaqah. Everything of wealth that you spend for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is from sadaqah.

It may be said that al-mutasaddiqin is more general than those who spend their wealth in what pleases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it includes doing every good, because the Messenger ﷺ said: "Every tasbihah is a sadaqah, every tahlilah is a sadaqah, commanding good is a sadaqah, forbidding evil is a sadaqah, removing harm from the road is a sadaqah, helping a man with his animal, carrying him upon it or lifting his goods onto it, is a sadaqah, a good word is a sadaqah, and with every step you take toward prayer is a sadaqah, and in the intimacy of one of you is a sadaqah" [[Reported by Muslim (1006/53) from Abu Dharr, and its wording: that some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, the people of abundant wealth have taken the rewards; they pray as we pray, fast as we fast, and give sadaqah from the surplus of their wealth." He said: "Has Allah not made for you what you may give in charity? Indeed, with every tasbihah is a sadaqah, every takbirah is a sadaqah, every tahmidah is a sadaqah, every tahlilah is a sadaqah, commanding good is a sadaqah, forbidding evil is a sadaqah, and in the intimacy of one of you is a sadaqah." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, one of us fulfills his desire and yet has a reward for it?" He said: "Do you see, if he had placed it in something unlawful, would he have borne a burden for it? Likewise, if he places it in what is lawful, he has a reward."]].

If we take this generality, then al-mutasaddiqin and al-mutasaddiqat include whoever performs any act of obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. But it is well known that al-mutasaddiqin and al-mutasaddiqat immediately bring to mind those who spend their wealth in what pleases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

As for His saying "And the charitable men and the charitable women," there is no need for us to elaborate on explaining sadaqat, what a person should give in charity, and whether it is permissible to give all of his wealth and leave his dependents in poverty, or it is not permissible. For this has another place. The main point is that Allah, the Exalted, praised whom? The charitable men and the charitable women.

He said: "And the fasting men and the fasting women" [Al-Ahzab 35]. In sadaqah there is giving; in fasting there is abstaining. "Al-sa'imin" are those who worship Allah, the Exalted, through fasting. Fasting is worship of Allah by abstaining from the things that break the fast, from the break of dawn until sunset. It has types: among it is what is a pillar of Islam, among it is what is obligatory but not a pillar, among it is what is a specific recommended fast tied to a specific time, and among it is what is a general recommended fast. Four types. So the obligatory fast that is a pillar of Islam is?
* Student: Ramadan.
* Shaykh: And other than it? There is no other. And the obligatory fast that is not among the pillars of Islam?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Other than it. The vow, which you made obligatory upon yourself.
* Student: The making up of missed days.
* Shaykh: No, making up missed days is among the pillars of Islam.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Correct, like the fasting of expiations.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, not at all. When a person breaks his oath, he did not obligate himself to fast; rather, he committed the cause.
Among it is what is a recommended fast tied to a specific time?
* Student: (...) Monday and Thursday.
* Shaykh: Yes. And among it is 'Ashura, the nine days of Dhul-Hijjah, and the Day of 'Arafah. Apparently these do not fall under the specific category, or do they fall under the specific? The six days of Shawwal, do they fall under the specific? But they are in the whole month. And among it is what is unrestricted, such as a person fasting a day for Allah, the Exalted, except that it is disliked to fast alone on Friday. Rather, one should either fast a day before it or a day after it.

The fasting men and fasting women refrain from their pleasures and desires: from eating, drinking, sexual intercourse, and what follows from them. But these are the fundamentals of pleasures. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said in the sacred hadith about the fasting person: "He leaves his food, his drink, and his desire for My sake" [[Reported by Muslim (1151/164), and Ahmad, the wording is his (9112), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Does fasting not enter into patience? Yes, but it is an act of worship in its own right, and it includes patience.

"And the fasting men and the fasting women, and the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them" [Al-Ahzab 35], from the unlawful.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Which of them?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: In it are the three types of patience.
"Al-hafizin furujahum and al-hafizat": "those who guard their private parts" from what? The author said: "(from the unlawful)." It is a comprehensive phrase that includes guarding the private parts from fornication, guarding the private parts from looking, and guarding the private parts from forbidden acts that are less than fornication. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explained who guards his private parts and who does not. He, the Exalted, said: "And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are transgressors" [Al-Mu'minun 5-7].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 35 (part 3 of 5):

The most important thing to guard the private part against is zina (fornication). It is the committing of indecency in the front or the back passage. However, if it involves a male, it is called liwat (sodomy), and liwat is greater than zina, and we seek refuge in Allah. The punishment for liwat is execution in every case. Indeed, the more correct view is that its punishment is killing in every case, whether the doer is muhsan (married) or not. This is on condition that he is mukallaf, meaning an adult of sound mind. If a male commits liwat with another male, and both are sane and adult, then both must be killed, even if they are not muhsan. But how are they to be killed? The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and those after them differed on this. It was said that they are stoned to death, like the married adulterer. It was said that they are thrown from the highest place in the town and stones are thrown after them. It was said that they are burned with fire, as Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, did when he wrote to Khalid ibn al-Walid after Khalid told him that there was a man who was being mounted as a woman is mounted. Abu Bakr wrote to him to burn him, as a way of exaggerating his punishment.

So, the most obligatory thing to guard the private part against is zina. Likewise, looking must be guarded against, so a person must guard his private part from being looked at, even intercourse with one of the same sex. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A woman should not look at the private part of a woman, and a man should not look at the private part of a man."[[Narrated by Muslim (338/74) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "A man should not look at the private part of a man, nor a woman at the private part of a woman." The hadith...]] So it is obligatory to guard the 'awrah (private parts) from being looked at, except by one's wife and what his right hand possesses. Likewise, guarding the private part extends to forbidden acts other than zina, liwat and looking, such as masturbation, which is known among people as the "secret habit." It occurs among males, and it also occurs among females; even females practise it. This too is forbidden and not lawful, because in it there is no guarding of the private part. A person who seeks to fulfil his desire with other than his wife or what his right hand possesses falls under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾. So it is forbidden by the Qur'an and also by the Sunnah. We have mentioned that among its evidences is the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, — proceed with the hadith..:
"Whoever is unable [to marry], then fasting is a shield for him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1905) and Muslim (1400/3) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]] What is the point of evidence from the hadith?
* Student: That the Prophet, peace be upon him, guided to fasting (...). If there were goodness in it, he would have guided a person to it.
* Shaykh: If it were permissible, he would have guided to it.
* Student: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "I have not found anything that brings one closer to Allah except that I have commanded you to it."[[Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/76) with his chain from al-Muttalib al-Makhzumi that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "I have not left anything of what Allah has commanded you except that I have commanded you to it, and I have not left anything of what Allah has forbidden you except that I have forbidden you from it."]] (...).
* Shaykh: The point of evidence is that the Messenger guided to fasting, which is harder than this act. If this act were permissible, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, would have guided to it, because it is easier and more convenient. 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Prophet, peace be upon him, was never given a choice between two matters without choosing the easier of them, so long as it was not sinful."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3560) and Muslim (2327/78), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] So when he did not choose this easier option, it is known that it is a forbidden sin.
* Student: Shaykh, the use of liwat... Allah, glory be to Him, named it fahisha (indecency).
* Shaykh: Fahisha?! No, it is not fahisha.
* Student: Fahisha, yes. So we apply liwat to it. Is there not an offence to the Prophet in this?
* Shaykh: No, not at all; this is a well-known usage.
* Student: What (...)?
* Shaykh: No, in fact the relative noun (nisbah) may be ascribed to the mudaf (the first term of an idafah) or to the mudaf ilayhi (the second term). This is what the Arabic language requires. The people of Lut (qawm Lut), meaning: "Lutiyy," i.e., one ascribed to these people.
* Student: If he masturbates while fasting in Ramadan, and he is muhsan, is there expiation (kaffarah) on him?
* Shaykh: No, there is no expiation on him. Expiation is only for intercourse.
* Student: There is a report from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who was asked about a man having intercourse with a woman in her back passage, and he said: "That is the minor sodomy (al-liwatiyyah al-sughra)."[[Narrated by Ahmad (6706) from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather.]]?
* Shaykh: The hadiths about intercourse with a woman in the back passage all have criticism in their chains, but some of them strengthen others, and they indicate its prohibition. It has already passed us in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they ask you about menstruation. Say, it is harm﴾ [al-Baqarah 222]. It passed us that among its benefits is the prohibition of intercourse in the back passage. It has passed us.
* Student: I meant on this name, that is, "liwatiyyah", on this act.
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, "minor sodomy."
