On this basis they built their approval (istiḥsān) of matters that are undoubtedly forbidden, such as permitting usury (ribā), claiming it stimulates the economy and strengthens the nation, and permitting insurance, which is in reality gambling (maysir), which Allah linked with wine, idols (anṣāb), and divining arrows (azlām), and other things that they consider part of the name of the Islamic religion on the pretext that Islam is suitable for every time and place.
We say: suitable (ṣāliḥ). We do not say: subject (khāḍi'). Act by Islam at any time, place, or nation and see for yourself whether it conflicts with benefits or fosters benefits. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾
Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor...﴾ to the end.
* From this noble verse is derived: Reminding the Prophet ﷺ of matters in which it is good to admonish, by His saying: ﴿And when you said﴾, where we said it is governed by an omitted verb whose implied meaning is "remember."
* And from its benefits: Showing Allah's favor upon Zayd ibn Ḥārithah through Islam and adherence to it, to the extent that when his father and uncles came seeking him, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave him the choice between them and himself, he chose to remain with the Messenger ﷺ.
* And from its benefits as well: Manumission is a blessing from the one who frees upon his freed person, and so it is. The scholars of inheritance (al-farḍiyyūn) express manumission in terms of blessing.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: It is permissible to join non-legislative matters with "and" when the meanings differ. We said that the Messenger is not equated with Allah with "and" in matters other than legislative ones. Here the Messenger's blessing has been joined to Allah's blessing with "and," even though it is not a legislative matter. What permitted this is the difference between the two blessings: the first blessing is Islam, and the second blessing is manumission.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: A wife is subordinate to her husband, by His saying: ﴿Keep for yourself your wife﴾. It is as if he holds her, guards her, and protects her, and as if she is subject to him, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you﴾ [al-Mā'idah 4].
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Consulting people of sound judgment, because Zayd consulted the Prophet ﷺ.
* And from its benefits: The one who is consulted must give what he sees, even if by his own ijtihad (independent reasoning), as what he sees to be best. The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) advised Zayd to keep her, by his own ijtihad, fearing that the hypocrites and polytheists would stir up trouble against him. But this does not mean that the one giving counsel is correct in what he decides. He may err in what he decides, but at the time of giving his advice he sees that this is correct.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: It is better for a husband not to hasten to divorce and to keep his wife, by His saying: ﴿Keep for yourself your wife﴾. So he advised him against divorce, although the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) had other aims. Nevertheless, this does not prevent there being several reasons for the command to keep her. It is known that Allah, mighty and majestic, said in His clear Book: ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good﴾ [al-Nisā' 19].
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Confirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood and that it is a true message, by His saying: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him.﴾ For if the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had been lying, which is far from him, he would have concealed such things, because they are difficult for him to bear.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, mighty and majestic, may act contrary to what the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) was inclined to. This means that the Prophet's ﷺ ijtihad may be contrary to what Allah, glorified and exalted, wills. By His saying: ﴿that which Allah is to disclose﴾, the Messenger concealed this matter within himself, but Allah acted against him in this and disclosed it.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The fear of people may occur from the prophets, but they are not left to persist in it, by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾.
* And from it: The obligation to give precedence to fear of Allah, mighty and majestic, over fear of anyone, by His saying: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. So it is obligatory upon a person not to fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah, and to fear Allah, mighty and majestic, in making the truth clear and acting upon it. He should not say: "People will mock me, people will ridicule me, people will make fun of me." Let it be so, for he gains nothing by this mockery and ridicule except elevation in the sight of Allah, glorified and exalted.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: A marriage is not valid until the first husband's right over the wife has completely ended, by His saying: ﴿And when Zayd had no longer any need of her, We married her to you﴾. So the marriage took place after Zayd had entirely finished with her. It is not an objection to this that the apparent meaning of the verse permits marriage immediately after divorce. We say: the need and the purpose do not end except with the end of the 'iddah (waiting period), since if a man wished to return to his wife during the 'iddah, and she was revocable (raj'iyyah), he could do so.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Affirmation of Allah's greatness and sovereignty, by His saying: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾, because of His greatness and sovereignty.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The virtue of Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, since Allah, glorified and exalted, gave her in marriage to His Messenger ﷺ. What is its basis? Others were given in marriage to him by their guardians and families, but as for her, Allah, mighty and majestic, Himself arranged her marriage. This is a great distinction for her.
* And from its benefits: Allah, glorified and exalted, rewards His servant more than his deed. This woman, as has been mentioned, married Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, although Zayd was a freed client (mawlā), while she was of the pure Arab stock. This may have been a diminishment of her right and rank, so Allah elevated her standing by having His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ marry her, by Himself, blessed and exalted. There is no doubt that this is an elevation of her standing. Having been under this freed man, although she was of the pure Arab stock and there was some shame upon her in that, Allah raised her standing through this matter.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: What is established regarding the Prophet's ﷺ rulings is also established for his community. From where do we derive this? What is the basis for this?
* The student: The basis is that this ruling applies to him and to the Muslims.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Because this ruling was addressed to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), then... ﴿so there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them﴾. This shows that whatever rulings are established for the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) apply to his community as followers of him, unless evidence specifies otherwise.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The permissibility of a man marrying the wife of one he has adopted. From where is this taken? ﴿so there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾.
* And from its benefits: Adopted sons (ibn al-tabannī) are not legally called sons, and what Allah called them, by His saying: ﴿their adopted sons﴾ and His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your [true] sons﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 4]. From this benefit it follows that His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [al-Nisā' 23] — this qualifier is not to exclude an adopted son, because he was never included among the sons, such that he would need to be excluded.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The cosmic command of Allah, mighty and majestic, must come to pass. The question is now directed to one person.
* A student: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever to be fulfilled﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 37].
* The Shaykh: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever to be fulfilled﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 37]. If someone says: "﴿amr Allah﴾ is a singular noun in the construct state, so it includes both the cosmic and the legislative command. How shall we answer him, when we have just restricted it to the cosmic command?"
* The student: That Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions legislative matters, and they are not realized.
* The Shaykh: Legislative. Correct.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done. Because a legislative command is not something that is carried out by everyone; there are some who do not carry it out.
Then He, exalted, said: ﴿There is no discomfort upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has ordained for him﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 38] to the end.
* From the noble verse is derived: There is no discomfort upon the Prophet ﷺ in what Allah has made lawful for him, even if it differs from what people are accustomed to, because of the generality of His saying: ﴿any discomfort﴾ and ﴿concerning that which Allah has ordained﴾; since (mā) is a relative pronoun, whatever Allah has made lawful for the Messenger, there is no discomfort upon him in it.
* And also derived from it: There is no discomfort upon a person other than the Messenger in what Allah has made lawful for him. There is no discomfort upon him in what Allah has made lawful for him. From where is this derived? Because what is established regarding the Prophet ﷺ is established for his community, unless there is evidence otherwise. However, a person must consider the circumstances of people and what may be disapproved of him in it, so that he does not expose himself to blame and disparagement. Considering people's circumstances is a necessity, except in legislative matters, for the duty of a person is to make them clear and to make them known.
* A student: Should this not be specified by the hadith: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes... no. How, "worldly" (dunyā), what does it mean?
* The student: I mean, in the matter of marriage, their abstaining from marrying a wife of an adopted son may fall under worldly matters.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is a worldly matter, because Allah did not forbid it.
* The student: So why do we not say: there is no discomfort upon him in what (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, only in what Allah has made lawful for him specifically.
* A student: The lawful is connected to (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, and in what Allah has forbidden him there is discomfort.
* The student: The matter of blame and disparagement in what Allah has made lawful for him, how...
* The Shaykh: Yes, the people's blame of him, not Allah's blame. That is: some lawful things, if a person does them, fall outside of manliness (murū'ah) according to people's custom. So considering this matter is not derived from this verse. Considering this matter is a necessity. That is, suppose there is something lawful, but people criticize you for it. It is not one of the legislative matters that must be made clear, so it is better for a person to leave it.
* The student: Should this not be specified by the hadith: «Had it not been that your people are recent in disbelief»[[Ibn Majah (2955) narrated with his chain from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about al-Ḥijr, and he said: «It is part of the House.» I said: "What prevented them from including it in the House?" He said: «Their expenses fell short.» I said: "Then why is its door raised, so that none can climb up to it except by a ladder?" He said: «That was the action of your people, so that they might admit whomever they wished and prevent whomever they wished. Had your people not been recent in disbelief, fearing that their hearts would recoil, I would have looked into changing it and including in it what was taken from it, and I would have made its door level with the ground.»]]?
* The Shaykh: No. This is from considering interests and averting harms, because when a harm is established, it is not permissible for a person to engage in it. He must refrain from it, so it does not fall within what Allah has made lawful for him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 36–40 (part 4 of 4):

* It is derived from this noble verse that the Prophet ﷺ is subject to obligation, and that he may face hardship regarding what Allah has not made lawful for him. This is shown by His words, ﴿in what Allah has ordained for him﴾. From this it is derived that the Messenger ﷺ is one of Allah's servants, or one of His worshippers, who does not step outside His obedience and His law (shari'ah), as Shaykh al-Islam Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab said: "The Messenger Muhammad ﷺ is a servant who is not to be worshipped, and a messenger who does not lie." That is so, and the rest of the discussion of the verse will come, Allah willing.
(...) Is clear explanation through action more eloquent than clear explanation through speech, or not? If you can join it... Has it been mentioned? I don't think we mentioned it.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: (...) with the benefits: indeed, clarification through action is more eloquent and stronger than clarification through speech. From where is this taken? From the fact that Allah, exalted is He, married Zaynab bint Jahsh to His Messenger ﷺ, for this is more effective in reassurance and in the establishing of the ruling. Glory be to Allah! Have we mentioned that there is evidence in the verse that whatever ruling was established for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is also established for the ummah?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: We mentioned it, and we clarified the aspect of the indication, and we clarified that the decree of Allah in creation (al-amr al-kawni) must necessarily come to pass.
So then, ﴿there is no hardship upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾. What did we take from it?
* Student: That there is no hardship upon the Prophet ﷺ in what he does, even if it opposes people in what Allah has made lawful (...).
* Shaykh: Obligation?
* Student: Obligation. That the Prophet ﷺ is one of the servants of Allah (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, good.
"I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿the practice of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what Allah legislated for His Messenger in this verse is legislated for those who came before him, by His words: ﴿the practice of Allah concerning those who passed away before﴾.
* Perhaps there is also a benefit derived from it, which is that the law of those before us is law for us, because Allah made this the practice of the earlier ones. However, this may be disputed, and it is said: Allah has made clear that what He legislated for His Prophet, or what He removed from him as hardship regarding what was ordained for him, is the practice of those before him, and that does not mean that it must agree with it.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that the command of Allah has been written and decreed, by His words: ﴿and the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾. And is the intended "command" here the creational (kawni) or the legislative (shar'i)? The creational.
Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear no one except Allah﴾. Based on the author's i'rab (grammatical analysis) that ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for His words ﴿those who passed away before﴾...
* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the praise of the earlier messengers, by His words: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him﴾.
* And among its benefits as well: praise of whoever conveyed any part of the law of Allah from among non-messengers. The reason for this is that the messengers were only praised because they conveyed the message and did not fear anyone, so whoever is like them in this is worthy of praise.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that among the attributes of the messengers, peace be upon them, is that they do not fear anyone in conveying the message; rather, they fear Allah in failing to convey it. They do not fear people in conveying it, and they fear Allah in failing to convey it.
* And among its benefits: that conveying the message is from the fear of Allah, for had it not been for the fear of Allah they would not have conveyed His message.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of messages in those who came before, by His words: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾. Know that there is no nation among the nations except that Allah sent to it a messenger, so that the argument against Allah would be void and the excuse would be removed.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that the protection of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, is at its utmost degree of protection, by His words: ﴿and Allah is sufficient as a reckoner﴾. This is if we take "al-hasib" to mean the Guardian (al-hafiz), the sufficient, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿and whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [at-Talaq 3]. But if we take "al-hasib" to mean the One who calls to account (al-muhasib), then a benefit is derived from it, namely the perfection of Allah's reckoning of His servants, and that nothing escapes Him.
* It is derived from the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, by His words: ﴿and Allah is sufficient as a reckoner﴾. Whether we take "al-hasib" to mean the one who calls to account or the Guardian, there is no reckoning except with knowledge, and no protection except with knowledge.
* * *
* Student: (...) ﴿Those who convey﴾: the present tense verb (yuballighun, "they convey") indicates continuity.
* Shaykh: No. It may also indicate the description of a state, a narration of the state (hikayat al-hal). Did you not know that the present tense verb is used for something past by way of narration?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What the author pointed to.
* Student: The generality of the verse in what Allah ordained for him is lawful, meaning, this one, a person does not have... absolutely.
* Shaykh: What kind?
* Student: A person in things...
* Shaykh: Permissible ones.
* Student: He does not have absolute freedom.
* Shaykh: This is the basic principle, but we mentioned during the explanation that a person should take into account the feelings of people in some matters.
Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [al-Ahzab 40]. ﴿Ma﴾ is a negation particle. Is it Hijazi (operating like laysa) or non-operating?
The answer: non-operating, because the operation belongs to (kana) and not to it.
﴿Muhammad was not...﴾, meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿the father of any one of your men﴾. He did not say, "What was the Messenger of Allah," but said, ﴿Muhammad was not﴾, speaking of him as a person among the people. Then He said afterward, ﴿but the Messenger of Allah﴾, thereby affirming for him the messengership.
And His words, ﴿Muhammad was not the father of any one of your men﴾: ﴿father﴾ is with an alif (abā), because it is the predicate of kāna. ﴿The father of any one of your men﴾. So he is not the father of Zayd, meaning his biological father, so marrying his wife Zaynab is not forbidden to him.
His words, ﴿Muhammad was not the father of any one of your men﴾: is this by adoption (tabanni) or by adoption and birth? By adoption and also by birth, because the Messenger ﷺ's three sons all died before reaching manhood; they all died while still young.
Some scholars said: the intended meaning of ﴿the father of any one of your men﴾ is by adoption, because He said ﴿from your men﴾, attributing the men to them, and did not say "the father of any one of the men." On this view, there is no evidence in the verse that he is not the father of any man by lineage or by adoption. This is the closer view: that the intended meaning of ﴿the father of any one of your men﴾ is by adoption, in order to negate what was well known among them, that Zayd ibn Harithah was a son of the Messenger ﷺ.
His words, ﴿Muhammad was not the father of any one of your men﴾, have already passed with us earlier, along with ﴿and his wives are their mothers﴾. Some of the early generation (salaf) recited: "and he is a father to them." How is this reconciled with this verse?
The reconciliation is to say here: he is not the father of any of the men by adoption, but he is a father to the believers in terms of teaching, guidance and direction.
﴿But the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets﴾. ("But" ﴿wa lakin﴾ ... "was" ﴿kana﴾ ... ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾.) The author informed us that ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an omitted verb whose estimated form is "was" (kāna): "the Messenger of Allah."
﴿Rasul﴾ means: one who is sent (mursal), i.e., sent by Allah, mighty and majestic is He, to His servants.
﴿And the seal of the prophets﴾: meaning, "and he was the seal of the prophets" (so no son of his who is a man after him would be a prophet). This explanation that the author adopted is open to scrutiny, because he says, "the seal of the prophets," therefore there is no son of his after him who is a man and thus a prophet. This is based on the premise that a prophet's son must be a prophet after him, and this is not necessary, for not all prophets' sons became prophets. It is true that many prophets had sons who became prophets, such as Abraham, for example, but this does not mean that every prophet, from the fact of being a prophet, must have prophet sons if he leaves children behind.
Rather, the meaning of His words, ﴿the seal of the prophets﴾, is that there is no prophet after him. This is the meaning of the verse, which admits of no other.
﴿And the seal﴾ has two readings: one with a kasra (khatimi) and the other with a fatha (khatama). In my view, it is with the kasra: ﴿and the seal of the prophets﴾, as an active participle (ism fa'il), meaning the one who seals them. In the reading with a fatha on the ta', as the instrument of sealing, meaning the one by which something was sealed, the ﴿khatam﴾ is the ring (al-khatam), which is what a thing is sealed with, like the ring worn on the finger on which the owner's name is written. When one wants to seal a letter, one seals it with this ring.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is both khatim (seal, one who seals) and khatam (that by which the seal is made): khatim because he is their last, and khatam as if the messages were stamped by him, so that no message can come after him. This is the benefit of the two readings.
His words, ﴿and the seal of the prophets﴾: as you see in the Qur'an, and in the Sunnah too there are many proofs indicating that he is the seal of the prophets, peace be upon them, and on this basis there is no prophet after him.
If you say: Has it not been established that Jesus, peace be upon him, will descend at the end of time while being a prophet?
The answer: Yes, he will descend as a prophet, but Jesus's prophethood has not been renewed. Rather, he was a prophet before he was raised up, and his prophethood was not renewed after the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the seal of the prophets.
Will Jesus come with a new law? No. If you say: Does he not impose the jizyah, break the cross, kill the swine, and accept nothing but Islam?
The answer: Yes, and these rulings differ from the present rule of the law. Does that mean he brings new rulings? The answer: No, because the Prophet ﷺ's report of that is an affirmation of it, so it becomes part of the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ. It is well known that the Sunnah of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is his saying, his action and his tacit approval. So when he said that about Jesus, affirming it, it became part of his Sunnah. Then Jesus did not come with a new prophethood, nor did he come with a new legislation, and there is no difficulty in that.
﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾. ﴿Kana﴾ refers to the past. What about now? No. So ﴿kana﴾ here has its time stripped away, and it is used only to establish the attribute, which is knowledge.
(﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾: from His knowledge that there is no prophet after him.) That is: among the knowledge that Allah, exalted is He, knows that there is no prophet after him. That is why He said: ﴿but the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab 40].
And His words, ﴿of all things, Knowing﴾: does it include even the deeds of the children of Adam? Yes: ﴿And We have created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16], before he does it.
He said: "When the Master Jesus descends, he will rule by his law." ("When the Master descends"): did Allah describe him as "sayyid" (master)?
* Student: Yes, ﴿and a master and chaste﴾ [Al 'Imran 39].
* Shaykh: Who is this? Is it not Yahya? Did Allah not describe him as sayyid in Surah Al 'Imran? ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near (45). And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾ [Al 'Imran 45–46].
* Student: ﴿Distinguished﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿Distinguished﴾. But He did not say "sayyid." In any case, I fear that this word has entered the author's speech from the expressions of the Christians, for they constantly say "the Master Messiah, the Master Messiah." There is no doubt that he is a master, peace be upon him, because he is one of the prophets.
He says: "He will rule by his law," and then he does not bring a new law, so it does not contradict the verse: ﴿and the seal of the prophets﴾.
You know that two objections arise regarding the matter of Jesus's descent:
First: that he is a prophet, so how can he be a prophet when the Messenger is the seal of the prophets?
Second: that some rulings of the law would be changed by him, and we have answered that.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 36–40 (part 1 of 4):

﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 36] ﴿مَا﴾ here is negating. ﴿كَانَ﴾ is a past defective verb (kana al-naqisah), and its predicate is ﴿لِمُؤْمِنٍ﴾, the prepositional phrase. ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ is its postponed noun (ism).

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ meaning: this is a matter that cannot be. It negates possibility, but it is the legislative (shar'i) impossibility, not the decreed (qadari) one. A believing man or woman may have a choice in their affair regarding what Allah and His Messenger have decreed, but in the law this is not permitted.

He says: (﴿﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا﴾ ﴾ ﴿﴿أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ ﴾ with the taa' and the yaa' (both readings) ﴿﴿لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ ﴾ meaning: the choice ﴿﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ ﴾ contrary to the command of Allah and His Messenger).

His words ﴿لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ , as previously mentioned, include both males and females: ﴿لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾.

His words ﴿إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا﴾: the qada' (decree) here means the legislative decree, because the universal decree (al-qada' al-kawni) cannot be opposed by anyone, believer or disbeliever. Is that not so? Because the universal decree must come to pass. So the meaning here of ﴿إِذَا قَضَى﴾ is a legislative decree.

His words ﴿إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ join the Messenger with a waw, because the Messenger's legislative decree (ﷺ) is part of Allah's decree.

His words ﴿إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا﴾: is ﴿أمرًا﴾ here the singular of "matters" (umur) or the singular of "commands" (awamir)? It is the singular of "matters," meaning: if He decrees an affair, whether that affair is a command or a prohibition.

﴿إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا﴾ ﴿﴿أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ ﴾ and ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾: with the taa' reading the matter is clear, because its subject (ism) is feminine, so the verb is feminized on its account ﴿﴿أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ ﴾.

As for the yaa' reading, the verb is masculine even though the subject is feminine, but here feminization is not required, for two reasons:

The first reason: a separation between the verb and its subject, and here it is between the verb and its ism.

The second: the feminine marking in al-khiyarah is a metaphorical (majazi) feminine. Ibn Malik says:

*"It is obligatory to feminize the verb only with a connected pronoun, or with a noun that is clearly feminine by its nature."*

His words ﴿الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ mean the choosing. The author has informed us that al-khiyarah here is a verbal noun (ism masdar) meaning "choosing," or meaning "selecting," like al-tiyarah meaning "taking omens" (tatayyur). So it is a verbal noun meaning "choosing." If you wish, say: meaning "selecting."

His words ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾: someone may say that the expected wording would be "min amrih" (from his affair), since ﴿لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ is singular, and the expected sentence would be: "It is not for a believing man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have a choice in their affair." But it is plural, because (mu'min) and (mu'minah) occur indefinite in a negated context, which gives generality, so the pronoun returns to them according to meaning, not according to wording.

His words ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ mean: from their affair. It is also possible that ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ means: from the command of Allah to them. On the first reading the idafah (construction) is of the type where a thing is attributed to its agent; on the second it is attributed to its object.

The author's words (khilafa) are in the accusative here, as an object of al-khiyarah in the sense of choosing. That is, it was not for them to choose against the command of Allah and His Messenger. Now the meaning of the verse is clear: Allah says that it is not possible for a believing man or woman, not possible in the law or in the decree? In the law. When Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, they may not oppose the command of Allah and His Messenger, nor choose contrary to it. Why is it impossible? Because the faith in their hearts prevents them from opposing it. Do you not see the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer"? Because if faith were in his heart at the time of fornication, he would not have fornicated. "A thief does not steal while he is a believer"? [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6810) and Muslim (57/100), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] So when faith settles in the heart, its possessor cannot oppose the command of Allah and His Messenger.

The author said: (It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh and his sister Zaynab, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) proposed for marriage on behalf of Zayd ibn Harithah. She disliked that when she learned of it, having first thought that the Prophet (ﷺ) had proposed to her for himself; then she was pleased, following the verse).

Thus the author mentions that it was revealed concerning this story, and this story is weak, because it is mu'dal (a chain with two or more consecutive narrators missing) and munqati' (disconnected), so it is weak. In truth we are not concerned with the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul). The occasion of revelation does have benefit, in that it sometimes reveals and clarifies the meaning. But what matters is the ruling: it is not possible for a believer, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, to choose contrary to the command of Allah and His Messenger, ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾. This is because they must agree with the command of Allah and His Messenger, due to the faith in their hearts. For this reason, whenever a believer intends a sin, his faith reminds him of Allah and he refrains. Do you not see the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about the seven whom Allah will shade in His shade? He said: "A man whom a woman of rank and beauty invited" [to sin]. And this invitation was in a secluded place where no one saw them but Allah, yet he said: "Indeed I fear Allah." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (660) and Muslim (1031/91), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] So what prevented him? His faith prevented him from committing the immorality, despite the ease of its causes. Likewise, "one of the three men whom the cave closed upon, when his cousin let him have her, and when he sat between her legs as a man sits with his wife" (I believe that in this situation desire would be intense and strong, and only strong faith would restrain it), she said to him: "O man, fear Allah, and do not break the seal except by right." So he got up from her, although she was the most beloved of people to him. [Narrated by al-Bukhari (2215), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.] This is from faith, without doubt.

So we are not concerned whether it was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh and her brother 'Abd Allah or about others.

What matters is that the state of the believer prevents him from opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger. As for what the author mentioned, he says: "The Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to Zaynab bint Jahsh" [al-Hakim (6933) narrated with his chain from 'Umar ibn 'Uthman al-Jahshi, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was among those who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); she was a beautiful woman. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to her on behalf of Zayd ibn Harithah, and she said: "I do not accept him." She was the unmarried woman (ayyim) of Quraysh. He said: "Indeed I have accepted him for you," and the hadith continues.] She had been proposed to, as others have mentioned, by noble men of standing, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) proposed to her, so they thought he had proposed to her for himself. Then afterward he made clear to them that he had proposed her for Zayd ibn Harithah. Who is Zayd ibn Harithah? He was the freed client (mawla) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). According to what the historians (ahl al-siyar) mention, he had been a slave of Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she gave him to the Prophet (ﷺ), who freed him. When she learned that he had proposed her for Zayd, she refused. When the verse was revealed, she accepted that. This is not strange for the Companions, if the hadith is sound: it is not strange that they would give precedence to the command of Allah and His Messenger over what their souls desire.

* Student: (...) The Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to her, and (...) for Zayd. What is the meaning of (wa'anna)?
* Shaykh: 'Anna (to mean "concerning").
* Student: And 'anna?
* Shaykh: No, we do not have (ʿadā) and (ʿanā) here. ("The Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to her for Zayd ibn Harithah, and she disliked that.") I think it is not important. Cross it out.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا مُبِينًا﴾ [Al-Ahzab 36]: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾ ﴿مَنْ﴾ is an interrogative noun?!
* Student: Conditional.
* Shaykh: What made you know it is conditional?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: No, other than the answer.
* Student: The protasis verb (fi'l al-shart).
* Shaykh: The protasis verb, because it is jussive. ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾ but it is jussive by the deletion of the weak letter: ﴿مَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾. Disobedience (ma'siyah) is opposition to the command, or if you wish, say: disobedience is the opposite of obedience (ta'ah), whether it is committing what is forbidden or abandoning what is commanded. But when obedience and disobedience are mentioned together, obedience means doing what is commanded and disobedience means doing what is prohibited.

When it is said alone, "disobedience" or "obedience" alone, it includes both.

He says: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾, whether one disobeys both together, meaning a command from Allah and a command from His Messenger, and disobedience occurs in it, or one disobeys Allah alone or the Messenger alone, he has indeed gone astray with a clear straying. An example of disobeying both is His saying: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ [At-Taghabun 16], and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When I command you with a matter, do of it what you are able." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7288) and Muslim (1337/412), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] If a person opposes this, he has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger, because the command here is from Allah and from His Messenger. Sometimes a command comes in the Qur'an without the Sunnah, so if a person disobeys it he becomes a disobeyer of Allah. And sometimes it comes in the Sunnah without the Qur'an, so if a person disobeys it he becomes a disobeyer of the Messenger.

But know that disobedience to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is disobedience to Allah, because the Messenger speaks on behalf of the one who sent him. If you disobey him, you have disobeyed the one who sent him. If a man came to you and said: "So-and-so has sent me to you, and he says: Let him do such-and-such," and you opposed the messenger, you would in reality be opposing whom? The sender. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ﴾ [An-Nisa 80] ("Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah"). So whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, whether individually or jointly, is in the same position.

﴿مَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا مُبِينًا﴾: this is the apodosis of the condition, and it is joined with the fa' (fa'), because it is joined with ﴿قَدْ﴾. There are rules for the apodosis that must be joined with the fa', which were recited to you before. What is this verse?
* Student: 
*"Nominal, imperative, and the jamid (non-derived) verb, with ma, lan, qad, and with the future particles (sawfa, sa)."*
* Shaykh: Yes.
*"Nominal, imperative, and the jamid verb, with ma, lan, qad, and with the future particles."*
How many? Seven. If the apodosis is one of these seven things, it must be joined with the fa' obligatorily. Only a rare thing departs from this rule, such as the poet's saying:

*"Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them..."*

He did not say "fa-Allah yashkuruha" (then Allah rewards them). But this is rare, or a poetic necessity. Here, among the seven, we have ﴿قَدْ﴾: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا مُبِينًا﴾. The author said (mubinan) with the kasra. We have said before that (abana), the quadriliteral, can be transitive and can be intransitive. If it is intransitive, it means (bana), and its active participle is (bayyin), not (mubin). If it is transitive, it means (azhara), to make clear.

Here he said: ﴿ضَلَالًا مُبِينًا﴾. Can it mean (azhara), "a straying that makes [something] manifest"? It cannot.

So it is from the intransitive (abana), whose active participle is bayyin, not mubin.

As for "not mubin in the sense of manifest": what is mubin in the sense of manifest? Like His saying: ﴿إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [Ya-Sin 69] ("It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an"). Is this intransitive or transitive? Transitive, certainly, because the Qur'an makes realities manifest. For this reason He said after it: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 70] ("That it may warn whoever is alive and the word may take effect against the disbelievers").

﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا مُبِينًا﴾.

He says: (So the Prophet (ﷺ) married her to Zayd. Then after some time his gaze fell on her, and his love for her reached his soul, while Zayd's dislike for her grew. Then he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I want to divorce her." He said: ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ﴾ ("Keep your wife"), as Allah said: ﴿وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 37] ("And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor").)

What the author mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him, has been related from some exegetes of the early generations and later ones. But as Ibn Kathir said, these are reports that one should dismiss, because they are false statements that do not befit the station of the Prophet (ﷺ). When a person reads the story, he imagines that the Messenger (ﷺ) was a lover among lovers. Such a false story is like the story of Dawud (peace be upon him), in which they claim that Dawud asked one of his soldiers to let him marry his wife, but he refused, so he devised a trick against him. Look how? What was the trick? He said: "We will send him out with the army so that he will be killed, and then I will marry his wife." Could this happen from a prophet of Allah? Never. If someone said that it occurred from one of the common people, it would be said: how unjust this man is, and how ignorant! How much more so from a prophet of Allah!

Could anyone imagine that the Messenger (ﷺ) fell in love with this woman? Note that some people, and even some exegetes, may Allah protect us, have begun to utter this phrase: "The Messenger loved the woman Zaynab." But this is a false statement. Later, if Allah wills, in discussing the interpretation of the verse, the meaning of the verse will be explained: it is clear and plain. The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) did not say to him: ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 37] ("Keep your wife and fear Allah") while concealing his love for her. Because Allah said in the same verse: ﴿وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ﴾ ("And you concealed in yourself what Allah was to disclose"). Allah made clear that He would disclose what he had concealed in himself. If what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) concealed in himself was love, Allah would have disclosed it. But what did Allah disclose? What He disclosed was his marriage to her, that He married her to him. So the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) had concealed within himself what Allah had informed him: that he would marry her, without any love or relationship. But the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) knew, through what Allah had informed him, that he would marry her. So when this man came to consult him, he said: ﴿اتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ ("Fear Allah"), do not divorce the woman. Then Allah rebuked His Messenger: why did he say to him, "Fear Allah and keep her," when he knew that Allah would marry him to her? The matter is clear, with no difficulty in it.

The problem, however, is that some exegetes take from one another without scrutiny and without reflection on the matter. Some people even apologized and said: a person's love for a woman, even if she is with another husband, is not something to be denied. What is denied is attempting to reach this woman by an illegitimate means. As for a love for a woman who is married to another falling into one's heart, there is no harm in it, and it is something that nature and temperament may prompt. And although this matter needs examination regarding this view, which is that a person's love for another man's wife is either love for the category (jins) or love for the individual (shakhs). If it is love for the category, is that permissible or not? It is permissible. I do not mean by category sexual desire, I mean the category of this sort of women. This is what I mean by "category": if it means that he desires women of this kind, there is no harm in it. A person, whenever he hears, for example, that a man's wife is righteous, devout, and guards the unseen what Allah has entrusted, loves her and wishes to have one like her.

As for personal love, in my view its permissibility is doubtful. A person who becomes attached to a woman with a personal attachment or personal love must try to free himself from it, because it is a problem. Love in reality is alluring; love is like an iron chain that draws a person. When his heart becomes attached to a woman, the usual outcome is that he tries to reach her. If she is unmarried, he may propose to her; if she is married, it is a problem.

So what I see in this matter is that if he loves her with a love of category, meaning he loves the kind of woman she is, there is no doubt that there is no obstacle and no harm arises from it. But if he loves her with a personal love, the matter is serious.

* Student: What do you mean?

* The Shaykh: He means that he loves this woman herself. For example, her husband saw that she performs her duties and he loved her personally.

﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah."﴾ [al-Ahzab 37] ﴿When﴾ (idh). The author says: "It is in the accusative governed by (udhkur, 'remember'). Where is (udhkur)? It is omitted; it is in the accusative governed by an omitted (udhkur), meaning: remember, O Muhammad, ﴿when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ and so on. Remember this statement so that you are prepared for the admonition that will be conveyed to you, because Allah, the Exalted, admonished him in this verse with a great admonition, to the extent that 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "If Muhammad (ﷺ) had concealed any part of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse."[[Narrated by Muslim (177 / 288) from the hadith of 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.]]' As you will see."

﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself"﴾ (the one on whom Allah bestowed favour with Islam, and you bestowed favour with emancipation).

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear that this man, whose name is left unspecified here and then clarified later, has two favours upon him: the first favour is from Allah, and the second is from the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Here He said: ﴿the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you [bestowed favour]﴾, using the conjunction waw, which indicates joint participation. This is not a matter of legislation (shar') or lawmaking (tashri') that would allow us to say that it is permissible to associate Allah with the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rather, this is a matter of blessing, giving and grace. So how did He combine the Messenger's favour (ﷺ) and Allah's favour with the conjunction waw that indicates association?

The answer is that He combined them with the waw that indicates association, because the two favours are different. The first favour is what? Islam. The second is the favour from the Messenger (ﷺ), namely emancipation. Since the two favours differ, the waw no longer indicates sharing, because sharing between two different things is impossible.

(﴿...to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour﴾ by emancipation. He was Zayd ibn Harithah, who was one of the captives of the Jahiliyyah. The Prophet (ﷺ) bought him before the Prophethood, freed him and adopted him.) It is well known that Zayd ibn Harithah, may Allah be pleased with him, was a slave of Khadijah, and she gave him to the Prophet (ﷺ). This is what is known in the biographies (sirah).

Whatever the case, Zayd ibn Harithah was a slave of the Messenger (ﷺ), then he freed him and also adopted him. He raised his status by adding him as a son to himself, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad, until Allah nullified that in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab 40], and in His saying: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body, and He has not made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ [al-Ahzab 4].

(Say: ﴿"Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah"﴾ regarding the matter of divorcing her.) ﴿Keep to yourself﴾: here (amsik) is followed by (ʿalā), because it means "hold down upon yourself your wife," i.e., keep her attached to you and do not part from her.

﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾, and what is meant is Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her. Zayd had married her on the advice of the Prophet (ﷺ), then he came to consult him about divorcing her. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾, meaning: do not divorce her. And he commanded him to fear Allah, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, as an encouragement for him to keep her. Although the man had not committed a sin, since divorce is permitted for men, this was by way of encouraging him to keep her.

Some exegetes said: he (i.e., Zayd ibn Harithah) mentioned Zaynab with a fault, so the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ﴿fear Allah﴾, meaning: do not describe her with a fault. The meaning is not "fear Allah by not divorcing her," because the basic ruling on divorce is that it is permissible: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾. The conjunction waw is a particle of coordination. ﴿And you concealed﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿you said﴾, meaning: and remember also when you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. Allah left unspecified what he concealed, but He made clear that He would disclose it. Let us see what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, disclosed.

﴿And you concealed within yourself that which﴾: this is a relative noun (ism mawsul) in the accusative position as the object of ﴿you concealed﴾, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the subject (mubtada') and ﴿is to disclose it﴾ is its predicate. The clause is the relative clause (silah) of the relative noun and has no place in the i'rab. Meaning: you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. Here He did not say: "that which Allah will disclose," but He said: ﴿that which Allah is to disclose﴾. The clause here is nominal, and He used the nominal clause, which indicates permanence, as if this were a matter that must necessarily happen: Allah must disclose it, and this is what occurred. The meaning of ﴿is to disclose it﴾ is: make it manifest. It is the counterpart of His saying ﴿you concealed﴾. ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾: the counterpart is there, but the counterpart differs in form: the form for concealing came in the present tense, while the form for disclosing came in the nominal clause.

He said: (﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾ — manifesting his love for her and that if Zayd divorced her, you would marry her.) This is what the author claimed, following many exegetes, that what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concealed was his love for this woman, and Allah disclosed that. But if you reflect on the verses, you will find that what he concealed was the intention to marry her by the command of Allah, the Exalted. Allah commanded him to marry her after Zayd ibn Harithah. It seems, and Allah knows best, that this was to console her heart, since she had married Zayd ibn Harithah, who was a freedman, while she was of pure Arab lineage. So Allah, the Exalted, wanted to reward her for submitting to the advice of the Prophet (ﷺ) by having the Messenger (ﷺ) marry her. This is one aspect. On the other hand, Allah commanded him to marry her so that what was well known among them in the Jahiliyyah would be removed: what? That the adopted son's wife is not lawful for the one who adopted him to marry. This is clarification through action, which is stronger than clarification through speech.

He said: (﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾ — manifesting his love for her and that if Zayd divorced her, you would marry her.) When we look at what Allah disclosed, we find that it was his marriage to her, not that he loved her. Allah did not say in the Qur'an: "You love her," nor did He mention being inclined to love.

He said: (﴿And you feared the people﴾: meaning, you feared their speech and their talk, that they would say he married his son's wife.) This was regarded by the Arabs as a shameful matter; they considered it one of the abominations.

Allah, the Exalted, said: (﴿And Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ in all matters. Marry her and do not mind what people say.) Then Zayd divorced her and her waiting period ended. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her﴾ and so on.

Allah said: ﴿And you feared the people while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. Fear of whom? Of the people. But here He left it unrestricted. He said: ﴿and Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾, and He did not mention the object of comparison, for the sake of generality, because omitting it always conveys generality. Meaning: He has more right that you fear Him than anyone: than the people, than the jinn, and than others.

His saying ﴿that you fear Him﴾ means: that you be afraid of Him. But khashyah (dread) is fear accompanied by knowledge, as in His saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28]. Khashyah is also fear accompanied by the greatness and majesty of the One feared. Thus fear (khawf) is lower than khashyah, because fear can occur without knowledge, and because fear arises from the weakness of the one who fears, not from the strength of the one feared. For this reason khashyah is the higher rank and the stronger: ﴿and Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾.

(﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her﴾: a need. ﴿We married her to you﴾: so the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon her without permission, and he fed the Muslims bread and meat.)

* The student: "We have 'without permission' (bi-ghayr idhn)."

* The Shaykh: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her﴾, i.e., he had no need. This is evidence that Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, divorced her willingly, and that his need of her was fulfilled, and that he did not divorce her under pressure or compulsion.

His saying ﴿We married her to you﴾: is it legal or predestined? Both legal and predestined, but what matters is the legal. For if the intended meaning were only predestined, there would be no difference between her and the Mothers of the Believers, since the Mothers of the Believers were also married by Allah in predestination. Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "Your families married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3213) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is evidence that it was a legal marriage, but it is also predestined at the same time.

His saying ﴿We married her to you﴾: in this there are two pronouns as objects. The first pronoun is the kaf (you), and the second is �she, ha'. This follows the rule. Ibn Malik says:

"Put the most specific first in attachment,
and put whichever you wish first in separation."

The pronoun of the addressee is more specific than the pronoun of the third person; for this reason He said ﴿We married her to you﴾.

The wisdom behind this is His saying: ﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them﴾. ﴿So that﴾ (li-kay): the lam here indicates reason, and kay is a particle of the verbal noun, since after the lam it is purely a verbal particle, meaning "because." And (lā) is negation. His saying ﴿discomfort﴾ means: narrowness and hardship. His saying ﴿concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾: who are their adopted sons? Those whom they adopted. These are the adopted ones, and these adopted ones are not sons, as Allah said: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ [al-Ahzab 4].

Reflect on His saying: ﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾, and He did not say "their sons whom they adopted," because this sonship is void and invalid by the Law. For this reason He said ﴿their adopted sons﴾.

From this we learn that the view of those who say, regarding Allah's saying ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [an-Nisa' 23], that His saying ﴿from your loins﴾ is a restriction excluding the adopted son, is without basis. This is because Allah never called the adopted son a son; rather He negated sonship from him, saying: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾, and here He said: ﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾. Since the adopted son is not called a son by the Law, there is no need to add a qualifier to exclude him. Why? Because he is not included in the first place, so as to be excluded by this qualifier ﴿who are from your loins﴾. Rather, the qualifier is a restriction excluding the foster son, as is the view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him.

He said: ﴿So that there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them﴾. ﴿When they no longer have need﴾: the subject refers to whom? To the adopted sons.

His saying ﴿when they no longer have need of them﴾ contains an indication that if that had been by pressure from the adoptive father, there would have been discomfort in it. Rather, they must have fulfilled their need of them and ended their desire for them.

He said: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed﴾. ﴿The command of Allah﴾: the author said: "decreed and enacted." Is the command of Allah cosmic (kawni) or legislative (shar'i)? It is cosmic, because the legislative command may be carried out or may not be carried out, but the command that must be carried out is the cosmic command of Allah. When Allah commands something cosmically, it must come to pass.

The summary of this verse, or its explanation, is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminded His Prophet (ﷺ) of this great matter, namely His saying to Zayd ibn Harithah when he came to consult him about divorcing his wife: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah.﴾ This was while the Prophet (ﷺ) knew that Allah would marry her to him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, should at least have remained silent and said: "Consider what becomes clear to you in this matter." But he advised him to keep her. Why? Because he feared that people would say: he married his adopted son's wife. So the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was apprehensive about this matter, but Allah, the Exalted, directed him with this sound direction.

Then He, Exalted, said: (﴿There is no discomfort for the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾: what Allah made lawful for him) and so on.

﴿There was not﴾: (mā) is a negation, and (kāna) is a past verb of incomplete (nāqiṣ) type, and its subject is ﴿discomfort﴾. However, the extra (min) is in it; why? To establish the negation and emphasise it.

His saying ﴿upon the Prophet﴾ is its predicate, placed first.

﴿There was not upon the Prophet any discomfort in what Allah has ordained for him﴾. The meaning of ﴿in what He ordained﴾ is: in what Allah made lawful for him, whatever it is. So everything Allah makes lawful, there is no blame on him before Allah. If there is no blame on him before Allah, then it is not permissible for anyone to speak about what Allah has made lawful for him and say: why did he do it? Why did he act so? It will come, if Allah wills, in the lessons that this is general for the Messenger and for others.

His saying ﴿in what He ordained﴾: the verb (faraḍa) sometimes takes the preposition (li, for), and sometimes takes (ʿalā, upon). With (li), as in this verse: ﴿in what Allah ordained for him﴾; with (ʿalā), as in "Allah has ordained upon us such and such." If it takes (ʿalā), it means "obligated"; if it takes (li), it means "made lawful." Why? Because the basic meaning of (faraḍa) is "to determine," and what is determined may be obligatory or may be permitted.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿the way of Allah﴾, i.e., like the way of Allah. It is in the accusative by removal of the preposition. Meaning: Allah, the Exalted, negated discomfort from him in what was made lawful for him, because this is the way of Allah, the Exalted, with those who came before. ﴿The way of Allah﴾ means: His method, and the meaning is like the method of Allah, the Exalted, with the prophets who came before.

He said: (﴿Concerning those who passed on before﴾: from the prophets, that there is no discomfort upon them in that, as a widening for them in marriage) ﴿And the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾: its doing, ﴿a decree determined﴾: decided.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is like the other prophets before him; whatever Allah made lawful for him, there is no discomfort upon him in it. That is, there is no restriction either from Allah or from the servants of Allah. Likewise the earlier prophets had no discomfort in what Allah ordained for them; they did what they wished so long as the matter was lawful for them.

Then He said: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah﴾. The author said in its grammatical analysis: (﴿Those who﴾ is an adjective (na't) of the word before it.) Where is the word before it, "those who"? ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed on before﴾, i.e., concerning those who convey.

His saying ﴿who convey the messages of Allah﴾: the plural of risālah (message), and what is meant by it is that with which they were sent. They convey what (...) with it. Tabligh (conveying) means delivery, and from it is what came in the hadith: "There is no delivering for me today."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3464) and Muslim (2964 / 10), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

﴿And fear none except Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab 39]: because khashyah is an act of worship, and worship is only for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is the basic principle, although khashyah may sometimes not be worship; it may be natural fear which a person does not perform as worship for the one feared. Thus a distinction is made between a person's fear of people and a person's fear of Allah. He said: (So they do not fear the speech of people regarding what Allah has made lawful for them, and likewise in other matters.)

﴿And Allah suffices as Reckoner﴾: Preserver of the deeds of His creation and Reckoner of them. What is the grammatical analysis of ﴿Allah suffices﴾?

* A student: (...) a prepositional phrase (jār wa majrūr).

* Another student: (...).

* The Shaykh: As he said. Fine. And ﴿bi-Allāh﴾?

* The student: A superfluous particle.

* The Shaykh: A superfluous preposition. Continue.

* The student: "Allah" is the subject. ﴿Reckoner﴾?

* The Shaykh: Wait. The subject is what?! Is it in the accusative or in the genitive?

* The student: "Allah" is a subject in the genitive, marked by a kasrah instead of the nominative.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 36–40 (part 3 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Subject (fa'il). So it is not "ma huwa fa'il" (what is it?)... Then:
* The student: (...) implied (muqaddara).
* The Shaykh: No. Who knows? This i'rab (grammatical analysis) has come up for us many times.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: A fa'il in the nominative, marked by a presumed (muqaddara) dammah on its final letter.
* The Shaykh: The word Allah is a noun in the genitive, governed by the preposition bi (with).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: ﴿ḥasīban﴾ is a tamyīz (specification of a noun).
* The Shaykh: A tamyīz of what? Fine.

So, ﴿kafā﴾ takes bi as a superfluous (zā'id) preposition (ḥarf jarr), and this is common. It may also take the agent directly, as in the words of the poet:

*"Old age and Islam have sufficed a man as a restrainer (nāhiyan) ..........................."*

Here it did not take bi, but the more common usage is with bi.

* * *

He, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair.﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 36]

* From the benefits of this noble verse: The requirement of faith is that the believer not oppose the command of Allah and His Messenger, by His saying: ﴿It is not for a believing man...﴾ to the end.
* And from its benefits: Whenever faith grows stronger, compliance grows stronger. What is its basis? Because a ruling attached to a description grows with the strength of that description and weakens with its weakness. Accordingly, the third benefit follows: whenever faith diminishes and weakens, opposition increases. For this reason the people of knowledge said: faith increases through obedience and decreases through disobedience.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Whatever the Messenger ﷺ decreed of matters is as if Allah had decreed it, by His saying: ﴿when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter﴾.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: All good lies in what Allah and His Messenger have decreed, by His saying: ﴿that they should have any choice﴾, meaning they do not choose other than it, because they see that good lies in what Allah and His Messenger have decreed.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Disobedience is error, by His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾
* And from its benefits: Whenever disobedience is greater or more frequent, the error is more manifest and clear. Its basis is what we pointed out earlier: a ruling attached to a description increases with its increase and decreases with its decrease.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Disobedience to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is like disobedience to Allah, by His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ So if someone comes to us and we forbid him from a matter for which a prohibition has come in the Sunnah, and he says, "This is not in the Qur'an," what do we say to him? We say: "What is not in the Sunnah is not in the Qur'an either." The Prophet ﷺ anticipated this when he said: «Soon one of you will be reclining on his couch, and a matter from my commands will reach him, and he will say: "We do not know. Whatever we find in the Book, we follow." Indeed, I was given the Book and its like along with it.»[[Ibn Majah (12) narrated with his chain from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib al-Kindi that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Soon a man will be reclining on his couch, relating a hadith from my hadith, and he will say: 'Between us and you is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whatever we find in it that is lawful, we consider lawful, and whatever we find in it that is unlawful, we consider unlawful.' Indeed, what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made unlawful is like what Allah made unlawful."]]
What the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) anticipated has occurred. Indeed, they have openly declared that nothing is valid as evidence except what has come in the Qur'an. And as you have now seen: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you over them as a guardian.﴾ [al-Nisā' 80]
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The permissibility of joining Allah and His Messenger with "and" (wa) in legislative rulings. How so? ﴿when Allah and His Messenger have decreed﴾ and ﴿whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾. This is unlike cosmic matters (al-umūr al-kawniyya), in which the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is not associated with Allah using "and." For this reason, when a man said to him, "Whatever Allah wills and you will," he said: «Have you made me a rival to Allah? Rather: whatever Allah alone wills.»[[Al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad (783) narrated with his chain from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Whatever Allah wills and you will." He said: "You have made a rival to Allah. Rather: whatever Allah alone wills."]]
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood, by His saying: ﴿when Allah and His Messenger have decreed﴾ and ﴿whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾. The prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ is general for all of mankind from the time he was sent until the Hour is established. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But [he is] the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 40]. The seal has nothing after it. Because the Messenger's ﷺ law is general and comprehensive until the Day of Resurrection, it is suitable for every time, place, and nation. Its being suitable means that acting by it does not conflict with benefits (maṣāliḥ) at any time or place; rather, it is itself the benefit. This is not what some people have done, who twisted this expression, claiming that religion, or Islam, is "suitable for every time and place" in the sense that it is subject to every time and place. They made the Shari'ah a follower rather than the one followed. They said: if the age, in their opinion, requires a benefit, the Shari'ah does not oppose it. On this basis they built their approval (istiḥsān) of matters that are undoubtedly forbidden, such as permitting usury (ribā), claiming it stimulates the economy and strengthens the nation, and permitting insurance, which is in reality gambling (maysir), which Allah linked with wine, idols (anṣāb), and divining arrows (azlām), and other things that they consider part of the name of the Islamic religion on the pretext that Islam is suitable for every time and place.
We say: suitable (ṣāliḥ). We do not say: subject (khāḍi'). Act by Islam at any time, place, or nation and see for yourself whether it conflicts with benefits or fosters benefits. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾
Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor...﴾ to the end.
* From this noble verse is derived: Reminding the Prophet ﷺ of matters in which it is good to admonish, by His saying: ﴿And when you said﴾, where we said it is governed by an omitted verb whose implied meaning is "remember."
* And from its benefits: Showing Allah's favor upon Zayd ibn Ḥārithah through Islam and adherence to it, to the extent that when his father and uncles came seeking him, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave him the choice between them and himself, he chose to remain with the Messenger ﷺ.
* And from its benefits as well: Manumission is a blessing from the one who frees upon his freed person, and so it is. The scholars of inheritance (al-farḍiyyūn) express manumission in terms of blessing.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: It is permissible to join non-legislative matters with "and" when the meanings differ. We said that the Messenger is not equated with Allah with "and" in matters other than legislative ones. Here the Messenger's blessing has been joined to Allah's blessing with "and," even though it is not a legislative matter. What permitted this is the difference between the two blessings: the first blessing is Islam, and the second blessing is manumission.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: A wife is subordinate to her husband, by His saying: ﴿Keep for yourself your wife﴾. It is as if he holds her, guards her, and protects her, and as if she is subject to him, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you﴾ [al-Mā'idah 4].
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Consulting people of sound judgment, because Zayd consulted the Prophet ﷺ.
* And from its benefits: The one who is consulted must give what he sees, even if by his own ijtihad (independent reasoning), as what he sees to be best. The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) advised Zayd to keep her, by his own ijtihad, fearing that the hypocrites and polytheists would stir up trouble against him. But this does not mean that the one giving counsel is correct in what he decides. He may err in what he decides, but at the time of giving his advice he sees that this is correct.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: It is better for a husband not to hasten to divorce and to keep his wife, by His saying: ﴿Keep for yourself your wife﴾. So he advised him against divorce, although the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) had other aims. Nevertheless, this does not prevent there being several reasons for the command to keep her. It is known that Allah, mighty and majestic, said in His clear Book: ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good﴾ [al-Nisā' 19].
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Confirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood and that it is a true message, by His saying: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him.﴾ For if the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had been lying, which is far from him, he would have concealed such things, because they are difficult for him to bear.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, mighty and majestic, may act contrary to what the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) was inclined to. This means that the Prophet's ﷺ ijtihad may be contrary to what Allah, glorified and exalted, wills. By His saying: ﴿that which Allah is to disclose﴾, the Messenger concealed this matter within himself, but Allah acted against him in this and disclosed it.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The fear of people may occur from the prophets, but they are not left to persist in it, by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾.
* And from it: The obligation to give precedence to fear of Allah, mighty and majestic, over fear of anyone, by His saying: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. So it is obligatory upon a person not to fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah, and to fear Allah, mighty and majestic, in making the truth clear and acting upon it. He should not say: "People will mock me, people will ridicule me, people will make fun of me." Let it be so, for he gains nothing by this mockery and ridicule except elevation in the sight of Allah, glorified and exalted.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: A marriage is not valid until the first husband's right over the wife has completely ended, by His saying: ﴿And when Zayd had no longer any need of her, We married her to you﴾. So the marriage took place after Zayd had entirely finished with her. It is not an objection to this that the apparent meaning of the verse permits marriage immediately after divorce. We say: the need and the purpose do not end except with the end of the 'iddah (waiting period), since if a man wished to return to his wife during the 'iddah, and she was revocable (raj'iyyah), he could do so.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: Affirmation of Allah's greatness and sovereignty, by His saying: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾, because of His greatness and sovereignty.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The virtue of Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, since Allah, glorified and exalted, gave her in marriage to His Messenger ﷺ. What is its basis? Others were given in marriage to him by their guardians and families, but as for her, Allah, mighty and majestic, Himself arranged her marriage. This is a great distinction for her.
* And from its benefits: Allah, glorified and exalted, rewards His servant more than his deed. This woman, as has been mentioned, married Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, although Zayd was a freed client (mawlā), while she was of the pure Arab stock. This may have been a diminishment of her right and rank, so Allah elevated her standing by having His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ marry her, by Himself, blessed and exalted. There is no doubt that this is an elevation of her standing. Having been under this freed man, although she was of the pure Arab stock and there was some shame upon her in that, Allah raised her standing through this matter.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: What is established regarding the Prophet's ﷺ rulings is also established for his community. From where do we derive this? What is the basis for this?
* The student: The basis is that this ruling applies to him and to the Muslims.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Because this ruling was addressed to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), then... ﴿so there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them﴾. This shows that whatever rulings are established for the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) apply to his community as followers of him, unless evidence specifies otherwise.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The permissibility of a man marrying the wife of one he has adopted. From where is this taken? ﴿so there will be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾.
* And from its benefits: Adopted sons (ibn al-tabannī) are not legally called sons, and what Allah called them, by His saying: ﴿their adopted sons﴾ and His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your [true] sons﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 4]. From this benefit it follows that His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [al-Nisā' 23] — this qualifier is not to exclude an adopted son, because he was never included among the sons, such that he would need to be excluded.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: The cosmic command of Allah, mighty and majestic, must come to pass. The question is now directed to one person.
* A student: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever to be fulfilled﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 37].
* The Shaykh: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever to be fulfilled﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 37]. If someone says: "﴿amr Allah﴾ is a singular noun in the construct state, so it includes both the cosmic and the legislative command. How shall we answer him, when we have just restricted it to the cosmic command?"
* The student: That Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions legislative matters, and they are not realized.
* The Shaykh: Legislative. Correct.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done. Because a legislative command is not something that is carried out by everyone; there are some who do not carry it out.
Then He, exalted, said: ﴿There is no discomfort upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has ordained for him﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 38] to the end.
* From the noble verse is derived: There is no discomfort upon the Prophet ﷺ in what Allah has made lawful for him, even if it differs from what people are accustomed to, because of the generality of His saying: ﴿any discomfort﴾ and ﴿concerning that which Allah has ordained﴾; since (mā) is a relative pronoun, whatever Allah has made lawful for the Messenger, there is no discomfort upon him in it.
