His words ﴿then divorced them⁠﴾, without saying "and divorced them" or "so divorced them," show that if the divorce is delayed from the contract for a long time, the ruling does not change, just as if he divorces her immediately the ruling also does not change. So ﴿then divorced them⁠﴾ means: after the contract.

Divorce (talaq) linguistically means releasing the tether of a camel or similar; that is, removing the tether is called talaq. It is a noun of verbal noun (ism al-masdar) from (tallaqa). The verbal noun of tallaqa is tatlia, like kallama whose verbal noun is takliman, and the noun of the verbal noun is kalam. Tallaqa has the verbal noun tatliq, and the noun of the verbal noun is talaq.

So talaq linguistically is the removal of a tether. In terminology or in the Sharia, divorcing a woman means removing the bond of marriage, or part of it. If the divorce is irrevocable (ba'in), by which the wife is not made lawful again, it is the removal of the bond of marriage absolutely. If it is revocable (raj'i), it is the removal of part of it, since he may take her back.

His words: ﴿then divorced them before you have touched them⁠﴾ mean: before you have had intercourse with them. This is a case of euphemism (kinayah) for what is disliked to mention, by indicating it through something else. For this reason intercourse is not mentioned in its explicit wording in the noble Qur'an, but is alluded to in each place with what fits the context: sometimes expressed as "coming to" (al-ityan), sometimes as "going into" (al-ifda'), sometimes as touching (al-mass), sometimes as contact (al-mulamasah), and similar. All of this is using words that hearing does not find repugnant.

﴿before you have touched them⁠﴾: he said: (And in a reading: ﴿tumassuhunna⁠﴾), that is, "you have intercourse with them."

He says: ﴿then you have no right against them of a waiting period which you should count﴾. ﴿fama lakum⁠﴾: the ma here is negating, ﴿lakum⁠﴾ is a prepositional phrase functioning as a fronted predicate, and ﴿min⁠﴾ is a superfluous preposition for an additional meaning. We have said it is a superfluous preposition that is superfluous. Is the second word "superfluous" (za'id) an emphasis or an establishment?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: We say: it is a superfluous superfluous preposition. Is it emphasis or establishment?

* Student: Establishment.

* The Shaykh: Establishment. It is a preposition superfluous in wording, but it adds to the meaning. The first "za'id" is from za'ada (intransitive), and the second "za'id" is from za'ada (transitive). Where are you all in grammar, folks? Za'ada is a past verb, both transitive and intransitive. Are you with me? If I say: zada iman al-rajul — the faith of the man increased — is it transitive or intransitive? Intransitive. If I say: zadahum iman an — it is transitive.

So we say: this is a superfluous preposition from za'ada intransitive; za'id from za'ada transitive; that is, superfluous in itself, and adding meaning to something else.

The point is that His words ﴿min 'iddatin⁠﴾: min is a superfluous preposition in wording, not in meaning.

﴿'iddatin⁠﴾ is a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), nominative, marked by a presumed damma on its end, which could not be manifested because the position is occupied by the vowel of the superfluous preposition.

If someone said to us: may we make (ma) here a Hijazi negation? It is not permissible. Who says it is not permissible? Why?

* Student: Because it is fronted.

* The Shaykh: Because the predicate is fronted. Ibn Malik says:

...................... *** ma'a baqa al-nafy wa tartib zukin

His words: ﴿then you have no right against them of a waiting period which you should count⁠﴾. The author said: (you enumerate it).

﴿min 'iddatin⁠﴾: what is the 'iddah? 'Iddah linguistically is a noun taken from 'adad (number). In terminology or in the Sharia, it is a legally defined period of waiting, in life or after death, imposed on a wife separated from her husband, a waiting period of a wife separated in life or after death, legally defined. Legally defined what?

(﴿ta'taddunaha⁠﴾: you count it by menstrual cycles and other means) — by menstrual cycles if she is of those who have cycles, as its completion is three cycles; and (other means) if she is not of those who have cycles, namely pregnant women and those who do not menstruate due to young age or menopause. The pregnant woman's 'iddah is the delivery of the child, and the one who does not menstruate has an 'iddah of three months.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the meaning is that you entrusted your affair to Him and relied upon Him. This means: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ [Ghafir 44].

He says: (﴿So for you there is no waiting period for them which you should count, so provide for them⁠﴾: give them what they can enjoy, that is, if no dowry was named for them; otherwise they have only half of the named amount, as Ibn 'Abbas said, and al-Shafi'i held this view.)

His words: ﴿so provide for them⁠﴾. The fa is a conjunctive particle. ﴿Mattiuhunna⁠﴾ means: give them what they may enjoy. From where? From dirhams, from garments, from goods, from property, from any thing. Allah, glorified and exalted, made it absolute, just as it is absolute in quantity and in kind. Quantity — what do I give her? If I want to give her dirhams, how many do I give her?

﴿Provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]: according to the husband's circumstances.

His words: ﴿so provide for them⁠﴾ after His words: "if you divorce believing women, so provide for them" — excepted from this is the one for whom a dowry was named; for the one for whom a dowry was named, only half of it is obligatory, by the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified﴾ [al-Baqarah 237]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, explained that they have half of what was specified for them, and this applies when a dowry was named for her, whether little or much.

He said: (﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾) meaning, let them go without harm. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded two things: provision (tamti', ), which is giving wealth, and a fair release (al-sarah al-jamil), which is good conduct. This means the separation should be with consent, and with gentle words that console the heart. When a woman is divorced after the marriage contract was made but before the marriage was consummated, there is no doubt that her heart is broken and she is affected. People will ask: why was she divorced before he consummated the marriage? What is the reason? Did he find a defect in her? Did he hear something about her? This is especially so if she was also willing toward the husband, and he divorced her before he had been intimate with her. There will certainly be a reaction within her. So the Most Merciful of the merciful has commanded us to provide for them with wealth and to release them with a fair release, through kind words and good treatment. For example, we say to her: "This is a matter that was not decreed for us, and it is a matter that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed. I am not separating from you, for example, because of your bad character, or because I heard something bad about you, or anything similar to such speech," so that she parts from him in good spirits and with an open heart. Then whatever speech comes from her or from her family afterwards may be avoided. For if he divorces her without providing for her, or provides for her less than she deserves, or releases her in an unfair manner, speech may arise from her or from her family about the man, about his honor and his household, and similar things. This is one of the courtesies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with which He trained His servants. If a man divorces a woman before touching (al-mass, ), he is obligated to do two things: provision with what? With wealth, and a fair release through speech and action, a cheerful face and a relaxed heart, and similar things.

Someone may say: how can this be, since the man would not divorce her in this situation unless he disliked her without doubt? If he had even the slightest affection for her, he would have consummated the marriage and been intimate with her, and perhaps things would change. That is: if he has lost some interest in her, but there is still affection in his heart for her, would he take the risk of divorcing her before intercourse?

Reason does not require that. Reason requires that you wait and be intimate with her, because perhaps, what? Perhaps things will change. For this reason, divorce during menstruation (al-hayd, ) was forbidden, because when a man's wife is menstruating, he does not have intercourse with her, so he remains displeased with her, and there is no cause that calls for affection, which is intercourse. Therefore it was forbidden. This is one of the wisdoms behind the prohibition of divorce during menstruation, but it is not the only wisdom.

﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾. If Allah wills, its benefits will come later.

(...) The establishment of the Prophet's (ﷺ) prophethood, because of His saying...

* The student: (...)

* The Shaykh: No, the Prophet (ﷺ) is a bringer of good news in His saying: ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾; and from this it follows that he brought the causes that necessitate good news, namely righteous deeds and acts of worship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet (ﷺ) combined glad tidings with warning, because of His saying: ﴿a bringer of good news and a warner﴾. Before this benefit there is another: that he is also a warner. Being a warner and being a bringer of good news are two benefits, and combining them is a third benefit.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Messenger (ﷺ) is a caller to Allah, because of His saying: ﴿and a caller to Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: an indication that the caller must make his call to Allah, the Exalted, not to the advantage of his own self, because of His saying: ﴿a caller to Allah﴾, for this is the description of the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Among its benefits: that the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) call to Allah was by His permission, because of His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾. From this another benefit follows, which is Allah's approval of what the Messenger (ﷺ) was calling to. Is this not so? Because Allah does not permit except what He loves and is pleased with.

* Among them: that the Prophet's (ﷺ) call is based on the law of Allah.

(...) in its manner and in what he calls to, because of His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾. So he is a caller to Allah by His permission; that is, according to His command and by His law. He calls to the way of Allah with wisdom and good admonition, and he argues with them in the best manner. Likewise, he calls to the law of Allah and does not go beyond it.

* Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) cannot legislate from himself, because of His saying: ﴿a caller to Allah by His permission﴾, not by anything from himself.

* Among them: that what the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) calls to is from Allah. From this benefit follows that obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to the Messenger is disobedience to Allah. For this reason, when a woman came to Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "You say that those women who file their teeth for beauty are cursed by the Book of Allah, and I opened the Mushaf, or read the Mushaf from its beginning to its end, and did not find that." He said: "Yes." Then he recited the hadith to her, and recited the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7] [[Al-Bukhari (4886) and Muslim (120/2125), and the wording is his, with their chains from 'Abdullah who said: "Allah has cursed the tattooers and those who are tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair and those who have it plucked, and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah." He said: "This reached a woman from the Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, who used to recite the Qur'an. She came to him and said: 'A report reached me that you cursed the tattooers, those who are tattooed, those who pluck facial hair, those who file their teeth for beauty, and those who alter the creation of Allah.' 'Abdullah said: 'Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and who are in the Book of Allah?' The woman said: 'I have read what is between the two covers of the Mushaf and did not find it.' He said: 'If you had read it, you would have found it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it"...'" The hadith.]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of permission for Allah. What is permission? Is it "udhun" (ear) or something else?

Permission (idhn) is not ear (udhun). We affirm permission for Allah, the Exalted. Allah's permission, as was mentioned earlier in the tafsir, is divided into two types: legislative (shar'iyyah) and cosmic (kawniyyah).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought is a light, like a lamp that illuminates darkness, because of His saying: ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾.

* Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) has no shadow. Pay attention: this benefit needs discussion, or not? He has no shadow; that is, if he stood in the sun when it was inclined, there would be no shadow for him.

* The student: That is not correct.

* The Shaykh: Not correct, with ﴿a shining lamp﴾?!

* The student: The lamp is not (...).

* The Shaykh: A lamp illuminates, and it has no shadow.

* The student: A figurative illumination.

* The Shaykh: A figurative lamp. Otherwise, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) has a shadow like others, because he is a human being.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that everyone who judges by the law of the Prophet (ﷺ) is upon a shining lamp, right or not? Because of His saying: ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾.

* Among them: the virtue of the Prophet (ﷺ), in that Allah combined for him these great qualities: prophethood, messengership, witnessing, glad tidings, warning, and calling to Allah by His permission. How many is that? That is six, and the shining lamp makes seven.

Then He, the Exalted, said:
﴿And give glad tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾ [Al-Ahzab 47] ... to the end.

* From this noble verse it is derived: that the Prophet (ﷺ) is obligated to give glad tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And give glad tidings﴾. The command implies obligation, especially for the Prophet (ﷺ), since the command is always obligatory. Why? Because when Allah commands His Messenger to do something, He commands him to do it and to convey it to the people. Conveying the message by the Messenger (ﷺ) is obligatory. For this reason we say that the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is obligated to convey even the sunnahs, so he must inform of the sunnah and practice it until the conveyance is complete. After that, it becomes recommended for him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of faith. Its basis is that those who are characterized by it are the people of glad tidings, because of His saying: ﴿And give glad tidings﴾.

* Among them: the reward of the believers with this great bounty: ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾.

* Among them: an explanation of Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, favor upon the believers, and that the bounty is His bounty, because of His saying: ﴿that they will have from Allah﴾, not from anyone else. For this reason He placed ﴿from Allah﴾ first, though it is connected to ﴿a great bounty﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the reward for faith is greater than what the servant has done, from His saying: ﴿a great bounty﴾, and His saying: ﴿from Allah﴾. That is, it is derived from both. As for the first, it is derived from His saying: ﴿great﴾, and when something is described as great, it is very great. As for the second, He attributed the bounty to whom? To Allah: ﴿from Allah﴾. As the proverb says: "The gift is according to the status of the giver."

If this bounty is from Allah, it will be a bounty beyond imagination. For this reason, in the hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) taught Abu Bakr to supplicate with in his prayer, he said: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You and have mercy on me" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6326) and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. That it is from the presence of Allah carries a distinction.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [Al-Ahzab 48].

* The student: (...) love of Allah (...)?

* The Shaykh: Is that what we said, the virtue of faith in the first point?

* The student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...).

* The student: (...) and it was not shining?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because light is more complete, since it combines heat and illumination, so it has two attributes.

He said: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ ... to the end.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the prohibition of obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, but not absolutely. Rather, obeying them is forbidden in what contradicts the command of Allah. So if they command something that does not contradict Allah's command, obeying them is not forbidden. For example, if a disbeliever told you to make a key for this door, would we say it is forbidden for you to obey him? No. So do not obey them in what contradicts the command of Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is at its most eloquent. We find that in some places it mentions the hypocrites before the disbelievers, but in this verse it mentions the disbelievers before the hypocrites. This is because in the context of reward and in the context of blame, it mentions the hypocrites first: ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾ [An-Nisa 140], ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ [Al-Ahzab 73]. This is because the sin of the hypocrite is greater than the sin of the open disbeliever. Here, however, who opposes the Messenger openly? The disbeliever. For this reason He placed him before the hypocrite, because the hypocrite does not command contrary to the law as the disbeliever does, since he conceals his hypocrisy. Therefore He said: ﴿Do not obey the disbelievers﴾, beginning with them, because their opposition to the law is more clear and apparent than that of the hypocrites.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a prohibition may be directed at something that has not been done, lest it be done, from His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) did not obey them, but he was forbidden from obeying them lest he do so in the future.

* Among them: that a prohibition may come concerning matters that are remote or impossible. Its basis is: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, for this is remote or impossible for the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the disbelievers and the hypocrites, from His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾.

* Among them: the strengthening and consolation of the Prophet (ﷺ), from His saying also: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾.

* Among them: that it is the nature of the disbelievers and the hypocrites to harm the believers, from His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾. But someone may say: this is the harm to the Prophet (ﷺ).

We say: whoever harms the Prophet (ﷺ) harms the believers. Also, whoever opposes the messengers will oppose their followers and harm them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of patience upon the harm of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, from His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾, for this is a command to be patient with their harm.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of relying upon Allah, from His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, and the command implies obligation.

* Among its benefits: that the Prophet (ﷺ) does not possess for himself any benefit or harm, nor for others, all the more so. From His saying: ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾: he is in need of his Lord and is commanded to rely upon Him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the greatness of Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, sufficiency for those who rely upon Him, from His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾. We have mentioned earlier that this is meant to express wonder at the sufficiency of Allah for whoever relies upon Him.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them﴾ [Al-Ahzab 49] ... to the end.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the importance of marriage (nikah) and divorce (talaq), because Allah, the Exalted, opened it with the call that seeks to alert the one being addressed to what will be delivered to him.

* Among them: that adherence to the rulings of the law in marriage and divorce is one of the requirements of faith. Its basis: from His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, for it is one of the requirements of their faith that they carry out what they were commanded.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there is no divorce before marriage, from His saying: ﴿when you marry believing women, then﴾, and "then" indicates sequence. So there is no divorce before marriage. There is no difference in this between a divorce directed at a specific woman and one in general terms. So if a man says to a woman: "If I marry you, you are divorced," and then he marries her, she is not divorced, why? Because the divorce occurred before the marriage.

Likewise, if he says: "Every woman I marry is divorced," then when he marries a woman she is not divorced, because there is no divorce except after marriage.

* Among its benefits: there is no ila' (oath of abstention, ), no zihar (a form of divorce by likening the wife to a forbidden relative, ), and no prohibition on a woman except after marriage. Since divorce, which is the greatest separation, is only after marriage, then so is what is less than it, except that if a man prohibits a specific woman and then marries her afterwards, he owes an expiation of an oath (kaffarat yamin, ). Likewise, zihar, if he intends prohibition by it and makes zihar on a woman before marrying her, he owes an expiation of an oath, and he does not owe the expiation of zihar, because zihar is valid only from one's wife.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of divorce, from His saying: ﴿then you divorced them﴾. Allah did not blame the believers for divorce, and if it were forbidden, He would have blamed them for it.

* Among its benefits also: is divorce before consummation permissible or not? From His saying: ﴿then you divorced them before you had touched them﴾. This is a benefit other than (the permissibility of divorce in general), because divorce before consummation may involve some diminishment of the woman's right. So it is said: this man, had he not known that there was some affliction in her, would not have divorced her before he consummated the marriage and touched her, because the custom is that when a person marries, he marries out of desire. So if he divorces her before touching her, it is evidence that there is something in her.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that if he divorces her before intercourse, there is no 'iddah (waiting period, ) owed by her. There is disagreement about this. Some scholars, who are the majority (al-jumhur), hold that if he was alone with her (khalwah, ), then she must observe the 'iddah. They placed seclusion in the position of intercourse. This is what the Rightly Guided Caliphs ruled, and it is the position of the majority of the Companions, indeed the majority of the Ummah. Only a small group opposed this, among them al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, in his new opinion. He held that if he did not have intercourse with her, there is no 'iddah upon her, even if he was alone with her. There is no doubt that this is the apparent meaning of the verse. But what is transmitted from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, especially the Rightly Guided Caliphs, establishes that she must observe the 'iddah if he was alone with her.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of a provision (mut'ah) for a woman divorced before consummation. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿so provide for them﴾. This is qualified by another verse, which concerns the case where a dowry has been specified for her. If a dowry has been specified for her, then he owes only half of the dowry, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified a dowry for them, then half of what you specified [is due], unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:237].
* Another benefit of this noble verse: the use of euphemism for what is shameful to mention, based on His saying: ﴿before you have touched them﴾.
* Another benefit of this noble verse: that a woman widowed by her husband must observe the waiting period ('iddah) in all cases, even if he did not consummate the marriage with her. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾. God attached this ruling to what? To divorce. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait for four months and ten days﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:234] remains upon its general application: that a widow must observe the waiting period even if he did not consummate the marriage with her.
* Another benefit of this noble verse: the mercy of God, glorified and exalted is He, toward His servants and creation, in that He made the provision obligatory for the woman divorced before consummation. The reason is that it consoles her heart and removes the worry and grief that overcome her after the divorce.
* Another of its benefits: the obligation of releasing [the wife] in a good manner when parting, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and release them with a fair release﴾.
* Another benefit of this noble verse: that the waiting period is a right of the husband. Its basis is His saying: ﴿then you have no right over them﴾, so it is a right of the husband over the woman.
* Another of its benefits: that a person should keep count of his wife's waiting period, take care of it, and not leave her neglected, not knowing about her. This is based on His saying: ﴿that you count﴾. This is evidence that it is part of the duty of husbands to count their wives' waiting periods, keep track of them, and monitor them, because she is his bed as long as she is in the waiting period, if it is a revocable divorce.

Does the phrase ﴿when you marry believing women﴾ imply that if they marry women from the People of the Book, the ruling changes? No. Why? Because this is a qualifier that describes the usual case, and the scholars of usul (principles of jurisprudence) have mentioned that a qualifier describing the usual case has no implied meaning (mafhum). From where is this taken?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿believing women﴾, because this ruling covers believing women and others.

Also among its benefits: there is no waiting period for a divorce before consummation, even if a long time has passed, based on His saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾.

And another benefit in it: divorce is in the hand of the husband, based on His saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾. So neither the father, nor the grandfather, nor the paternal uncle, nor the maternal uncle, nor anyone else may divorce on behalf of a person.

And another benefit in it: there is no waiting period for a woman who is not divorced, such as one whose marriage is annulled by khul' (divorce initiated by the wife) or otherwise? Or is there some debate about this? What do you say about this benefit: that there is no waiting period for one who is separated during life by other than divorce?

* Student: It is not derived.
* The Shaykh: It is not derived. Why?
* The student: Because it did not say: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but in the case of divorce, its implied meaning is that the waiting period applies only to divorced women. This is the Prophet's ruling. If the waiting period is for divorced women, then the meaning is that khul'd women have no waiting period. What do you say, everyone?
* The student: Because (...) its attributes?
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Is it not, for example, ﴿Then if you divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them﴾? Its meaning is: if you divorce them after consummation, then they must observe a waiting period. So He made the waiting period one of the rulings of divorce. Fine, what about other than divorce?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, that is not possible, because divorce has its own rulings. For this reason they say: a widow must observe the waiting period even if her husband did not consummate the marriage with her.

In any case, it may not be apparent to everyone, but the preponderant view is that a woman separated by other than divorce has no waiting period. The woman who obtains khul' only needs to be cleared by one menstrual cycle, and then she is free to remarry.

Do we also say that the verse includes combining financial and practical kindness? From where?

* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: What is this? Is this financial or practical?
* Student: Practical.
* The Shaykh: Practical. And the financial?
* Student: ﴿so provide for them﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿so provide for them﴾.

Fine, there is also a benefit here: the verse excludes the woman for whom a dowry has been specified.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is there? Where?
* Student: In the explanation.
* The Shaykh: The explanation?
* Student: What is the benefit?
* The Shaykh: The benefit: the woman for whom a dowry has been specified receives half of the dowry, and the husband owes her no provision.
* The student: (...) provision for the one for whom no dowry was specified (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good.

(...) as an honour to him and a manifestation of his prophethood. His saying, ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you﴾, combines for him the two descriptions of prophethood (nubuwwah) and messengership (risalah) in an explicit manner. Had he been described with messengership alone, it would have implied the description of prophethood, because every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. Yet combining the two descriptions is preferable, for the sake of explicit textual specification. In the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Malik concerning the remembrance recited at sleep, the Prophet (ﷺ) taught him that when he goes to his bed he should say among what he says: "I believe in Your Book which You have sent down, and in Your Prophet whom You have sent." When al-Bara' repeated it back, he said: "I believe in Your Book which You have sent down and in Your Messenger whom You have sent." The Prophet said to him: "And in Your Prophet whom You have sent."[[Agreed upon. Al-Bukhari (247) and Muslim (2710/56), from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Why? The scholars said: so that the two descriptions of prophethood and messengership are combined for him in a specific manner. The indication of messengership on prophethood is of the type of *dalalat al-iltizam* (implicative indication, indication by necessary implication), whereas the indication of prophethood on prophethood is of the type of *dalalat al-nass* (explicit indication, indication by direct specification). This is one aspect. Another aspect: if one says "and Your Messenger whom You have sent," it is not explicit in faith in Muhammad (ﷺ), since it could be understood as referring to the angelic messenger rather than the human messenger. Here He says: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you﴾ and did not say "O Messenger, indeed We have sent you." Why? So that the two descriptions of prophethood and messengership are combined for him by way of specification and explicit statement. But look at His saying: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67], where He says "O Messenger," then says "convey," because He is commanding him to convey, and this suits messengership.

He said: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾ over those to whom you were sent. The word ﴿witness﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (*hal*) from the kaf (you) in His saying ﴿We have sent you﴾. The term "witness" (shahid) is applied to one who informs and is applied to a judge, and the Prophet (ﷺ) is a witness who informs and judges. He informs about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning what He sent him with; and likewise he informs about those to whom he was sent, regarding their acceptance or rejection. Likewise he is a judge, for judgment belongs to Allah and His Messenger. The evidence that *shahid* means judge is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And a witness from her own people testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars. (26) But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful."﴾ [Yusuf 26, 27]. Thus *shahid* means informant and judge. He informs about Allah and informs about the servants of Allah: he informs about Allah concerning what was revealed to him, and informs about the servants of Allah concerning their acceptance or rejection. Likewise he is a witness over those who came before him from the nations, regarding the conveying of the messages of the messengers and regarding their peoples' denial of them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. So he is a witness to what Allah revealed to him and judges by it, a witness over those to whom he was sent, and a witness over those who came before him from the nations.

His saying ﴿and a bearer of good tidings﴾ is coordinated with ﴿a witness﴾; that is, "and We have sent you as a bearer of good tidings." Good tidings (*bushrah*) requires four things: a bringer of good news (mubashshir), one to whom it is brought (mubashshar), the good that is announced (mubashshar bih), and a means that leads to the announced good. Four matters. The Messenger (ﷺ) is a bearer of good tidings. I said that good tidings must have four elements: a bringer, a recipient, the good announced, and a means leading to the announced good. So if the Messenger (ﷺ) is a bearer of good tidings, there must be those whom he gives good news to, namely those to whom he was sent and who followed him in what he called to. There must also be something announced, and what is the announced good?
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No. Paradise. The announced good is Paradise. It has preceded us in these verses: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab 47]. And there must be a means leading to the announced good. What is it? Righteous deeds.
So the Prophet (ﷺ) explained and conveyed the message to those receiving the good tidings, explained the announced good and what it contains of reward and various kinds of bliss, and explained the means leading to it, which are righteous deeds. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) left his community upon a clear path, its night like its day, from which none deviates except one who is destroyed.

﴿and a bearer of good tidings and a warner﴾. The warner (*nadhir*) is one who brings warning, and warning is informing coupled with intimidation. Information coupled with intimidation is called *indhar* (warning). In the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, describing the Prophet's (ﷺ) sermon: "It was as if he were a warner of an army, saying: 'He has come upon you in the morning and in the evening.'"[[Muslim (867/43) related with his chain from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon, his eyes reddened, his voice rose, and his anger intensified, until it was as if he were a warner of an army, saying: "He has come upon you in the morning and in the evening..." — the hadith.]]

As for His saying ﴿a warner﴾, we say about it what we said about ﴿a bringer of good news﴾ [al-Baqarah 119]: it requires four things: one who warns, and what else? One who is warned, the thing warned of, and the means that lead to it. All of these were brought by the Prophet (ﷺ). Who is the one warned? The Ummah in general. The thing warned of is the Fire, and its causes are evil deeds. The one who warns is the Messenger (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) explained all these matters: he explained to all those warned and conveyed the message to them, or fulfilled the trust, and likewise he explained what is warned of and its various punishments and painful torment.
It is permissible to say: "I warned him of that" or "I warned him from it."

He said: (﴿a bearer of good tidings﴾ to whoever believes you, of Paradise; ﴿and a warner﴾, one who warns whoever denies you, of the Fire.)

﴿and as one who calls to Allah﴾ to His obedience. ﴿and as one who calls to Allah﴾ by His command. This is the fourth description: ﴿a witness and a bearer of good tidings and a warner (45) and one who calls to Allah by His permission﴾ [al-Ahzab 45, 46]. This is the fourth description: ﴿one who calls to Allah﴾, meaning he calls people to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The author's words "to His obedience" are open to question; rather, it is better to leave the verse on its apparent meaning: the Prophet (ﷺ) calls to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to reaching Him in the abode of His honour, and there is no reaching Him in the abode of His honour except by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition. So he calls to Allah, the Exalted, by obeying Him and avoiding what He forbids.

His saying ﴿and as one who calls to Allah﴾ does not explain here the manner of the call, but He explained it in another verse, His saying: ﴿Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl 125]. The call necessarily also requires four things: a caller, one who is called, the thing called to, and the means that lead to the thing called to. All of this was brought by the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) used to call people secretly and openly, according to what the interest and need required. His call was first secret, because he feared that this call would be confronted and crushed; then after that he called openly when Allah said to him: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists﴾ [al-Hijr 94]. Then he began calling those nearest, ﴿and warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 214], then those farther away, according to what the call required.

His saying ﴿calling to Allah﴾ means: not to yourself. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself at all, except when the sanctities of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, were violated, for he was the most intensely angry of people for Allah's sake.[[Al-Bukhari (6126), with his chain from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was never given a choice between two matters except that he took the easier of them, as long as it was not sinful; if it was sinful he was the furthest of people from it. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself in anything, except when a sanctity of Allah was violated, then he took revenge for Allah."]] This is because he did not call to himself, as is found among many callers in reality, who call to themselves, wanting people to exalt them and to take their words, so that if they are opposed in that, you find the person becoming upset, not because the command of Allah was opposed, but because he himself was opposed. One whose condition is this calls to himself and not to his Lord. So examine yourself: is there in you any secret of this? If there is in you a secret of this, then correct the matter. And if you do not become angry except for Allah and are not pleased except for Allah, this is the true caller.

His saying ﴿to Allah by His permission﴾: the permission here includes both the *idhn kawni* (cosmic permission, by way of divine decree) and the *idhn shar'i* (legislative permission). If what is meant is what is called to, then it is the legislative permission; that is, if the meaning is "calling to Allah the Exalted by His command, which commanded you to call to it," then the intended is the legislative permission. If what is meant is "calling to Allah the Exalted by His decree," that is, insofar as He empowered you for that and prepared the causes for you, then this is cosmic permission. The verse includes both. The Messenger (ﷺ) calls by Allah's decree and destiny, and he also calls by His religion and law; he is a caller by both together.

He said: ﴿and as one who calls to Allah by His permission﴾. The fifth description: ﴿and as a radiant lamp﴾. That is, like it in being guided by it. ﴿Lamp﴾ (*siraj*) is what one is illuminated by. Do we call the thing before us a *siraj* or not?
Describing him as "radiant" (*munir*) is either to state the reality, since every lamp has light, or to state that this lamp had strong illumination, so that it illuminates what is around it. The latter is the closer, because among the established rules is that if a statement is uncertain between being *ta'sis* (establishing a new meaning) or *tawkid* (emphasis), the default is that it is *ta'sis*, because *ta'sis* adds meaning, unlike *tawkid*, which only adds strength. So on this basis the more apparent view is that this is a description of the lamp with regard to its strength and brightness. There is no doubt that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a sign by which one is guided in darknesses; he opened for people the light of knowledge and the light of faith, until he left his community upon a clear path, its night like its day.

These five descriptions that Allah the Exalted explained to His Messenger (ﷺ) can be supplemented with a sixth and a seventh description. The sixth is His saying ﴿Indeed We have sent you﴾, for this establishes messengership for him. The seventh is His saying ﴿O Prophet﴾, for this also establishes prophethood. On this basis, how many descriptions of the Messenger (ﷺ) does the verse include? Seven descriptions: prophethood, messengership, witnessing, bearing good tidings, warning, calling to Allah by His permission, and being a radiant lamp.

﴿and as one who calls to Allah by His permission and as a radiant lamp (46). And give good tidings to the believers﴾. This is a conjunction, but it specifies the one who receives good tidings in His saying ﴿a bearer of good tidings﴾. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾. "The believers" here is meant to include both believers and Muslims together, for it has already passed that when *iman* (faith) is mentioned alone, it includes *Islam*, and when *Islam* is mentioned alone, it includes *iman*; and when both are mentioned together, *iman* is in the heart and *Islam* is in the limbs. So His saying ﴿give good tidings to the believers﴾ did not say "give good tidings to the Muslims," because among the Muslims there are those whose Islam is outward, while faith in their hearts is either absent or weak. Those who have the unqualified good tidings are who? The believers, whose faith has taken firm root in their hearts and who act upon the requirements of faith. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. (62) Those who believed and were fearing Allah (63) For them is good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 62-64]. So unqualified good tidings are only for the believers.

His saying ﴿the believers﴾: whenever the word "the believers" comes alone, as I said a little while ago, it includes both the believer and the Muslim.

He said: "Give them good tidings ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾." What is it that puts "bounty" in the accusative?
* Student: ﴿That (anna)﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿That (anna)﴾; its noun is delayed. ﴿That they will have from Allah a great bounty.﴾ The great bounty is Paradise, and nothing is greater than the bounty of Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185]. There is no bliss greater than entering Paradise with what it contains, indeed the highest thing in it is looking upon the Face of Allah, blessed and exalted.

He said: ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty (47). And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. Since people are divided into three categories — believer outwardly and inwardly, disbeliever outwardly and inwardly, and believer outwardly but disbeliever inwardly — Allah explained these categories in His saying ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ after His saying ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾. Allah the Exalted links these categories in several places in the Qur'an. At the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah He mentioned the three categories, did He not?
In Surat al-Ahzab, when He mentioned the trust and its bearing, He mentioned the three categories. And here He mentioned the three categories: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ The disbeliever is everyone who disbelieves in Allah, whether his disbelief is through denial or through arrogance, since all disbelief revolves around these two matters: either denial, which is rejection, or arrogance against obedience. Whoever disbelieves in Allah and openly declares his disbelief is of the disbelievers; whoever conceals his disbelief is of the hypocrites. The hypocrite, then, is one who shows Islam and conceals disbelief, taken from *nafqa'* of the jerboa (*nafiqa' al-yarbu'*). The *nafqa'* of the jerboa is its burrow. The jerboa has a trick: it digs a hole in the ground, makes a door for it, and places a thin crust at the far end of the burrow, so that when it is trapped with its door, it breaks through this thin crust. Thus it is said: "the jerboa's *nafqa'*." The hypocrite's conduct is like this: when he is trapped, he does what lets him escape, but in hypocrisy, as Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].

﴿Do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ This prohibition is a prohibition against what has not yet occurred, lest it occur, and not a prohibition against what already exists, lest it continue; and there is a difference between them. It is a prohibition against what has not occurred, lest it occur, and not a prohibition against what already exists, lest it continue. If you say to someone, "O so-and-so, do not steal," while he is stealing, it is a prohibition against what already exists, lest it continue. If you say it to someone who has not stolen but intended to steal, or did not intend it, this is a prohibition against what has not occurred, lest it occur. So His saying ﴿and do not obey the disbelievers﴾ does not mean that the Messenger (ﷺ) was obeying them, far be that from him, but rather it is lest their harming him, their troubling him, and their embarrassing him should cause him to concede something of what he was commanded, in order to ward off their harm. Otherwise, the Messenger (ﷺ) could never obey the hypocrites or the disbelievers in disobedience to Allah. But the human soul may strive in some matter and see that it is in the interest to concede some things to ward off what is greater in the view of the one obligated, while the matter is not so.

For this reason He said: ﴿and disregard their harm﴾. Some exegetes said: the noun is attached to the object; that is, "do not harm them." Other exegetes said: it is attached to the subject; that is, "disregard their harming you, do not pay attention to it and do not be concerned with it." Which of them is more correct? The first or the second? Reflect. Have you understood the meaning?
﴿Disregard their harm﴾: that is, disregard your harming them, so it is attached to the object. Or ﴿disregard their harm﴾: disregard their harm to you, or disregard their harming you; do not be concerned with it and do not pay attention to them. The second is definitely correct?
Because the first is not valid: the Messenger (ﷺ) did not harm them; rather, he was harmed by them. So in this case is the verbal noun attached to the subject or to the object?

...to the agent. That is, leave their harm to you. This command is either a threat, or a confirmation and strengthening, or both. If it is for a threat, meaning the threat against these disbelievers and hypocrites, that is, "leave their harm to you, for Allah will avenge you against them," as shown by His words: ﴿And rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ Or the meaning is confirmation, that is, "leave their harm," meaning be patient with them. This is then a form of Allah's support for His Messenger ﷺ, by commanding him to leave their harm, not to concern himself with it, and not to care about it, because the final outcome will be for whom? For the Messenger ﷺ, even with this harm they inflicted upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

And His words: ﴿Leave their harm and rely upon Allah.﴾

* Student: What is the difference between kufr (disbelief) and shirk (association of partners with Allah)?

* The Shaykh: The difference between them is that kufr is more general. Every mushrik is a kafir, but not every kafir is a mushrik. A person may deny something of what Allah has revealed and thereby be a kafir without being a mushrik.

﴿And rely upon Allah.﴾ Tawakkul (reliance upon Allah). The scholars have stated various definitions of it, but the closest thing said about it is: true dependence upon Allah in obtaining benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him. This is the best of what has been said in explaining tawakkul, because when a person depends upon Allah in obtaining benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him, that becomes stronger for him and more reassuring to his heart. However, tawakkul does not contradict taking the legislated means (al-asbab al-shar'iyyah) that have been established either through the Sharia or through sensory observation. Whoever claims that this contradicts tawakkul has erred. That is because the Messenger ﷺ, there is no doubt, is the imam of those who rely upon Allah and the master of the sons of Adam, yet he would take the means. He would protect himself from the cold and protect himself from the heat, and protect himself from adversity or from danger. He would wear armor, as is clear on the day of Uhud when he wore two coats of mail. Yet it is never said that the Messenger, peace be upon him, was weak in tawakkul.

Therefore, taking the means is part of complete reliance upon Allah, because warding off what you fear occurs through two matters: one from you, and another from Allah. The hidden things which you cannot perceive and have no power over are from Allah, and the apparent things over which you have power are from yourself. So you must do this and rely upon Allah regarding what you do not perceive and what your mind cannot reach.

* Student: What is the limit of taking the means (...)?

* The Shaykh: If one is not able to do it, then whatever one is able to do of the sensory and legislated means.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: Tying (the animal's leg), the 'aql (hobbling) is done by tying one of its legs. That is why 'aql is not a full binding. 'Aql means tying the rope on one of its hands only. Sometimes they tie it on both hands, right? That is 'aql. But binding everything, its neck and its head, no.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Even if he says it?

* Student: I fear someone will come and cut it...

* The Shaykh: Whoever cuts this will cut this.

* Student: Or I fear it will move (...)?

* The Shaykh: That goes against the norm. That is, what custom has established is a means. And Allah knows best.

* * *

(...) Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs (wakil).﴾ ﴿Kafa⁠﴾ is a past-tense verb, as is well known. The ba' is a superfluous (za'id) preposition used to beautify the wording. ﴿Allah⁠﴾, the word of majesty, is the subject in the nominative case, marked by a presumed damma on its final letter, which could not be manifested because the position is occupied by the vowel of the superfluous preposition.

﴿Kafa⁠﴾ sometimes takes an object directly, meaning the agent in it appears without the ba', such as: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾ [al-Ahzab 25]. And sometimes it takes the ba'. When does it take the ba' and when does it not?

When the intended meaning is wonder (ta'ajjub), that is, "how sufficient is Allah's sufficiency," it takes the ba', such as: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾, ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, and similar.

When the intended meaning is only to state sufficiency, it takes no preposition, such as: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, and such as your saying: "May Allah suffice you the evil of your enemies," and similar.

Here the intended meaning is wonder. That is, its meaning is: how mighty is Allah's sufficiency, and how complete is His sufficiency.

His words: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs⁠﴾ — ﴿wakilan⁠﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the agent of (kafa).

His words: ﴿wakilan⁠﴾ mean: a guardian and sufficient one, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him﴾ [at-Talaq 3], meaning: sufficient for him.

Know that Allah has named Himself al-Wakil, and He has named Himself al-Muwakkil, that is, He described Himself as al-Muwakkil. As for al-Wakil, it occurs often in the Book of Allah, and its meaning is the Sufficient, the Guardian, and similar. As for describing Allah as al-Muwakkil, that is, the One who appoints an agent, it is in His words: ﴿So if these disbelieve in it, We have already entrusted with it a people who are not disbelievers in it﴾ [al-An'am 89]. He said: ﴿We have entrusted with it a people who are not disbelievers in it.⁠﴾

The connection of His words ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs⁠﴾ to His words ﴿And rely upon Allah⁠﴾ is that when you rely upon Him, He suffices you for everything, protects you, and becomes a watcher over you.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them﴾ [al-Ahzab 49]. ﴿O you who have believed⁠﴾: We have previously discussed the opening of address with such a call, and that it indicates the importance of the matter, and that complying with what follows is among the requirements of faith, and that opposing it is among the deficiencies of faith.

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry⁠﴾: ﴿nakahtum⁠﴾ — the meaning of nikah here is the contract (al-'aqd). Nikah is applied both to the contract and to intercourse, because its original meaning in the Arabic language is joining and gathering, since the contract joins the husband to his wife and the wife to her husband. It is used with both meanings. But when it is attached to a non-spouse it means the contract, and when it is attached to a wife it means intercourse. So when one says "nakaha al-rajul zawjatahu," it means he had intercourse with her. When one says "nakaha fulanah bint fulan," the meaning is he contracted marriage with her. In the Qur'an it has the meaning of contract wherever it occurs. Strangely, some scholars say it has not come with the meaning of contract except in this verse, and that in the Qur'an it came with the meaning of intercourse. But this is not correct. The correct view is the opposite: it has not come in the Qur'an except with the meaning of contract.

Let us review the verses that come on this: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 221]. The meaning: contract. ﴿And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 221]: contract. ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾ [an-Nisa 22]: contract. ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [an-Nur 3]: contract. What else? We have left ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾ [al-Baqarah 230]. What? The contract. Yes, the contract. But the Sunnah clarified and added to this another condition, which is that he tastes her sweetness and she tastes his sweetness. Otherwise it is the contract. Clear? I say: what else? ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your slaves﴾ [an-Nur 32]: contract for them.

In sum, wherever it occurs in the Qur'an it means contract, even in this verse, clearly: the meaning is contract. ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them⁠﴾ means: before you have had intercourse with them. What do you have?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the contract. ﴿The adulterer does not marry⁠﴾ [an-Nur 3]: does not contract except with an adulteress or a polytheist, and an adulteress is only married by an adulterer or a polytheist.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, look at His words: ﴿does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist⁠﴾. As for the end of the verse, ﴿And that has been made unlawful to the believers﴾ [an-Nur 3]: if marrying an adulteress is unlawful and marrying an adulterer is unlawful, then if one contracts marriage with an adulteress while it is unlawful, either he believes it to be forbidden, and then he is an adulterer because he had intercourse with her while believing it forbidden; or he does not believe it forbidden and says: this is lawful. Then making lawful what Allah has forbidden is shirk, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, son of Mary﴾ [at-Tawbah 31]. This is the meaning of the verse, which admits of no other, and this is what Shaykh al-Islam and Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on them both, established.

Now, ﴿when you marry believing women⁠﴾ means: when you contract marriage with them.

* Student: Shaykh, if a man marries, and he finds his wife has had intercourse before, is he obliged to separate from her (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, he is only obliged if he knows she still persists in it. But if she repents, it is permissible for him to marry her.

He said: ﴿when you marry believing women⁠﴾. The phrase ﴿believing women⁠﴾ is based on what is most common: that a believer normally marries only a believing woman. But if she were a Jewish or Christian woman, the ruling would not differ. So this is a case of restriction to one of the two categories, not of abbreviation, and the other category is mentioned less because it is rare relative to marrying believing women.

﴿Then divorce them before you have touched them⁠﴾. His words ﴿then divorced them⁠﴾, without saying "and divorced them" or "so divorced them," show that if the divorce is delayed from the contract for a long time, the ruling does not change, just as if he divorces her immediately the ruling also does not change. So ﴿then divorced them⁠﴾ means: after the contract.

Divorce (talaq) linguistically means releasing the tether of a camel or similar; that is, removing the tether is called talaq. It is a noun of verbal noun (ism al-masdar) from (tallaqa). The verbal noun of tallaqa is tatlia, like kallama whose verbal noun is takliman, and the noun of the verbal noun is kalam. Tallaqa has the verbal noun tatliq, and the noun of the verbal noun is talaq.

So talaq linguistically is the removal of a tether. In terminology or in the Sharia, divorcing a woman means removing the bond of marriage, or part of it. If the divorce is irrevocable (ba'in), by which the wife is not made lawful again, it is the removal of the bond of marriage absolutely. If it is revocable (raj'i), it is the removal of part of it, since he may take her back.

His words: ﴿then divorced them before you have touched them⁠﴾ mean: before you have had intercourse with them. This is a case of euphemism (kinayah) for what is disliked to mention, by indicating it through something else. For this reason intercourse is not mentioned in its explicit wording in the noble Qur'an, but is alluded to in each place with what fits the context: sometimes expressed as "coming to" (al-ityan), sometimes as "going into" (al-ifda'), sometimes as touching (al-mass), sometimes as contact (al-mulamasah), and similar. All of this is using words that hearing does not find repugnant.

﴿before you have touched them⁠﴾: he said: (And in a reading: ﴿tumassuhunna⁠﴾), that is, "you have intercourse with them."

He says: ﴿then you have no right against them of a waiting period which you should count﴾. ﴿fama lakum⁠﴾: the ma here is negating, ﴿lakum⁠﴾ is a prepositional phrase functioning as a fronted predicate, and ﴿min⁠﴾ is a superfluous preposition for an additional meaning. We have said it is a superfluous preposition that is superfluous. Is the second word "superfluous" (za'id) an emphasis or an establishment?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: We say: it is a superfluous superfluous preposition. Is it emphasis or establishment?

* Student: Establishment.

* The Shaykh: Establishment. It is a preposition superfluous in wording, but it adds to the meaning. The first "za'id" is from za'ada (intransitive), and the second "za'id" is from za'ada (transitive). Where are you all in grammar, folks? Za'ada is a past verb, both transitive and intransitive. Are you with me? If I say: zada iman al-rajul — the faith of the man increased — is it transitive or intransitive? Intransitive. If I say: zadahum iman an — it is transitive.

So we say: this is a superfluous preposition from za'ada intransitive; za'id from za'ada transitive; that is, superfluous in itself, and adding meaning to something else.

The point is that His words ﴿min 'iddatin⁠﴾: min is a superfluous preposition in wording, not in meaning.

﴿'iddatin⁠﴾ is a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), nominative, marked by a presumed damma on its end, which could not be manifested because the position is occupied by the vowel of the superfluous preposition.

If someone said to us: may we make (ma) here a Hijazi negation? It is not permissible. Who says it is not permissible? Why?

* Student: Because it is fronted.

* The Shaykh: Because the predicate is fronted. Ibn Malik says:

...................... *** ma'a baqa al-nafy wa tartib zukin

His words: ﴿then you have no right against them of a waiting period which you should count⁠﴾. The author said: (you enumerate it).

﴿min 'iddatin⁠﴾: what is the 'iddah? 'Iddah linguistically is a noun taken from 'adad (number). In terminology or in the Sharia, it is a legally defined period of waiting, in life or after death, imposed on a wife separated from her husband, a waiting period of a wife separated in life or after death, legally defined. Legally defined what?

(﴿ta'taddunaha⁠﴾: you count it by menstrual cycles and other means) — by menstrual cycles if she is of those who have cycles, as its completion is three cycles; and (other means) if she is not of those who have cycles, namely pregnant women and those who do not menstruate due to young age or menopause. The pregnant woman's 'iddah is the delivery of the child, and the one who does not menstruate has an 'iddah of three months.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the meaning is that you entrusted your affair to Him and relied upon Him. This means: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ [Ghafir 44].

He says: (﴿So for you there is no waiting period for them which you should count, so provide for them⁠﴾: give them what they can enjoy, that is, if no dowry was named for them; otherwise they have only half of the named amount, as Ibn 'Abbas said, and al-Shafi'i held this view.)

His words: ﴿so provide for them⁠﴾. The fa is a conjunctive particle. ﴿Mattiuhunna⁠﴾ means: give them what they may enjoy. From where? From dirhams, from garments, from goods, from property, from any thing. Allah, glorified and exalted, made it absolute, just as it is absolute in quantity and in kind. Quantity — what do I give her? If I want to give her dirhams, how many do I give her?

﴿Provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah 236]: according to the husband's circumstances.

His words: ﴿so provide for them⁠﴾ after His words: "if you divorce believing women, so provide for them" — excepted from this is the one for whom a dowry was named; for the one for whom a dowry was named, only half of it is obligatory, by the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified﴾ [al-Baqarah 237]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, explained that they have half of what was specified for them, and this applies when a dowry was named for her, whether little or much.

He said: (﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾) meaning, let them go without harm. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded two things: provision (tamti', ), which is giving wealth, and a fair release (al-sarah al-jamil), which is good conduct. This means the separation should be with consent, and with gentle words that console the heart. When a woman is divorced after the marriage contract was made but before the marriage was consummated, there is no doubt that her heart is broken and she is affected. People will ask: why was she divorced before he consummated the marriage? What is the reason? Did he find a defect in her? Did he hear something about her? This is especially so if she was also willing toward the husband, and he divorced her before he had been intimate with her. There will certainly be a reaction within her. So the Most Merciful of the merciful has commanded us to provide for them with wealth and to release them with a fair release, through kind words and good treatment. For example, we say to her: "This is a matter that was not decreed for us, and it is a matter that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed. I am not separating from you, for example, because of your bad character, or because I heard something bad about you, or anything similar to such speech," so that she parts from him in good spirits and with an open heart. Then whatever speech comes from her or from her family afterwards may be avoided. For if he divorces her without providing for her, or provides for her less than she deserves, or releases her in an unfair manner, speech may arise from her or from her family about the man, about his honor and his household, and similar things. This is one of the courtesies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with which He trained His servants. If a man divorces a woman before touching (al-mass, ), he is obligated to do two things: provision with what? With wealth, and a fair release through speech and action, a cheerful face and a relaxed heart, and similar things.

Someone may say: how can this be, since the man would not divorce her in this situation unless he disliked her without doubt? If he had even the slightest affection for her, he would have consummated the marriage and been intimate with her, and perhaps things would change. That is: if he has lost some interest in her, but there is still affection in his heart for her, would he take the risk of divorcing her before intercourse?

Reason does not require that. Reason requires that you wait and be intimate with her, because perhaps, what? Perhaps things will change. For this reason, divorce during menstruation (al-hayd, ) was forbidden, because when a man's wife is menstruating, he does not have intercourse with her, so he remains displeased with her, and there is no cause that calls for affection, which is intercourse. Therefore it was forbidden. This is one of the wisdoms behind the prohibition of divorce during menstruation, but it is not the only wisdom.

﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾. If Allah wills, its benefits will come later.

(...) The establishment of the Prophet's (ﷺ) prophethood, because of His saying...

* The student: (...)

* The Shaykh: No, the Prophet (ﷺ) is a bringer of good news in His saying: ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾; and from this it follows that he brought the causes that necessitate good news, namely righteous deeds and acts of worship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet (ﷺ) combined glad tidings with warning, because of His saying: ﴿a bringer of good news and a warner﴾. Before this benefit there is another: that he is also a warner. Being a warner and being a bringer of good news are two benefits, and combining them is a third benefit.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Messenger (ﷺ) is a caller to Allah, because of His saying: ﴿and a caller to Allah﴾.

* Among its benefits: an indication that the caller must make his call to Allah, the Exalted, not to the advantage of his own self, because of His saying: ﴿a caller to Allah﴾, for this is the description of the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Among its benefits: that the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) call to Allah was by His permission, because of His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾. From this another benefit follows, which is Allah's approval of what the Messenger (ﷺ) was calling to. Is this not so? Because Allah does not permit except what He loves and is pleased with.

* Among them: that the Prophet's (ﷺ) call is based on the law of Allah.

(...) in its manner and in what he calls to, because of His saying: ﴿by His permission﴾. So he is a caller to Allah by His permission; that is, according to His command and by His law. He calls to the way of Allah with wisdom and good admonition, and he argues with them in the best manner. Likewise, he calls to the law of Allah and does not go beyond it.

* Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) cannot legislate from himself, because of His saying: ﴿a caller to Allah by His permission﴾, not by anything from himself.

* Among them: that what the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) calls to is from Allah. From this benefit follows that obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to the Messenger is disobedience to Allah. For this reason, when a woman came to Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "You say that those women who file their teeth for beauty are cursed by the Book of Allah, and I opened the Mushaf, or read the Mushaf from its beginning to its end, and did not find that." He said: "Yes." Then he recited the hadith to her, and recited the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7] [[Al-Bukhari (4886) and Muslim (120/2125), and the wording is his, with their chains from 'Abdullah who said: "Allah has cursed the tattooers and those who are tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair and those who have it plucked, and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah." He said: "This reached a woman from the Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, who used to recite the Qur'an. She came to him and said: 'A report reached me that you cursed the tattooers, those who are tattooed, those who pluck facial hair, those who file their teeth for beauty, and those who alter the creation of Allah.' 'Abdullah said: 'Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and who are in the Book of Allah?' The woman said: 'I have read what is between the two covers of the Mushaf and did not find it.' He said: 'If you had read it, you would have found it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it"...'" The hadith.]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of permission for Allah. What is permission? Is it "udhun" (ear) or something else?

Permission (idhn) is not ear (udhun). We affirm permission for Allah, the Exalted. Allah's permission, as was mentioned earlier in the tafsir, is divided into two types: legislative (shar'iyyah) and cosmic (kawniyyah).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought is a light, like a lamp that illuminates darkness, because of His saying: ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾.

* Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) has no shadow. Pay attention: this benefit needs discussion, or not? He has no shadow; that is, if he stood in the sun when it was inclined, there would be no shadow for him.

* The student: That is not correct.

* The Shaykh: Not correct, with ﴿a shining lamp﴾?!

* The student: The lamp is not (...).

* The Shaykh: A lamp illuminates, and it has no shadow.

* The student: A figurative illumination.

* The Shaykh: A figurative lamp. Otherwise, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) has a shadow like others, because he is a human being.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that everyone who judges by the law of the Prophet (ﷺ) is upon a shining lamp, right or not? Because of His saying: ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾.

* Among them: the virtue of the Prophet (ﷺ), in that Allah combined for him these great qualities: prophethood, messengership, witnessing, glad tidings, warning, and calling to Allah by His permission. How many is that? That is six, and the shining lamp makes seven.

Then He, the Exalted, said:
﴿And give glad tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾ [Al-Ahzab 47] ... to the end.

* From this noble verse it is derived: that the Prophet (ﷺ) is obligated to give glad tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And give glad tidings﴾. The command implies obligation, especially for the Prophet (ﷺ), since the command is always obligatory. Why? Because when Allah commands His Messenger to do something, He commands him to do it and to convey it to the people. Conveying the message by the Messenger (ﷺ) is obligatory. For this reason we say that the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is obligated to convey even the sunnahs, so he must inform of the sunnah and practice it until the conveyance is complete. After that, it becomes recommended for him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of faith. Its basis is that those who are characterized by it are the people of glad tidings, because of His saying: ﴿And give glad tidings﴾.

* Among them: the reward of the believers with this great bounty: ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾.

* Among them: an explanation of Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, favor upon the believers, and that the bounty is His bounty, because of His saying: ﴿that they will have from Allah﴾, not from anyone else. For this reason He placed ﴿from Allah﴾ first, though it is connected to ﴿a great bounty﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the reward for faith is greater than what the servant has done, from His saying: ﴿a great bounty﴾, and His saying: ﴿from Allah﴾. That is, it is derived from both. As for the first, it is derived from His saying: ﴿great﴾, and when something is described as great, it is very great. As for the second, He attributed the bounty to whom? To Allah: ﴿from Allah﴾. As the proverb says: "The gift is according to the status of the giver."

If this bounty is from Allah, it will be a bounty beyond imagination. For this reason, in the hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) taught Abu Bakr to supplicate with in his prayer, he said: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You and have mercy on me" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6326) and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. That it is from the presence of Allah carries a distinction.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [Al-Ahzab 48].

* The student: (...) love of Allah (...)?

* The Shaykh: Is that what we said, the virtue of faith in the first point?

* The student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...).

* The student: (...) and it was not shining?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because light is more complete, since it combines heat and illumination, so it has two attributes.

He said: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ ... to the end.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the prohibition of obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, but not absolutely. Rather, obeying them is forbidden in what contradicts the command of Allah. So if they command something that does not contradict Allah's command, obeying them is not forbidden. For example, if a disbeliever told you to make a key for this door, would we say it is forbidden for you to obey him? No. So do not obey them in what contradicts the command of Allah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is at its most eloquent. We find that in some places it mentions the hypocrites before the disbelievers, but in this verse it mentions the disbelievers before the hypocrites. This is because in the context of reward and in the context of blame, it mentions the hypocrites first: ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾ [An-Nisa 140], ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ [Al-Ahzab 73]. This is because the sin of the hypocrite is greater than the sin of the open disbeliever. Here, however, who opposes the Messenger openly? The disbeliever. For this reason He placed him before the hypocrite, because the hypocrite does not command contrary to the law as the disbeliever does, since he conceals his hypocrisy. Therefore He said: ﴿Do not obey the disbelievers﴾, beginning with them, because their opposition to the law is more clear and apparent than that of the hypocrites.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a prohibition may be directed at something that has not been done, lest it be done, from His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) did not obey them, but he was forbidden from obeying them lest he do so in the future.

* Among them: that a prohibition may come concerning matters that are remote or impossible. Its basis is: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, for this is remote or impossible for the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to the disbelievers and the hypocrites, from His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾.

* Among them: the strengthening and consolation of the Prophet (ﷺ), from His saying also: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾.

* Among them: that it is the nature of the disbelievers and the hypocrites to harm the believers, from His saying: ﴿And leave off their harm﴾. But someone may say: this is the harm to the Prophet (ﷺ).
