The second opinion is that what is meant by His saying ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ is: of those women who gave themselves (as a gift). So the choice is yours whether to accept or not accept. And whichever of them you refused, there is no blame upon you afterward for seeking her. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse is general, covering both meanings together. This is what we have followed previously, that if a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, then the obligation is to apply it to all of them.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ refers to the choice.) The referent is "the choice": ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ and ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾, meaning: that choice derived from the two clauses.

(﴿أَدْنَى﴾ means: nearer to ﴿أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾, "that their eyes may be comforted, that they may not grieve, and that they may be pleased with what you give them." ﴿كُلُّهُنَّ﴾ refers to the thing given the choice, "all of them.")

His saying ﴿أَدْنَى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾: how is that? That is, what is the reason that this is nearer to their eyes being comforted? Because when they know that the choice between dividing and not dividing comes from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, their eyes are comforted, since they are content with the ruling of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. But if it were from the Prophet (ﷺ), that if he wished he divided and if he wished he did not divide, there would be some discomfort in their souls, since each one of them might think that this comes from the Prophet (ﷺ) and not from the law of Allah. So when the women know that this is from the law of Allah, their eyes are comforted.

His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾ is derived either from "qarār" (settling) or from "qarr," which means coolness. For when the eye becomes cool, its meaning is that it is not grieved; and when it becomes hot, its meaning is grief. For this reason they say: "the tear of grief is hot," because it comes out of the eye when it heats up from grief. But if there is no grief, it cools and settles.

His saying ﴿أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is conjoined with His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾. Is ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ in the subjunctive? Since ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾ is in the subjunctive by ﴿أَنْ﴾ and ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is conjoined to it, is it in the subjunctive? No, it is built on sukūn (a silent ending), because it is attached to the feminine plural nūn, and the nūn of the verb is assimilated into the feminine plural nūn; for "يحزن" is the verb, and the second nūn is the feminine plural nūn, which is the subject.

* Student: What about the conjunction "wāw"? Does it have no function?
* Shaykh: No, it has a function, but the verb here is built on sukūn in a position of naṣb (subjunctive) in ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾.

As for His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ﴾: the "wāw" is a conjunction particle, and ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾, not to ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾. For if it were conjoined to ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾, the meaning would be corrupted: the meaning would be "and that they not grieve and not be pleased," and the intended meaning is the opposite. So the intended meaning is: that this is nearer to their eyes being comforted and their being pleased.

If you say: what is the benefit of placing the second clause ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ in the middle?
We say: because its connection to His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾ is stronger. For His saying ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is meant to express the complete comfort of the eye; that is, that their eyes are comforted so that no grief remains in them at all. For this reason this clause was inserted between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined.

His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾: ﴿آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾ with the long vowel means "I gave them," because ﴿آتَى﴾ takes two objects; its first object is the pronoun ﴿هُنَّ﴾, and its second object is omitted, which the author supplied with the words (what was mentioned). And what was mentioned? He said: the thing given the choice, meaning: that they are pleased with what you have given them of the choice between dividing and not dividing.

We have already explained the reason why they are pleased with that: when the ruling comes from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, they are pleased with it, unlike if it were from the Prophet (ﷺ) at the outset, when they might not be pleased, since each one of them would think that this is a whim of the Prophet (ﷺ).

* Student: ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it is inserted between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, and it is conjoined. But now it is inserted, meaning that it is not correct for us to conjoin what follows it to it; rather it is conjoined to what precedes it.

He said: ﴿كُلُّهُنَّ﴾ is an emphasis of the subject in ﴿يَرْضَيْنَ﴾. He said this because if it were an emphasis of the pronoun in His saying ﴿بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾, it would be in the accusative: ﴿بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلَّهُنَّ﴾. But it is, as he said, an emphasis of the subject in His saying ﴿يَرْضَيْنَ﴾.

Is it not correct that it be an emphasis of the pronoun in His saying ﴿أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾? It is not correct; for if it were an emphasis of that, it would be in the genitive, "kullihinna." So it is necessarily an emphasis of His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾.

(﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ means: of the matter of the women and the inclination toward some of them.) When Allah the Mighty and Majestic made clear that the Prophet (ﷺ) was given the choice, He made clear that He, the Mighty and Majestic, knows what is in the hearts: a person's inclination toward some women over others. Allah the Exalted has explained this known matter by His saying: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave her as if suspended.﴾ [An-Nisa' 129]. This is a matter confirmed by reality and witnessed by it, for a person can never make his affection for two wives completely equal, even if it is supposed that one of them is preferred by him in one respect and the other in another respect. Equality is impossible, and this is what His saying the Exalted supports: ﴿you will never be able to be equitable between wives﴾.

As for His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: is a threat and warning derived from it, or is it derived that this is a matter you do not control? The apparent meaning is the second: that this is a matter we do not control.

(...) concerning His punishment. This is like a justification for His saying ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. He, the Exalted, is All-Knowing of everything, and among that is what is in our hearts of inclination toward some women over others. And His saying ﴿Forbearing﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]: what is forbearance? Forbearance is not hastening punishment, and it is not the abandonment of punishment. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim said:

"He is the Forbearing, so He does not hasten His servant with punishment, so that he may repent of disobedience."

So forbearance is the delay of punishment, not pardoning it. He delays punishment for what reason? So that this sinner may repent to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and the punishment will be lifted from him.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this]﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. He said: ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ﴾ with the taa' and the yā': ﴿لا تحل﴾ and ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ﴾. As for the reading ﴿لا تحل﴾, there is no difficulty, because "an-nisā'" is the plural of "niswah," and "niswah" is the plural of "imra'ah" (woman), for "imra'ah" has no plural from its own form, but has a plural from its meaning, like "al-ibil" (camels), the plural of "ba'īr," which has no singular from its own form. So His saying ﴿لا تحل لك النساء﴾ has no difficulty. But His saying ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ﴾: how is the verb masculine when the subject is feminine? Answer.

* Student: Shaykh, repeat the question.
* Shaykh: We will not repeat the question.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is a hidden, attached verb, or it is completed by "lā tahillu," but with attachment. But with separation it is permissible: ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾. The author said: (after the nine whom you chose). Is it "allatī" or "al-lātī" in your copies?
* Student: "allatī."
* Shaykh: "The nine whom you chose." The sense of the statement would require him to say "allātī ikhtarnak" (those who chose you). The meaning is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, they chose Allah and His Messenger. When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them, so He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. On this basis this is a case of immediate reward, and they have a deferred reward as well, because when they chose Allah and His Messenger over the life of this world and its adornment, Allah thanked them, so He forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from marrying others besides them, or from divorcing one and marrying another. So He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this]﴾. This is one of the two opinions on the verse.

The second opinion: the meaning of the verse, ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾, is: after what has been mentioned to you, which is His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their bridal payments, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives], and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 50]. The meaning on this basis is: women are not lawful to you after what we have mentioned to you. Accordingly, it is not lawful for the Prophet (ﷺ) to marry any woman of the Arabs other than the daughters of his paternal uncles, the daughters of his paternal aunts, the daughters of his maternal uncles and the daughters of his maternal aunts who emigrated with him. Nor is it lawful for him to marry a woman from the People of the Book, since she is not one of these.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse includes both meanings together: it is not lawful for him to marry over the Mothers of the Believers, nor to marry besides these. If you say: could we not say that the first meaning, "women are not lawful to you besides these women," includes the second meaning, so there is no need for the second opinion? Do you understand this or not? If we say: "It is not lawful for you besides these who are with you," this includes the second opinion, that it is not lawful for him besides those mentioned in "We have made lawful to you your wives." So what is the benefit of the second opinion then?

The answer to this is that if it is supposed that these women die during the lifetime of the Messenger (ﷺ), is it lawful for him to marry others besides those whom Allah made lawful to him? In that case the second opinion has a benefit. This benefit appears if it is supposed that the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) who are with him die before him, for then it is not lawful for him to take women except those Allah mentioned: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 50].

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52] by dropping one of the two taa's in the original.) ﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ﴾: he says: (by dropping one of the two taa's in the original). The word ﴿تَبَدَّلَ﴾ originally was "tatabaddal." The evidence that its original form is "tatabaddal" and that it is not a past tense verb is that ﴿أن﴾ entered upon it and put it in the subjunctive, and only the imperfect is entered by ﴿أن﴾ and put in the subjunctive. Otherwise the word ﴿تَبَدَّلَ﴾ could be a past tense verb, but since ﴿أن﴾ entered upon it and governed it in the subjunctive, it is known that it is an imperfect verb from which one of the two taa's was dropped. Is there a parallel to this? Yes, there is a parallel, such as ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend﴾ [Al-Qadr 4], meaning "tatanazzal" (descend), and ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire blazing﴾ [Al-Layl 14], meaning "tatalaẓẓā" (blazing). Who asks?

* Student: (...) the Messenger (ﷺ), does this contradict the first opinion?
* Shaykh: Which is?
* Student: That the Messenger (ﷺ) in the last days of his life wanted to divorce.
* Shaykh: Yes, and he divorced Hafsah too; he divorced Hafsah and then took her back.
* Student: How can it be with this meaning, that "it is not lawful for you women..."?
* Shaykh: It does not contradict it. That is, it is not permissible for him to marry others, "it is not lawful for you women after this," and it is not permissible for him to divorce one in order to marry another besides her. For He said: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾; He did not say "nor to divorce"; He said: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning by divorcing one and marrying another.

(﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾ means: by divorcing them, or some of them, and marrying in place of the one divorced.) This too is not lawful for him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) did not do it after this verse was revealed. He did not divorce one in order to marry another, nor did he marry others besides them; rather they remained with him until he died. But he died leaving two wives during his lifetime, and who were they? Khadijah; and after her? Zaynab bint Khuzaymah. He married her after her husband was martyred at Uhud, and she remained with him for months, then she died, and the rest of his wives were those he left at his death.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 33, verses 51–52 (part 2 of 3):

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take other wives in place of them, even though their beauty may please you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. What is meant is outward beauty, or inward beauty, or both. The verse includes both. The Prophet (ﷺ), like other men, may marry a woman for her beauty, but with religious commitment. He may also marry her for her religion, or for her knowledge and understanding. So His words ﴿even though their beauty may please you﴾ include both outward and inward beauty. His words ﴿may please you﴾ mean that the admiration reached you, because of the perfection of their outward and inward beauty.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: He said: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ of the slave-women, so they are lawful to you... and so on. That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepted what his right hand possesses. This is because jealousy does not arise in a wife toward a slave-woman in the same way it does toward another wife. Jealousy does not arise in a wife toward a slave-woman because the slave-woman does not compete with her or equal her, and because the slave-woman has no turn (qasm). The right of turns is not obligatory for slave-women.

﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained what He had made lawful for His Messenger and what He had made unlawful for him, He concluded the verse by mentioning His watchfulness, may He be blessed and exalted, over all things. Allah explained His watchfulness over all things in order to encourage caution against opposing His command. If He, glorified and exalted, is watchful over all things, then a person will be cautious and fear opposing Him.

As for His words ﴿And Allah is﴾, we have previously discussed similar examples several times. We said that the past tense here is stripped of its indication of time. The meaning is not that Allah was in a past time and that the ruling later changed. Rather, it establishes that Allah, glorified and exalted, is characterized by watchfulness. His words ﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾: "over all things" includes what is hidden and what is apparent, what is specific to the Messenger (ﷺ) and what is general to him and to the Ummah. It includes deeds of the limbs and deeds of the hearts, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16].

Now let us return to deriving benefits from the noble verse.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them and take to you whom you will. And whom you seek from those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], to the end.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, may single out whom He wills with His rulings. This is shown by His words ﴿You may put off﴾ and ﴿take to you﴾, according to the view that the intended meaning is the turn (qasm). Allah gave him the choice between committing to the turn and not committing to it. This is one of the particular privileges of the Prophet (ﷺ). As for the Ummah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side leaning." [Abu Dawud (2133), and the wording is his, and al-Tirmidhi (1141), from Abu Hurairah.] This indicates the obligation of justice among wives for the Ummah.

According to the second view regarding His words ﴿You may put off﴾ and ﴿take to you﴾, that it means accepting or rejecting the woman who has given herself to the Prophet, there is also evidence that Allah granted His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) latitude in matters concerning marriage. He may accept, and he may refuse.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to retract a right after waiving it, based on His words ﴿And whom you seek from those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. This applies when the right is renewable. But if the right is not renewable, then when a person waives it, he cannot take it back. An example: a woman waived her share or right to maintenance for a past period, such as when the husband had stopped providing for her for a year, and she waived the right. Can she take it back?

She cannot take it back, because the right here is not renewable. It concerns a past matter. If a woman waives her right to the turn, can she reclaim it in the future? Yes, she can reclaim it, because her right renews. Unless it was made a condition in the marriage contract, such as the husband stipulating to his new wife that he will not divide turns for her, and she accepted. In that case she cannot reclaim it, because it became a condition of the contract. A condition in a contract must be fulfilled, because it falls under the general scope of Allah's words: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfill [your] contracts﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 1]. This differs from the case where she waived it after the contract. Then the waiver stands, and she cannot reclaim it, because she cannot waive a future right.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is subject to obligation, based on His words ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾. This is because negating an attribute of something indicates that it is possible for it to have that attribute. If it were absent from the outset, there would be no need to negate it. This shows that blame could have fallen upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is evidence that he is charged with the rulings of the Message.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists). From where is this taken? ﴿And whom you seek﴾, meaning: whom you desire and wish. The Jabriyyah hold that a person has no will. Rather, he is compelled and driven to his deeds without any will of his own.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes and wisdoms behind rulings, that rulings are tied to their causes and purposes. From where is this taken? ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. The affirmation of wisdom in Allah's cosmic and decreed rulings is very numerous, and all of them also refute the Jabriyyah. This is because the Jabriyyah hold that the acts and rulings of Allah, glorified and exalted, have no cause or wisdom, and that He acts not for a cause and wisdom but merely by will. Does this support the position of the Mu'tazilah, who hold that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best (al-aslah) or what is good (al-salah)? I do not know. Do you know this or not? This came up for us in the Safariniyyah creed, where he said:

*So it is not obligatory upon Him to do what is best, nor what is good; woe to him who does not prosper.*

The Mu'tazilah say that it is obligatory upon Him to do what is best when the good and the better conflict, and to do what is good when the good and the corrupt conflict. He said: it is obligatory upon Allah to do what is best when the good conflicts with the better, and the good when the good conflicts with the corrupt. But the correct view is that there is a distinction here. If we say it is obligatory in the sense that our intellects have made it obligatory upon Allah, then this is false, because intellects cannot make anything obligatory upon Allah. They are too lowly and too contemptible to obligate anything upon Allah. If we say that it is obligatory by the requirement of His wisdom, then this is true and correct, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does nothing except that it is best. As Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah does not like corruption﴾ [Al-Baqarah 205], ﴿And Allah does not like corrupters﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 64], and ﴿Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good﴾ [Al-A'raf 170].

Since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, praised the doers of good and negated that He loves corruption or corrupters, this indicates that it is impossible for Him to will corruption. Accordingly, we say: the Mu'tazilah erred in obligating this upon Allah by their intellects, because the intellect is too lowly and contemptible to obligate anything upon Allah. Intellect may see something as obligatory when in reality it is not, because intellects are limited. It may judge something to be best when it is not. Allah pointed to this in His words: ﴿But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 216]. As for saying that it is obligatory by the requirement of His wisdom, this is true. So here we say: affirming causes refutes the Jabriyyah, who are also the Jahmiyyah in this matter. It provides no support for the Mu'tazilah's view that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best or good.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: caring for the hearts of the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) and bringing joy to them. From where is this taken? ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. This is because it shows consideration for the hearts of these women, so that their eyes may be comforted.

* Also among its lessons: it is appropriate to consider the believer by bringing joy to him and removing sadness from him, based on His words ﴿nor grieve﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], meaning: that they should not be overcome by grief and distress over what has passed. This state of the believer contradicts the state of Satan, for Satan strives with everything that saddens the children of Adam, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Private conversation is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who have believed﴾ [Al-Mujadilah 10]. Therefore, whoever tries to bring sadness upon his Muslim brother resembles Satan, who seeks to bring sorrow upon the believers.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defends His Prophet (ﷺ) through various defensive methods. The aspect of this is that when Allah gave him the choice, He made clear that this ruling came from Allah. That is so that when the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) know that this ruling is from Allah, whatever dissatisfaction or grief was in their souls disappears. Undoubtedly, a person's contentment with what comes from Allah is more complete than his contentment with what comes from other than Allah. This is one aspect.

Although a believer is content with what comes from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) just as he is content with what comes from Allah, yet since the Prophet (ﷺ) was a husband to these women, it may occur to their minds that the Messenger's (ﷺ) dividing turns or not dividing them, or accepting or refusing, is merely a matter of his own desire. If they believed that it was merely his own desire, grief would enter them. But when they know that this is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who granted him this latitude, the grief departs from them.

From this benefit another may branch out, which is that a person should ward off from himself whatever he might be blamed for. Whatever you fear people might blame you for, repel the suspicion from yourself. This has a basis. What is it?

* Student: (...) the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ), he said: "Slowly, both of you, she is Safiyyah." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2035), and Muslim (2175/24), from Safiyyah bint Huyayy.]

* Shaykh: And what is the second?

* Student: (...).

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: using emphasizing particles where the need calls for them, based on His word ﴿all of them﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], lest someone wrongly think that the contentment of some of them and the removal of grief from some of them is sufficient. Rather, contentment must be for all of them.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of outward and inward matters, based on His words ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51].

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: what is in the heart, which a person does not control, is not held against him. This is because when He mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) was given the choice, He said: ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, meaning: of the things you do not control. For this reason, it is permissible for a person, or rather it is not forbidden for a person, to prefer one of his wives over another in love, because love has its seat in the heart, and a person cannot direct his heart and subject it to make himself love or hate.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the seat of volitions is the heart, based on His words ﴿what is in your hearts﴾. Is the meant heart the physical heart or the metaphorical heart, which is the intellect? The physical heart, because the correct view is that the physical heart is the one on which matters depend, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599/107), from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]

Scholars have differed over whether the intellect is in the heart or in the brain. The apparent meaning of the Noble Quran is that the intellect is in the heart, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth so that they would have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 46]. This is also supported by the Sunnah, in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt." This indicates that the intellect is in the heart. However, Imam Ahmad said that it has a connection to the brain. That is, it is in the heart, but it has a connection to the brain. For this reason, if the brain is corrupted, the intellect is corrupted. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in several places in his speech that the brain is the seat of perception and the shaping of things, and that the heart is the seat of management and direction. So the brain is like the heart's secretary: it prepares matters for it, forms them, and shapes them, then sends them to the heart, and the heart commands, forbids, approves, or rejects.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names: the All-Knowing (al-'Alim) and the Forbearing (al-Halim). Al-'Alim is the One who encompasses everything in knowledge. Knowledge, according to the jurists or the usulis (scholars of legal theory), is the perception of a thing with certainty and correspondence to reality. Their phrase "with certainty" excludes doubt, supposition, and suspicion, which are not called knowledge because they are not certain. Their phrase "corresponding to reality" excludes compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab), because a person who has compound ignorance perceives a thing in a way that does not correspond to reality. Their phrase "perception of a thing" excludes simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basit), because simple ignorance involves no perception at all. This is what knowledge is.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not acquire new knowledge. What is renewed is the known object. The relation of Allah's knowledge to the known has two states: a relation to it before it occurs, and a relation to it after it occurs. The relation before it occurs means that He knows it will happen. The relation after it occurs means that He knows it has happened. The one upon which reward and punishment are based is the second relation, the relation to the object after its occurrence. On this basis the difficulty raised by some scholars concerning His words ﴿And We will surely test you until We make evident those of you who strive﴾ [Muhammad 31] is resolved. Regarding ﴿until We make evident﴾: does this mean He did not know those who strive? We say: yes, He knows. But the knowledge upon which reward is based is knowledge of the thing after it occurs. So what renews is not the knowledge but the known.

Does Allah's knowledge relate to the necessary, the possible, and the impossible, or to the necessary and the possible but not the impossible, or to the possible only? What do you say? To all of them: the necessary, the possible, and the impossible. As for His knowledge of the necessary, it is His knowledge of the names and attributes that He deserves, because this is knowledge of the necessary, since Allah has the perfection that is due to Him.

As for His knowledge of the impossible, it is found in His words: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any deity. [If there were], each deity would have taken away what it created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 91], and His words: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [Al-Anbiya 22]. This is knowledge of the impossible. As for the possible, what a person does and does not do is known. This is knowledge of the possible.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of the name al-Halim (the Forbearing). Al-Halim is the One who does not hasten punishment, not the One who does not punish. The One who does not punish is al-'Afuww (the Pardoner). This is the difference between al-Halim and al-'Afuww. He, glorified and exalted, is Forbearing, who does not hasten punishment, and Pardoning, who pardons sin so that He does not punish for it.

Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty may please you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52].

* From this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is charged with obligations like other people. That is, things are made lawful for him and unlawful for him. From this benefit another branches out, which is that obligation can never be lifted from anyone, no matter how high his rank in religion. This refutes those who claim that when saints reach a certain rank, obligation falls from them. We know that the highest of creation in the sight of Allah are the prophets and messengers, and the highest of them is Muhammad (ﷺ). If he was subject to obligation, then whoever is below him is so all the more.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 51–52 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rewards those who perform His obedience and follow His pleasure, and this is part of the requirement of His name al-Shakur (the Appreciative). Allah, exalted is He, named Himself al-Shakur in His saying: ﴿And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾ [al-Taghabun 17]. Among His appreciation is that He, glorified and exalted is He, bestows favours upon the one who performs obedience to Him according to what that obedience requires, based on the view that His saying ﴿from after this﴾ means: from after the giving of choice.
As for the second opinion, that what is meant is "from after these women," this benefit does not arise. However, we have mentioned that when a verse is suitable for two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is obligatory to interpret it as both.
* It is derived from this noble verse that it is not permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to divorce any of his wives in order to marry another in her place, based on His saying: ﴿nor that you exchange them for other wives﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not forbid divorce; rather, He forbade him to exchange them for other wives, and there is a difference between divorce and exchanging them for other wives.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ, like other human beings, is pleased by the beauty of women, both outward and inward, based on His saying: ﴿and even if their beauty pleased you﴾ [al-Ahzab 52].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of a man marrying a woman for her beauty, based on His saying: ﴿and even if their beauty pleased you﴾. This is supported by the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "A woman is married for four things: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty and her religion. So win the one who is religious." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5090), and Muslim (1466/53), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]
* It is derived from this noble verse that intercourse with a woman by right of ownership (milk al-yamin) is less burdensome for the woman than intercourse by marriage, based on His saying: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted a person not to act justly among his concubines, because jealousy among them is not like jealousy among wives. Therefore He said: "or what your right hand possesses."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of slavery (al-riq), based on His saying: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾. Slavery is established in Islam, and whoever denies its establishment has denied the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Muslims, and so he is an apostate until he repents and acknowledges the establishment of slavery. People in this matter are of two extremes and a middle position. Among them are those who enslave free persons; among them are those who deny the establishment of slavery absolutely; and among them are those who affirm slavery through its lawful causes and conditions. We hear of some groups of people who enslave their children and sell them to others, and this is common in Africa and East Asia, to the extent that some barbarians and rabble thought that this permits intercourse through this corrupt ownership, so they began buying their daughters from these people and having intercourse with them through this corrupt ownership. This does not establish ownership, and it is not a cause of slavery.
It has been established in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that Allah said: "There are three whose opponent I will be on the Day of Resurrection: a man who gives in My name and then betrays; a man who sells a free person and consumes his price; and a man who hires a labourer, takes full work from him, but does not give him his wage." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (2227) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] This is one category of people.
The second category: those who deny slavery absolutely, even where its lawful causes exist. This is said by those civilised nations that claim civilisation and progress. But it is strange that they deny the slavery that has lawful, divine causes, while they enslave the servants of Allah with a slavery harsher than Islamic slavery, without any lawful cause. The present problem of South Africa is only one example of this, for they enslave black people in a shameful manner and deprive them of their rights, and this is far more repugnant than lawful Islamic slavery. Moreover, lawful Islamic slavery contains no repugnance, because when you reflect on the texts concerning the rules of slaves, you find that the Shariah permitted their enslavement only for their own benefit, since the causes of slavery are one while the causes of freedom are many, and because the slave is obligated to be treated with kindness by his owner. On this basis, the third path, which is affirming slavery through the lawful divine causes, is the truth. It is indicated by the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus, and none denies it except an obstinate person, and whoever denies it is a disbeliever.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of expressing the whole by a part, based on His saying: ﴿what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab 52].
* From it also: the preference of the right hand over the left, in that ownership is attributed to it rather than to the left. The left hand is never used to express the whole self; rather, the general term "hands" is used and the right hand is used, but the expression with the left is not reported.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of one of Allah's names, al-Raqib (the Watchful), in His saying: ﴿and Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. Al-Raqib means al-Hafiz (the Preserver). Belief in Allah's watchfulness, glorified and exalted is He, necessitates for the servant perfect vigilance of Allah and fear of Him, and that he not dare to disobey Him nor fall short in His obedience. For if one of the kings, the kings of this world, had appointed a watcher over you, which is what is called the intelligence and investigation men, could you speak or do anything that would cause your punishment before that king? The answer: No. Indeed, they warn one another, saying: "Let there not be among you any of the intelligence men, let there not be among you any of the security men," and the like, and they fear him. This is with respect to the created being, so the watchfulness of the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, is more perfect and greater.
* It is derived from this noble verse: the eloquence of the Qur'an, in that it concludes the verses with what suits the rulings contained in them. Since the context is one of permitting and forbidding, it concluded with His saying: ﴿and Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾, meaning: He watches you if you oppose what has been legislated for you.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verses 51–52 (part 1 of 3):

Then He said: ﴿You may defer whom you wish of them, and take to you whom you wish, and whomever you seek out of those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you.﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51] ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ The author says: (with a hamzah and a yā' in its place, meaning "tu'akhkhir," "delays"). ﴿تُرْجِئُ﴾ and ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ mean "delay."

His saying ﴿مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ is the object of ﴿تُرْجِي﴾.

(﴿مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ means: your wives, regarding their turn. ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾ means: takes in. ﴿إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ means: from among them, so that you go to her. ﴿وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ﴾ means: you seek. ﴿مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ﴾ means: from the division (qasm, the equal allotment of nights among wives). So there is no blame upon you in seeking her and taking her to you. He was given the choice in this, after the division had been obligatory upon him.)

The author's words now indicate that His saying ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ refers to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) who were under his care, and that the meaning of ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ is to delay them, so that he does not allot a night to them, and ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾ is to take them in, so that he allots a night to them. Thus the verse was revealed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) division among his wives, and Allah the Exalted gave him the choice between deferring and taking in; that is, He gave him the choice between dividing among the wives and not dividing. In this there is latitude for the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the division: if he wished he divided, and if he wished he did not divide. This is one of the two opinions in the interpretation of the noble verse, and the context may support it: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their bridal payments﴾ up to His saying ﴿You may defer whom you wish of them﴾, meaning: of your wives, ﴿and take to you whom you wish﴾. So deferring means leaving off the division, and taking in means dividing.

The second opinion regarding the matter is that ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ means: of those women who gave themselves to you (as a gift). That is, if you wish you accept, and if you wish you refuse. ﴿وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ﴾ means: if you had refused her first and then wanted her again, there is no blame upon you. We have already mentioned a principle of tafsir: if a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, then the obligation is to take it as bearing both meanings. For this reason Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse includes both meanings together: that the Messenger (ﷺ) was given the choice between dividing and not dividing, and was given the choice between accepting a gift and not accepting it. And also, if he did not divide and then wished to divide, he may do so; and if he refused a gift and then wished to accept it, he may do so. The woman, if he did not divide for her and then he wished to divide for her, has no right to refuse, because the choice is in the hand of the Prophet (ﷺ).

* Student: Shaykh, (...) is taken to mean abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) (...) the Messenger was (...) which indicates that he used to divide?
* Shaykh: Yes, but he divided from himself. A division from himself, peace and blessings be upon him, that was not obligatory from Allah. That is, he divided of his own accord, even though he had the choice.
* Student: What is the evidence that he had the choice?
* Shaykh: This verse.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but it is suitable, and the early scholars (salaf) interpreted it that way, so it is suitable for both meanings.
* Student: (...) evidence for (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, there is a specific evidence. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has two wives and leans toward one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of him inclining."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2133) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is a threat.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, leaving it entirely, and if he wished, he may return (to her).

(﴿مِنْهُنَّ﴾ means: your wives, regarding their turn. ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾ means: takes in to you. ﴿مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ means: from among them, so that you go to her.)

(﴿وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ﴾ means: you sought. ﴿مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ﴾ means: from the division. So there is no blame upon you in seeking her and taking her in. He was given the choice in this, after the division had been obligatory upon him.)

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, has informed us that the verse concerns the ruling on division with respect to the Prophet (ﷺ), and that Allah the Exalted gave him the choice between dividing among his wives and not dividing, and that whoever he did not divide for, if it became apparent to him to divide for her, there is no hardship upon him. This is one of the two opinions on the verse.

The second opinion is that what is meant by His saying ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ is: of those women who gave themselves (as a gift). So the choice is yours whether to accept or not accept. And whichever of them you refused, there is no blame upon you afterward for seeking her. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse is general, covering both meanings together. This is what we have followed previously, that if a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, then the obligation is to apply it to all of them.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ refers to the choice.) The referent is "the choice": ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ and ﴿وَتُؤْوِي﴾, meaning: that choice derived from the two clauses.

(﴿أَدْنَى﴾ means: nearer to ﴿أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾, "that their eyes may be comforted, that they may not grieve, and that they may be pleased with what you give them." ﴿كُلُّهُنَّ﴾ refers to the thing given the choice, "all of them.")

His saying ﴿أَدْنَى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾: how is that? That is, what is the reason that this is nearer to their eyes being comforted? Because when they know that the choice between dividing and not dividing comes from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, their eyes are comforted, since they are content with the ruling of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. But if it were from the Prophet (ﷺ), that if he wished he divided and if he wished he did not divide, there would be some discomfort in their souls, since each one of them might think that this comes from the Prophet (ﷺ) and not from the law of Allah. So when the women know that this is from the law of Allah, their eyes are comforted.

His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾ is derived either from "qarār" (settling) or from "qarr," which means coolness. For when the eye becomes cool, its meaning is that it is not grieved; and when it becomes hot, its meaning is grief. For this reason they say: "the tear of grief is hot," because it comes out of the eye when it heats up from grief. But if there is no grief, it cools and settles.

His saying ﴿أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is conjoined with His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾. Is ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ in the subjunctive? Since ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾ is in the subjunctive by ﴿أَنْ﴾ and ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is conjoined to it, is it in the subjunctive? No, it is built on sukūn (a silent ending), because it is attached to the feminine plural nūn, and the nūn of the verb is assimilated into the feminine plural nūn; for "يحزن" is the verb, and the second nūn is the feminine plural nūn, which is the subject.

* Student: What about the conjunction "wāw"? Does it have no function?
* Shaykh: No, it has a function, but the verb here is built on sukūn in a position of naṣb (subjunctive) in ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾.

As for His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ﴾: the "wāw" is a conjunction particle, and ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾, not to ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾. For if it were conjoined to ﴿يَحْزَنَّ﴾, the meaning would be corrupted: the meaning would be "and that they not grieve and not be pleased," and the intended meaning is the opposite. So the intended meaning is: that this is nearer to their eyes being comforted and their being pleased.

If you say: what is the benefit of placing the second clause ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ in the middle?
We say: because its connection to His saying ﴿تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾ is stronger. For His saying ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ is meant to express the complete comfort of the eye; that is, that their eyes are comforted so that no grief remains in them at all. For this reason this clause was inserted between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined.

His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾: ﴿آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾ with the long vowel means "I gave them," because ﴿آتَى﴾ takes two objects; its first object is the pronoun ﴿هُنَّ﴾, and its second object is omitted, which the author supplied with the words (what was mentioned). And what was mentioned? He said: the thing given the choice, meaning: that they are pleased with what you have given them of the choice between dividing and not dividing.

We have already explained the reason why they are pleased with that: when the ruling comes from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, they are pleased with it, unlike if it were from the Prophet (ﷺ) at the outset, when they might not be pleased, since each one of them would think that this is a whim of the Prophet (ﷺ).

* Student: ﴿وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ﴾ (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, it is inserted between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, and it is conjoined. But now it is inserted, meaning that it is not correct for us to conjoin what follows it to it; rather it is conjoined to what precedes it.

He said: ﴿كُلُّهُنَّ﴾ is an emphasis of the subject in ﴿يَرْضَيْنَ﴾. He said this because if it were an emphasis of the pronoun in His saying ﴿بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ﴾, it would be in the accusative: ﴿بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلَّهُنَّ﴾. But it is, as he said, an emphasis of the subject in His saying ﴿يَرْضَيْنَ﴾.

Is it not correct that it be an emphasis of the pronoun in His saying ﴿أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾? It is not correct; for if it were an emphasis of that, it would be in the genitive, "kullihinna." So it is necessarily an emphasis of His saying ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾.

(﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ means: of the matter of the women and the inclination toward some of them.) When Allah the Mighty and Majestic made clear that the Prophet (ﷺ) was given the choice, He made clear that He, the Mighty and Majestic, knows what is in the hearts: a person's inclination toward some women over others. Allah the Exalted has explained this known matter by His saying: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave her as if suspended.﴾ [An-Nisa' 129]. This is a matter confirmed by reality and witnessed by it, for a person can never make his affection for two wives completely equal, even if it is supposed that one of them is preferred by him in one respect and the other in another respect. Equality is impossible, and this is what His saying the Exalted supports: ﴿you will never be able to be equitable between wives﴾.

As for His saying ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: is a threat and warning derived from it, or is it derived that this is a matter you do not control? The apparent meaning is the second: that this is a matter we do not control.

(...) concerning His punishment. This is like a justification for His saying ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. He, the Exalted, is All-Knowing of everything, and among that is what is in our hearts of inclination toward some women over others. And His saying ﴿Forbearing﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]: what is forbearance? Forbearance is not hastening punishment, and it is not the abandonment of punishment. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim said:

"He is the Forbearing, so He does not hasten His servant with punishment, so that he may repent of disobedience."

So forbearance is the delay of punishment, not pardoning it. He delays punishment for what reason? So that this sinner may repent to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and the punishment will be lifted from him.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this]﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. He said: ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ﴾ with the taa' and the yā': ﴿لا تحل﴾ and ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ﴾. As for the reading ﴿لا تحل﴾, there is no difficulty, because "an-nisā'" is the plural of "niswah," and "niswah" is the plural of "imra'ah" (woman), for "imra'ah" has no plural from its own form, but has a plural from its meaning, like "al-ibil" (camels), the plural of "ba'īr," which has no singular from its own form. So His saying ﴿لا تحل لك النساء﴾ has no difficulty. But His saying ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ﴾: how is the verb masculine when the subject is feminine? Answer.

* Student: Shaykh, repeat the question.
* Shaykh: We will not repeat the question.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is a hidden, attached verb, or it is completed by "lā tahillu," but with attachment. But with separation it is permissible: ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾. The author said: (after the nine whom you chose). Is it "allatī" or "al-lātī" in your copies?
* Student: "allatī."
* Shaykh: "The nine whom you chose." The sense of the statement would require him to say "allātī ikhtarnak" (those who chose you). The meaning is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, they chose Allah and His Messenger. When they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them, so He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. On this basis this is a case of immediate reward, and they have a deferred reward as well, because when they chose Allah and His Messenger over the life of this world and its adornment, Allah thanked them, so He forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from marrying others besides them, or from divorcing one and marrying another. So He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [this]﴾. This is one of the two opinions on the verse.

The second opinion: the meaning of the verse, ﴿لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾, is: after what has been mentioned to you, which is His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their bridal payments, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives], and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 50]. The meaning on this basis is: women are not lawful to you after what we have mentioned to you. Accordingly, it is not lawful for the Prophet (ﷺ) to marry any woman of the Arabs other than the daughters of his paternal uncles, the daughters of his paternal aunts, the daughters of his maternal uncles and the daughters of his maternal aunts who emigrated with him. Nor is it lawful for him to marry a woman from the People of the Book, since she is not one of these.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that the verse includes both meanings together: it is not lawful for him to marry over the Mothers of the Believers, nor to marry besides these. If you say: could we not say that the first meaning, "women are not lawful to you besides these women," includes the second meaning, so there is no need for the second opinion? Do you understand this or not? If we say: "It is not lawful for you besides these who are with you," this includes the second opinion, that it is not lawful for him besides those mentioned in "We have made lawful to you your wives." So what is the benefit of the second opinion then?

The answer to this is that if it is supposed that these women die during the lifetime of the Messenger (ﷺ), is it lawful for him to marry others besides those whom Allah made lawful to him? In that case the second opinion has a benefit. This benefit appears if it is supposed that the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) who are with him die before him, for then it is not lawful for him to take women except those Allah mentioned: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 50].

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52] by dropping one of the two taa's in the original.) ﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ﴾: he says: (by dropping one of the two taa's in the original). The word ﴿تَبَدَّلَ﴾ originally was "tatabaddal." The evidence that its original form is "tatabaddal" and that it is not a past tense verb is that ﴿أن﴾ entered upon it and put it in the subjunctive, and only the imperfect is entered by ﴿أن﴾ and put in the subjunctive. Otherwise the word ﴿تَبَدَّلَ﴾ could be a past tense verb, but since ﴿أن﴾ entered upon it and governed it in the subjunctive, it is known that it is an imperfect verb from which one of the two taa's was dropped. Is there a parallel to this? Yes, there is a parallel, such as ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend﴾ [Al-Qadr 4], meaning "tatanazzal" (descend), and ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire blazing﴾ [Al-Layl 14], meaning "tatalaẓẓā" (blazing). Who asks?

* Student: (...) the Messenger (ﷺ), does this contradict the first opinion?
* Shaykh: Which is?
* Student: That the Messenger (ﷺ) in the last days of his life wanted to divorce.
* Shaykh: Yes, and he divorced Hafsah too; he divorced Hafsah and then took her back.
* Student: How can it be with this meaning, that "it is not lawful for you women..."?
* Shaykh: It does not contradict it. That is, it is not permissible for him to marry others, "it is not lawful for you women after this," and it is not permissible for him to divorce one in order to marry another besides her. For He said: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾; He did not say "nor to divorce"; He said: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning by divorcing one and marrying another.

(﴿وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾ means: by divorcing them, or some of them, and marrying in place of the one divorced.) This too is not lawful for him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) did not do it after this verse was revealed. He did not divorce one in order to marry another, nor did he marry others besides them; rather they remained with him until he died. But he died leaving two wives during his lifetime, and who were they? Khadijah; and after her? Zaynab bint Khuzaymah. He married her after her husband was martyred at Uhud, and she remained with him for months, then she died, and the rest of his wives were those he left at his death.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 33, verses 51–52 (part 2 of 3):

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take other wives in place of them, even though their beauty may please you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52]. What is meant is outward beauty, or inward beauty, or both. The verse includes both. The Prophet (ﷺ), like other men, may marry a woman for her beauty, but with religious commitment. He may also marry her for her religion, or for her knowledge and understanding. So His words ﴿even though their beauty may please you﴾ include both outward and inward beauty. His words ﴿may please you﴾ mean that the admiration reached you, because of the perfection of their outward and inward beauty.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: He said: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ of the slave-women, so they are lawful to you... and so on. That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepted what his right hand possesses. This is because jealousy does not arise in a wife toward a slave-woman in the same way it does toward another wife. Jealousy does not arise in a wife toward a slave-woman because the slave-woman does not compete with her or equal her, and because the slave-woman has no turn (qasm). The right of turns is not obligatory for slave-women.

﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained what He had made lawful for His Messenger and what He had made unlawful for him, He concluded the verse by mentioning His watchfulness, may He be blessed and exalted, over all things. Allah explained His watchfulness over all things in order to encourage caution against opposing His command. If He, glorified and exalted, is watchful over all things, then a person will be cautious and fear opposing Him.

As for His words ﴿And Allah is﴾, we have previously discussed similar examples several times. We said that the past tense here is stripped of its indication of time. The meaning is not that Allah was in a past time and that the ruling later changed. Rather, it establishes that Allah, glorified and exalted, is characterized by watchfulness. His words ﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾: "over all things" includes what is hidden and what is apparent, what is specific to the Messenger (ﷺ) and what is general to him and to the Ummah. It includes deeds of the limbs and deeds of the hearts, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16].

Now let us return to deriving benefits from the noble verse.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them and take to you whom you will. And whom you seek from those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], to the end.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, may single out whom He wills with His rulings. This is shown by His words ﴿You may put off﴾ and ﴿take to you﴾, according to the view that the intended meaning is the turn (qasm). Allah gave him the choice between committing to the turn and not committing to it. This is one of the particular privileges of the Prophet (ﷺ). As for the Ummah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side leaning." [Abu Dawud (2133), and the wording is his, and al-Tirmidhi (1141), from Abu Hurairah.] This indicates the obligation of justice among wives for the Ummah.

According to the second view regarding His words ﴿You may put off﴾ and ﴿take to you﴾, that it means accepting or rejecting the woman who has given herself to the Prophet, there is also evidence that Allah granted His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) latitude in matters concerning marriage. He may accept, and he may refuse.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to retract a right after waiving it, based on His words ﴿And whom you seek from those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. This applies when the right is renewable. But if the right is not renewable, then when a person waives it, he cannot take it back. An example: a woman waived her share or right to maintenance for a past period, such as when the husband had stopped providing for her for a year, and she waived the right. Can she take it back?

She cannot take it back, because the right here is not renewable. It concerns a past matter. If a woman waives her right to the turn, can she reclaim it in the future? Yes, she can reclaim it, because her right renews. Unless it was made a condition in the marriage contract, such as the husband stipulating to his new wife that he will not divide turns for her, and she accepted. In that case she cannot reclaim it, because it became a condition of the contract. A condition in a contract must be fulfilled, because it falls under the general scope of Allah's words: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfill [your] contracts﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 1]. This differs from the case where she waived it after the contract. Then the waiver stands, and she cannot reclaim it, because she cannot waive a future right.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is subject to obligation, based on His words ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾. This is because negating an attribute of something indicates that it is possible for it to have that attribute. If it were absent from the outset, there would be no need to negate it. This shows that blame could have fallen upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is evidence that he is charged with the rulings of the Message.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists). From where is this taken? ﴿And whom you seek﴾, meaning: whom you desire and wish. The Jabriyyah hold that a person has no will. Rather, he is compelled and driven to his deeds without any will of his own.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes and wisdoms behind rulings, that rulings are tied to their causes and purposes. From where is this taken? ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. The affirmation of wisdom in Allah's cosmic and decreed rulings is very numerous, and all of them also refute the Jabriyyah. This is because the Jabriyyah hold that the acts and rulings of Allah, glorified and exalted, have no cause or wisdom, and that He acts not for a cause and wisdom but merely by will. Does this support the position of the Mu'tazilah, who hold that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best (al-aslah) or what is good (al-salah)? I do not know. Do you know this or not? This came up for us in the Safariniyyah creed, where he said:

*So it is not obligatory upon Him to do what is best, nor what is good; woe to him who does not prosper.*

The Mu'tazilah say that it is obligatory upon Him to do what is best when the good and the better conflict, and to do what is good when the good and the corrupt conflict. He said: it is obligatory upon Allah to do what is best when the good conflicts with the better, and the good when the good conflicts with the corrupt. But the correct view is that there is a distinction here. If we say it is obligatory in the sense that our intellects have made it obligatory upon Allah, then this is false, because intellects cannot make anything obligatory upon Allah. They are too lowly and too contemptible to obligate anything upon Allah. If we say that it is obligatory by the requirement of His wisdom, then this is true and correct, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does nothing except that it is best. As Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah does not like corruption﴾ [Al-Baqarah 205], ﴿And Allah does not like corrupters﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 64], and ﴿Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good﴾ [Al-A'raf 170].

Since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, praised the doers of good and negated that He loves corruption or corrupters, this indicates that it is impossible for Him to will corruption. Accordingly, we say: the Mu'tazilah erred in obligating this upon Allah by their intellects, because the intellect is too lowly and contemptible to obligate anything upon Allah. Intellect may see something as obligatory when in reality it is not, because intellects are limited. It may judge something to be best when it is not. Allah pointed to this in His words: ﴿But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 216]. As for saying that it is obligatory by the requirement of His wisdom, this is true. So here we say: affirming causes refutes the Jabriyyah, who are also the Jahmiyyah in this matter. It provides no support for the Mu'tazilah's view that it is obligatory for Allah to do what is best or good.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: caring for the hearts of the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) and bringing joy to them. From where is this taken? ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51]. This is because it shows consideration for the hearts of these women, so that their eyes may be comforted.

* Also among its lessons: it is appropriate to consider the believer by bringing joy to him and removing sadness from him, based on His words ﴿nor grieve﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], meaning: that they should not be overcome by grief and distress over what has passed. This state of the believer contradicts the state of Satan, for Satan strives with everything that saddens the children of Adam, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Private conversation is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who have believed﴾ [Al-Mujadilah 10]. Therefore, whoever tries to bring sadness upon his Muslim brother resembles Satan, who seeks to bring sorrow upon the believers.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defends His Prophet (ﷺ) through various defensive methods. The aspect of this is that when Allah gave him the choice, He made clear that this ruling came from Allah. That is so that when the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) know that this ruling is from Allah, whatever dissatisfaction or grief was in their souls disappears. Undoubtedly, a person's contentment with what comes from Allah is more complete than his contentment with what comes from other than Allah. This is one aspect.

Although a believer is content with what comes from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) just as he is content with what comes from Allah, yet since the Prophet (ﷺ) was a husband to these women, it may occur to their minds that the Messenger's (ﷺ) dividing turns or not dividing them, or accepting or refusing, is merely a matter of his own desire. If they believed that it was merely his own desire, grief would enter them. But when they know that this is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who granted him this latitude, the grief departs from them.

From this benefit another may branch out, which is that a person should ward off from himself whatever he might be blamed for. Whatever you fear people might blame you for, repel the suspicion from yourself. This has a basis. What is it?

* Student: (...) the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ), he said: "Slowly, both of you, she is Safiyyah." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2035), and Muslim (2175/24), from Safiyyah bint Huyayy.]

* Shaykh: And what is the second?

* Student: (...).

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: using emphasizing particles where the need calls for them, based on His word ﴿all of them﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51], lest someone wrongly think that the contentment of some of them and the removal of grief from some of them is sufficient. Rather, contentment must be for all of them.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted, of outward and inward matters, based on His words ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ [Al-Ahzab 51].

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: what is in the heart, which a person does not control, is not held against him. This is because when He mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) was given the choice, He said: ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, meaning: of the things you do not control. For this reason, it is permissible for a person, or rather it is not forbidden for a person, to prefer one of his wives over another in love, because love has its seat in the heart, and a person cannot direct his heart and subject it to make himself love or hate.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the seat of volitions is the heart, based on His words ﴿what is in your hearts﴾. Is the meant heart the physical heart or the metaphorical heart, which is the intellect? The physical heart, because the correct view is that the physical heart is the one on which matters depend, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599/107), from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]

Scholars have differed over whether the intellect is in the heart or in the brain. The apparent meaning of the Noble Quran is that the intellect is in the heart, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth so that they would have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 46]. This is also supported by the Sunnah, in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt." This indicates that the intellect is in the heart. However, Imam Ahmad said that it has a connection to the brain. That is, it is in the heart, but it has a connection to the brain. For this reason, if the brain is corrupted, the intellect is corrupted. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in several places in his speech that the brain is the seat of perception and the shaping of things, and that the heart is the seat of management and direction. So the brain is like the heart's secretary: it prepares matters for it, forms them, and shapes them, then sends them to the heart, and the heart commands, forbids, approves, or rejects.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names: the All-Knowing (al-'Alim) and the Forbearing (al-Halim). Al-'Alim is the One who encompasses everything in knowledge. Knowledge, according to the jurists or the usulis (scholars of legal theory), is the perception of a thing with certainty and correspondence to reality. Their phrase "with certainty" excludes doubt, supposition, and suspicion, which are not called knowledge because they are not certain. Their phrase "corresponding to reality" excludes compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab), because a person who has compound ignorance perceives a thing in a way that does not correspond to reality. Their phrase "perception of a thing" excludes simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basit), because simple ignorance involves no perception at all. This is what knowledge is.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not acquire new knowledge. What is renewed is the known object. The relation of Allah's knowledge to the known has two states: a relation to it before it occurs, and a relation to it after it occurs. The relation before it occurs means that He knows it will happen. The relation after it occurs means that He knows it has happened. The one upon which reward and punishment are based is the second relation, the relation to the object after its occurrence. On this basis the difficulty raised by some scholars concerning His words ﴿And We will surely test you until We make evident those of you who strive﴾ [Muhammad 31] is resolved. Regarding ﴿until We make evident﴾: does this mean He did not know those who strive? We say: yes, He knows. But the knowledge upon which reward is based is knowledge of the thing after it occurs. So what renews is not the knowledge but the known.

Does Allah's knowledge relate to the necessary, the possible, and the impossible, or to the necessary and the possible but not the impossible, or to the possible only? What do you say? To all of them: the necessary, the possible, and the impossible. As for His knowledge of the necessary, it is His knowledge of the names and attributes that He deserves, because this is knowledge of the necessary, since Allah has the perfection that is due to Him.

As for His knowledge of the impossible, it is found in His words: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any deity. [If there were], each deity would have taken away what it created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 91], and His words: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [Al-Anbiya 22]. This is knowledge of the impossible. As for the possible, what a person does and does not do is known. This is knowledge of the possible.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation of the name al-Halim (the Forbearing). Al-Halim is the One who does not hasten punishment, not the One who does not punish. The One who does not punish is al-'Afuww (the Pardoner). This is the difference between al-Halim and al-'Afuww. He, glorified and exalted, is Forbearing, who does not hasten punishment, and Pardoning, who pardons sin so that He does not punish for it.

Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty may please you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [Al-Ahzab 52].

* From this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is charged with obligations like other people. That is, things are made lawful for him and unlawful for him. From this benefit another branches out, which is that obligation can never be lifted from anyone, no matter how high his rank in religion. This refutes those who claim that when saints reach a certain rank, obligation falls from them. We know that the highest of creation in the sight of Allah are the prophets and messengers, and the highest of them is Muhammad (ﷺ). If he was subject to obligation, then whoever is below him is so all the more.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 33, verse 51–52 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rewards those who perform His obedience and follow His pleasure, and this is part of the requirement of His name al-Shakur (the Appreciative). Allah, exalted is He, named Himself al-Shakur in His saying: ﴿And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾ [al-Taghabun 17]. Among His appreciation is that He, glorified and exalted is He, bestows favours upon the one who performs obedience to Him according to what that obedience requires, based on the view that His saying ﴿from after this﴾ means: from after the giving of choice.
As for the second opinion, that what is meant is "from after these women," this benefit does not arise. However, we have mentioned that when a verse is suitable for two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is obligatory to interpret it as both.
* It is derived from this noble verse that it is not permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to divorce any of his wives in order to marry another in her place, based on His saying: ﴿nor that you exchange them for other wives﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not forbid divorce; rather, He forbade him to exchange them for other wives, and there is a difference between divorce and exchanging them for other wives.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ, like other human beings, is pleased by the beauty of women, both outward and inward, based on His saying: ﴿and even if their beauty pleased you﴾ [al-Ahzab 52].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of a man marrying a woman for her beauty, based on His saying: ﴿and even if their beauty pleased you﴾. This is supported by the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "A woman is married for four things: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty and her religion. So win the one who is religious." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5090), and Muslim (1466/53), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]
* It is derived from this noble verse that intercourse with a woman by right of ownership (milk al-yamin) is less burdensome for the woman than intercourse by marriage, based on His saying: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab 52]. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted a person not to act justly among his concubines, because jealousy among them is not like jealousy among wives. Therefore He said: "or what your right hand possesses."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of slavery (al-riq), based on His saying: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾. Slavery is established in Islam, and whoever denies its establishment has denied the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Muslims, and so he is an apostate until he repents and acknowledges the establishment of slavery. People in this matter are of two extremes and a middle position. Among them are those who enslave free persons; among them are those who deny the establishment of slavery absolutely; and among them are those who affirm slavery through its lawful causes and conditions. We hear of some groups of people who enslave their children and sell them to others, and this is common in Africa and East Asia, to the extent that some barbarians and rabble thought that this permits intercourse through this corrupt ownership, so they began buying their daughters from these people and having intercourse with them through this corrupt ownership. This does not establish ownership, and it is not a cause of slavery.
It has been established in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that Allah said: "There are three whose opponent I will be on the Day of Resurrection: a man who gives in My name and then betrays; a man who sells a free person and consumes his price; and a man who hires a labourer, takes full work from him, but does not give him his wage." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (2227) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] This is one category of people.
